Three tools then revise the factorization: requery adds trajectories where the rendering shows parts the tracker missed, merge joins motions that move together, and split separates those that do not. Thus the number of motions follows the scene. Without masks, DynMF2 clearly outperforms the mask-based baselines in view synthesis on iPhone and NVIDIA and in 3D tracking on iPhone. It recovers what masks leave out, from thin parts and details to small movers far in the background. Its motions segment the moving parts of MOVi-F and iTACO scenes competitively, although DynMF2 is never trained to segment. What moves in a scene is not decided in advance: it emerges from the rigid motions themselves.

authors.name: Agelos Kratimenos, Yile Hua, Kostas Daniilidis

papers.title: A Mesh for Every Moment
papers.summary: We present MEMO (a Mesh for Every MOment), a method that reconstructs the geometry of complete dynamic scenes, captured by multiple synchronized cameras, and extracts a mesh at every frame. Existing dynamic Gaussian splatting methods either model appearance alone or target isolated objects segmented by foreground masks, and all of them recover meshes by TSDF fusion or Poisson reconstruction, whose fixed grids limit the detail they can capture. At the core of MEMO is a per-Gaussian motion model inspired by Gaussian processes, which represents each Gaussian's position and rotation over time as a combination of temporal Gaussian kernels. The model keeps every Gaussian a valid surface element throughout the sequence and carries an implicit representation of the dynamic geometry, so a mesh can be derived at any time from a field defined by the Gaussians. Although common in real captures, large and fast motion poses a challenge that dynamic Gaussian splatting methods usually overlook. To account for it, we design a track-based initialization scheme that fits each Gaussian's initial trajectory to point tracks in closed form. We evaluate MEMO on Blender-Moments, a new benchmark of nine animated scenes with ground-truth meshes at every frame, and on two real-world datasets. MEMO reconstructs the most accurate geometry among state-of-the-art methods, and remains competitive in novel-view synthesis and training time. Project page: https://memo-4d.github.io

authors.name: Roy Or-El, Jeong Joon Park, Ira Kemelmacher-Shlizerman

papers.title: LuxAvatar: Real-Time Relightable Head Avatars via Causal Neural Shading of 3D Intrinsic Proxies
papers.summary: We present LuxAvatar, a feed-forward framework for real-time head avatar animation and relighting from a single portrait. To achieve both 3D controllability and complex facial light transport, we factorize avatar synthesis into an animatable 3D intrinsic Gaussian proxy and a causal autoregressive neural shader. This proxy disentangles canonical geometry and reflectance attributes, rapidly rasterizing deformed Gaussians into view- and motion-consistent PBR buffers. Conditioned on these buffers, our neural shader formulates forward rendering as a conditional video diffusion process, bypassing explicit PBR computation to synthesize realistic shading effects under target illumination. We achieve real-time streaming through heterogeneous distillation from a pretrained multi-step bidirectional relighting teacher to a two-step causal autoregressive neural shader, inheriting broad synthetic lighting priors while minimizing conditioning and decoding latency. To further specialize these priors to human heads, we construct a hybrid relighting dataset for domain-specific fine-tuning, capturing authentic facial dynamics and physically grounded light transport. Extensive experiments show that our framework enables 3D-controllable, real-time portrait animation and relighting, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in visual fidelity, motion control, and lighting accuracy.

authors.name: Yipengjing Sun, Chenyang Wang, Boyao Zhou, Jiapeng Zhu, Ka Leong Cheng, Shengping Zhang

papers.title: Improving and Expanding Video Editing Capabilities Without Videos
papers.summary: Image editing models can follow a wide range of instructions, but video editing models still lag behind, limited in part by the difficulty of collecting paired source and edited videos. Is it possible to transfer advanced image editing capabilities to video editors without new paired videos? We introduce Image-to-Video Transfer (I2VT), which improves pretrained video editors and expands them to new editing tasks using an image editor. It enables efficient post-training with no architectural changes and no new videos, using only individual images. Our key idea is to let the video editor role-play as an image editor: it edits an image as a one-frame video, with the image editor guiding the video editor's predictions at each denoising step. Although the video editor sees only single images during training, at test time it applies the improved and expanded capabilities to whole video clips while preserving temporal consistency. To push the boundaries of video editing, we introduce OpenVE++, an extension of OpenVE-Bench that adds four new editing tasks useful for video production, including action changes, expression changes, body movements, and scene relighting. Our experiments across three different video editors show that I2VT improves existing editing capabilities and expands them to new tasks, and our models achieve state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on both OpenVE-Bench and OpenVE++.

authors.name: Ji Xie, Yanhao Jia, Xiangpeng Yang, Martin Q. Ma, Sihan Xu, Erik Cambria, Louis-Philippe Morency

papers.title: Tracking Any Point with Agentic Visual Reasoning
papers.summary: A general-purpose Vision-Language Model (VLM) has surpassed expert vision models in many domains such as object detection and video recognition. However, point correspondence is known to be challenging for VLMs since it goes beyond object-level recognition: it requires pixel-level localization of the same physical surface point across observations, even when appearance changes or the point disappears and later reappears. In this paper, we introduce AgenTAP, a VLM-based agent that directly predicts point coordinates and visibility and actively reasons over videos. Starting from its own estimate, the agent autonomously chooses what to inspect and uses the resulting evidence to verify point identity and refine its predictions. With GPT-6 Astra, it surpasses expert vision models in both point localization and visibility prediction, without correspondence-specific fine-tuning. We further use AgenTAP to re-identify physical points after disappearance and reconnect fragmented tracks, constructing EgoTAP-4D, a dataset of 3D point trajectories in long real-world egocentric videos. On sampled reappearing points, its predictions approach human agreement, and adding EgoTAP-4D to D4RT training improves average 3D tracking performance.

authors.name: Xuweiyi Chen, Jin Yao, Linzhan Mou, Lei Gong, Di Liu, Cheng Zhang, Ziqiao Ma, Sihan Xu, Adam W. Harley, Shengyi Qian, Zezhou Cheng

papers.title: AnyCam: Anything Can Represent Camera for Video Generation
papers.summary: Camera-controlled video generation re-renders a video along a target camera trajectory, yet moving the camera around an object, the most natural way to change the viewpoint of an object-centric scene, remains difficult. Existing methods condition either on camera parameters, which are scale-ambiguous in monocular video, or on explicit geometry such as warped point clouds or depth, which breaks down under large viewpoint changes. We present AnyCam, a method that represents the camera with an anchor object in the scene: we reconstruct it in 3D and render it along the target trajectory, a camera signal that is scale-aware, view-complete and easy to specify relative to the object. A video diffusion model transfers the content and dynamics of the source video to the new viewpoint. Its H-Concat layout aligns source and target frames in time, so the model can be distilled into AnyCam-AR, a streaming few-step generator for on-the-fly camera control. Both models are trained on paired videos with pixel-aligned anchor renderings from multi-camera videos and static-scene captures. Experiments on diverse datasets and trajectories show that AnyCam performs favorably against camera-controlled video generation and 3D reconstruction methods in camera control and visual quality.

authors.name: Weijie Lyu, Zhixin Shu, Yuntian Ke, Ming-Hsuan Yang

papers.title: Beyond the section plane: Robust 3D reconstruction of multiplex immunofluorescence exposes limitations of 2D spatial cell statistics
papers.summary: Spatial analysis of the tumour microenvironment with multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) typically relies on single thin tissue sections, which misrepresent the 3D tissue organisation and bias spatial cell statistics in ways that remain largely unquantified. We reconstruct 24 breast and lung tumour tissue microarray cores in 3D, each from 15-20 serial mIF sections, and compare spatial cell statistics in 3D with those from individual sections. Our pipeline combines affine pre-alignment with dense deformable refinement using RoMa v2, achieving a median target registration error of 1.79 $\mu$m, well below nuclear size, which allows nuclei to be linked across sections. While cell-type proportions are preserved in 2D (Pearson corr. $r \geq 0.99$), 3D analysis reveals up to 3.8 times shorter nearest-neighbour distances, 13-19% higher neighbourhood entropy, and 2-4 times more contacts per cell. Tissue composition can thus be reliably estimated from individual sections, whereas cell-cell interactions require volumetric analysis.

authors.name: Junming Ma (Department of Information Technology, Uppsala University, Uppsala, Sweden), Olle Edgren Sch\"ullerqvist (Department of Information Technology, Uppsala University, Uppsala, Sweden, SciLifeLab, Uppsala University, Uppsala, Sweden), Hui Yu (Department of Immunology, Genetics and Pathology, Uppsala University, Uppsala, Sweden), Carina Strell (Department of Immunology, Genetics and Pathology, Uppsala University, Uppsala, Sweden), Patrick Micke (Department of Immunology, Genetics and Pathology, Uppsala University, Uppsala, Sweden), Joakim Lindblad (Department of Information Technology, Uppsala University, Uppsala, Sweden, SciLifeLab, Uppsala University, Uppsala, Sweden), Artur Mezheyeuski (Vall d'Hebron Institute of Research & Institute of Oncology, Barcelona, Spain), Nata\v{s}a Sladoje (Department of Information Technology, Uppsala University, Uppsala, Sweden, SciLifeLab, Uppsala University, Uppsala, Sweden)

papers.title: Confidently Lost: Silent Failure and Edge Deployment of Dense Visual SLAM under Photon Starvation
papers.summary: Dense visual SLAM built on learned two-view geometry is evaluated in good light; in low light it fails silently. Two frames of 9-level quantized noise, no scene at all, give MASt3R-SLAM's network a cross-view geometric self-consistency of 0.936; a real dark frame pair gives 0.935. Starved of structure, the network invents the same geometry for both views and the system trusts the agreement: on a dark sequence it consumes 1,605 frames, emits 7 keyframes, rejects no factor-graph edges and reports full frame rate, while over 95% of the correspondences it accepts violate the ground-truth epipolar geometry. One inflated statistic is read by two subsystems against thresholds in opposite directions, so keyframing starves while relocalization accepts almost every candidate. The same statistic, read at keyframe-pair baselines, separates the confident collapse from working runs on the ETH3D dark sequences without ground truth or extra computation (in-sample). Low-light-adapted weights take tracked trajectories from 1/6 to 5/6, as does retuning two thresholds; neither yields accurate ones, because the adaptation withdraws confidence from wrong geometry rather than finding right geometry. Replayed on a Jetson AGX Orin carried by a legged robot, the mechanism's signature reproduces on the two darkest of four routes, and which of its faces appears varies with route geometry and sensor encoding. The network does not lose confidence in the dark; it manufactures it.

authors.name: Shrikrishna Bhagirath Rajule, Srinath Neelamagam, Aniket Bera

papers.title: Innata-0: A Native Embodied World System with Model-Agent Co-Design
papers.summary: The physical world is open-ended, dynamic, and partially observable. While foundation models have advanced embodied intelligence, standalone models struggle with long-horizon execution, and simply integrating models with agents may lead to inconsistencies between planning and physical control. To support reliable and adaptive behaviors in the physical world, we introduce Innata-0, a native embodied world system. Innata-0 jointly designs an embodied world-action model and an agent to combine their complementary strengths. The model, Innata-0-WAM, adopts a tri-tower Mixture-of-Transformers architecture that integrates understanding, prediction, and action generation. The agent, Innata-0-Agent, coordinates long-horizon execution through memory, verification, and recovery. A co-design protocol is further proposed to align model training with agent execution and leverage validated experiences to support subsequent adaptation and model improvement. Extensive evaluations demonstrate strong embodied capabilities across understanding, world prediction, and robotic manipulation. Innata-0 represents our first step toward physical intelligence, and we see it as the beginning of a much longer journey.

authors.name: Innata Team, Yu Bai, Ziyi Bai, Yuxuan Cai, Chenrui He, Wenhao Li, Zhe Lin, Heng Wang, Hai Yuan, Zhiwei Yu, Yuanhang Zhang, Luyou Chen, Tiezhu Gao, Zheng Geng, Jinbang Guo, Dongxu Han, Diqi He, B\"orje F. Karlsson, Jintao Li, Zhiyu Li, Xiongkun Linghu, Guang Liu, You Liu, Zhen Luo, Mengsi Lyu, Yufeng Lyu, Zheng Lyu, Quanyue Ma, Chunlei Men, Ziqiang Ni, Tengfei Pan, Yijun Shen, Liang Sun, Shaoxuan Xie, Xiang Yang, Guocai Yao, Hongjun Zhang, Yingli Zhao, Yonghua Lin, Zhongyuan Wang, Huan Yang

papers.title: Real-time Food Recipe Generation with Mobile Deep Learning and Large Language Model
papers.summary: Finding recipes that match available kitchen ingredients can be cumbersome and inefficient. This paper addresses this challenge by developing a mobile application that generates tailored food recipes based on ingredients identified using a mobile camera. Leveraging deep learning and large language model (LLM), our system offers a seamless and efficient solution for real-time recipe generation. By integrating deep learning for accurate ingredient recognition with LLM for generating detailed and practical recipes, our approach ensures users receive precise cooking instructions based on actual ingredients on hand. Extensive dataset augmentation and model training have resulted in a robust system capable of high performance. Experimental results demonstrate that EfficientNet, used for food recognition, offers a balance of accuracy and computational efficiency, making it ideal for mobile applications. This dual-approach method enhances the cooking experience, reduces food waste, and provides a comprehensive, real-time tool for everyday cooking needs, bridging a significant gap in current food recommendation systems.

authors.name: Wei Jun Leung, Mun Hong Lee, Joo Wee Quek, Desmond Loy, Yifei Wang, Yan Ning Ang, Pai Chet Ng, Kan Chen, Jeannie Lee

papers.title: PhoneWatchUI: A Dataset of Smartphone and Smartwatch Images from App Stores
papers.summary: Smartwatch apps are unique as they must condense functionality into a tiny screen of a few square centimeters. Yet, public GUI datasets are almost exclusively phone- or web-centric. We present PhoneWatchUI: 966.2k publisher-curated gallery image records from 72k store-specific app IDs on the US Apple App Store and Google Play, collected during October 2026. The Apple App Store part covers 37.6k apps with explicit Apple Watch platform metadata: 143.8k watch and 212.2k phone images labeled by their source galleries. The Google Play part covers 34.3k keyword-selected apps and 610.2k gallery images, provisionally labeled as watch, phone, or others by aspect ratio. Image records link to app metadata (title, description, category, ratings, developer, price) and retain source URLs, device-label provenance, and dimensions where available. We describe the dataset composition, image properties, and limitations. PhoneWatchUI enables research on cross-device GUI adaptation, wearable GUI retrieval and generation, as well as app-store analysis that links textual claims to visual evidence. Dataset is available at: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Jl-wei/PhoneWatchUI

authors.name: Jialiang Wei, Walid Maalej

papers.title: NeuroRefine: Six-Head MLP Content Conditioning and Qwen Refinement for Faithful fMRI Decoding
papers.summary: Reconstructing seen images from fMRI has advanced through diffusion models, but the current state-of-the-art Brain-IT pipeline still has a lossy bottleneck: its low-level branch outlines the figure well, yet the diffusion model that follows frequently mispaints colour, object identity and layout. We move one step backward and condition the refiner directly on the fMRI-derived low-level image, using six one-hidden-layer MLP heads (scene, main-subject category, count, colour, object, layout) to predict the content prompt that guides a frozen Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 model. On the 930 shared NSD concepts, scored with Brain-IT's own metric code on the same ground truth, NeuroRefine reaches a CLIP image cosine of 0.755 against 0.735 for Brain-IT enhanced and produces markedly sharper images, while the saturated 2-way identification is unchanged. The low-level image supplies an explicit spatial prior rather than a lossless layout: refinement trades some layout agreement (0.541 against 0.638) for semantic fidelity and texture. We then show that the standard panel is multi-factor: a high PixCorr can coexist with completely different content, so we read the low-level and semantic factors separately and quantify where they disagree. Finally, we trace the cortical sources of the prompt heads across subjects and report their causal lesion profile and the fMRI noise ceiling. Direction errors are left to future work.

authors.name: Runqi Xu, Vince D. Calhoun

papers.title: OnCue: Generating Safety-Critical Driving Scenarios under Occlusion with Temporal Control
papers.summary: Occluded hazards challenge autonomous driving because visibility timing determines available avoidance actions. Existing scenario generators control hazard motion without jointly specifying exposure and reference-contact times. We propose OnCue, a framework that generates safety-critical encounters in real driving logs with these temporal conditions. Scene geometry provides hidden starts and timed waypoints for pedestrian, cyclist, and vehicle trajectory generation. An offline response oracle labels encounters as Reactive (avoidable after exposure) or Anticipatory (avoidable only with earlier visibility) and stores safe maneuvers as training demonstrations. On the Waymo Open Motion Dataset, 90.1-96.6% of valid trajectories meet both requested times within +/-0.2 s. OnCue matches the requested reaction window between them in 92.8% of shared vehicle requests versus at most 42.1% for adapted adversarial generators. Across matched cyclist encounters, longer windows lower PDM-Closed collision from 59.1% to 5.5%, while the learned planner LatentDriver shows the opposite trend. OnCue demonstrations reduce LatentDriver target collision by 54.8 points on held-out Reactive tests, but reduce overall no-target progress by 12.7 m. These results highlight the value of temporal control for evaluating and improving planners under occlusion.

authors.name: Kailang Ma, Li Song, Weining Ren, Zirui Li, Xianjie Dai, Jingguang Li, Zuyi Guo, Benwang Chen, Heye Huang

papers.title: Greedy Decoding Hides Good Plans: Sample-and-Verify Planning for Vision-Language Driving Models
papers.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly adopted for end-to-end driving planning, yet their performance is typically evaluated based on a single greedily decoded trajectory. However, greedy decoding may overlook better trajectories within the model's output distribution. Experiments on WOD-E2E and NAVSIM reveal a consistent performance gap between greedily decoded trajectories and the best sampled candidates, showing that planning errors can arise from trajectory selection, rather than trajectory generation alone. On WOD-E2E, when the ego vehicle should start moving, the model often assigns probability to different possible start times, causing greedy decoding to repeatedly favor waiting and produce a stationary plan even though moving trajectories are available. Motivated by these findings, we propose Sample-and-Verify (SaV), which keeps the VLM planner frozen and samples multiple candidate trajectories. A lightweight verifier is trained from ground-truth futures to estimate the relative quality of these candidates. It uses trajectory kinematics, candidate-set agreement and likelihood, and ego-motion features to select the final trajectory. On WOD-E2E, SaV reduces ADE and FDE by approximately 15% across three VLM planners on the validation set. Changes in RFS are smaller: two planners show slight decreases on val-456, while Alpamayo-1.5 improves from 7.74 to 7.81 RFS on the official test set as ADE@5s decreases by 11%. On NAVSIM, SaV reduces ADE@4s by 10-24% across three VLM planners, while PDMS changes are less consistent. These results show that trajectory selection can substantially improve displacement accuracy without additional planner training. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/hzxbzp/sample-and-verify.

authors.name: Zhipeng Bao, Wenjie Zhao, Yiping Li, Haohua Que, Qianwen Li

papers.title: Structure-Aware Multimodal Retrieval Under Data Scarcity, Privacy Constraints and Out-of-Domain Content
papers.summary: Purpose: Figure retrieval from reference atlases in expert domains like forensic pathology, dentistry and geology must work without labels or training pairs, on content that often cannot leave local hardware, and on images outside the training data of image-text encoders. This work proposes a structure-aware pipeline that satisfies all three, retrieving figures through the page structure recovered by layout geometry and a local open-weight 8B VLM. Methods: A geometry-based pairing method is introduced, in which the model receives a schematic of the detected boxes and selects each picture's caption without access to pixels or text. Caption retrieval is evaluated on three private corpora (29 books, 10,421 figures, 218 queries) with blind human grading, against a lexical baseline, generated descriptions and five image-text encoders. Results: Geometric pairing was correct for 96%, 92% and 77% of pictures in the three domains, against 76%, 45% and 53% for the better of two document parsers. A hosted model given the schematic was equally accurate, while coordinates as text lost 22 points. Caption retrieval obtained an nDCG@5 of 0.85, 0.87 and 0.76, against 0.54, 0.51 and 0.27 for the best cross-modal encoder and 0.41, 0.28 and 0.30 for generated descriptions. Pairing errors carried over to retrieval. Conclusion: The proposed pipeline achieves accurate figure retrieval with small local models and no in-domain training, where general and biomedical image-text encoders fall far behind. Its geometry-only pairing is the most accurate of five methods and exposes no content, even to a hosted model. Code and prompts are released.

authors.name: Argyrios Zafeiriou, Dionysios Koulouris, Ilias Maglogiannis

papers.title: SpiderSkel: Sub-Pixel Multi-Tangent 2D Skeletonization from Inscribed-Disc Geometry
papers.summary: Skeletonization reduces a binary shape to a compact medial representation, but pixel-grid discretization perturbs the boundary-contact geometry underlying the medial axis, creating tension among connectivity, reconstruction fidelity, and skeleton compactness. SpiderSkel is a family of training-free two-dimensional skeletonization methods built on multi-tangent inscribed-disc geometry. A tie-aware exact Euclidean distance transform retains tied nearest boundary sites rather than collapsing them to a single label; medial candidates are localised to sub-pixel positions from the inscribed disc's tangent contacts, filtered by the angular span of those contacts, and completed by connectivity-aware refinement. Across nineteen public benchmarks comprising 11,323 images of shapes, retinal vessels, cracks and roads, and document images, a single operating point fixed across datasets yields skeletons that, on every image, have exact skeleton topology under the component/hole certificate, remain fully connected, and have exact per-object reconstruction topology. The three SpiderSkel variants are the only evaluated methods to satisfy all three properties across every category; within each category, every variant is Pareto-optimal with respect to all twenty-two baselines in strict sub-pixel reconstruction Dice versus reduction rate. Incremental engines for all three variants reproduce the skeleton of a complete recomputation exactly across 23,040 verified edit steps, with median update latencies of 15.4-18.1 ms per foreground edit and 4.3-4.4 ms per canvas edit, and speedups reaching 33.0-fold on canvas edits.

authors.name: Zhexian Zhou, Lian Ren, Xiao Feng, Sebastian Scherer

papers.title: PRISM: Perceptual Rate-Controllable Extreme Image Compression with Visual State-Space Models
papers.summary: Generative codecs built on pretrained diffusion priors achieve high perceptual quality at ultra-low bitrates (below 0.05 bpp). However, most methods still require a separate model for each bitrate, and offer no control over the amount of detail synthesized. Their rate efficiency also depends on the entropy model, where Mamba-based state-space models (SSMs) have recently improved autoregressive context modeling. However, conventional SSM scans are not aligned with the decoding order, and each decoding pass restarts from an empty state, discarding context accumulated in previous passes. We propose PRISM, an extreme image compression method that addresses these limitations. A single model provides two continuous controls: a rate knob that traverses the rate-distortion curve and a realism knob that adjusts the level of detail synthesized. Its visual state-space (VSS) context model introduces a decode-order-aligned (DOA) scan, which predicts each latent from a state that summarizes all decoded context, and cross-tap state carry, which initializes each tap with a summary of the previous one. Experiments show that PRISM outperforms both variable-rate and fixed-rate codecs, requiring on average 22% less bitrate than the strongest baseline at equal FID while also achieving higher PSNR.

authors.name: Md Adnan Faisal Hossain, Fengqing Zhu

papers.title: Measuring the Value of One Shared Image at Robot Handoffs in Vision-and-Language Navigation
papers.summary: When the lead robot cannot continue, what should it send the teammate that must finish the route? We replay a frozen receiver at each contact under alternative messages. Across 3,920 autonomous departures in 106 environments, adding the view before the lead's last action block to its executed actions raised success by 7.51 percentage points (pp) per RxR handoff and 8.54 pp per SAGE handoff. Per departure the gains were 2.23 and 1.44 pp, respectively. The lead continuing in simulation defines the empirical full-history ceiling (Solo). At contact, the lead had accumulated a median of 41 frames. Sending one frame when available recovered 24% of the full-history advantage over actions alone in SAGE and 30% in RxR. Over an estimated progress cue in SAGE, the image rescued 100 routes and reversed 54 successes. Near-goal receivers finished outside less often (63.1% to 51.7%, post hoc). In secondary comparisons the earlier view outperformed the contact view by 6-7 pp per handoff. Exact-route specificity and image gains at controlled starts with mostly unknown progress or outside the goal region remained unresolved. Gains were detectable from about 7 kB per handoff. Random transmission matched within size bins nearly equaled the learned sender's team success. At a required handoff, a view of the approach to the last maneuver helps the receiver finish.

authors.name: Yuze Lu

papers.title: SEEK: Self-Evolution through Execution Knowledge for Agentic Robot Manipulation
papers.summary: General-purpose multimodal foundation models enable robots to adapt during deployment from observations and execution feedback, without task-specific demonstrations or training. However, the robot retains what it learns only in the model's working context. Once the task ends, it loses this execution knowledge, such as how to carry a bowl between two grippers. On the next attempt at the task, the robot may take just as long and repeat the same mistakes. To avoid this repetition, robots must retain execution knowledge across attempts. Yet replaying past actions is insufficient, because their effects depend on the current conditions. Procedures that determine actions from the current scene address this, but when they meet conditions that earlier attempts did not cover, revising them requires the measured effects of earlier actions. We therefore propose SEEK, an agentic framework that retains both, enabling robots to improve across attempts while keeping the underlying model fixed. To adapt retained knowledge to the current scene, SEEK adopts a Self-Evolving Programmatic Policy (SEPP) that encodes manipulation as executable procedures and determines each action from current observations. As the robot executes these procedures, SEEK records the measured effects of its actions, including those from failed attempts, in a Persistent Action-Effect Bank (PAEB). Where a retained procedure applies, it acts without a model request; where it meets a condition it does not cover, this evidence guides its revision. On RoboDojo, knowledge retained over ten attempts raises SEEK's average task score from 27.0 to 54.4 and its success rate from 19.7% to 48.0% across all 42 tasks. On 34 of these tasks with GPT-6.2 Astra, SEEK reaches 80.1 after five attempts, against 49.6 for the same model acting directly, and uses 77.6% fewer model requests. https://zeyangguan.github.io/SEEK-Agentic-Robot-Manipulation/

authors.name: Zeyang Guan, Qihao Zhao, Rui Gong, Zhang Haitian, Yalun Dai, Yangyu Huang, Lingao Xiao, Haozhe Du, Xuehui Yu, Ye Lu, Jianjun Gao, Ruoyu Wang, Haowen Bai, Hao Li, Scarlett Li, Kim-Hui Yap

papers.title: iMFPO: Improving Mean Flow Policy Optimization with Drift-Aware Velocity Alignment for Embodied Control
papers.summary: Flow-based generative policies offer expressive action modeling for embodied control, yet achieving efficient one-step generation under reward-driven policy optimization remains challenging. In particular, evolving action distributions during online reinforcement learning may introduce inconsistencies between instantaneous-velocity learning and interval-averaged action generation. To address this challenge, we propose iMFPO, a one-step generative policy optimization framework with decoupled velocity learning and drift-aware velocity alignment. A shared interval-conditioned actor supports instantaneous-velocity supervision and interval-averaged action generation. JVP-corrected velocity regression is jointly optimized with reward-driven policy objectives, with action-level guidance from a frozen PPO teacher during training. At inference, iMFPO directly generates actions through interval-averaged velocity prediction, achieving one-step control without iterative flow integration. Across Go2, G1, H1, and Spot, zero-latent evaluation yields mean returns of 35.69, 34.44, 416.23, and 29.86. On Go2, action-generation latency drops from 15.57 ms to 0.41 ms relative to 64-step RFPO. Code: https://github.com/AIGeeksGroup/iMFPO. Website: https://aigeeksgroup.github.io/iMFPO.

authors.name: Lisiyu Pan, Ting Huang, Zeyu Zhang, Hao Tang

papers.title: Targeted Adaptation of World-Action Models via Interaction and Motion Heads
papers.summary: World-Action Models (WAMs) are a promising new paradigm of robot manipulation policies that jointly generate future video and actions. Successful manipulation requires both identifying where to interact and modeling how the robot and objects move. Yet standard adaptation methods, such as full fine-tuning and LoRA, do not explicitly select parameters aligned with these manipulation-specific capabilities. Motivated by this challenge, we discover two functionally specialized families of attention heads: Next-Interaction Heads, which localize upcoming grasp-and-release targets, and Motion Heads, which track movement across frames. Furthermore, we introduce HeadLight, a parameter-efficient refinement method that jointly adapts Next-Interaction Heads and Motion Heads. On RoboTwin tasks unseen during fine-tuning, HeadLight achieves 62.28% success, compared with 57.89% for full fine-tuning and 58.66% for LoRA, while updating only 1.1% of parameters. Inference-time ablations further validate the functional importance of these heads: ablating Motion Heads reduces manipulation success from 57.89% to 0.94%, while ablating Next-Interaction Heads lowers it to 40.61%, both substantially more than ablating equally many random heads. Finally, we show that our approach is effective across multiple WAM architectures and real-robot manipulation settings.

authors.name: Yuze Zhu, Jacky Li, Yusen Luo, Ken Jiankun Zheng, Chancharik Mitra, Trevor Darrell, Roei Herzig

papers.title: QK-Bench: Benchmarking Quantitative Kinematic Understanding for Dynamic Spatial Intelligence
papers.summary: Spatial intelligence concerns both scene structure and its temporal evolution. Yet a semantically correct description can conceal a quantitative error: recognizing that objects are approaching does not determine their closing speed or whether they will meet. Such errors are critical in collision avoidance, trajectory tracking, and reactive grasping, where actions depend on motion magnitude, timing, and relative geometry. We study quantitative kinematic understanding in multimodal large language models (MLLMs): resolving motion magnitude, rate, reference-frame dependence, and future spatial evolution from visual evidence. We introduce the Quantitative Kinematics Benchmark (QK-Bench), comprising 2,341 multiple-choice QA pairs from 379 videos and 17 tasks spanning Object-Centric Kinematics, Camera Ego-Motion Kinematics, and Multi-Object Kinematic Relations. Hidden geometric and temporal signals support trajectory construction and filtering, while fixed kinematic rules map physical quantities to verifiable answers, including categorical labels. Trajectory and question validation ensure target reliability and sufficient visual support in the sampled frames. All models receive a unified monocular RGB input. Evaluations of proprietary, open-source, and spatial MLLMs reveal substantial limitations: the strongest model achieves only 41.2\% overall accuracy, and spatial MLLMs show no consistent advantage. These findings indicate that current advances in spatial intelligence do not reliably transfer to quantitative kinematic understanding.

authors.name: Lennox Wei, Jiaqi Yao, Shixin Sun, Yuanzheng Zhang, Jianhua Han, Meng Tian, Shaohui Liu, Wangmeng Zuo

papers.title: End-to-End Image-Goal Navigation for Agile Quadrotors via Recurrent State Distillation
papers.summary: Image-goal navigation asks a robot to reach the viewpoint of a target photograph without a map or goal pose. In three dimensions, this requires not only recognizing the goal but also estimating 3D displacement and generating continuous control actions to approach and settle at the target view. This is difficult because the same visual difference between current and goal image can require very different actions depending on the robot's velocity, yet monocular images alone reveal neither metric scale nor body motion. As a result, existing image-goal policies are limited to planar action spaces and rely on a state estimator for flight control. Policies that map directly from images to low-level control commands have been demonstrated for agile flight, but not toward goal images in unseen environments. We present the first image-goal navigation policy that directly commands thrust and angular rates for agile quadrotor flight in unseen 3D environments, without relying on state estimation (e.g., SLAM, VO, or SfM) or a separate velocity controller. We train a recurrent vision-based policy through a four-stage pipeline that combines geometric and motion supervision with privileged-teacher distillation and end-to-end reinforcement learning fine-tuning. On 1000 held-out flights in unseen environments, the policy achieves an 82.3% success rate with a mean terminal position error of 0.10m across successful flights. Deployed zero-shot on a real quadrotor, the policy reaches an 84% success rate over 25 trials in an unseen indoor environment.

authors.name: Simone Nascivera, Ismail Geles, Davide Scaramuzza

papers.title: MulCLIP: A Multi-level Alignment Framework for Enhancing Fine-grained Long-context CLIP
papers.summary: Vision-language models such as CLIP excel at image-text alignment but struggle with long, detailed descriptions due to training on short captions. Recent methods address this limitation using region proposals to align visual regions with sentences, but at substantial deployment cost. We present MulCLIP, an end-to-end multi-level alignment framework that directly exploits natural long-text structure without region proposals. Instead of simply stacking objectives, MulCLIP aligns different textual granularities through compatible training signals: global contrastive alignment for long captions and short summaries, Word-Patch Reconstruction over locally calibrated features for within-sample word-patch semantics, and Subcaption-Aggregated Patch alignment for context-rich subcaption grounding. Experiments on benchmarks spanning varying caption lengths show consistent gains, and ablations confirm that the proposed objectives are complementary and jointly improve the overall framework. Code will be released at https://github.com/truongchau2602/MulCLIP.

authors.name: Chau Truong, Hieu Ta Quang, Zhenzhen Liu, Dung D. Le

papers.title: Rehearse in 3D, Render in 2D: Physically Consistent and Editable Robot World Models
papers.summary: Embodied world models aim to predict future interactions that are both visually realistic and physically consistent. Yet explicit 3D motion prediction alone does not guarantee that object structure and contact relationships are preserved. Beyond motion prediction, 3D representations provide an explicit state space for imposing structural and physical constraints. Building on this insight, we introduce RehearsalWorld, an editable robot world model driven by 3D Interaction Rehearsal (3DIR). Given an initial RGB-D observation and robot actions, Interaction-Consistent Rehearsal (ICR) uses a pretrained 3D point-flow model as a motion prior. It refines the predicted trajectories through response-aware object grouping, persistent grasp memory, and contact structure refiner, preserving scene stability, object structure, and grasp attachments. Rehearsal-Aligned Video Generation (RAVG) then uses geometric projections of the rehearsal as temporal conditioning. We fine-tune a video generator on projection-video pairs to synthesize realistic interaction videos. Thanks to the decoupling of physical response from visual synthesis, RehearsalWorld also supports independent editing of material properties and camera viewpoints. Compared with PointWorld on real DROID grasping sequences, RehearsalWorld reduces gripper-relative offset by approximately 79% to 84% across deformable, articulated, and rigid objects and lowers reference motion error. For video prediction, it achieves a PSNR of 23.92 dB and an FVD of 149.

authors.name: Guangyu Liu, Hanzhang Wang, Huijia Zhang, Hanbei Zhan, Linjie Hu, Bin Xiao, Xuan Zhou, Dong Zhang, Hanwei Liu

papers.title: M$^{2}$AdaptVLA: Multimodal Memory-Augmented Vision-Language-Action Model with Predictive Test-Time Adaptation
papers.summary: Effective robotic manipulation calls for multimodal memory and rapid adaptation to shifts in contact dynamics. However, many existing policies, which retain either visual or wrench history, may miss key cues from the other modality. Moreover, even with wrench memory, fixed policies can struggle when contact conditions shift at deployment. To this end, we introduce M$^{2}$AdaptVLA, a vision-language-action model that integrates visual and wrench memories with predictive test-time adaptation. For visual memory, the model uses test-time training (TTT) to encode observation history in fast weights. Each entry in the bounded TTT bank combines the corresponding frame's features with a readout from these weights, preserving cues that predate the oldest retained frame. For wrench memory, a context gate controls how much the action expert draws on wrench history as it jointly denoises future actions and wrenches. For predictive test-time adaptation, the auxiliary wrench prediction loss also provides online self-supervision. Using measured wrenches as targets, we update low-rank policy adapters by backpropagating only through the final denoising step. Real-world experiments show that the TTT bank outperforms visual memory baselines on progress tracking, scene recall, and demonstration following. On contact-sensitive tasks, the context gate yields higher success rates than direct injection or gated cross-attention. Predictive test-time adaptation improves robustness to shifts in contact dynamics. On eight tasks requiring visual and wrench memory, M$^{2}$AdaptVLA achieves a mean success rate of 82.71%, a 31.46% absolute gain over the strongest baseline. The project page is available at https://tlf-tlf.github.io/M2AdaptVLAPage/.

authors.name: Liufan Tan, Tong Wang, Yuehao Yin, Jian Chen, Yihang Yin, Ying Qu, Wenyu Li, Ruyi Gan, Hao Wang

papers.title: Compact Vision-Language Navigation in Continuous Environmentsvia On-Policy Training and Route-Bearing Output
papers.summary: Instruction-following robots need navigation policies that reach high accuracy and remain inexpensive to train and to run on a single graphics processing unit (GPU). The most accurate vision-language navigation policies for continuous environments rely on language models with 4 to 8 billion parameters, long observation histories, and large auxiliary corpora. Two properties of the standard training setup limit smaller policies. Imitation labels cover the states that an expert visits, whereas the running policy reaches states that its own errors produce. In addition, an image-plane waypoint exists only while the route lies inside the camera view. We present \textbf{\paper}, a monocular red-green-blue (RGB) policy with 2 billion (2B) parameters that addresses both limitations. \paper adapts Qwen3-VL-2B with low-rank adapters and processes an eight-frame memory and the current view in one forward pass. The policy predicts the route direction as a bearing in the body frame of the agent, which remains defined for every heading, and a deterministic controller converts this bearing into motion. This design allows training to relabel the states that the policy itself visits. On-policy correction improves success, while bearing decoding outperforms image-plane waypoint scanning across all evaluated start headings with identical weights. On the \valunseen split, \paper achieves \rFinSR\% success on Room-to-Room in Continuous Environments (\rtor), averaged over three seeds, and \rRxFinSR\% on its Room-Across-Room counterpart (\rxr). Inference requires \rDecMs\,ms and \rInferGB\,GiB of memory, while training takes \rCostTrainTyp\ GPU-hours on one 12\,GB consumer GPU.

authors.name: Reshad Ul Karim, Syeda Maliha Tabassum, Md. Khalilur Rhaman, Md Rashad Al Hasan Rony

papers.title: Blind spatially varying PSF estimation for fluorescence microscopy
papers.summary: Optical aberrations degrade fluorescence microscopy images and measuring the underlying point spread function (PSF) often requires dedicated acquisitions or isolated emitters. Here we introduce DeepBlur, a neural network that estimates spatially varying two-dimensional PSFs directly from single images of biological structures. Trained entirely on physical simulations spanning aberrations, illumination and noise, it adapts to diverse imaging conditions without requiring user-supplied optical parameters. Using a deformable mirror, we acquire 1,290 images and assess blind PSF estimates against independent references. DeepBlur estimates agree closely with these references and improve deconvolution of experimentally aberrated images. Local PSF estimation also enables correction of spatially varying defocus and improves random-illumination super-resolution reconstruction in biological tissue. Available through DeepInv, a napari plugin and a web demonstration, DeepBlur can be readily integrated into computational microscopy workflows.

authors.name: Minh Hai Nguyen, Florian Sarron, Paul Escande, Sylvain Cantaloube, Thomas Mangeat, Pierre Weiss

papers.title: SOLVE: Sparse, Ordered Keyposes Make LLM Agents Versatile and Efficient Robot Manipulator
papers.summary: LLM agents have made remarkable progress in robot manipulation, yet they suffer from expensive inference, dense step-by-step control, and tool bottlenecks. We introduce SOLVE, a training-free, versatile and efficient agent policy: a multimodal LLM agent writes a sparse, ordered sequence of 6-DoF end-effector keyposes per call, observes the result, and writes the next, while a motion planner interpolates between them. The agent decides the number and spacing of keyposes for both fast long-range motion and fine-grained manipulation. This granularity matches the sparsity of teleoperated manipulation: most demonstrations in DROID can be compressed into a few keyposes instead of dense actions. SOLVE grounds keyposes with sparse depth queries answered by noisy sources, such as multi-view triangulation, stereo, or monocular depth, and copes with that noise itself. It also improves from execution feedback, reflecting on its own rollouts and distilling a few rules per task. SOLVE reaches state-of-the-art performance of 74.5% on RoboDojo and 84.5% on RoboLab, with only $1.7 per episode on average, 12x less than previous dense-control agent policies. On a real robot, the same agent achieves an 88% success rate (75 of 85 episodes) over 16 challenging zero-shot tasks. Our project page is at https://serenos.github.io/solve-website.

authors.name: Xiang Li, Hongyu Zhou, Ya-Li Li, Tao Li, Rui Zhang, Junjie Lai, Weihua Zhang, Shengjin Wang

papers.title: Real2SimLab: A Unified Platform for Real-to-Simulation Transfer
papers.summary: Real-to-simulation transfer, which builds simulations from real-world observations, has long been studied in research and industry. Recently, coding agents have become capable of generating simulation programs from video recordings, and several benchmarks have been proposed to evaluate them. However, each individual benchmark defines its own inputs, deliverables, and scoring pipeline. This leads to $N \times M$ integrations when evaluating $N$ methods on $M$ benchmarks. To this end, we present Real2SimLab, a unified platform for real-to-simulation transfer. It evaluates a method by running its written program and scoring the output simulation with the original scorer of each benchmark. Moreover, Real2SimLab provides a pipeline to create training data and reward annotations for real-to-simulation methods. Our pipeline carefully avoids data contamination by filtering out the video recordings that exist in benchmarks. For each video recording, a program is first produced, and then our pipeline computes its reward with the same code that Real2SimLab uses for evaluation. So far, it supports 47 coding agents and 5 non-agent methods on 6 benchmarks. Both the platform and Awesome-Real2Sim, our research map of nearly 300 real-to-simulation papers, are open source, and we invite the Real2SimHub community to build them together.

authors.name: Yongchang Zhang, Jie Huang, Yunhe Ni, Ningyu Zhou, Guangyu Zhao, Ruixun Liu, Rui Huang, Yidi Wu, TianZe Zhang, Zixiang Jiang, Xiang Li, Kevin Shen, Yiwu Zhong

papers.title: FineDex: Bridging Fine-Grained Human-Object Interaction Generation to Dexterous Humanoid Manipulation
papers.summary: Dexterity is, at its core, finger-level control, yet existing dexterous manipulation and human-object interaction (HOI) generation methods rarely let one specify how an interaction is performed: five-fingered hands are often reduced to grippers, or finger usage is copied from individual human demonstrations. We present FineDex, a framework that makes finger-level intent both expressible and executable. FineDex learns coordinated human body, hand, and object motions that follow fine-grained instructions on hand selection, individual fingers, and contacts with articulated objects. To bridge generation and execution, FineDex leverages generated interactions as actionable priors for an agent that discovers physically feasible contact strategies through practice in a physics-based digital twin. By adapting at test time without per-instance retraining, FineDex generalizes across fine-grained instructions and object configurations. Experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art HOI generation quality and fine-grained controllability, substantial improvements in dexterous manipulation success, and successful deployment on a real dexterous humanoid robot.

authors.name: Yujia Zeng, Yuxin Chen, Yuzhen Song, Runhan Huang, Chensheng Peng, Yiyang Shao, Koushil Sreenath, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Yilun Du

papers.title: Cairn: Object-Centric 3D Trajectory Priors for Steering Frozen VLAs
papers.summary: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) are capable low-level controllers, but they tie where objects go to the layouts they were trained on: when objects are moved or obstacles block the way, they carry them to the wrong place or into collisions. Fine-tuning on new layouts needs robot data for each one and erodes skills the model already has. We introduce Cairn, which keeps the VLA frozen and steers it at test time along learned 3D trajectories of the object in its gripper. A small prior reads point clouds of the scene and the held object, along with its pose when grasped and the instruction, and samples SE(3) trajectories up to its release that lead it around obstacles and turn it to fit through gaps. The prior and the VLA form the two levels of a hierarchical planner in which feedback runs both ways: the VLA's intended motion chooses and reshapes the trajectories, and the chosen one guides the VLA's denoising. Its predicted actions, mapped to the held object's poses through the grasp, are pulled toward the next waypoint, while the VLA's weights stay untouched. Across 1,941 held-out LIBERO scenes with displaced objects and obstacles, Cairn raises the success rate of a frozen {\pi}0.5 from 24.5% to 95.1%, above that of a {\pi}0.5 fine-tuned on our training layouts, without hurting standard LIBERO. On the third-party LIBERO-PRO benchmark, it raises success from 27.3% to 38.0%, and from 54.4% to 81.1% on the episodes it steers. On a real Franka, with a prior trained purely in simulation, it guides the frozen DROID {\pi}0.5 around an obstacle and to a placement at the limit of the arm's reach, where it otherwise fails. All code, models and data will be made public.

authors.name: Agelos Kratimenos, Kostas Daniilidis, Evangelos Chatzipantazis

papers.title: A Structure-Agnostic Multi-Objective Evolutionary Weight-Sharing Compression Framework for Deep Neural Networks
papers.summary: Deep neural networks (DNNs) have large parameter sets that are costly to store and to deploy on resource-constrained devices. Weight-sharing compression replaces the many distinct weight values of a network with a small codebook of shared values, called codewords. Prior methods build the codebook by clustering, typically with K-means, which is expensive on models with millions of parameters and must be refit for every codebook size. To stay tractable, clustering is often applied per layer, which requires the network's layer boundaries, tensor shapes, and channel counts. We propose Uniform-Binned Entropy-Constrained Scalar Quantization (UB-ECSQ) with NSGA-II, a retraining- and gradient-free, structure-agnostic, multi-objective compression framework that treats the network as a closed-box. It flattens all parameters into a single vector that shares one codebook. Uniform Binning Quantization (UBQ) maps the vector onto equal-width uniform bins in linear time and represents each occupied bin by its centroid. Entropy-Constrained Scalar Quantization (ECSQ) then merges neighboring bins, trading the added distortion against the entropy of bin occupancy. Dynamic programming finds the optimal merge from bin statistics alone, without any forward or backward pass. NSGA-II searches over only two variables, the number of bins and the merge ratio, and returns a Pareto front of compressed models that trade accuracy against compression ratio (CR). Within a 1% drop in accuracy, and averaged over five seeds, our Pareto fronts reach CRs of 20.8 and 12.9 for ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, 10.4 to 12.3 for ResNet-18/34/50/101 on ImageNet-1K, 18.4 for VGG16-BN, and 9.0 for ViT-B/16. At this budget, our framework attains a higher CR than every baseline evaluated in each setting. Over the whole objective space, our final Pareto front also achieves the highest hypervolume in all eight settings.

authors.name: Rasa Khosrowshahli, Shahryar Rahnamayan, Beatrice Ombuki-Berman

papers.title: Wall-to-Wall Amazon Forest Height Mapping with Planet NICFI, Aerial LiDAR, and a U-Net Regression Model
papers.summary: Tree canopy height is a key indicator of forest biomass, productivity, and structure, yet measuring it accurately at regional or larger scales, whether from the ground or remotely, remains challenging. The objective of this study is to generate the first complete canopy height map of the Amazon forest at $\sim$4.78 m resolution using Planet NICFI imagery and deep learning. Specifically, we (i) trained a U-Net regression model with canopy height models (CHM) derived from tropical airborne LiDAR and their corresponding Planet NICFI images to estimate canopy height, (ii) evaluated the accuracy of our map against existing global products based on Sentinel-2/1 and Maxar Vivid2 imagery, and (iii) assessed its capacity to capture small-scale canopy height changes. Tree height predictions on the validation sample had a mean absolute error of 3.68 m, with minimal systematic bias across the full range of tree heights in the Amazon forest. The main biases are a slight overestimation (up to 5 m) for heights of 5-15 m and an underestimation for most trees above 50 m. Outperforming existing global model-based canopy height products in this region, the model accurately estimated canopy heights up to 40-50 m with minimal saturation. We determined that the Amazon forest has an average canopy height of $\sim$22 m (standard deviation $\sim$5.3 m) and exhibits large-scale patterns, ranging from the tallest forests of the Guiana Shield to shorter forests along wetlands, rivers, rocky outcrops, savannas, and high elevations. Events such as logging or deforestation could be detected from changes in tree height, and the results demonstrated a first success in monitoring the height of regenerating forests. Finally, the map of the Amazon forest canopy height is displayed.

authors.name: Fabien H. Wagner, Ricardo Dalagnol, Griffin Carter, Mayumi C. M. Hirye, Shivraj Gill, Le Bienfaiteur Sagang Takougoum, Samuel Favrichon, Michael Keller, Jean P. H. B. Ometto, Lorena Alves, Cynthia Creze, Stephanie P. George-Chacon, Shuang Li, Zhihua Liu, Adugna Mullissa, Yan Yang, Erone G. Santos, Sarah R. Worden, Martin Brandt, Philippe Ciais, Stephen C. Hagen, Sassan Saatchi

papers.title: Class Agnostic Instance-level Descriptor for Instance Search
papers.summary: Despite the great success of the deep features in content-based image retrieval, the visual instance search remains challenging due to the lack of effective instance-level feature representation. Supervised or weakly supervised object detection methods are not the appropriate solutions due to their poor performance on the unknown object categories. In this paper, based on the feature set output from self-supervised ViT, the instance-level region discovery is modeled as detecting the compact feature subsets in a hierarchical fashion. The hierarchical decomposition results in a hierarchy of instance regions. On the one hand, this kind of hierarchical decomposition well addresses the problem of object embedding and occlusions, which are widely observed in real scenarios. On the other hand, the non-leaf nodes and leaf nodes on the hierarchy correspond to the instance regions in different granularities within an image. Therefore, features in uniform length are produced for these instance regions, which may cover across a dominant image region, an integral of multiple instances, or various individual instances. Such a collection of features allows us to unify the image retrieval, multi-instance search, and instance search into one framework. The empirical studies on three benchmarks show that such an instance-level descriptor remains effective on both the known and unknown object categories. Moreover, the superior performance is achieved on single-instance and multi-instance search, as well as image retrieval tasks.

authors.name: Qi-Ying Sun, Wan-Lei Zhao, Hui-Ying Xie, Yi-Bo Miao, Chong-Wah Ngo

papers.title: Towards High-Resolution Industrial Image Anomaly Detection
papers.summary: Current anomaly detection methods primarily focus on low-resolution scenarios. For high-resolution images, conventional downsampling often misses subtle anomalies due to the loss of fine-grained discriminative information. Although recent studies have explored lightweight networks or image tiling with ensemble strategies, they still fall short of industrial requirements for both accuracy and efficiency. To address the above issues, we propose HiAD, a general framework for high-resolution anomaly detection that identifies anomalies of varying sizes under constrained computational resources. Specifically, HiAD employs a dual-branch architecture that integrates anomaly cues across different scales to comprehensively capture both subtle and large-scale anomalies. Furthermore, it incorporates a multi-resolution feature fusion module that injects multi-scale semantic context into patch-level representations, thereby suppressing ultrafine texture variations while retaining anomaly-relevant structural details. To improve adaptability and efficiency, HiAD constructs a detector pool with an adaptive strategy selection mechanism that automatically identifies the optimal detector assignment strategy for varying input data, enabling robust anomaly detection while effectively controlling computational costs. HiAD requires neither additional supervision nor auxiliary learnable parameters and can be seamlessly integrated with a wide range of anomaly detection methods. Extensive experiments are conducted on multiple high-resolution anomaly detection benchmarks, including the specifically constructed MVTec-HD, VisA-HD, and RealIAD-HD benchmarks, as well as the existing MVTec 2 benchmark. The results consistently demonstrate the effectiveness and superior performance of HiAD across diverse experimental settings. The code is available at https://github.com/cnulab/HiAD.

authors.name: Ximiao Zhang, Min Xu, Xiuzhuang Zhou

papers.title: Delta-SVD: Efficient Compression for Personalized Text-to-Image Models
papers.summary: Personalizing a text-to-image diffusion model by full fine-tuning gives the strongest subject fidelity but produces a full copy of the model per subject: a thousand personalized Stable Diffusion checkpoints approach five terabytes, so storage, not compute, is what fails to scale. We present Delta-SVD, which compresses the weight change that personalization makes rather than the model. Given only a finished checkpoint and its base, it takes a truncated SVD of each layer's weight delta and keeps the few components that carry its spectral energy, selected by a per-layer energy threshold or by a global byte budget filled by water-filling, optimal for the continuous relaxation and empirically near-optimal for discrete rank allocation. Nothing is trained and no subject image is read, so the method applies to legacy and third-party checkpoints for which training-time adapters such as LoRA were never produced. The factors merge back into dense weights at load time, so serving runs at the uncompressed model's exact latency, whereas whole-model 8-bit and 4-bit quantization slow inference by 1.5-3.4 times. On the 30-subject DreamBooth benchmark, Delta-SVD matches the uncompressed model to within 0.01 DINO at 7-fold compression and keeps 98% of its fidelity at 33-fold compression. Among post-hoc baselines, only dense-delta quantization at 411 MiB matches it; below that size Delta-SVD dominates pruning, random-rank selection, and both whole-model and dense-delta quantization on the storage-quality frontier. The same holds on 84 diverse CustomConcept101 subjects, where a 9 MiB adapter reproduces the uncompressed outputs at paired DINO 0.77, and on a fully fine-tuned SD3.5-medium MMDiT, where a 531 MB adapter matches the uncompressed model to within 0.01 DINO.

authors.name: Tangyuan Zhang, Shangyu Chen, Qixiang Chen, Junyu Yan, Jingwen Ye, Jianfei Cai

papers.title: GazeVLM: Gaze-Guided Foveated Inference for Efficient Vision-Language Models
papers.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) achieve remarkable multimodal performance but introduce substantial computational cost due to the large number of visual tokens. Existing approaches typically rely on token pruning, sparse attention, or additional control modules, often introducing accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. This paper presents GazeVLM, a training-free framework that leverages human gaze as a natural guidance signal for efficient inference. GazeVLM allocates computation to gaze-relevant regions through a gaze-guided region-of-interest (ROI) representation and an optional two-scale design that preserves global context. We also construct GazeVLM-VQA, to the best of our knowledge, the first real-world wearable-gaze visual question answering (VQA) dataset specifically constructed for VLM inference, containing reference images, human gaze traces, and gaze-aligned question-answer pairs. Experiments on the GazeVLM-VQA benchmark demonstrate that GazeVLM improves both answer quality and efficiency across Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B and Qwen3-VL-8B models. It reduces visual tokens by up to 84.2%, prefill FLOPs by up to 92.8%, and achieves up to 11.6 times prefill speedup, while improving answer-match accuracy by up to 8.6 percentage points (pp). These results show that aligning VLM computation with human visual attention provides a promising path toward efficient VLM inference. We publicly release the GazeVLM-VQA dataset (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1mdi-GezeIkmege3segUQCnvnK6P-skaw?usp=sharing).

authors.name: Lei Wang, Jiawen Qi, Qinyu Chen

papers.title: LongScape: Advancing Long-Horizon Embodied World Models with Context-Aware MoE
papers.summary: Video-based world models hold significant potential for generating high-quality embodied manipulation data. However, current video generation methods struggle to achieve stable long-horizon generation: classical diffusion-based approaches often suffer from temporal inconsistency and visual drift over multiple rollouts, while autoregressive methods tend to compromise on visual detail. To solve this, we introduce LongScape, a hybrid framework that adaptively combines intra-chunk diffusion denoising with inter-chunk autoregressive causal generation. Our core innovation is an action-guided, variable-length chunking mechanism that partitions video based on the semantic context of robotic actions. This aligns chunk boundaries with robotic interaction events and motion dynamics, enabling the model to flexibly generate diverse dynamics. We further introduce a Context-aware Mixture-of-Experts (CMoE) framework that adaptively activates specialized experts for each chunk during generation to produce high-quality videos with coherent chunk transitions. Extensive experiments on two embodied benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art generation performance. Notably, LongScape maintains high generation quality and temporal consistency over 1,000-frame rollouts. When used as synthetic training data, LongScape videos lift the success rate of a downstream VLA policy by 9.8 percentage points over real-only training, outperforming augmentation with other long-video generators. Our code is available at: https://github.com/tsinghua-fib-lab/Longscape.

authors.name: Lei Jin, Yu Shang, Yiding Ma, Xin Zhang, Chen Gao, Wei Wu, Yong Li

papers.title: Assemble the Puzzle: Cross-Agent Utility-Aware Feature Scheduling for Bandwidth-Limited Cooperative Perception
papers.summary: Cooperative perception (CP) lets connected vehicles and roadside units detect objects beyond the inherent range limitation and occlusion of single-agent systems, yet its practicality is constrained by limited Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication bandwidth. Existing methods improve bandwidth efficiency by letting collaborating agents send only selected feature cells driven by local detection confidence, serving a centralized ego agent's request. They overlook realistic communication scheduling and neglect cross-agent redundancy. We present JigsawComm, a decentralized utility-aware feature scheduling framework that learns to ``assemble the puzzle'' of multi-agent features. Choosing who sends each region requires a utility that measures what each agent's features contribute to the collaboration. JigsawComm incorporates a lightweight feature utility estimator, learned without utility labels from the cooperative model's own leave-one-agent-out counterfactuals, which aligns utilities onto a single comparable scale across agents. From one broadcast of compact utility maps, every agent ranks the observers of each cell and sends the cells it observes best to maximize coverage and, budget permitting, second best for accuracy refinement. Each agent also broadcasts its onboard detector's lightweight bounding box list, enabling an intermediate-late hybrid fusion with our feature-anchored box consensus, which synergistically enhances the final perception results with all available observations. With every transmitted byte counted, JigsawComm at 0.45 KB per vehicle outperforms all baselines on the real-world V2X-Real benchmark, and under measured C-V2X traces on CooperScene it retains 74.5 of its 79.8 AP@0.5, at least 15.5 points above every prior art baseline.

authors.name: Chenyi Wang, Muhammad Waqar, Wujie Wen, Ming F. Li

papers.title: Guiding Visual Autoregressive Models through Spectrum Weakening
papers.summary: Classifier-free guidance (CFG) has become a widely adopted practice for enhancing generation quality and improving condition alignment. Recent studies have explored guidance mechanisms for unconditional generation, yet these approaches remain fundamentally tied to assumptions specific to diffusion models. In this work, we propose a spectrum weakening framework for visual autoregressive (AR) models. The method is training-free and condition-free, constructing a controllable weak model in the spectral domain without architectural modifications. Specifically, we selectively retain spectral components along the channel dimension of internal representations to weaken features without requiring a complete spatial layout. We further apply spectrum renormalization to maintain feature scales during generation. Comprehensive empirical and ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of our approach, including raster-scan, random-order, and scale-wise AR, spanning discrete and continuous modeling and covering class and text-condition scenarios, demonstrating high-quality unconditional generation and strong prompt alignment for conditional generation.

authors.name: Chaoyang Wang, Tianmeng Yang, Yunhai Tong

papers.title: HPC: Hierarchical Point-based Latent Representation for Streaming Dynamic Gaussian Splatting Compression
papers.summary: While dynamic Gaussian Splatting has driven significant advances in free-viewpoint video, maintaining its rendering quality with a small memory footprint for efficient streaming transmission still presents an ongoing challenge. Existing streaming dynamic Gaussian Splatting compression methods typically leverage a latent representation to drive the neural network for predicting Gaussian residuals between frames. Their core latent representations can be categorized into structured grid-based and unstructured point-based paradigms. However, the former incurs significant parameter redundancy by inevitably modeling unoccupied space, while the latter suffers from limited compactness as it fails to exploit local correlations. To relieve these limitations, we propose HPC, a novel streaming dynamic Gaussian Splatting compression framework. It employs a hierarchical point-based latent representation that operates on a per-Gaussian basis to avoid parameter redundancy in unoccupied space. Guided by a tailored aggregation scheme, these latent points achieve high compactness with low spatial redundancy. To improve compression efficiency, we further undertake the first investigation to compress neural networks for streaming dynamic Gaussian Splatting through mining and exploiting the inter-frame correlation of parameters. Combined with latent compression, this forms a fully end-to-end compression framework. Comprehensive experimental evaluations demonstrate that HPC substantially outperforms state-of-the-art methods. It achieves a storage reduction of 67% against its baseline while maintaining high reconstruction fidelity.

authors.name: Yangzhi Ma, Bojun Liu, Wenting Liao, Dong Liu, Zhu Li, Li Li

papers.title: Learning Image-based Tree Crown Segmentation from Enhanced Lidar-based Pseudo-labels
papers.summary: Mapping individual tree crowns is essential for understanding and caring for our environment by improving the accuracy of urban tree inventories and precise monitoring of forest health. However, automatically separating tree crowns in aerial imagery is challenging because of factors like complex crown textures and frequent partial overlap between neighbouring trees. We present a method to train deep learning models to segment individual tree crowns from RGB and multispectral imagery, using pseudo-labels derived from aerial laser scanning (ALS) data. We show that incorporating information from a zero-shot instance segmentation model, Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2), improves model training. Our method enables training domain-specific optical image-based models without requiring manual training annotation. We trained and evaluated the models with data from an urban area in Southern Finland and compared their performance with several baselines. Our best model achieved a mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 0.621 on manually delineated tree crowns in a geographically separate test area. This represents a 21% increase in mIoU over the directly evaluated SAM 2-enhanced pseudo-labels (0.513) and a 19% increase over the best image-based baseline (0.524). Incorporating SAM 2 into the pseudo-label generation process improved the best model mIoU by 9.9%, from 0.565 to 0.621, while the average mIoU across the tested models increased by 8.4%, from 0.557 to 0.604. These results highlight that automatically generated and foundation-model-enhanced pseudo-labels can provide effective domain-specific supervision for individual tree crown segmentation without manual training annotation, despite the noise in the initial ALS-based segments.

authors.name: Julius Pesonen, Stefan Rua, Josef Taher, Niko Koivum\"aki, Xiaowei Yu, Teemu Hakala, Eija Honkavaara

papers.title: Saliency-Aware Multi-Route Thinking: Grounding and Reasoning on Vision-Language Agents
papers.summary: Vision-language (VL) agents increasingly combine extended reasoning with ex ternal visual tools. Yet long traces can drift from the image as generated text accumulates, while directly inserting tool outputs can turn one incorrect detection into a persistent premise. We ask how inference-time computation can improve reasoning without surrendering control to the tool. We propose Saliency-Aware Principle Selection (SAP), a training-free method that evolves compact reason ing principles rather than lengthening a single token trajectory. Each principle generates independent routes from the original image and prompt. A frozen ground ing tool scores whether objects cited along these routes are visually supported; agreement, diversity, and uncertainty further control drift, collapse, and overcon fidence. The tool supplies selection evidence but never writes the reasoning or answer. Across object-hallucination benchmarks, SAP consistently improves vi sually grounded prediction under a unified model and decoding budget. Broader evaluations spanning reasoning, knowledge, OCR, documents, diagrams, and real world imagery show that this gain does not come at the expense of general VL capability. Cross-architecture and model-scale experiments further demonstrate that the principle-selection mechanism transfers beyond a single backbone, while controlled ablations confirm that both multi-route exploration and evolutionary se lection are necessary. Because routes run in parallel, SAP also reduces serial latency relative to an equally long chain. Together, these results show that scaling over governed reasoning behaviors can preserve visual evidence more effectively than simply extending the chain.

authors.name: Mingjia Shi, Yinhan He, Yaochen Zhu, Cassie Dong, Jundong Li

papers.title: CORAL: Correspondence Alignment for Improved Virtual Try-On
papers.summary: Existing methods for Virtual Try-On (VTON) often struggle to accurately transfer garment appearance, especially in unpaired settings where accurate person-garment correspondence is required. These methods do not explicitly supervise person-garment alignment, leaving correspondence to be learned implicitly within the generation model. In this paper, we first analyze full self-attention in DiT-based architectures and show that person-to-garment query-key matching aligned with local geometric correspondence is closely related to try-on quality. Building on this insight, we introduce CORrespondence ALignment (CORAL), a DiT-based framework that explicitly aligns query-key matching with robust external correspondences. CORAL integrates two complementary components: a correspondence distillation loss that aligns reliable matches with person-to-garment attention, and an entropy minimization loss that sharpens the attention distribution. For evaluation, we further propose a VLM-based evaluation protocol to better reflect human preference. CORAL consistently improves over the baseline, enhancing both global shape transfer and local detail preservation. Extensive ablations validate our design choices.

authors.name: Jiyoung Kim, Youngjin Shin, Siyoon Jin, Dahyun Chung, Jisu Nam, Tongmin Kim, Jongjae Park, Hyeonwoo Kang, Seungryong Kim

papers.title: Beyond Anatomy: Interpreting Graph-Based ASD Classification Across ABIDE Settings
papers.summary: Graph neural networks can classify resting-state functional MRI connectomes, but a high score on one configuration leaves open which representation choices matter and whether the result supports broader clinical use. We examine this problem through two ABIDE-I analyses. On a balanced 400-subject subset, an AAL-based graph convolutional network (73.3%), an MSDL-based configuration (84.0%), and a five-model graph attention ensemble (95.0%) report high nominal performance. However, we show that this 95.0% result, which substantially exceeds typical multi-site ABIDE benchmarks (65-70%), stems from a single site-stratified test split of 60 subjects and does not reflect out-of-distribution generalization to unseen acquisition centers. In a separate 1,035-subject analysis with different preprocessing and parcellation, BrainGAT reaches 58.26% mean accuracy, below an SVM at 69.37%. We interpret these as comparisons of complete pipelines and retain both the favorable ensemble result and the negative broader-cohort result. Analysis of the existing summaries shows that atlas substitution changes the number of possible region pairs approximately ninefold, that accuracy on 60 test subjects changes by 1.67 percentage points per prediction, and that the best accuracy and AUC belong to different broader-cohort classifiers. Regional attribution on the baseline GCN (not the 95% GAT ensemble) highlights default-mode-network features but reflects classifier reliance rather than validated clinical biomarkers. Unresolved metric aggregation and diagnosis-aware harmonization limit the findings to exploratory classification evidence.

authors.name: Syeda Hareem Madani, Noureen Bibi, Adam Rafiq Jeraj, Sumra Khan, Anas Zafar, Rizwan Qureshi

papers.title: ABRA: Teleporting Fine-Tuned Knowledge Across Domains for Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
papers.summary: Although recent Open-Vocabulary Object Detection architectures, such as Grounding DINO, demonstrate strong zero-shot capabilities, their performance degrades significantly under domain shifts. Moreover, many domains of practical interest, such as nighttime or foggy scenes, lack large annotated datasets, preventing direct fine-tuning. In this paper, we introduce Aligned Basis Relocation for Adaptation (ABRA), a method that transfers class-specific detection knowledge from a labeled source domain to a target domain where these classes have no annotations, and no images are selected for them. ABRA decouples a detector into class-agnostic domain experts, obtained through Objectification, and class-specific residuals learned on top of them, and projects each source residual onto the singular subspaces of the target domain expert, without training. Extensive experiments across challenging domain shifts demonstrate that ABRA successfully teleports class-level specialization under multiple adverse conditions. Our code is available on GitHub.

authors.name: Mattia Bernardi, Chiara Cappellino, Matteo Mosconi, Samuele Bertaina, Enver Sangineto, Angelo Porrello, Simone Calderara

papers.title: Rethinking Vector Field Learning for Generative Segmentation
papers.summary: Taming diffusion models for generative segmentation has attracted increasing attention. While existing approaches primarily focus on architectural tweaks or training heuristics, there remains a limited understanding of the intrinsic mismatch between continuous flow matching objectives and discrete perception tasks. In this work, we revisit diffusion segmentation from the perspective of vector field learning. We identify two key limitations of the commonly used flow matching objective: gradient vanishing and trajectory traversing, which result in slow convergence and poor class separation.
