authors.name: Junyan Lin, Jianqi Ma, Shujie Duan, Hanxin Zhu, Zhihao Hu, Jinming Liu, Shuai Li, Jun Zhang, Xin Jin, Chang Wen Chen, Weidong Zhang

papers.title: G0.7: Scaling Up a Fast World Action Model with Long Context
papers.summary: World action models (WAMs) adapt pretrained video generators for robot control by jointly predicting future camera frames and actions, transferring physical priors learned from video into manipulation policies. However, generating future frames before every action makes test-time inference too slow for closed-loop control, while most existing policies remain restricted to short observation histories. Building on Fast-WAM, which showed that video prediction shapes policy representations during training so that future frame synthesis can be skipped at deployment, we present G0.7, a generalist world action model scaled along two axes: extending the context window from a single observation to up to five minutes of history, and scaling pretraining to a large-scale corpus of robot teleoperation and human egocentric (ego) video. Across public simulation suites and real-robot deployments, direct action decoding (Fast mode) matches imagine-then-act (IDM) inference from the same checkpoint while running in 60 ms per 16-step action chunk on a single RTX 5090 (7.6x faster than IDM) and supporting pause-free real-time chunking. Performance scales consistently with pretraining data, with human ego video driving the largest gains in out-of-distribution generalization: G0.7 achieves a 70.8 mean score across five simulation benchmark suites, 48% and 54% zero-shot pick-and-place success on Galaxea R1 Pro and R1 Lite, 96.7% in-distribution and 93.3% out-of-distribution success on video-conditioned in-context learning tasks, and 86.9% mean task progress across seven real-world post-training tasks including multi-minute box folding, drink preparation, and product bagging. Project page: https://www.galaxea-ai.com/model-g07.html

authors.name: Tianyuan Yuan, Baijun Ye, Shicheng Cao, Xing Nie, Xiaopeng Yu, Ke Dong, Zijie Zhao, Shenling Qiu, Yizhao Xu, Feiyang Xue, Haonan Liu, Haoyu Zhang, Haobo Jia, Zheng Liu, Bowen Zhang, Haodong Yang, Anqi Yang, Jiahui Niu, Yue Sun, Tailai Cheng, Jianpeng Yu, Yang Wen, Longhao Wei, Zibin Dong, Shiduo Zhang, Yicheng Liu, Hang Zhao

papers.title: EditText: Structure-Aware Generation and Selective Visual Transport for Fine-Grained Text Editing
papers.summary: Fine-grained text editing aims to accurately replace text in a specified region while preserving the source text's font, color, and texture, as well as visual consistency in unedited regions. We present EditText, a unified framework for fine-grained text editing that combines target character generation with visual transport from the source image. The model uses dual-condition Fill inputs: a masked image and a source text style reference, both sharing a spatial reference with the target image. The masked image hides the original text and retains unedited content as a source canvas; the style reference supplies appearance cues that guide new character generation together with the target text. We introduce an Attention Transport framework in which Source Weight describes the attention allocated to a condition and the Spatial Aggregation Kernel describes its internal spatial attention distribution. Accurate transfer of source details depends on attention strength, the retention of details in condition features, and spatially accurate aggregation. For selected non-edit queries, we therefore preserve the total attention weight assigned to the masked image while redistributing its attention toward spatially corresponding neighborhoods, enabling selective visual transport. Multi-stage training, combined with a Glyph-aware Structural Loss on local target character structure, teaches the model to generate accurate text, preserve source text appearance, and retain unedited details. We also introduce TBench, a fine-grained text editing benchmark covering Alphabetic, Logographic, and Arabic numerals, to evaluate character updates, appearance preservation, and the preservation of unedited details. On TBench, EditText achieves state-of-the-art non-edit-region SSIM (0.9769) and full-image LPIPS (0.0460).

authors.name: Zhaobin Chu, Guandong Li, Xin Lv, Zhiwei Zeng

papers.title: MediaStormBench-CameraLog: Can Multimodal Models Identify a Camera's Log Curve?
papers.summary: MediaStormBench is a multimodal benchmark for real-world film and television production, with each subset drawn from MediaStorm's day-to-day work. We release its first subset, MediaStormBench-CameraLog (CameraLogBench), on a common foundational task in footage ingest and initial color grading: identifying the Log curve of a clip without metadata. Cameras record Log footage by compressing a wide range of scene light into code values with a vendor-defined logarithmic curve, and color can be restored correctly only once that curve is known. The curve, however, is recorded only in file metadata, easily lost in transcoding and team hand-offs. A colorist then has to try candidate curves one by one against a waveform scope, and a wrong choice shifts the tones and colors of the whole clip. Recovering the curve from the image alone is challenging, because vendor curves cluster tightly in code value and are coupled with unknown exposure. CameraLogBench is built on professionally shot footage and tests whether multimodal models can identify the curve, with a probe that removes the correct option to expose guessing from priors. Because every candidate curve is strictly defined by a published vendor formula, we derive four controls from one implementation of these formulas: graded negatives, synthetic frames of identical scenes, in-context specification digests, and a training-free formula baseline, which together decouple semantic priors from photometric measurement. Across 11 models, real-footage accuracy barely exceeds always guessing the most frequent curve; when the correct option is removed, models almost never abstain, revealing heavy reliance on scene and brand priors. Supplying the vendor specification sharply improves recognition on calibrated charts but hardly helps on natural images without a photometric reference, exposing a gap between reading a specification and measuring pixels.

authors.name: Ming Ma, Wenhao Hu, Qichao Wang, Yuhao Wang, Junpeng Zhao, Qiyi Wang, Fangrui Zhang, Zhiqian Lai, Shanxin Guan, Haoyi Pei, Hongan Chen, Rui Gong

papers.title: What to Change, What to Keep: Experience-Evolving Agents for Video Recasting
papers.summary: Video recasting aims to transform the entities and environments of existing videos into new visual worlds while preserving their essential actions and interactions. However, achieving coherent transformations remains challenging, as coordinated edits can disrupt the original event structure. In this paper, we introduce RecastAgent, an experience-guided agentic framework for source-conditioned video recasting that operates under frozen model weights. Our framework employs an Experience-Guided Planner to choose edit prompts and input video states under qualitative visual critique, allowing the agent to build upon partial progress or backtrack to preserve source structure. Across tasks, an Experience Accumulation module distills completed trajectories into conditional, evidence-linked principles that record both an editing strategy and its scope of validity. We additionally construct a benchmark of 67 source videos with 134 paired-specification tasks across six creative categories for evaluation. Experiments demonstrate that RecastAgent outperforms single-pass and agentic rewriting baselines across Bernini and Ditto. Furthermore, accumulated experience improves performance on held-out test videos and transfers zero-shot to external benchmarks like FiVE-Bench and VE-Bench.

authors.name: Shiying Zhang, Yuxia Zhu, Huaze Xue, Shengqi Dang, Yizhen Wu, Yijie Li

papers.title: MaskedVGGT: Masked Multi-View Transformers Are Scalable 3D Learners
papers.summary: Multi-view feed-forward models show strong scalability, but their reliance on costly geometric annotations limits data scaling. Existing 3D self-supervised approaches reduce this reliance through cross-view completion (e.g., CroCo, MuM, Muskie) or novel-view synthesis (e.g., RayZer, E-RayZer), typically learning image representations and cross-view interactions jointly. We argue that learning single image representations from scratch is unnecessary for 3D pretraining methods, as doing so fails to benefit from the continuing advances in 2D foundation models (e.g., DINO, CLIP, frontier VLMs). We introduce MaskedVGGT, which freezes a strong pretrained 2D encoder and pretrains only an added, randomly initialized multi-view transformer, focusing on learning interactions across views. MaskedVGGT pretrains the multi-view transformer through masked self-distillation without annotations: a student predicts targets at masked locations based on complete anchor views and heavily masked remaining views, while an exponential-moving-average teacher provides prediction targets based on unmasked inputs. In experiments across model sizes up to 1B parameters, MaskedVGGT pretraining followed by fine-tuning outperforms single-stage supervised VGGT-$\Omega$ training with the same training data, model architecture, and total number of optimization updates. MaskedVGGT also outperforms E-RayZer, CroCo, MuM, and Muskie, providing evidence for the effectiveness of building multi-view pretraining on strong 2D representations. Finally, extending pretraining with additional unlabeled videos further improves generalization, and the learned representations transfer to diverse downstream tasks. These results demonstrate an effective division of learning: reuse strong image representations from 2D pretraining and learn cross-view interactions from unlabeled multi-view data without relying on geometric annotations.

authors.name: Zichen Zou, Xiaosong Jia, Wen-Ming Chen, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-Gang Jiang

papers.title: SynAVID: A Synthetic Audio-Visual Immersive Dataset of Dynamic Scenes
papers.summary: Immersive scene modeling requires synchronized visual and auditory observations under changing viewpoints and scene conditions. Obtaining such observations and references for controlled scene changes remains challenging. We introduce SynAVID, a synthetic audio-visual immersive dataset comprising eight indoor and outdoor scenes. Each minute-scale episode combines fixed camera arrays and moving trajectories with synchronized, viewpoint-dependent binaural audio. Shared scene dynamics, sound-source events, and observer poses drive visual rendering and geometry-aware acoustic synthesis. We evaluate existing methods for visual reconstruction, binaural audio reconstruction, and audiovisual editing. Mixed-observation configurations generally improve visual reconstruction on fixed and moving test views, while transiently occupied and sparsely observed regions remain challenging. Methods rank differently on spectral, interaural, and perceptual audio metrics. Geometric and instance annotations expose uneven observation support and local Gaussian representations beyond aggregate scores. Paired references assess target edits and surrounding content, while controlled geometry changes produce listener-dependent acoustic responses. The project page is available at https://avery-xu.github.io/synavid-project/.

authors.name: Jun Xu, Sujing Li, Chunhao Bi, Zhengxue Cheng, Ronghua Wu, Qunshan Gu, Li Song

papers.title: GOLD-SLAM: Gaussian-splatting Omnidirectional LiDAR-Depth SLAM
papers.summary: Panoramic cameras capture nearly the entire spherical field of view in a single frame. However, the mismatch between this panoramic coverage and the field of view of LiDAR poses a substantial challenge for panoramic Gaussian splatting SLAM that relies on LiDAR depth priors. We introduce GOLD-SLAM, a Gaussian-splatting Omnidirectional LiDAR-Depth SLAM system that combines high-quality rendering with accurate geometric reconstruction. It performs tracking and mapping in the spherical domain and uses tracked visual features in regions without LiDAR coverage to improve pose estimation. To address insufficient coverage of newly observed surfaces and floating artifacts during incremental mapping, we introduce Depth-Aware Map Extension and Pruning (DAEP). To enable broader evaluation, we collect a new dataset, WHOLE, using a UAV platform across Weak-geometry, High-dynamic, Omnidirectional, Low-light, and Easy scenarios. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks and WHOLE demonstrate competitive rendering quality and improved geometric accuracy relative to perspective systems. Compared with existing panoramic baselines, GOLD-SLAM improves mean PSNR by 5.56-9.10 dB and reduces mean Depth-L1 by 71.9-83.9%. To assess deployment feasibility on resource-constrained platforms such as UAVs, we evaluate an embedded configuration of GOLD-SLAM on a Jetson Orin NX (16 GB), demonstrating online operation at the cost of reconstruction quality.

authors.name: Weicong Zhang, Yuan Huang, Yu Zheng, Lin Chenxiao, Yingying Li, Lilong Fan, Liangdong Zhuang, Yufan Chen, Ruiping Liu, Junwei Zheng, Jiaming Zhang

papers.title: MinPair: Measured Minimal Pairs for Fine-Grained Control in Text-to-Motion Generation
papers.summary: Text-to-motion generation has made great progress in capturing what action to perform, yet it remains limited in controlling how that action is executed. For example, when only the height word of a kick request changes, none of the tested state-of-the-art methods reaches all three of knee, waist and head height. The other words of a caption usually imply an attribute such as height, so neither the training loss nor the standard metrics require a model to use the word that states it. A model has to use this word only when it alone separates two otherwise identical captions. We introduce MinPair, which creates such caption pairs from real motion clips. It starts from rule-based motion descriptors that measure the 3D body motion of each clip. From these descriptors a language model writes MinPair captions, timed body-part captions that say how each body part moves. The same descriptors show in which attributes two clips of the same action differ. A measured minimal pair joins the true caption of one clip with an altered copy in which only one attribute takes the value measured in the other clip. A contrastive pair loss then requires a diffusion denoiser to reconstruct the clip more accurately from its true caption than from the altered copy. Training needs no synthetic motion and inference stays unchanged. Control is tested on 22 target tasks and on caption edits that each change one attribute. MinPair captions alone help motions reach their targets and improve the standard metrics M2M, R@3 and FID, yet a model trained on them still ignores most single-word edits. The pair loss raises the share of followed template edits from 11% to 60%, while the standard metrics do not improve further. With body-part captions, MinPair reaches more targets than state-of-the-art methods that were trained on up to 99 times more motion data.

authors.name: Lennart Schiweck, Crist\'obal Curio

papers.title: EEG-World: Context-Conditioned Dynamics of the Watching Brain
papers.summary: Brain encoding models predict neural responses from audiovisual input, but typically overlook how ongoing brain activity shapes an individual's response. We introduce EEG-World, a recurrent world model that forecasts 10 seconds of EEG band-power dynamics from 6 seconds of preceding EEG and the subsequent audiovisual stimulus. Pretrained on continuous EEG, EEG-World learns shared neural dynamics and adapts to unseen individuals through lightweight subject-specific readouts. Using 2,584 hours of EEG from 78 participants, we show that nonlinear recurrent forecasting surpasses strong history-aware linear baselines at scale. EEG-World achieves a forecasting correlation of 0.261 versus 0.233 for the strongest history-and-video linear model, with a 3.3-second forecasting-horizon advantage. Its learned dynamics transfer to unseen participants, outperforming the linear baseline in 23 of 24 individuals after calibration. While ongoing EEG history accounts for most predictive performance, controlled stimulus analyses reveal an additional video-dependent component. This component also enables evaluation of visual representations, with V-JEPA 2 improving clip-locked prediction by 35% over combined CLIP and DINOv2 features. Our results demonstrate the value of transferable neural dynamics for individual EEG forecasting and highlight the importance of separating state-driven from stimulus-driven predictability.

authors.name: Junxiang Zhang, Jiayu Zuo, Wenhao Ye, Junfeng Xia, Xiang Chen, Mo Wang, Quanying Liu

papers.title: Biomechanically Grounded Prediction of Selective Motor Control and Clinical Outcomes from Infant Video
papers.summary: Early identification of cerebral palsy (CP) relies on observational assessments of spontaneous infant movement, such as the General Movement Assessment (GMA) and the Baby Observational Selective Control AppRaisal (BabyOSCAR), which require trained raters and substantial scoring time. Existing automated approaches derive hand-engineered features from two-dimensional keypoints, which describe image-plane motion rather than the three-dimensional behavior of individual joints. We present Baby Biomechanical 3D Body (BB3D), an infant-adapted, biomechanical pipeline that estimates joint-angle trajectories from single-camera video. Against a multi-view markerless motion capture reference in 17 infants, BB3D's median Procrustes-aligned error was 17.5~mm for joint centers and 20.4~mm for marker sites. A spatio-temporal transformer, pretrained on BB3D joint-angle trajectories from 1k+ single-camera recordings, and fine-tuned on 550 videos from 350 infants, predicted each individual BabyOSCAR item with a mean within-site AUC of 0.79 and the BabyOSCAR total with a Spearman correlation of 0.86 on held-out recordings. Without being trained on diagnosis, the predicted total separated infants with CP from those without CP with an AUC of 0.86, exceeding a replicated two-dimensional feature classifier (0.67) but below the expert clinician rater's total (0.97). Predicted scores also carried information about functional ability and body distribution, though less than expert clinician scores. These results show that biomechanically grounded representations of monocular video can support scalable, joint-level assessment of selective motor control in infancy

authors.name: Divya Joshi, Ruize Yang, Colleen Peyton, R. James Cotton

papers.title: Decision-Native Multimodal Clinical Modeling via Anatomical Grounding and Confidence Calibration
papers.summary: Structured clinical decisions from volumetric computed tomography (CT) require anatomically grounded predictions and calibrated confidence estimates. However, existing 3D medical multimodal models often suffer from uncalibrated autoregressive decoding and shortcut reliance on irrelevant anatomical regions. We introduce Radev, a decision-native multimodal model that integrates anatomy-guided visual compression, direct candidate prediction, and counterfactual confidence supervision. To bridge global context with fine-grained slice details, a frozen 3D encoder extracts reusable organ-level features, which are dynamically selected by the query to attend to 2D slice features within predicted anatomical bounds. The resulting compact visual tokens enable the language backbone to estimate candidate probabilities in a single forward pass without autoregressive decoding. We further propose Counterfactual-Calibrated Training (CCT) to compare predictions under intact and intervened organ representations. CCT encourages confidence to decrease when removing target-organ evidence degrades decision quality, while penalizing excessive confidence drops under unrelated-organ removal. To facilitate rigorous evaluation, we construct CT-Verdict, a comprehensive benchmark spanning binary finding presence, multiple-choice questions, and ordinal severity assessment across both in-distribution and external cohorts. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Radev significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both decision accuracy and confidence calibration, while generalizing robustly under distribution shifts. Project page at https://juntaojianggavin.github.io/projects/Radev/ .

authors.name: Juntao Jiang, Wenqi Zhong, Guangyu Guo, Dexia Chen, Yilong Hu, Yunhao Bai, Zhenyu Yi, Jianwei Xu, Tony C. W. Mok, Muxuan Gao, Ling Zhang, Yong Liu, Jiangning Zhang, Zhongwei Qiu

papers.title: RFW-W: Scaling Physical Asset Universes for Generative Embodied Simulation
papers.summary: Scaling embodied simulation requires diverse objects with executable physical representations. We present RFW-W, a physical asset universe connecting rigid, articulated, and deformable asset sources to task-conditioned scene composition. Its reported inventories comprise 1,010,386 asset records: 524,611 rigid assets in 1,212 categories (RFW-R), 402,410 articulated assets in 531 categories (RFW-A), and 83,365 jointly verified deformables in 485 categories (RFW-S). These taxonomies contribute 2,228 dataset--category entries. RFW-R couples category-guided generation with collision geometry, composed physical properties, and interaction annotations; RFW-A uses reusable agent-authored procedural generators with explicit part and joint structure; RFW-S uses structure-aware simulation representations, calibration, and independent testing. A common interface preserves physical requirements specific to each asset type for retrieval and scene assembly. Quantitative evaluations demonstrate that RFW-R provides broader asset coverage and stronger scene-fulfillment capabilities than existing datasets. Across five RoboTwin tasks, using 100 demonstrations per task for each asset source, policies trained on RFW-R achieve macro success rates of 71.2% in clean settings and 41.8% under randomization, exceeding the strongest baseline by 15.8 and 10.6 percentage points, respectively. RFW-W provides a scalable and unified asset foundation for generating physically grounded, task-conditioned embodied worlds.

authors.name: Jiawei Weng, Rui Zhang, Saining Zhang, Changjian Pan, Yuanbo Lyu, Jiarui Guo, Yongzhi Li, Guolin Liu, Jialu Liu, Jiankun Wang, Yi Yang, Peishuo Li, Zhiheng Li, Jiaying Wan, Junhao Chen, Weiqing Xiao, Jingrun Du, Wenyi Li, Weiyi Lin, Zenan Meng, Hu Wei, Lin Qu, Zongzheng Zhang, Hao Zhao, Chaojian Li

papers.title: 3DSS: 3D Surface Splatting for Inverse Rendering
papers.summary: We present 3D Surface Splatting (3DSS), the first differentiable surface splatting renderer for physically-based inverse rendering from multi-view images. Our central insight is that surface separation, which groups the surfels covering a pixel by the surface they sample, can be formulated with the reconstruction kernels themselves: two surfels sample the same surface when their kernels overlap in depth. Compositing each resulting surface layer with a coverage opacity derived from its accumulated Elliptical Weighted Average (EWA) weight yields anti-aliased silhouettes and informative visibility gradients at sparsely covered edges. With forward microfacet shading under co-optimized HDR environment lighting, 3DSS jointly recovers shape, spatially-varying BRDF, and illumination, and its oriented surfels convert directly into meshes by oriented-point surface reconstruction. On the real-world Stanford-ORB and the TensoIR Synthetic benchmarks, 3DSS outperforms state-of-the-art mesh-based and major comparable implicit and Gaussian-based methods in novel view synthesis and relighting, with geometry on par with the strongest baselines.

authors.name: Mae Younes, Adnane Boukhayma

papers.title: Distortion-Corrected Diffusion MRI Using Rotated-View EPI and Joint Field-Map/Image Estimation with Gaussian Primitives
papers.summary: Echo planar imaging (EPI) is the standard acquisition technique for diffusion and functional neuroimaging, enabling rapid imaging but suffering from geometric distortions caused by B0 field inhomogeneities. Existing correction methods first reconstruct distorted images using parallel imaging, then estimate the B0 field and correct the distortion in the image domain. In this sequential process, reconstruction artifacts at high acceleration factors and low SNR at high diffusion b-values degrade B0 estimation and limit the overall correction quality. We propose a physics-informed framework that jointly estimates the B0 field, the distortion-free image, and the shot-to-shot phase directly from k-space data, without depending on an intermediate parallel-imaging reconstruction. All three are represented as superpositions of Gaussian primitives embedded within an EPI forward model; the explicit, continuous parameterization captures both smooth regions and tissue boundaries and is evaluated on rotated sampling grids without resampling. The diffusion-weighted image is modeled as real and non-negative, with the image phase absorbed into a per-shot phase factor. Acquiring the blip-up/blip-down data at several phase-encoding orientations, the rotated-view principle of PROPELLER applied to full-FOV single-shot EPI, distributes distortions across orientations, improving point spread function isotropy and providing stronger constraints for B0 estimation. On in vivo brain diffusion EPI at R=4 and 5, the proposed method attains the closest brain-boundary agreement with a distortion-free structural reference, with the largest improvement over sequential methods at high b-value.

authors.name: Wenqi Huang, Zhitao Li, Nan Wang, Yimeng Lin, Mengze Gao, Yurui Qian, Sevgi Gokce Kafali, Xiaozhi Cao, Kawin Setsompop, Daniel Rueckert, Congyu Liao

papers.title: AVENUE: Audio-Video EditiNg Understanding and Evaluation
papers.summary: Audio-video (AV) editing aims to modify audio and video content according to a target prompt. Unlike single-modality editing, AV editing requires models to infer a modality-selective edit scope from the prompt alone: determining not only what should change, but also which modality should be preserved. Faithfully evaluating such models therefore requires both (i) benchmarks that span diverse edit types and modality categories, and (ii) evaluation that is itself modality-aware and sample-specific. However, existing AV editing benchmarks provide limited coverage of edit types and modality combinations, while current evaluation systems are often modality-blind and sample-agnostic, making it difficult to assess whether models faithfully preserve the unintended modality. To address these gaps, we introduce AVENUE, Audio-Video EditiNg Understanding and Evaluation, comprising two contributions: (1) a benchmark of 1,291 source clips and 7,957 editing instructions across audio-targeted, video-targeted, and AV-coupled edit types, curated and human-verified from VGGSound; and (2) a sample-specific, modality-aware evaluation framework that specifies, for each sample, both the intended change and the content that must remain intact. We evaluate representative AV editing models spanning three editing paradigms : joint, sequential, and separate, providing the first systematic analysis of modality-selectivity across paradigms. Our findings reveal a fundamental open challenge: when editing one modality, existing models frequently induce unintended changes in the other, regardless of paradigm. AVENUE provides a benchmark and modality-aware evaluation framework to drive progress toward more controllable AV editing models. Our dataset is publicly available on Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/datasets/AVENUE-dataset/AVENUE.

authors.name: Hayeon Kim, Yoojin Jang, Jaejun Yoo

papers.title: Self-Distilling Future Video Representations for World Action Models
papers.summary: World Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising approach to learning generalist robot policies using rich spatiotemporal priors from pre-trained video diffusion models. A recent line of WAMs improves inference efficiency by conditioning a separate action decoder on intermediate future video representations extracted from a single denoising step, avoiding costly iterative denoising required for video generation. This design makes action prediction depend directly on the quality of these future representations. In this paper, we introduce Future REpresentation learning via self-Distillation with temporal context (FRED), a framework that trains WAMs to improve the quality of future video representations from noise in a single denoising step. Specifically, FRED uses self-distillation to predict future representations from noise, using representations extracted from ground-truth future observations as targets. We further condition the video model on historical observations, providing temporal context for predicting future representations better. Across diverse real-world manipulation scenarios, FRED consistently outperforms competing WAMs. It achieves particularly large gains on long-horizon and out-of-domain tasks under zero-shot environment generalization, and substantially improves human-to-robot skill transfer, reaching 50.0% task success on tasks absent from robot training data and demonstrated only in human videos, compared with 10.7% for the best competing WAM.

authors.name: Huiwon Jang, Suhyeok Jang, Hyeonmo Kang, Seungku Kim, Jinwoo Shin, Sihyun Yu

papers.title: TacInno: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models the Contact Dynamics Beyond Vision and Action
papers.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently been equipped with tactile sensing to perceive visually subtle contact events in contact-rich manipulation. However, adding tactile input yields inconsistent gains, and some visuo-tactile VLA models rely little on tactile input, because much of the tactile change, such as the gel deformation during gripper closure, is predictable from visual observations and executed actions. To address this problem, we introduce TacInno, which isolates the contact dynamics that vision and executed actions cannot explain, termed tactile innovation, and uses tactile innovation only as a training target. Specifically, the TacInno tokenizer, conditioned on visual observations and executed actions, compresses the future tactile change into a discrete code, and the policy, TacInno-VLA, learns to predict the code, adding no module for the code at deployment. TacInno-VLA achieves average success rates of 87.5% across six simulation tasks and 70.5% across four real-world tasks, outperforming the strongest visuo-tactile baseline by 10.7 and 9.0 percentage points, respectively. Ablation studies validate the contributions of visual and action conditioning, multi-frame encoding, and auxiliary code prediction. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of tactile innovation as a supervision signal for contact-rich manipulation.

authors.name: Weile Li, Yunfan Lou, Muqing Shi, Zihao Zhang, Zhenbiao Huang, Boxian Yao, Xiyu Zhu, Zhibo Pang

papers.title: Beyond Code and Pixels: Co-Generating Editable and Visually Rich Presentations
papers.summary: Generating PPTX presentations is a structured task that requires semantic planning, visual composition, precise layout, and editability, motivating collaboration among specialized agents. However, programmatic methods offer editability but often produce rigid designs, while image-based methods provide visual richness but flatten content into difficult-to-edit pixels. A hybrid system can combine these strengths, but must coordinate interdependent decisions across content, layout, and appearance. To address this challenge, we propose SlidesWeaver, a hybrid multi-agent system that coordinates language and vision agents through shared deck- and slide-level states. Specifically, it uses staged multimodal commitment, diffusion-based composition planning, and two generation schedules for different priorities between composition freedom and accurate text preservation, while preserving native text and geometry. Across 1,728 generations spanning 24 system-model configurations, SlidesWeaver achieves consistently superior overall quality across all evaluated dimensions while maintaining structural control, editability, and practical generation efficiency.

authors.name: Wenrui Zhou, Jiashun Liu, Sujie Hu, Bang Liu, Ling Pan

papers.title: OVOK: A Recursive Self-Improving Agentic Framework for Video-Based Articulated Robot State Estimation
papers.summary: Recovering articulated robot state from video supports metric spatial sensing for manipulation, scene reconstruction, and action planning. Yet the problem is ill-posed: different intrinsics, camera-to-robot poses, and joint angles can explain similar observations. Prior task-specific regressors typically assume known intrinsics, fit one robot through laborious data collection and robot-specific training, and still transfer poorly across scenes. Foundation models apply to any robot zero-shot, but their estimates have large errors. We present OVOK (One Video to Kinetics), a recursive self-improving agentic framework for this task. Under a human-authored protocol, an agentic initializer constructs robot-specific OVOK-4k; a proposer--executor--verifier loop then jointly evolves tools and executable workflows from feedback. Updated tools and workflows are accepted only when the verifier judges a positive improvement. The retained workflow is frozen for accurate inference. Experiments demonstrate that the evolved workflow achieves state-of-the-art results on DREAM-V and RoboKeyGen-V, delivering robust and accurate estimates.

authors.name: Cheng Dai, Renkai Luo, Guanfeng Tang, Siming Li, Hao Zhao

papers.title: Halley's Comet Over New Zealand In 1910: An Overview Of A Spectacular Apparition
papers.summary: Halley's Comet (1P/Halley) returns to the inner Solar System approximately every 76 years. In 1910, the comet put on a particularly wonderful display, whereby the comet attained an apparent magnitude of 1 or brighter, and had a tail of up to 120{\deg} in length. Many New Zealanders saw Comet 1P/Halley and submitted articles to newspapers across the land. Those articles were mostly from lay-people who reported their observations of this, the most famous of all comets. There were, however, numerous serious amateur and professional astronomers who made detailed observations and took world-class photographs of the comet. In this paper, we present the results of a thorough search through historical records and media publications in Aotearoa/New Zealand, to investigate how extensively Comet 1P/Halley was observed from this island nation. Where appropriate, we compare the observations described with international accounts, and find that those made from Aotearoa/New Zealand often echo what observers were witnessing around the world. We find that thousands of New Zealanders observed Comet 1P/Halley in 1910, and that the comet raised the interest in astronomy across the land resulting in the establishment of a number of astronomical societies that remain active to the current day.

authors.name: John Drummond, Wayne Orchiston, Carolyn Brown, Jonathan Horner

papers.title: Continuous Universal Fake Factors for jet-to-tau background estimation
papers.summary: We study Continuous Universal Fake Factors (CUFF), a method for estimating backgrounds from jets misidentified as hadronic tau candidates. CUFF combines four reference-region fake factors for each target tau candidate failing Loose identification. Their weights depend on candidate features and target fail-Loose distributions after subtracting simulated contributions from genuine taus and electrons or muons misidentified as tau candidates. We use ATLAS 2015-2016 Open Data with tau candidates matched to jets with $20<p_T^{\rm jet}\leq60$ GeV. In eight mixtures of reference samples with known proportions, predicted total yields for the Medium identification selection differ from data after subtraction by $+0.7\%$ to $+4.3\%$, supporting the combination. In two validation regions, the corresponding differences are $-21.85\%$ and $-45.84\%$, with statistical uncertainties, including training fluctuations, of $1.58\%$ and $6.03\%$ relative to the data references. These discrepancies lie within broad empirical uncertainty ranges from simulation comparisons between regions, widened by limited simulation statistics. For Loose identification, CUFF and the Universal Fake Factor (UFF) method adapted to public data give similar inclusive yields in one validation region, while CUFF agrees more closely with the data reference in the other. CUFF also describes the shapes of several kinematic distributions more accurately than adapted UFF, including that of an observable not used as a model input. Across nine identification thresholds, relative yield differences vary gradually from $-26.4\%$ to $-19.7\%$ and $-50.2\%$ to $-40.6\%$ in the two regions, respectively, demonstrating consistent application of CUFF at continuously variable tau-identification thresholds without retraining.

authors.name: Lei Guo, Antonio De Maria, Chengxin Liao, Zihang Liu, Wenyi Jin, Jiarong Yuan, Yuchen Cai, Da Xu, Xuai Zhuang, Yanjun Tu, Yang Liu

papers.title: Syringe reuse in HCV transmission among people who inject drugs: behavioral thresholds and optimal control
papers.summary: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) transmission among people who inject drugs (PWID) is driven largely by syringe sharing and reuse, yet existing models rarely treat reuse as a behavior that individuals adopt and abandon. In this work, we develop and analyze a four-compartment epidemic model that explicitly incorporates syringe reuse as a distinct behavioral process, introducing a high-risk susceptible subgroup that acquires infection through both direct contact and syringe-mediated transmission. We establish the well-posedness and biological feasibility of the model, derive the basic reproduction number, and analyze the existence and stability of the disease-free and endemic equilibria along with closed-form behavioral threshold conditions for syringe-reuse adoption and cessation. Global sensitivity and scenario analyses reveal that while transmission and recovery parameters dominate epidemic potential, behavioral parameters governing the adoption and cessation of syringe reuse play a crucial role in disease persistence and control thresholds. The model's projected infection dynamics are broadly consistent with observed U.S. HCV incidence trends. We further formulate an optimal control problem targeting reuse initiation and cessation, and show through cost-effectiveness analysis that combined behavioral interventions outperform single-component strategies in reducing both infection and high-risk behavior. These results indicate that behavioral prevention aimed at syringe reuse is a necessary component of sustained HCV control among PWID.

authors.name: Mohammad Zaman, Emel Khan, Ishfaq Ahmad, Hiromi Seno

papers.title: CLEAR: A Contrastive-Masked Foundation Model for BESIII Event Understanding
papers.summary: The increasing diversity and complexity of decay channels at high energy physics experiments pose a challenge to analysis workflows, which require time-consuming, labor-intensive channel-specific selections and optimization. This motivates the development of foundation models capable of learning a unified representation transferable across different channels. In this paper, we introduce CLEAR (Contrastive Learning for Event Attention-based Representation), a foundation model designed for physics analysis at BESIII that combines masked modeling and contrastive learning to support decay channel classification and anomaly detection. Masked modeling trains the encoder to predict masked particle features by learning inter-particle correlations, while contrastive learning improves the local clusterability and linear separability of the representation space for discrimination. By further examining the balance between alignment and uniformity, we investigate how contrastive learning shapes the local neighborhood geometry of the representation space and how this geometry relates to classification and anomaly detection performance. Decay channel classification favors a balance between alignment and uniformity, whereas anomaly detection benefits from a greater relative weight on uniformity. For exclusive final-state identification, CLEAR achieves higher signal efficiency than conventional cut-based methods at matched purity and provides a framework that can potentially be extended to other high-energy physics experiments.

authors.name: Jingde Chen, Zijie Shang, Tong Liu, Yao Zhang, Beijiang Liu, Changzheng Yuan, Xiongfei Wang, Ke Li

papers.title: Shower Shapes and Data-Driven Simulation Studies using a Highly Granular Crystal ECAL
papers.summary: Electron shower shapes were measured using standard shower profile models for events observed with a highly granular crystal electromagnetic calorimeter prototype, with data taken from a 2025 test beam at the CERN Proton Synchrotron T9 beamline. The shower maximum, longitudinal shape parameter, and lateral variance were found to be well approximated by log-normal distributions. From these distributions, properties of the absorber were measured to be in agreement with existing literature. Energy-dependent correlations were observed between all parameters and most strongly between the shower maximum and the shower shape parameter. The distributions of energy and event-by-event pairwise log ratios of energy fractions in individual active volumes of the calorimeter conditional on the shower shape were found to be consistent with shifted and scaled Gamma and Fisher's-z distributions, respectively. Generative methods were developed to simulate the logarithm of shower shape variables using Gaussian copulas. Copula sampling for shower shape parameters was found to produce superior modeling of heavy tails observed for the shower maximum and longitudinal shape parameter distributions when compared to direct sampling from a correlated multivariate normal distribution. A copula method was also devised to sample full shower events conditional on the shower shape parameters by exploiting the observation that the vector of energy fractions follows a logistic Log-Gamma distribution, the joint relation implied by the observed Fisher's-z form of the pairwise log-ratios. The generative model was evaluated using standard manifold and classifier metrics and was found to approach the data-versus-data ceiling. The fastest generation time was found to be around 30 {\mu}s per particle shower.

authors.name: Jack Rolph, Yong Liu, Baohua Qi, Shu Li, Zhiyu Zhao, Haijun Yang

papers.title: Quantization concealment of angular momentum: dynamic origin of spins
papers.summary: Since their introduction, spins of elementary particles remain a phenomenological addition to modern quantum theories. While relatively recent studies on Dirac and other linearized equations of motion have revealed the spatial current nature of the spin magnetic moment (instead of the commonly pictured self-rotation), the dynamical origin of this circulating current remains unresolved. Here, we expose a long-overlooked generic shortcoming of wave mechanics ("quantization concealment of angular momentum") that undesirably reduces the canonical angular momentum of bound eigen-modes and renders incomplete the minimal coupling to magnetic fields. Recovering the kinetic orbital angular momentum resolves $1s$-orbital's counterintuitive "zero" angular momentum and reproduces all planar modes' anomalous Zeeman splitting. Regarding spins as effective remedy to the concealment offers natural explanations to their main puzzles: 1) dynamical origin of spin magnetic moment and 2) frame invariance of spin angular momentum. This implies absence of spin magnetic moment for free particles, a strong prediction verifiable through Stern-Gerlach experiments on electrons.

authors.name: Wenjie Long, Wei Ku

papers.title: Anomalous scaling of coalescence in a Hele-Shaw cell
papers.summary: We investigate the merging of two drops between two narrowly spaced plates, a so-called Hele-Shaw cell. For this, we solve the Hele-Shaw equations in two dimensions, driven by surface tension, focusing on early times after initial reconnection. Combining numerical simulations with theory, we show that the coalescence dynamics are self-similar at early times, with the size of the contact region between the drops growing as $t^{3/13}$. We find this power law using a matched asymptotic analysis, which reveals a complex geometry consisting of a small bubble that gets entrained between the drops as they come together. These predictions match perfectly to our simulations, and agree with the most recent experimental data.

authors.name: Luke Neville, Rodolfo Brand\~ao, Marco A. Fontelos, Jens Eggers

papers.title: Butterfly Effect in Kinetic Plasma Turbulence
papers.summary: The butterfly effect is a fundamental process in chaotic systems, but it has not previously been characterized in detail for a collisionless turbulent plasma. In this work, we apply particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of driven turbulence to study the emergence of the butterfly effect from a small initial perturbation to the simulated particles. In particular, we compare pairs of (baseline and perturbed) simulations that differ only by a localized initial perturbation (down to the single-particle level). We find that the effect of the localized perturbation spreads radially throughout the PIC simulation, causing a difference between each simulation pair that is exponentially amplified over time within the affected region. The fields, including the electric current density, eventually become statistically decorrelated. We construct an analytical model combining spatial expansion with exponential amplification to approximate the early-time evolution. Varying the initial perturbation primarily affects the early-time evolution, while having little effect on the final, decorrelated state. We describe parameter scans with varying plasma beta and temperature (covering sub-relativistic and ultra-relativistic regimes). Our results show that remarkably small perturbations will grow to decorrelate each pair of simulations within a few dynamical times; the imposed perturbation can no longer be resolved once it falls below the numerical precision floor set by the machine precision. These results confirm that the butterfly effect is very strong and robust in a collisionless plasma, with implications for the predictability of turbulent plasma systems.

authors.name: Louis Henderson, Vladimir Zhdankin

papers.title: Dressed Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory: Opening and Closing a Pandora's box
papers.summary: Dressed time-dependent density functional theory (DTDDFT) has been shown to overcome the inability of adiabatic TDDFT to describe excitation energies and oscillator strengths of double-excitation character, however, it is far from being a black-box method. Here, we outline and address several operational issues while benchmarking the approach on a range of molecules. We define a protocol to determine whether an excitation from adiabatic TDDFT needs a double-excitation correction, without requiring a priori knowledge of the state, and which Kohn-Sham states to build the frequency-dependent DTDDFT matrix from. We present an 'undownfolding' that replaces this frequency-dependent matrix by a linear frequency-independent one in a larger space, eliminating ambiguities in the iterative procedure required to diagonalize the former. We compare the performance of DTDDFT for both excitation energies and oscillator strengths, as measured by an approximate metric for their single-excitation character, for different choices of the underlying adiabatic density functional approximation, with and without employing the Tamm-Dancoff approximation, for molecular excitations predicted by wavefunction methods to have either partial or genuine double-excitation character. We propose a correction to DTDDFT to account for missing dynamical correlation that is removed in the truncation procedure inherent in the method, and discuss the possibility of unphysical imaginary frequencies reminiscent of the 'triplet instability' that may arise. We provide benchmark data for butadiene, hexatriene, octatetraene, cyclopentadiene, acrolein, naphthalene, ethylene, borole, and cyclopentadienone. In some cases, DTDDFT predicts frequencies with about as much accuracy as the same underlying adiabatic TDDFT predicts for the constituent and near-lying single excitations.

authors.name: Jack T. Taylor, Neepa T. Maitra

papers.title: Basin-Scale Nonlinear Dynamics of Thermohaline Ocean Circulation. Part I: Theory
papers.summary: Earth's thermohaline ocean circulation may support multiple equilibria and abrupt transitions. Similar bifurcation structures for different ocean models suggest common underlying dynamics across the model hierarchy. Here we propose a unifying framework from tracer conservation, in which surface fluxes are balanced by dissipative and advective tracer transport. We express this flux balance through a large-scale tracer gradient and a transport efficiency that measures how strongly circulation displaces the tracer field from its no-flow "conductive" state. The flux balance quantifies the transport contributions that sustain each circulation state and give rise to abrupt transitions. In a three-dimensional ocean-basin model, we find nonlinear salinity advection dominates the collapse threshold and linear dissipation dominates the recovery threshold. Temperature has additional dissipation from surface restoring, making thermal fluxes more dissipation-dominated than salinity fluxes. The tracer contrasts and boundary layers that a given circulation generates produce distinct transport regimes, approximately quadratic in circulation strength for weak flow and linear for strong flow. With a simple circulation closure, the flux balance reduces to longstanding box-model bifurcation results for the weak and strong flow regimes. Thus, by expressing thermohaline bifurcations through basin-scale transport, this framework connects box-model insight to the continuous equations. Furthermore, as this framework exposes the transport processes that balance a changing forcing, it provides constraints on a thermohaline ocean state and its trend toward tipping that overturning strength alone does not. In Part II, we develop flux-balance closures to forecast such tipping points.

authors.name: Conner W. Lester, Dylan E. McNamara, Till J. W. Wagner

papers.title: Electrical grid stabilisation through agent strategies : a mean-field game approach
papers.summary: We propose and solve a minimal model based on mean-field game theory to study decentralized power consumption strategies to stabilize power grids. The mean-field Kuramoto description of an electrical network is coupled to agents with anticipatory capacity for decision making in energy consumption. Each agent minimizes an individual cost which includes both a financial part (cost induce by consumption and by power reservation) imposed by a central authority, and a (personal) non-monetary part. This elementary model of active oscillators is exactly solvable in the steady state regime. We show that the synchronized regime of the network can be significantly extended by the game.

authors.name: Loumi Gatouillat, Guillaume Roux, Dganit Meidan, C\'ecile Appert-Rolland, Cosimo Gorini, Denis Ullmo

papers.title: Computing hydration free energies and crystalline solubility of drug-like molecules with MACE
papers.summary: Accurate prediction of thermodynamic solubility is critical in drug discovery, where it influences oral bioavailability and drives decisions in formulation chemistry. First-principles calculations of intrinsic solubility offer the potential to achieve superior generalization to existing direct, data-driven predictors, which often suffer significant performance degradation outside of their training distribution. Whilst free energy perturbation calculations provide a rigorous framework to estimate these quantities, their accuracy is typically limited by the quality of the empirical force field used. In this work, we present a computational workflow driven by the MACE family of machine learning interatomic potentials to compute the solubility of neutral drug-like molecules. We introduce $\lambda$-MACE, a potential optimised for condensed-phase free energy calculations, which enables hydration free energy calculations at experimental accuracy on an evaluation set of 70 compounds from the FreeSolv database selected for their relevance to medicinal chemistry. We further combine these hydration free energy calculations with sublimation free energy calculations to predict crystalline solubility given a known experimental crystal structure, on an additional set of 10 compounds. We achieve state-of-the-art performance for each leg of the calculation, with experimental accuracy for the hydration leg, and accuracy competitive with industry-standard DFT for the sublimation leg. However, the overall errors after combining both legs lead to accuracy of 1.53 log units. This is significantly above the experimental accuracy (0.17-0.6 log units). Closing this gap will require substantially tighter accuracy in each leg, on the order of half of chemical accuracy (0.5 kcal/mol), with crystalline thermodynamics the hardest remaining challenge.

authors.name: J. Harry Moore, Paul Mortenson, Davide Branduardi, Pavel Buslaev, Javier Antor\'an, Laurence Midgley, Nicholas J. Browning, G\'abor Cs\'anyi

papers.title: Physics-Based TCAD Modeling of Nanowire Cryotrons with Coupled Superconducting and Thermal Dynamics
papers.summary: Nanowire cryotrons (nTrons) provide gate-controlled superconducting switching, current gain, and high-impedance outputs for cryogenic computing, detector readout, and superconductor-semiconductor interfaces. We develop a physics-based Sentaurus TCAD framework that couples time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau dynamics, separate electron and phonon energy equations, and mixed-mode circuit simulation. Superconducting terminal-current corrections connect the custom solver to the native electrical solution, linking local suppression of superconductivity, heating and cooling, and current redistribution in the external circuit. To our knowledge, this is the first Sentaurus-based mixed-mode TCAD implementation for nTrons. We calibrate the model against experimental switching data at six gate currents using a single parameter set. The model achieves an RMS load-current error below 1 $\mu$A outside the switching region and switching-current differences of about 1 $\mu$A or less. Simulations show that a center gate gives the highest switching sensitivity, while a drain-side gate gives the largest post-switch resistance. Narrower channels switch at lower currents and exhibit higher resistance. Transient and bidirectional bias sweeps capture electrothermal hysteresis, gate-controlled switching latency, and bias-controlled recovery. Simultaneous activation of three gates lowers the switching threshold from about 104 $\mu$A with all gates inactive to about 12 $\mu$A, demonstrating cooperative suppression of superconductivity. The framework supports the design of nTron geometries, operating conditions, and multi-input architectures.

authors.name: Abdullah All Hasib, Md Shafayat Hossain, Ahmedullah Aziz, Shamiul Alam

papers.title: APEX: Agentic Platform for Ensemble eXploration
papers.summary: Ensemble-based methods provide a practical framework for history matching, prediction, and optimization of subsurface models. In methodological studies, however, performance is rarely assessed from a single run. Comparisons typically span cases, configurations, and random seeds, while each evaluation may require an expensive external simulator. Keeping such studies computationally bounded, auditable, and reproducible therefore requires more than implementing a numerical method: experiments must be validated before execution, computational costs estimated, repeated runs organized consistently, and configurations and outputs made traceable. To address these needs, we developed APEX (Agentic Platform for Ensemble eXploration), an open-source Python platform that provides a common framework for configuring, validating, executing, recording, and comparing ensemble-based experiments. APEX is organized around three concepts: an experiment defines what is executed, a run records a single execution, and a study coordinates and compares multiple experiments or runs. Experiments are specified through validated configurations, which can also be generated by a planner agent. Before execution, APEX estimates the maximum number of forward simulations required. If the estimate exceeds a user-defined threshold, submission is held for approval. Each run records provenance information, while studies repeat problems across variants and paired replicates and compare results using paired statistical analyses. Scientific and computational components, including methods, simulators, metrics, and optimizers, are implemented as plugins. A command line interface, Python client, REST service with a web interface, and tools for language model agents access these capabilities through a common service layer.

authors.name: Xiaodong Luo

papers.title: Statistical analysis of crossing beam speckle fields
papers.summary: Building on the statistical analysis of single beam speckles, this paper develops a statistical description of speckle fields formed by crossing laser beams. A formal definition of individual speckles and their domains allows us to quantify the effective size and abundance of speckles. For two crossing beams, the effective speckle size is derived from the local curvature of the intensity field, and the expected speckle abundance is found asymptotically with the Kac-Rice formula. Monte Carlo simulations of speckle abundance show excellent agreement with the theoretical abundance formula. The two beam speckle analysis is then applied to a symmetric quad beam configuration motivated by polarization smoothing and demonstrates that increasing the separation between beams reduces expected stimulated Brillouin scattering reflectivity from saturated speckles. The statistical model is then extended to an arbitrary number of beams using a coordinate free formulation to obtain the spectral density of laser driven electron density fluctuations.

authors.name: Ian D. Min-Roberts, Wojciech Rozmus, Pierre A. Michel

papers.title: Analytic sc$GW$ nuclear gradients with the resolution-of-identity approximation
papers.summary: We present the first fully analytic derivation and implementation of nuclear gradients for the finite-temperature sc$GW$ method. The derivation is formulated within the $\Phi$-derivable framework of sc$GW$, using a Lagrangian formulation to obtain the analytic gradients. With the resolution-of-identity approximation, the computational cost of evaluating the gradients scales as $O(N_{\tau}N_\text{aux}^{2}N_\text{AO}^{2})$, exhibiting the same asymptotic scaling as the parent sc$GW$ method. Using the newly implemented analytic gradients, we perform geometry optimizations for several molecular systems and benchmark the resulting structures against those obtained with Hartree--Fock, $G_{0}W_{0}$, MP2, CCSD, and CCSD(T). We find that sc$GW$ generally yields reasonable molecular geometries, with its performance being comparable to that of CCSD for several systems. Overall, these results demonstrate the potential of analytic sc$GW$ gradients for reliable geometry optimizations for molecular systems while retaining the favorable $O(N_{\tau}N_\text{aux}^{2}N_\text{AO}^2)$ scaling of the underlying method.

authors.name: Jianhao Li, Pavel Pokhilko, Chia-Nan Yeh, Miguel A. Morales, Dominika Zgid

papers.title: Numerical Studies of Ground State Atomic Parity Violation Measurements in Cesium
papers.summary: We report results of numerical simulations of an ongoing measurement designed to measure the electric dipole (E1) transition moment between hyperfine components of the ground state of atomic cesium. This E1 moment is non-zero solely due to nuclear weak interactions between the nucleons, leading to a nuclear anapole moment of the cesium nucleus. Through these simulations, we explore the effect on the microwave spectrum of a static transverse magnetic field, a spatial offset of the atomic beam from the axis of the radio-frequency (rf) cavity, the angular tilt of the rf cavity, and the ac Stark shift by the Raman-coupling beams used to generate the initial superposition state between ground state components. The results of these simulations help place limits on the experimental parameters, and help guide the future experimental procedures.

authors.name: Chunya Wang, Matthew Summers, Jonah A. Quirk, Diego Garcia, Carol E. Tanner, D. S. Elliott

papers.title: Azimuthally Resolved Energy Dissipation Rates in the Impingement Zone of Equal Free Impinging Liquid Jets: A Three-Dimensional Model
papers.summary: When two equal liquid jets collide, they form a thin sheet of liquid and lose some of their incoming kinetic energy (doi:10.1615/AtomizSpr.2025056396). Calculating the energy dissipation rate per unit mass requires estimating the volume of the region where the collision takes place. This paper develops a three-dimensional model of that region and uses it to calculate how the energy dissipation rate varies with angular position within the collision region. The model assumes that the thickness of the collision region varies linearly along each radial line from the stagnation point to its outer boundary. Combining the resulting volume with the kinetic energy lost during the collision provides equations for both the overall energy dissipation rate and the rate averaged over each narrow angular portion of the collision region (local energy dissipation rate). For equal jets with uniform inlet velocity profiles, the model predicts substantial differences in energy dissipation rate with angular position, even when the incoming jets and the resulting sheet have uniform mean velocities. The model also reproduces expected theoretical limits, including a cylindrical collision region for directly opposed jets. Preliminary micromixing results are consistent with the predicted variation, although independent validation of the assumed collision-region geometry and the location of energy dissipation is still needed.

authors.name: Robert J. Demyanovich

papers.title: Global self-organisation via driven interchange turbulence in a hard-core Z-pinch
papers.summary: Whereas most magnetic-confinement concepts seek to suppress turbulent transport, the levitated dipole exploits it, with plasma turbulently self-organising to concentrate into the stronger-field region near the levitating coil. In a sufficiently large device, this can create the conditions needed for fusion, despite stiff and vigorous transport. We study this process in global simulations of a driven hard-core Z-pinch using compressible ideal magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) with self-consistent evolution of the magnetic field. The results reveal how plasma and field jointly settle onto a continuously turbulent, finite-beta interchange-marginal family. Across a wide drive scan in two-dimensional simulations, quasi-universal pressure and density profiles result, with the magnetic-field profile changing from a decreasing vacuum-like form to one with an interior minimum at increasing beta. These profiles are robust to large changes to the heat and particle sources (including moving both to the outside of the device) as well as to different exhaust and boundary prescriptions. A designer consequently has little direct control over the selected profiles, including the final separation between the pressure maximum and coil, which is set by a turbulent boundary layer. We show that such results persist in the presence of three-dimensional fluctuations at modest beta, but that high-beta states become unstable to a field-parallel m=1 instability that is the analogue of the ballooning instability in a true dipole; this evacuates the core, destroying confinement. Based on a near-marginal expansion and a geometrical remapping, we argue that many features of our results should apply to any shearless closed-field-line system.

authors.name: Jonathan Squire, Christopher Hill, Laoisa Huckle

papers.title: Development of a low-level radio frequency system for remote in situ superconducting radio frequency cavity measurements and calibrations in conduction-cooling systems
papers.summary: We developed a low-level radio frequency (LLRF) system for superconducting radio frequency (SRF) cavity measurements in a conduction-cooling system. A voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) was used in a phase-locked loop (PLL) to track the frequencies of SRF cavity modes. {\tt{Python}}-based software developed in-house controlled and monitored the system. By introducing an additional circulator and associated components, we developed an LLRF system enabling fully remote in situ SRF cavity measurements for the first time. This design also enables remote in situ calibrations. Hence, our LLRF system improves safety through fully remote operation and enhances measurement precision through in situ calibrations, with safety always taking priority. These calibrations are important for measurements in conduction-cooling systems because temperature stability and uniformity in these systems are poorer than those in convection-cooling systems using costly liquid helium and can vary over time and with environmental conditions.

authors.name: C. Lim, K. Seol, S. E. Park, E. -S. Kim, E. Kako, S. Lee, B. R. Ko

papers.title: Systematic study of the performance of small robots on controlled laboratory substrates
papers.summary: The design of robots able to locomote effectively over a diversity of terrain requires detailed ground interaction models; unfortunately such models are lacking due to the complicated response of real world substrates which can yield and flow in response to loading. To advance our understanding of the relevant modeling and design issues, we conduct a comparative study of the performance of DASH and RoACH, two small, biologically inspired, six legged, lightweight (10 cm, 20 g) robots fabricated using the smart composite microstructure (SCM) process. We systematically examine performance of both robots on rigid and flowing substrates. Varying both ground properties and limb stride frequency, we investigate average speed, mean mechanical power and cost of transport, and stability. We find that robot performance and stability is sensitive to the physics of ground interaction: on hard ground kinetic energy must be managed to prevent yaw, pitch, and roll instability to maintain high performance, while on sand the fluidizing interaction leads to increased cost of transport and lower running speeds. We also observe that the characteristic limb morphology and kinematics of each robot result in distinct differences in their abilities to traverse different terrains. Our systematic studies are the first step toward developing models of interaction of limbs with complex terrain as well as developing improved limb morphologies and control strategies.

authors.name: Chen Li, Aaron M. Hoover, Paul Birkmeyer, Paul B. Umbanhowar, Ronald S. Fearing, Daniel I. Goldman

papers.title: A nonequilibrium-capturing unified gas-kinetic scheme II: multi-frequency radiation transport
papers.summary: Conventional discrete ordinate methods are widely used for thermal radiative transfer, but their fixed number of angular degrees of freedom (DoFs) incurs unnecessary computational cost near equilibrium. We therefore develop a nonequilibrium-capturing unified gas-kinetic scheme (NCUGKS) for multi-frequency radiation transport. The scheme preserves the mul tiscale capability of UGKS through interface evolution that couples transport and collision. Radiation intensity is expanded in an orthonormal basis of the discrete angular space. The expansion coefficients serve as angular DoFs, with their number adapted independently to local nonequilibrium in each cell, frequency group, and quadrant. At each time step, the coefficients to be evolved are selected using the exponentially decayed contribution from the previous step and the requirements of interface transport. The selected coefficients are advanced by the finite volume scheme and corrected to match the macroscopic radiation energy before higher-degree coefficients are discarded according to the prescribed relative tail tolerance. Therefore, in the optically thick limit, the resulting representation retains only one angular DoF per quadrant. Numerical tests spanning different optical regimes show close agreement with reference solutions, validating its accuracy. Furthermore, in terms of memory and computational efficiency, the proposed method reduces memory by factors from 21.7 to 154.0 and achieves speedups from 24.87 to 257.9 compared with the original discrete ordinate UGKS. NCUGKS thus provides the ability to accurately simulate multiscale ra diative transfer with reduced memory and computational costs. The proposed approach also offers a framework for adapting angular degrees of freedom in other discrete ordinate methods.

authors.name: Hongyu Liu, Xiaojian Yang, Xing Ji, Jianxian Qiu, Kun Xu

papers.title: BridgeSRDA: Efficient Probabilistic Super-Resolution Data Assimilation with Forecast-Informed Stochastic Interpolants
papers.summary: High-resolution ensemble data assimilation is computationally demanding because it requires repeated forecasts and updates of many flow states. We introduce BridgeSRDA, a probabilistic super-resolution data assimilation framework that combines low-resolution numerical forecasts with sparse, noisy observations to generate high-resolution analysis windows. A neural network learns forecast-informed stochastic transport, which is sampled to produce an ensemble of reconstructions. Each current analysis initializes the next low-resolution forecast, while the same window provides retrospective reconstructions and short-range nowcasts. We evaluate BridgeSRDA over ten independently initialized trajectories of a three-dimensional quasi-geostrophic flow in a narrow-jet regime different from training. At the training observation spacing, BridgeSRDA approaches the mean and structural reconstruction accuracy of a high-resolution local ensemble transform Kalman filter and reduces the mean absolute error ratio by approximately 32.5% relative to deterministic four-dimensional SRDA. With 30 ensemble members, BridgeSRDA requires approximately 17 s per analysis, compared with 31 s for the filter under the recorded conditions. Ten members reduce the cost to approximately 6.6 s with little change in mean accuracy, though fine-scale accuracy and interval coverage are affected. BridgeSRDA achieves a competitive continuous ranked probability score, but its ensembles are underdispersed: nominal 90% intervals contain approximately 62% of reference values. Boundary spread artifacts and reduced skill under sparser observations also warrant attention. These results demonstrate the potential of forecast-informed stochastic transport for probabilistic data assimilation, while highlighting the need to improve uncertainty calibration and robustness to changing observation networks.

authors.name: Aditya Sai Pranith Ayapilla, Yuki Yasuda, Ryo Onishi

papers.title: Deep-learning-enabled rapid spatially multiplexed wavefront sensing with a thin diffuser
papers.summary: Conventional wavefront sensing typically measures aberrations along a single guide-star direction, limiting the correction of field-dependent aberrations over a wide field of view. Spatial multiplexing with a thin diffuser enables simultaneous measurements across multiple isoplanatic patches, but the computational cost of reconstruction makes it difficult to track changing aberrations. We propose a deep-learning approach that combines recurrent all-pairs field transforms for displacement estimation with Zernike coefficient regression. Experimental results show that the method accurately reconstructs multiple wavefronts from a single speckle pattern and reduces three-channel reconstruction time from 2801.6 ms with conventional digital image correlation (DIC) to 23.1 ms. The reconstructed wavefronts agreed more closely with sequential single-channel references than those obtained by multiplexed DIC, and simulations showed that Zernike regression was more robust to noise than direct gradient integration. These results suggest a path toward dynamic wide-field aberration sensing and high-speed adaptive optics.

authors.name: Ming Xue, Shijie Wei, Shulei Zhao, Zhuojia Shi, Tengfei Wu, Xiaopeng Shao

papers.title: Carrier relaxation confines the Bogdanov--Takens degeneracy of an optically injected semiconductor laser
papers.summary: Optically injected semiconductor lasers are forced nonlinear oscillators whose locking boundaries are organized by codimension-two points. We ask which property of the carrier balance permits or forbids a Bogdanov--Takens (BT) point in the standard three-dimensional rate equations. Taking the carrier inversion $n$ as distinguished observable, the rate that enters the spectral conditions is the slope of the gain--loss balance, $\xi=\partial\dot n/\partial n=-2\Gamma/\kappa$, where $\Gamma$ is the damping of the relaxation oscillation and $\kappa=1+2Bn$ the normalized stimulated-emission factor. The two BT conditions become affine in $\xi$ and imply the exact sum rule $K^{2}=I[1-(1+\kappa)I]$ between injection amplitude $K$ and intracavity intensity $I$. The product of the two relaxation eigenvalues that survive at a saddle-node is bounded below by $1-16\Gamma^{2}$, so that no BT point exists for $\Gamma<1/4$, whatever $B$, the linewidth enhancement factor, the injection strength and the detuning; below this barrier every contact between Hopf and saddle-node curves is a fold--Hopf point. For $B=0$ the barrier is completed to an exact existence criterion. We prove that the unfolding of a BT point by injection strength and detuning is transversal if and only if two explicit curves cross transversally in the plane of locked states; for $B=0$ this is a simple root of an explicit function, and transversality fails exactly at the existence threshold. Two BT points at $\Gamma=1/2$, $\alpha=2$ are verified to be generic, and the contacts between Hopf and saddle-node curves are classified into fold--Hopf, BT and nilpotent triple-zero points.

authors.name: A. Mart\'in-Ruiz, E. Chan-L\'opez, Carlos Antonio Mar\'in-Mendoza

papers.title: Remote and Noncontact Acceleration and Suppression of Heat Convection on Object Surfaces using Intensity-Adjusted Acoustic Streaming
papers.summary: The temperature of objects in an environment is often controlled by accelerating or suppressing heat convection. Conventional methods generally involve insulation for heat retention and forced convection for cooling. However, there is no practical method for remotely and target-selectively controlling heat convection in objects in room environments. In this study, we demonstrated that intensity-adjusted acoustic streaming (ultrasound-driven airflow) can both suppress natural convection and induce forced convection on the surface of a heat source. The direct acceleration and deceleration of air over the object surface were induced by an ultrasonic beam with high temporal and spatial resolution. The experiment showed that it is possible to switch between insulating and cooling by adjusting the ultrasonic output intensity, and that it is essential for heat retention to prevent heat from escaping from the object surface by convection using acoustic streaming. We consider these results to lead to the realization of a situation where virtual heat-retaining blankets or cooling fans that are customized for specific objects in the environment can be ubiquitously attached to them, opening the door to applications such as temperature control of food and beverages and remote control of temperature profiles in manufacturing processes and laboratory settings.

authors.name: Yuki Yuzawa, Keisuke Hasegawa

papers.title: Existence of single-resonance parametric bound states in the continuum: System of Schr\"odinger equations
papers.summary: A bound state in the continuum (BIC) is an eigenmode of a linear wave system with its eigen-frequency embedded in the radiation continuum of scattering states. At the frequency of a BIC, scattering problems with given incident waves from infinity lose uniqueness. Due to their close connection with strong resonance effects, BICs have found many useful applications in classical and quantum wave systems. Existence theories of BICs have been established for some cases involving the so-called symmetry-protected BICs, Friedrich-Wintgen BICs, and Fabry-Perot BICs. The single-resonance parametric BICs (srp-BICs) are another important class of BICs. Such a BIC emerges from a single resonant state through tuning a real parameter. Using a simple system of two one-dimensional Schr\"odinger equations, we demonstrate the formation of srp-BICs and establish a rigorous existence theory.

authors.name: Xiuchen Yu, Ya Yan Lu

papers.title: Geometry Sets the Neutral MLIP-DFT Gap in Non-Covalent Binding, and Charged Systems Fail
papers.summary: Pretrained universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are widely expected to substitute for explicit quantum chemistry when screening molecular interactions. On non-covalent binding we find that this expectation holds for neutral chemistry and fails for charged chemistry. We audit the FAIRChem UMA OMol head, without task-specific fine-tuning, on 5,567 probe-target dimers from 18 benchmarks across nine fidelity arms, using RAPIDS (Rapid Atomistic Probe-target Interaction Discovery Scaffold), a training-free inference-time scaffold. First, on neutral chemistry RAPIDS reaches a mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.37 kcal/mol, matching or beating every explicit DFT single-point fidelity (1.42-1.50 kcal/mol), so the remaining MLIP-DFT gap is geometric rather than a learned-surface error. Second, charged systems form a qualitatively different regime: MAE jumps to 8.5-22.9 kcal/mol across three charged benchmarks; DFT single-point rescoring does not restore accuracy, geometry reoptimization restores it for ionic hydrogen bonds and ion-molecule dimers, and the failure persists across all three MLIP backbones. Third, the residual failures are structured: signed biases cluster by chemistry family, and whether a fidelity fails catastrophically transfers across families more reliably than error magnitude, enabling cost-aware fidelity selection. RAPIDS-Select, a closed-form rule on cheap precomputed features, uses about 37% less compute than a strong static DFT baseline at matched accuracy, and on a newly computed charged benchmark cuts the catastrophe rate from 68% to 5.7%. On WetSenseBench, a wet-lab-grounded host-guest selectivity benchmark from eight sensing studies, RAPIDS without DFT follow-up recovers 82.9% pair-level agreement on the seven studies above its ~1 kcal/mol precision floor.

authors.name: Rui Ding, Zixin Ding, Rodrigo Pires Ferreira, Diantong Li, Junhong Chen, Yuxin Chen
