On this coordinate, plots of the logarithm of the normalized discharging voltage are approximately straight lines through the origin, providing empirical models. For charging, the corresponding logarithmic plots are clearly curved, and the discharging model breaks down. Using the remaining distance from the final value as the dependent variable gives approximately straight logarithmic plots and provides a basis for revising the model. Rewriting the discharging model in equivalent differential and integral forms allows students to compare changes in charge-like and energy-like quantities with the charge transferred through the resistor and the energy dissipated in it. Standard circuit theory, introduced afterward, describes charging and discharging in a common form and gives these quantities their conventional meanings.

authors.name: Kazumasa Kushida

papers.title: Boundary-layer scheme selection outweighs microphysics in WRF simulations of the August 2018 Kerala extreme rainfall event
papers.summary: Because precipitation is regulated by intricate interactions between topography, cloud microphysics,cumulus convection, radiation, and boundary-layer processes, it is still difficult to accurately simulate orographically enhanced monsoon rainfall over the Western Ghats.

authors.name: Satyam Kumar, Akshay Sunil, Rashad PE

papers.title: Quantized response of amplification in non-Hermitian photonic time quasicrystals
papers.summary: Photonic time crystals amplify waves through periodic temporal modulation of the permittivity. We study a non-Hermitian photonic time quasicrystal, a temporal analogue of the non-Hermitian Aubry-Andre-Harper model of quasiperiodic lattices. Its modulation is incommensurate and has a complex phase, whose imaginary part, the complexification parameter, acts as an imaginary gauge field on the modulation harmonics. We find that the bulk amplification rate, as a function of this parameter, is organized into distinct phases, within each of which its slope is locked to an integer, known in quasiperiodic operator theory as Avila's acceleration. The phase boundaries are predicted from Fourier coefficients of rational approximants and confirmed by transfer-matrix and time-domain simulations. Under analytic distortions of the modulation waveform, the integer phases persist while their boundaries move. Consequently, two input frequencies in different integer phases have an amplification ratio that varies exponentially with the complexification parameter, which enables spectral selection. These results establish a topologically protected, quantized response law for amplification in such time-varying media.

authors.name: Shuhang Chen, Zhi Zheng, Qi Zhu

papers.title: Demonstration of H-mode Error Field Identification in a Single Discharge via Island Healing
papers.summary: Non-disruptive compass scan error field identification via island healing is demonstrated on KSTAR in a single H-mode discharge. This method can allow for up to a 75% reduction in the operational time necessary for a complete compass scan by reducing the required discharges from four to one. Previous experiments on DIII-D, JET, and MAST-U have demonstrated the technique in Ohmic and L-mode but required multiple discharges and high fidelity real time n = 1 magnetic diagnostics located close to the plasma, which are unlikely to be viable for future devices. The results presented here were made possible by implementing a new set of triggering algorithms relevant to fusion pilot plant operation into the KSTAR plasma control system, along with KSTAR's strong RMPs and long pulse lengths. This represents a significant step towards the disruption-free error field identification method being demonstrated for deployment on future disruption-averse tokamaks, including ITER and fusion pilot plants. Steps needed to close remaining gaps to viability are addressed.

authors.name: E. M. Bursch, A. Xie, J. L. Barr, S. K. Kim, N. C. Logan, S. M. Yang, J. G. Bak, W. Choi, Q. Hu, J. W. Juhn, J. Kim, J. Lee, N. Leuthold, J. K. Park, C. Paz-Soldan, L. Piron, G. Seo, J. Seo

papers.title: Cumulus parameterization controls simulated rainfall more than microphysics, but not at heavy thresholds: a 3 * 2 factorial WRF study over the Western Himalaya
papers.summary: Rainfall forecasts over the Western Himalaya remain poor, and the relative contributions of the cumulus and microphysics parameterizations to that error are not well constrained.

authors.name: Satyam Kumar, Akshay Sunil, Devesh Sheoran

papers.title: 5D Runge-Lenz Vector from Symplectic Reduction of 8D Harmonic Oscillator
papers.summary: We investigate the origin of the Runge-Lenz vector of the five-dimensional Kepler problem in the SU(8) dynamical symmetry of the eight-dimensional harmonic oscillator acting on its phase space. Using a complete basis of real $8\times 8$ matrices constructed from five-dimensional gamma matrices and the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ generators associated with the symplectic reduction, we decompose the conserved quantities of the harmonic oscillator into representations of $\mathrm{SO}(5) \times \mathrm{SU}(2)$ and identify the SU(2)-singlet sector. We show that the corresponding conserved quantities generate an SO(6) subgroup of the SU(8) dynamical symmetry. We then perform the Hurwitz transformation and symplectic reduction with respect to SU(2), obtaining the five-dimensional Kepler Hamiltonian. We explicitly show that the SO(6) moment map reduces to the angular momentum and the suitably normalized Runge-Lenz vector of the five-dimensional Kepler problem on a fixed negative-energy surface. This establishes the origin of the Runge-Lenz vector in the dynamical symmetry of the eight-dimensional harmonic oscillator.

authors.name: Hitoshi Ikemori, Shinsaku Kitakado, Yoshimitsu Matsui, Toshiyuki Okubo, Toshiro Sato

papers.title: Quartz Crystal Microbalance impedance of discrete adsorbates with lubricated contact
papers.summary: We present theoretical investigation of the shear force exerted on a horizontal plate undergoing fast (MHz range) longitudinal oscillations in presence of a spherical particle suspended in the liquid at close proximity to the plate. This hydrodynamic problem is relevant toward the analysis of frequency response (i.e., complex impedance) of Quartz Crystal Microbalance (QCM) to discrete (particulate) adsorbates. For low areal density of adsorbates, the contributions of individual particles remain additive, rendering the theory applicable towards quantitative interpretation of the experimental measurements. For adsorbates much smaller than the viscous penetration depth, the closed-form analytical expressions for the complex impedance were derived for particles of arbitrary density, assuming a lubricated contact (i.e., non-localized adsorption). The theoretical predictions were shown to be in an excellent agreement with accurate Finite Element numerical computations. The validity of the theoretical approach was confirmed by QCM measurements conducted for polystyrene nanoparticles in a broad range of sizes, from 32 nm to 510 nm, adsorbing onto gold/silica sensor upon varying the oscillation frequency.

authors.name: Alexander M. Leshansky, Boris Y. Rubinstein, Marta Sadowska, Zbigniew Adamczyk

papers.title: Plasma transport by carrier electrons: delocalization length for heat-flux
papers.summary: The kinetic understanding of the three magnetized heat-flux components is unified in the linear regime with a full electron-electron collision operator and a converged harmonic expansion of the electron distribution (up to $f_6$). The delocalization length $\lambda_d=\lambda_{ei} Z/\sqrt{Z+4.45}$ is an improved heat-flux non-locality metric accounting for the localizing effect of electron-electron collisions on the electron population carrying heat-flux. Magnetization also localizes the carrier electrons; the delocalization Hall parameter $\psi_d=13.4 \chi Z/(Z+4.45)$ shows that this occurs at a faster rate than magnetization of thermal conductivity ($\psi_{\kappa}= 9.94\chi(Z+0.17)/(Z+5.88)$). The traditional Knudsen number, which uses the electron-ion mean-free path, does not fairly represent non-locality across ionization and magnetization; $Kn_d = 8.28\lambda_{d\bot}/L_T$ should instead be used. Righi-Leduc suppression is found to be the square of the perpendicular suppression, with no additional length-scale required. This approach lays the groundwork for consistent treatment of kinetic plasma transport, with subsequent papers addressing the kinetically-modified induction equation.

authors.name: C. A. Walsh

papers.title: Scale-Dependent Statistics of Coherent Magnetic Structures in Early IMAP Observations
papers.summary: We analyze early Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe (IMAP) magnetic field observations (November 2025 to May 2026) to quantify the statistical properties of helical magnetic structures and their relationship with turbulence intermittency. Intermittent structures, such as current sheets, are identified using the Partial Variance of Increments (PVI) method, and the scale-dependent normalized magnetic helicity is computed over scales corresponding to 0.5-3 correlation lengths. Prior studies have typically applied the PVI-helicity method to individual events; here we extend this technique to the ensemble statistics of a multi-month sample spanning many correlation times. To separate coherent helical structures from random turbulent fluctuations, significance thresholds for helicity are determined using phase-randomized surrogate realizations. We find a clear scale dependence in the occurrence, duration, and waiting time of coherent magnetic helicity, reminiscent of the scale-transfer arguments underlying inverse cascade, selective decay, and Taylor relaxation theories. Event duration and waiting-time distributions are well described by power-law and exponential models over different ranges, consistent with previous findings. In addition, PVI and magnetic helicity are anticorrelated, suggesting that high-PVI regions are preferentially associated with the boundaries of flux ropes, while their interiors tend to exhibit lower PVI and stronger magnetic helicity.

authors.name: Sujan Prasad Gautam, Francesco Pecora, Subash Adhikari, Riddhi Bandyopadhyay, Jiaming Wang, Joshua Goodwill, William Taranto, Rayta Pradata, William H. Matthaeus, David J. McComas, Eric Christian, Nathan Schwadron, Matina Gkioulidou, Jamie Rankin, Timothy S. Horbury, Savvas Raptis, Drew L. Turner

papers.title: Impact of Cumulus Parameterization and Cloud Microphysics on WRF Simulation of an Extreme Rainfall Event over Maharashtra, India: A 3 by 3 Factorial Assessment
papers.summary: Simulating extreme monsoon rainfall over the Konkan coast and Western Ghats remains challenging at 9 km resolution, where convection is partly resolved and partly parameterised. This study evaluates the sensitivity of Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) simulations of the 5-7 July 2026 Maharashtra rainfall event to cumulus and cloud microphysics schemes. Nine simulations employed a 3 x 3 factorial design combining WSM6, WDM6 and Thompson microphysics with Kain-Fritsch, Tiedtke and Grell-Freitas cumulus schemes. Rainfall was evaluated against IMD 0.25-degree gridded observations, with IMERG and ERA5 as additional references. A descriptive factorial decomposition showed that cumulus parameterisation accounted for 97.3% of across-experiment variation in mean rainfall, 88.2% in RMSE and 84.7% in spatial correlation, while microphysics contributed 2.0%, 2.1% and 9.3%, respectively. Kain-Fritsch produced the highest spatial correlations (0.533-0.581) but substantially overestimated rainfall. Tiedtke achieved the smallest mean biases and RMSE, although compensating regional errors concealed a 28-34% rainfall deficit over the Konkan-Ghats belt and substantial underestimation on 7 July. Grell-Freitas showed large wet biases and relatively high RMSE. All nine simulations displaced the event-total rainfall maximum approximately 140-195 km northward. WSM6-Tiedtke achieved the lowest RMSE, whereas Thompson-Kain-Fritsch better represented the rainfall spatial pattern. The findings demonstrate that, for this event and fixed model configuration, cumulus parameterisation exerted substantially greater influence on simulated rainfall than cloud microphysics. However, a single-event, single-member experimental design does not establish a universally optimal physics configuration.

authors.name: Devesh, Satyam Kumar, Akshay Sunil

papers.title: Beyond the Federer paradox in tennis
papers.summary: Roger Federer won about 80% of his professional matches with only 54% of the points. Hierarchical scoring amplifies small advantages on points into large advantages on matches, but also allows a player to win with fewer points than the opponent. Using Monte Carlo simulations and exact Markov chain calculations, we show that in tennis, badminton, volleyball and table tennis this amplification is set almost entirely by the number of points per match. We then let a player win ordinary points with probability p1 and crucial points, those closing a game, set or match, with probability p2. In every sport a narrow region of the (p1, p2) plane exists where a player wins most matches with fewer than half of the points, because crucial points carry more influence than their share of points. Of ATP matches played in 1991-2025, 4.7% were won with fewer points, 16% more than independent points predict (5% including the serve), a constant excess. Pressure performance measured in other seasons predicts match outcomes beyond the points won, and Fabio Fognini won 51% of his matches with 49% of the points, in what we call the Fognini paradox.

authors.name: Andr\'es Mart\'in, Johann H. Mart\'inez, Javier M. Buld\'u

papers.title: Multi-pump amplification of frequency-separated Stokes waves in stimulated Brillouin side scattering
papers.summary: Multibeam stimulated Brillouin side scattering (SBSS) can be enhanced when one side-scattered light wave is amplified by several pump waves through different ion-acoustic waves (IAWs). This mechanism differs from models in which several pumps share the same scattered-light wave or the same IAW. Side-scattered light generated by different pumps can propagate in nearly the same direction but have different frequencies. We examine this process using a local temporal-growth calculation, a finite-width Gaussian k-space model, a three-dimensional envelope model, and two-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. These cross-beam three-wave interactions increase temporal growth and convective gain over the crossing angles considered. In the three-dimensional envelope calculations, direct SBS interactions alone produce weak, localized side scattering, whereas including the cross-beam interactions produces a strong response for the same incident fields and initial perturbations. The enhancement remains when the total incident power is fixed, so it comes from the cross-beam interactions rather than from extra laser power. The PIC simulations show stronger side scattering and several pump-specific IAWs, with a non-monotonic dependence on beam number. These results identify cross-beam amplification of frequency-separated side-scattered light as a gain pathway that should be considered when interpreting multibeam SBS experiments.

authors.name: Y. Chen, Qing Wang, H. Wen, Y. X. Li, S. Tan, C. Y. Zheng, Z. J. Liu, L. H. Cao, C. Z. Xiao

papers.title: Experimental Evidence for MeV Undulator Radiation Generated by Ultrarelativistic Positrons in a Periodically Bent Crystal
papers.summary: We report evidence for undulator radiation generated by ultrarelativistic positrons in a large-amplitude, long-period crystalline undulator. A pattern of Si$_3$N$_4$ stressors periodically bend the (110) planes of a Silicon crystal with a geometry measured independently by x-ray diffraction. Under planar alignment, the forward energy loss showed a localized excess at $6.8 \pm 0.3$~MeV, matching the predictions of simulations. Experimental results also indicate that an intense positron beam could make the undulator competitive in brilliance with state-of-the-art inverse-Compton gamma-ray sources.

authors.name: L. Bandiera, N. Canale, S. Carsi, M. Cavallina, F. Cescato, N. Charitonidis, D. De Salvador, M. Diaz Castro, E. Diociaiuti, P. Fedeli, L. G. Foggetta, A. Forlani, A. Gianoli, V. Guidi, L. Malagutti, F. Mancarella, S. Mangiacavalli, A. Mazzolari, R. Negrello, G. Patern\`o, M. Prest, J. Reyes Garrido, M. Romagnoni, A. Saputi, F. Sgarbossa, A. Sytov, V. V. Tikhomirov, E. Vallazza, D. Valzani

papers.title: Hydr\'oDex: gotta match 'em all!
papers.summary: First-order phase transitions can source a stochastic gravitational-wave background within reach of LISA and other future detectors, with sound waves in the plasma typically providing the dominant contribution. Predicting the resulting gravitational-wave signal requires determining the stationary fluid profiles around expanding bubbles. We present a complete hydrodynamic classification of these profiles in the constant-sound-speed model, which generalizes the bag model by allowing the sound speeds in front of and behind the wall, $c_+$ and $c_-$, to differ. Solving the matching conditions at the wall and evolving the surrounding plasma, we recover the known direct and inverse detonations, deflagrations, and hybrids, and uncover mixed hybrids, a new class with rarefaction waves on both sides of the wall and oppositely directed fluid flows. For a sufficiently pronounced hierarchy $c_+>c_-$, multiple stationary profiles can correspond to the same wall velocity $\xi_w$ and asymptotic transition strength $\alpha_N$. This non-uniqueness arises because this parametrization discards thermodynamic information and is resolved once the underlying microphysics is specified. We compute the kinetic-energy budget and acoustic gravitational-wave spectra within the sound-shell model, finding that mixed hybrids introduce no additional spectral feature and can be mimicked by ordinary direct or inverse hybrids with substantially different fluid profiles. Finally, we release Hydr\'oDex, a public code implementing the complete classification, profile construction, energy-budget calculation, and gravitational-wave prediction.

authors.name: Giulio Barni, Eric Madge

papers.title: A No-Go Theorem for Type-3 New General Relativity on $\Lambda$CDM Background
papers.summary: We investigate whether Type-3 New General Relativity can alleviate the cosmic growth tension. On a $\Lambda$CDM background, we derive the scalar perturbation equations and find the effective gravitational coupling to exceed Newton's constant throughout the parameter range compatible with ghost-free and background-hierarchy conditions. By confronting the theoretical model with growth-rate measurements from major galaxy redshift surveys, including WiggleZ, SDSS-IV eBOSS, BOSS, and VIPERS, we obtain constraints on the effective coupling that are consistent with the $\Lambda$CDM value. Consequently, the conditions for stability and tension reduction are mutually exclusive.

authors.name: Shivam Kumar Mishra, B. Mishra

papers.title: Run it Back: Autoregression vs. Video Diffusion for Final-Conditioned Weather Trajectories
papers.summary: Low-likelihood, high-impact extremes are projected to increase in severity and frequency in a warming climate. Sampling the precursors that lead to these events traditionally requires massive ensembles that scale poorly with lead time and rarity, and typical rare-event sampling and ensemble-boosting methods do not show how a single extreme might arise from diverse synoptic precursors. Recently, Lin et al. (2026) showed this is possible with final-conditioned 66-hour trajectories (trajectories constrained to end at an observed state) from cBottle-video, a pre-trained, off-the-shelf video diffusion climate emulator not explicitly fine-tuned for this task (Brenowitz et al., 2025). However, its ensembles were underdispersed and geostrophically inconsistent, and it reproduces conditioned frames only approximately, hindering autoregressive rollout. Here, we train Rewind-AR, a backward-in-time probabilistic autoregressive model with a FourCastNet~3 backbone (Bonev et al., 2025), and generate final-conditioned ensembles for the same three cases: the 2021 Pacific Northwest heatwave, Hurricane Ian, and Superstorm Sandy (in the Supplementary Information). The leading modes of Rewind-AR's antecedent 500 hPa geopotential height explain far more of the across-member variance than cBottle-video's for both hurricane position and heatwave surface temperature, and Rewind-AR better reproduces the day-over-day heatwave intensification observed in ERA5. Finally, geostrophic inconsistencies close to the conditioning frame seen in cBottle-video are not reproduced by Rewind-AR. Nevertheless, up to 22% of Rewind-AR members become numerically unstable within 66 hours, so improving rollout physical consistency and stability over long lead times is a natural next step.

authors.name: Jerry Lin, Elizabeth A. Barnes

papers.title: Can Language Models Build Molecules in Three Dimensions?
papers.summary: Chemical drawings convey which atoms are bonded and how stereocentres are configured, but not molecular shape. Every simulation starts from three-dimensional coordinates, and building them from a drawing remains a manual step. We introduce MolDraft, a curated benchmark of 300 drawing-structure pairs spanning natural products, hypervalent compounds, and coordination complexes. Given an image and a short instruction, an AI system must generate a complete set of atomic coordinates, which are checked for molecular identity, stereochemical configuration, and coarse ligand geometry. We evaluate nine multimodal language models using the same agent setup. The share of molecules built correctly, the resolve rate, ranges from 25.0% to 76.0% and falls as molecules grow, most sharply above about 80 atoms. Only 29 of the 300 molecules are resolved by all nine models, and literature structures, mostly metal complexes, are the hardest source for every model. Language models can thus build many molecules in three dimensions, but not yet reliably reproduce the coordination chemistry of the research literature.

authors.name: Hanyong Xu, Yunheng Zou, Olalla Nieto Faza, Juan Bernardo P\'erez S\'anchez, Aiwei Yin, Al\'an Aspuru-Guzik, Varinia Bernales

papers.title: DUV (257 nm) LIDT of Anti-Reflective Coatings
papers.summary: Laser-induced damage threshold in the deep ultraviolet (DUV) was used to perform tests on AR coated windows intended for industrial processes. The 257 nm wavelength was generated from Yb:YAG fundamental (1030 nm) and the long-term LIDT stability (up to 100000 shots) was selected as representative for minimal industrial qualification. Selected setup for the fourth harmonics generation consists of two stages, generation of second harmonic and subsequently the fourth harmonic with 13,4% conversation efficiency. In both 1-on-1 and S-on-1 experiments, the optics coated with Al2O3/SiO2 by ion beam sputtering technique demonstrated the highest LIDT value of 0.73 and 0.5 J/cm2 respectively. Various damage morphologies, color centers, ballistic damage, delamination, and blistering were observed across the samples with respect to the 1-on-1 and S-on-1.

authors.name: Martin Mydlar (HiLASE Centre, Institute of Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Dolni Brezany, Czechia), Hana Turcicova (HiLASE Centre, Institute of Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Dolni Brezany, Czechia), Priyadarshani Narayanasamy (HiLASE Centre, Institute of Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Dolni Brezany, Czechia), Mihai George Muresan (HiLASE Centre, Institute of Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Dolni Brezany, Czechia), Ondrej Novak (HiLASE Centre, Institute of Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Dolni Brezany, Czechia), Jan Vanda (HiLASE Centre, Institute of Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Dolni Brezany, Czechia), Tomas Tolenis (ELI Beamlines Facility, The Extreme Light Infrastructure ERIC, Dolni Brezany, Czechia), Jan Brajer (HiLASE Centre, Institute of Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Dolni Brezany, Czechia), Tomas Mocek (HiLASE Centre, Institute of Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Dolni Brezany, Czechia)

papers.title: COSIMA Cookbook: a community-driven resource for ocean and sea-ice modelling science
papers.summary: The COSIMA Cookbook is an open educational resource for analysing ocean and sea-ice model output in Jupyter notebooks. It has been developed by the Consortium for Ocean--Sea Ice Modelling in Australia (COSIMA) as a community resource for researchers, students, and practitioners working with large gridded datasets, especially output from the ACCESS ocean--sea ice model configurations. The Cookbook is organised around a gastronomy theme: "Cooking Tutorials" teach generic, transferable techniques for handling model output, while "Easy Recipes", "Advanced Recipes" and "Regional Specialties" are self-contained notebooks that show how to perform concrete diagnostics and analyses. Along the way, the notebooks demonstrate open-source tools for the scientific analysis of large data, including Intake catalogues, Xarray, Dask, xgcm, xESMF, eofs, Parcels, matplotlib and Cartopy. The Cookbook addresses the steep entry cost of analysing climate model output: it packages expert, often tacit, knowledge into complete, well-documented and reusable workflows, in the same medium in which researchers actually work. It is developed openly on GitHub, is published as a documentation website, and is continuously reviewed and extended by its community through pull requests and regular hackathons. The easy access to data and analysis it provides has contributed to the international adoption of ACCESS ocean and sea-ice model configurations, and has facilitated well over 100 peer-reviewed papers and more than 20 PhD projects.

authors.name: Navid C. Constantinou, Julia Neme, Wilton Aguiar, Matthis Auger, Ashley J. Barnes, Romain Beucher, Dhruv Bhagtani, Christopher Yit Sen Bull, Hannah Dawson, Noah Day, Fabio Boeira Dias, Edward W. Doddridge, Anupiya Ellepola, Denisse Fierro-Arcos, Angus Gibson, Aidan Heerdegen, Andy McC. Hogg, Ryan M. Holmes, Maurice F. Huguenin, Wilma Huneke, Jemma Jeffree, Andrew E. Kiss, Minghang Li, Paige Martin, Josu\'e Mart\'inez-Moreno, Jan Jaap Meijer, Thomas Moore, Ruth Moorman, Adele K. Morrison, James Munroe, Aditya Narayanan, Micael Oliveira, Ellie Q. Y. Ong, Madelaine G. Rosevear, Christina Schmidt, Taimoor Sohail, Paul Spence, Dougal T. Squire, Anton Steketee, Charles Turner, Felipe Vilela da Silva, Marc White, Luwei Yang, Claire Yung, Jan Zika

papers.title: Dark and bright solitons in a multimodal lithium tantalate microresonator
papers.summary: Bright-soliton and dark-pulse microcombs provide complementary outputs. Integrating both states in a single resonator would expand the operating capabilities of an integrated coherent source, but requires opposite group-velocity-dispersion (GVD) channels while reconciling localized interfamily interaction for dark-pulse formation with spectral isolation for independent bright-soliton pumping. Wavelength-addressed access to both states is achieved in a LiTaO$_3$ microring through two TE-like transverse mode families. The higher-order TE$_{10}$ family fulfills two distinct roles in different spectral regions. Within localized avoided-mode-crossing regions, mode-resolved spectroscopy implicates TE$_{10}$ in perturbing the normal-GVD TE$_{00}$ resonance sequence. Away from these regions, TE$_{10}$ retains anomalous GVD and remains spectrally isolated as an independently pumpable bright-soliton channel; at representative pump resonances, the closest resonance of the non-addressed family is separated by 75--192 loaded cavity linewidths. With the input polarization held fixed, pumping TE$_{00}$ and TE$_{10}$ resonances generates dark-pulse and bright-soliton microcombs, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first experimental realization of a dark-pulse microcomb in an integrated LiTaO$_3$ microring. These results establish transverse-mode-family engineering as a route to combining localized modal interaction with independent spectral addressing in a single microresonator.

authors.name: Huizong Zhu, Yuyao Guo, Xiangfei Cheng, Yiqun Wu, Juanjuan Lu

papers.title: Proceedings of "Machine learning for trigger, reconstruction and generation" LHCP26, 20/05/2026
papers.summary: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly embedded in every stage of the LHC data-processing chain, from event generation to final reconstruction. This contribution reviews the latest ML developments from the ALICE, ATLAS, CMS and LHCb collaborations that were made public in the year preceding LHCP2026, following the workflow of the experiments: event generation and detector simulation, real-time trigger selection, and online/offline reconstruction. Highlights include generative models that accelerate the simulation of specific ALICE detector components by up to six orders of magnitude, the CMS AXOL1TL and ATLAS GELATO unsupervised anomaly- detection triggers now operating in Run 3, a quantised Deep Sets jet tagger for the CMS Phase-2 Level-1 trigger, ML-based jet energy correction and flavour tagging at LHCb, the first empirical scaling laws for transformer-based flavour taggers in ATLAS, and several transformer and graph- based reconstruction algorithms (ATLAS GN3 flavour tagging and MaskFormer tracking, LHCb GarNet, CMS MLPF) developed for HL-LHC operation.

authors.name: Marco Giacalone for the ALICE Collaboration

papers.title: R{\o}mer all ears: An auditory analog of Ole R{\o}mer's demonstration of the finite speed of light using smartphones as an acoustic vernier
papers.summary: We present an undergraduate experiment for teaching Ole Roemer's 1676 method for demonstrating the finite speed of light. Two smartphones emit periodic sound pulses whose synchronization is evaluated directly by the observer's hearing, acting as an "acoustic vernier" that achieves millisecond travel-time resolution without microphones or external sensors. Because the measurement relies strictly on propagation delays between stationary stations, it establishes a direct experimental analogy to Roemer's original argument and dispenses with auxiliary wave phenomena absent from the 1676 analysis, such as acoustic beats or the Doppler effect. The pedagogical strength of the experiment lies precisely in this direct appeal to the senses. Loss of synchronization becomes perceptible starting at a separation of approximately 5 m and grows progressively clearer across several tens of meters. Despite its simplicity, systematic blind measurements determine the speed of sound in air with single-run uncertainties of 2 to 5 m/s (around 1%) and agree within 1.1% with theoretical predictions across ambient temperatures from 9 to 25 $^\circ$C. Beyond numerical measurement, anchoring the method in explicit sensory perception helps to clarify the recurring conceptual entanglement between Roemer's geometric delay and the kinematic Doppler effect, while highlighting how this same travel-time principle underpins contemporary astrophysical techniques, such as pulsar timing and eclipse timing variations (ETV).

authors.name: La\'is Florencio de Oliveira, Gabriel Antonio Carit\'a, Jo\~ao Teles de Carvalho-Neto

papers.title: Interaction-Free Polarimetry
papers.summary: The combination of interaction-free measurement and the quantum Zeno effect has been shown to both increase the signal-to-noise ratio of imaging, and reduce the energy absorbed by the imaged object. So far, however, it has not been used for quantitative polarimetry, the reconstruction of a sample's Mueller matrix. In this paper, we extend this to the polarimetry of diattenuating samples. For polarisation components that the sample strongly absorbs, the protocol identifies the sample with far less absorbed energy than a single-pass measurement, a benefit for delicate samples probed with high-frequency radiation. For weakly absorbing components the repeated passes through the sample absorb more, so the benefit is confined to strongly diattenuating features. A Fisher-information analysis shows that, for a sample with a lossless transmitting axis, the protocol locates the absorbing axis with far fewer absorbed photons than single-pass polarimetry, while it measures partial transmittances no more efficiently per absorbed photon, and that the same sorting of lossy components to one output port responds to retardance and depolarisation.

authors.name: Shushmi Chowdhury, John Rarity, Jonte R. Hance

papers.title: Time Travel Paradoxes and Entangled Timelines
papers.summary: For time travel to be consistent with the known laws of physics, the resulting paradoxes must be resolved. It has been suggested that the notion of parallel timelines may provide a resolution, by allowing different events to happen in different timelines. However, so far, a concrete mechanism by which parallel timelines can be created has never been satisfactorily formulated in a way that makes the relationships between the timelines clear. In this paper, we propose such a mechanism based on the Everett (many-worlds) interpretation of quantum mechanics. The timelines in our model are variants of the "worlds" of the Everett interpretation that can connect to each other via the time machine. They are created by the entanglement of the time machine with the environment and the resulting decoherence; therefore, we call them "entangled timelines" or E-CTCs. As the entanglement gradually spreads out to additional systems, the timelines spread out as well, providing a local and well-defined mechanism for branching timelines. The E-CTC model is similar to Deutsch's familiar D-CTC model but differs from it mainly by imposing a different consistency condition, based on pure states, which allows the information about the entanglement to be preserved. These differences allow us to create a clearer practical definition of the timelines and avoid some of the surprising consequences of the D-CTC model's non-linear evolution.

authors.name: Barak Shoshany, Zipora Stober

papers.title: Functional classification of metabolic networks
papers.summary: Chemical reaction networks underpin biological and physical phenomena across scales, from microbial interactions to planetary atmosphere dynamics. Bacterial communities exhibit complex competitive interactions for resources, human organs and tissues demonstrate specialized biochemical functions, and planetary atmospheres can display diverse organic and inorganic chemical processes. Despite their complexity, comparing these networks remains a challenge due to the vast degrees of freedom shaped, respectively, by evolution, cell differentiation, and planetary formation. In biological systems, comparative genomics has been pivotal in tracing evolutionary trajectories and classifying organisms via DNA sequences. However, purely genomic classifications often fail to capture functional roles within ecological systems. Metabolic changes driven by nutrient availability highlight the need for classification schemes that integrate metabolic information. Here we introduce a computational framework for comparing chemical reaction networks by measuring distances between the nullspaces of their stoichiometric matrices, corresponding to the spaces of unconstrained steady-state fluxes and conservation laws. Applying this framework to human gut microbiome data shows that nullspace geometry captures organization that is not reducible to phylogenetic relatedness or network-overlap. External phenotype prediction shows that stoichiometric nullspace geometry provides phenotype-specific information complementary to competing descriptors, with phenotype-specific advantages that persist when complete genera are withheld. The generalizability of metabolic Grassmann distances is illustrated by application to chemical reaction networks in human tissue and planetary atmospheres, highlighting its potential for developing functional comparisons from geometric descriptors across diverse chemical reaction systems.

authors.name: Jorge Reyes, J\"orn Dunkel

papers.title: Fate of an impurity strongly interacting with a thermal Bose gas
papers.summary: We spectroscopically study mobile impurities immersed in a homogeneous bosonic bath (a box-trapped Bose gas), varying the bath temperature and the strength of impurity-bath interactions. We compare our results to those for a quasipure Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC), and find that for strong impurity-bath interactions, the spectra narrow with increasing temperature, while the impurity energy shift is suppressed. Near the critical temperature for condensation, many-body effects still play an important role, and only for a nondegenerate bath, the system approaches the classical Boltzmann-gas behavior. The key spectral features are reproduced within the theory of an ideal Bose polaron.

authors.name: Ji\v{r}\'i Etrych, Sebastian J. Morris, Simon M. Fischer, Gevorg Martirosyan, Christopher J. Ho, Moritz Drescher, Manfred Salmhofer, Zoran Hadzibabic, Tilman Enss, Christoph Eigen

papers.title: Quantum theory of electrically levitated nanoparticle-ion systems: Motional dynamics and sympathetic cooling
papers.summary: We develop the theory describing the quantum coupled dynamics of the center-of-mass motion of a nanoparticle and an ensemble of ions co-trapped in a dual-frequency linear Paul trap. We first derive analytical expressions for the motional frequencies and classical trajectories of both nanoparticle and ions. We then derive a quantum master equation for the ion-nanoparticle system and quantify the sympathetic cooling of the nanoparticle motion enabled by its Coulomb coupling to a continuously Doppler-cooled ion. We predict that motional cooling down to sub-kelvin temperatures is achievable in state-of-the-art experiments even in the absence of motional feedback and in the presence of micromotion. We then extend our analysis to an ensemble of $N$ ions, predicting a linear increase of the cooling rate as a function of N and motional cooling of the nanoparticle down to tenths of millikelvin in current experimental platforms. Our work establishes the theoretical toolbox needed to explore the ion-assisted preparation of non-Gaussian motional states of levitated nanoparticles.

authors.name: Saurabh Gupta, Bernard Faulend, Dmitry S. Bykov, Tracy E. Northup, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero

papers.title: Multiscale Numerical Modelling of Ultrafast Laser-Matter Interactions: Maxwell Two Temperature Model Molecular Dynamics (M-TTM-MD)
papers.summary: In this work, we present a comprehensive numerical framework that couples numerical solutions of Maxwell's equations using the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) approach, Molecular Dynamics (MD), and the Two-Temperature Model (TTM) to describe ultrafast laser-matter interactions in metallic systems at the atomic scale. The proposed Maxwell-Two-Temperature Model-Molecular Dynamics (M-TTM-MD) bridges the gap between electromagnetic field propagation, electron-phonon energy exchange, and atomic motion, allowing for a self-consistent treatment of energy absorption, transport, and structural response within a unified simulation environment. The calculated electromagnetic fields incorporate dispersive dielectric properties derived using the Auxiliary Differential Equation (ADE) technique, while the electronic and lattice subsystems are dynamically coupled through spatially and temporally resolved energy exchange terms. The changes in the material topography are then reflected in the updated grid for the FDTD scheme. The developed M-TTM-MD model provides a self-consistent numerical framework that offers insights into laser-induced phenomena in metals, including energy transport and surface dynamics under extreme nonequilibrium conditions.

authors.name: Othmane Benhayoun, Martin E. Garcia

papers.title: A van der Waals photon-ratchet for enhancing spin defect emission and quantum sensing
papers.summary: Spin defects in two-dimensional materials are promising platforms for quantum information technologies and nanoscale sensing. The negatively charged boron vacancy (VB-) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is particularly attractive due to its sensitivity to temperature, magnetic fields, and pressure, but its application is limited by intrinsically weak photoluminescence (PL). Here we demonstrate a van der Waals heterostructure that enhances the PL intensity of VB- by up to 45x at 4 Kelvin while preserving compatibility with ultrathin optoelectronic platforms. A type-I band alignment at the PbI2-hBN interface facilitates efficient interlayer coupling to the defect, and strong spectral overlap supports fluorescence resonance energy transfer. Ab initio calculations indicate that this coupling enables a photon-ratcheting mechanism, in which optical absorption in PbI2 generates a nonlinear polarization that drives VB- excitation. This process is consistent with interlayer energy transfer while maintaining minimal electronic and spin hybridization and preserving optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) contrast. The heterostructure further exhibits improved sensitivity to external magnetic fields. These results establish a route for the enhancement of defect emission via interlayer optical coupling and introduce a general materials strategy for amplifying weak quantum defect signals in nanomaterials.

authors.name: Eveline Mayner, Yaroslav Zhumagulov, Cristian de Giorgio, Feihong Chu, Prabhu Swain, Georg Fantner, Andras Kis, Oleg Yazyev, Aleksandra Radenovic

papers.title: Engineered Simultaneity: The Physical Impossibility of Consolidated Price Discovery Across Spacelike-Separated Exchanges
papers.summary: We define engineered simultaneity: the construction of a system that requires temporal comparison of events at spacelike-separated locations, implements this comparison via an implicit simultaneity convention, and represents the result as an objective measurement rather than a conventional choice. We show that the National Best Bid and Offer (NBBO) -- the cornerstone of U.S. equity markets -- is an instance of engineered simultaneity. The NBBO requires determining "current" prices across exchanges whose spatial separation places their price events outside each other's light cones. Special relativity proves that the temporal ordering of such events is frame-dependent: there exist inertial reference frames in which the NBBO differs from the value reported by the Securities Information Processor. The impossibility is not approximate; it is exact and unavoidable within the causal structure of Minkowski spacetime, and general relativity and indefinite causal order only compound it. We formalize the argument using the causal precedence relation and connect it to Lamport's theorem on distributed ordering. The operational form of the result needs no moving observers: the NBBO depends on where it is computed, and every participant who is not at the consolidation point holds a different one. The same construction recurs inside a single exchange, where orders are stamped at a perimeter and sorted by the stamp. Read as a practitioner suggests, as a bound on the worst-case error of distributed price discovery, the NBBO is defensible, and we propose that it be published as one. We separate what a central market is for (aggregating supply and demand) from what the latency race is about (sequencing arrivals), note that races of this kind cost about $5 billion a year in global equities, and record that in June 2026 the SEC proposed to rescind the order protection rule that makes the NBBO binding.

authors.name: Paul Borrill

papers.title: An Implicit Compact-Kernel Material Point Method for Computational Solid Mechanics
papers.summary: The numerical performance of the material point method (MPM) is strongly governed by the particle-grid kernel, which controls the trade-off among smoothness, locality, numerical diffusion, contact accuracy, and computational cost. Although wide-support smooth kernels can effectively suppress cell-crossing instability, they often introduce increased numerical diffusion, artificial contact gaps, and higher transfer cost. In contrast, the suitability of compact-kernel designs for implicit computational solid mechanics remains unclear. In this work, we develop an implicit formulation of the Compact-Kernel Material Point Method (CK-MPM) building on the framework of Liu et al. [2025], and assess its performance through benchmark problems in linear and nonlinear solid mechanics. Numerical assessment comprises cantilever bending, Hertzian contact, narrow-clearance free fall, and colliding hyperelastic rings, supplemented by a transfer-only diffusion test and spatial and temporal refinement studies. Implicit CK-MPM mitigates the cell-crossing stress noise and numerical energy loss observed in linear MPM, while retaining bending and energy responses comparable to those of quadratic B-spline MPM. Meanwhile, its more localized transfers improve contact-pressure accuracy and reduce the artificial contact gaps and early-contact artifacts associated with the wider-support quadratic kernel. These results demonstrate that the developed implicit formulation retains CK-MPM's favorable balance between smoothness and transfer locality in static and dynamic solid-mechanics analysis.

authors.name: Qirui Fu, Yupeng Jiang, Minchen Li

papers.title: Machine-Learning-Enhanced Mapping of Activity and Selectivity in CO$_2$ Hydrogenation across Metal-Alloy Surfaces
papers.summary: Adsorption energy distributions (AEDs) have emerged as a powerful and increasingly adopted descriptor for catalytic performance in high-entropy alloys and, more recently, in conventional metallic alloy nanocrystal catalysts. By accounting for diverse adsorption sites and crystallographic facets, AEDs more fully represent nanoparticle-based catalytic surfaces and show strong promise for accelerating rational design and discovery of heterogeneous catalysts, especially for CO$_2$ hydrogenation. However, previous high-throughput screenings have not provided simultaneous facet-level insight into catalytic activity, product selectivity, and thermodynamic stability. Here, we implement and extend the AED framework to individual crystallographic facets, combining facet-resolved adsorption fingerprints with Wulff-derived facet abundances and an interpretable latent-space analysis of C1-product selectivity. We employ universal machine-learned force fields trained on Open Catalyst data to compute adsorption energies across 226 experimentally observed metals, binary alloys, and previously unexplored ternary alloys, encompassing $\approx$1.4 million adsorption configurations on $>$2,600 crystallographically distinct surfaces. Using distribution-based similarity analysis and principal component analysis of AED moments, we identify composition-facet combinations with adsorption landscapes associated with activity and qualitative selectivity trends toward C1 products such as methanol and methane. Our framework links surface structure to adsorption-based catalytic trends, providing experimentally testable composition-facet candidates for further investigation and validation.

authors.name: Prajwal Pisal, Ond\v{r}ej Krej\v{c}\'i, Patrick Rinke

papers.title: Variational approach to droplet motion on uneven solid surfaces, including contact line dynamics and evaporation
papers.summary: We show how dynamical equations for liquid films and drops on uneven surfaces, including contact line dynamics and evaporation/condensation effects, may be formulated as a variational dynamics, generated via Onsager's variational principle. The theory applies in the isothermal overdamped-dynamics limit. We apply this general approach to obtain several well-known results on contact line dynamics and to study drops pinning and sliding on inclined corrugated surfaces. This approach constructs the dynamical equations starting from the free energy of the system and therefore has the advantage that it naturally incorporates the correct equilibrium properties.

authors.name: Gyula I T\'oth, David N Sibley, Agnes J Bok\'anyi-T\'oth, Dmitri Tseluiko, Andrew J Archer

papers.title: PEPSKit.jl: A Julia package for projected entangled-pair state simulations
papers.summary: We present PEPSKit$.$jl, a Julia package for simulating two-dimensional quantum many-body systems with infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPS). PEPSKit$.$jl builds on the TensorKit$.$jl package for tensor computations and provides high-level algorithms for iPEPS simulations that support both Abelian and non-Abelian symmetries, as well as fermionic systems. This work gives an overview of the main package features, which include support for ground-state, time-evolution, and finite-temperature simulations in systems with different physical symmetries and lattice geometries. These capabilities are illustrated through various examples and technical benchmarks.

authors.name: Paul Brehmer, Lander Burgelman, Zheng-Yuan Yue, Gleb Fedorovich, Jutho Haegeman, Lukas Devos

papers.title: Matter-wave Interferometers as Open-system Dark Matter Detectors
papers.summary: Matter-wave interferometers (MWIs) offer a uniquely quantum route to dark matter (DM) detection: DM can reveal itself through phase and decoherence between spatially separated wavepackets, even when energy deposition is negligible and no resolvable recoil displacement occurs. We formulate these effects in an open effective field theory for MWIs using the Schwinger--Keldysh formalism, which highlights a structural asymmetry between the two detection channels. For elastic spin-independent DM scattering, decoherence inherits novel Bose enhancement or Pauli blocking factors, while the phase is at most linear in the DM occupation number. By retaining the DM's coherence time, this framework spans Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics across a wide range of DM masses, and systematically organizes corrections beyond the heavy-probe limit.

authors.name: Leonardo Badurina, Kathryn M. Zurek

papers.title: Volatility Forecasts with Market Trends
papers.summary: We show how volatility forecasts for financial markets can be refined by accounting for the current trends in these markets. Empirically, volatilities tend to increase day after day in times of strong up- or down-trends. This effect is particularly pronounced during down-trends. We find that it can accurately be modeled by including quadratic polynomials of the current trend strength as explanatory factors. Such factors can improve the predictive power of a wide range of volatility models, ranging from linear EWMA-based models over GARCH models and range-based models to stochastic volatility models. Our results are based on a robust statistical analysis of three decades of daily futures prices across equity-, bond-, FX- and commodity markets.

authors.name: Sara A. Safari, Christoph Schmidhuber

papers.title: Chirality of a $\mathbb{Z}_q$ Model as Orientation-Odd Phase Shifts in Oscillator Networks
papers.summary: Chiral interaction between discrete $\mathbb{Z}_q$ variables, which distinguishes clockwise from counterclockwise steps, arises in settings ranging from statistical physics to combinatorial optimization. When such an interaction is realized by continuous phases, however, its kernel fixes the phase coupling only at the $q$ grid points, so which part of the coupling carries the discrete chirality is not determined. We show that for any realization that matches the discrete values and treats a kernel and its mirror image alike, the kernel is chiral if and only if the coupling has a nonzero odd part, and that neither property of the realization can be dropped. Among the realizations that reproduce all discrete energies and equilibria, the one with the fewest harmonics is unique and satisfies the second property automatically, so that its sine components measure the discrete chirality exactly; a faithful realization with an even coupling, as in existing oscillator Ising and Potts machines, represents only nonchiral kernels. In the induced dynamics this odd part is an orientation-odd phase shift, which changes sign with the orientation of the coupling, in contrast to the Sakaguchi phase lag. In oscillator networks it is realized by direction-dependent delays, and mixed-level circuit simulations show that exchanging the delays reverses the chirality of the locked states.

authors.name: Yi Cheng, Zongli Lin

papers.title: Emergent odd response in active chiral films
papers.summary: Active chiral fluids can support an anomalous transport coefficient known as odd (or Hall) viscosity. Hydrodynamic descriptions of such fluids typically introduce odd viscosity phenomenologically. How such a response emerges from specific microscopic interactions remains incompletely understood. Here, building on classical shear rheology, we microscopically derive an odd rheological response in active chiral films: thin layers of torque-exerting, elongated particles anchored to a no-slip surface. A canonical realization of such a film is the bacterial carpet, in which flagellated bacteria are tethered head-down to a solid surface while their flagella remain free to spin and inject angular momentum into the surrounding fluid. Using a Smoluchowski kinetic theory for the orientational dynamics of these anchored particles, we derive their stress response to an imposed shear flow. We reveal that shear-induced reorientation leads to a flow-aligned polarization and a transverse surface traction from which the odd-viscosity tensor follows in closed form. This approach stands in contrast with existing microscopic theories, in which the axis of torque injection is insensitive to the flow rather than set by it. Numerical solutions of the kinetic theory further highlight saturation of the transverse traction at strong shear, driven by this orientation dynamics -- signaling departure from linear response. Our results demonstrate how odd viscosity can emerge self-consistently as a coarse-grained rheological signature of active fluid-structure interaction and establish active chiral films as a new controllable setting for odd hydrodynamics.

authors.name: Seema Chahal, D. Naveen Kumar, Brato Chakrabarti

papers.title: The role of weak interfaces in the tensile deformation and fracture of particle-filled polymers studied by phase-field model
papers.summary: Weak particle-matrix interfaces play a critical role in the tensile fracture of particle-filled polymer composites, but how they govern progressive debonding, fracture localization, and the resulting changes in macroscopic mechanical properties remains insufficiently understood. In this study, a cohesive-zone phase-field model incorporating a hyperelastic polymer matrix and a smeared interface is employed to investigate the coupled evolution of interfacial debonding and matrix fracture in particle-filled polymer composites. The model is calibrated against and compared with uniaxial tensile responses of particle-filled polyurethane composites and then used to study how interfacial strength, interfacial fracture energy, and matrix fracture properties affect the macroscopic stress-strain response and damage evolution. The results show that weak interfaces can induce an intermediate softening regime in the stress-strain response, characterized by a reduced effective tangent stiffness and associated with distributed interfacial damage. Interfacial strength mainly controls the initiation of debonding, whereas interfacial fracture energy affects whether debonding can develop progressively in a distributed manner or rapidly localizes into a dominant crack band. Comparisons with well-bonded reference systems further demonstrate that weak interfaces may reduce the maximum stress but increase the strain at break by promoting distributed debonding around particles and delaying the formation of a dominant crack band. These findings clarify the dual role of weak interfaces and provide a mechanistic understanding of interface-controlled tensile failure in particle-filled polymer composites.

authors.name: Xu Chen, Ya Duan, Xiaoying Zhuang, Timon Rabczuk

papers.title: The Role of Preceding CMEs and SIRs in Enhancing Shock Acceleration of Electrons
papers.summary: The role of large-scale pre-existing interplanetary structures, including preceding coronal mass ejections (CMEs) and stream interaction regions (SIRs), in shaping the shock acceleration environment for energetic electrons remains not fully understood. In this study, we investigate nine interplanetary shocks observed by the Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory (STEREO) that are associated with significant MeV electron enhancements, as such enhancements are rarely observed at interplanetary shocks. We combine remote-sensing observations, drag-based modeling, and in-situ measurements to analyze the shock propagation through pre-existing interplanetary structures. Eight of the nine events are associated with a preceding slow or intermediate-speed CME, while six shocks are in-situ observed propagating within preceding ICMEs, indicating that large-scale upstream trapping structures are a common feature of these events. Further analysis identifies three distinct scenarios associated with enhanced electron acceleration: shocks propagating through preceding ICMEs, shock-SIR interactions, and direct injection of flare-accelerated electrons into SIRs. As a representative shock-in-ICME event, the 2012 January 29 low-$\beta$, quasi-perpendicular shock ($\theta_{Bn}\sim87^\circ$) is further investigated using observations together with one-dimensional Monte Carlo test-particle simulations of a shock propagating into a large-scale upstream magnetic loop. The simulation suggests that the upstream loop prolongs electron residence near the shock and substantially enhances acceleration efficiency. These results demonstrate that large-scale interplanetary structures can precondition the upstream magnetic environment, providing favorable conditions for prolonged electron residence and efficient shock acceleration.

authors.name: Xiaomin Chen, Seve Nyberg, Rami Vainio, Immanuel Christopher Jebaraj, Chuan Li, Nina Dresing

papers.title: Multi-Threshold Sampling: Signal Space, Sampling Operators, and First Recorded Crossing Time
papers.summary: Multi-threshold sampling encodes signals through crossing times at prescribed thresholds, offering an alternative to uniform time-domain sampling. Its potential to reduce hardware requirements and power consumption motivates its use in high-speed pulse acquisition, including scintillation detector readout. We model the relation between signal statistics and recorded-crossing statistics by composing measurable stochastic crossing, timing, and selection operators. The threshold noise processes are independent across thresholds. The sampler applies independent timing jitter at each analog crossing before quantization and enforces dead time separately at each threshold in the recording window. We express the joint cumulative distribution function of first recorded crossing times using path infima and suprema when crossings at each threshold share the same timing jitter. Specializing this formula to a single threshold gives the marginal distribution, from which we obtain the conditional standard deviation. We use these formulas to approximate the corresponding exact quantities under independent timing jitter at each crossing and bound each approximation error. In a scintillation example, the shared-jitter formulas and independent-jitter waveform simulations agreed within Monte Carlo sampling uncertainty for the joint and marginal distributions and for the conditional standard deviation. Engineers can use these results to choose thresholds and assess how sampler changes affect timing precision.

authors.name: Ao Qiu, Qingguo Xie

papers.title: Mutual Linearity in Nonlinear Population Dynamics
papers.summary: Mutual linearity, the persistence of affine relations among stationary observables under arbitrarily strong changes of one transition rate, is known for Markov jump processes and chemical reaction networks. We show that generalized Lotka--Volterra dynamics form a new class of mutually linear systems, even though species can go extinct and attractors can be chaotic. Any change to one species' equation acts on the others as one effective press and keeps all abundances affinely related: piecewise across extinctions, and as time averages on chaotic attractors.

authors.name: Shiling Liang

papers.title: Time Interfaces Enable Free-Space Excitation of Frozen Electromagnetic Waves and Topological Edge States in Graphene
papers.summary: Time-varying two-dimensional materials, such as graphene under ultrafast photoexcitation, offer a promising platform for engineering temporal interfaces for electromagnetic waves. Rapidly promoting valence electrons to the conduction band generates a high-energy, non-thermal hot-electron population that subsequently thermalizes with the pre-existing thermal electron population. We study the excitation of plasmonic modes in graphene by the time interface created by ultrafast photoexcitation using a graphene electron-transport model self-consistently coupled to electromagnetic simulations. We find that, in addition to dynamic, propagating plasmonic modes, the time interfaces excite static, spatially varying electromagnetic modes in the interaction region, sustained by streaming transverse electrons. We also demonstrate a novel technique for coupling free-space light directly to highly localized topological edge states at the magnetic-inversion boundary on graphene, eliminating the need for near-field excitation techniques.

authors.name: Shivaksh Rawat, Samyobrata Mukherjee, Jeffery Allen, Monica Allen, Gennady Shvets

papers.title: Morphogenic necking of surfaces
papers.summary: Surface morphogenesis occurs across biological scales, from subcellular vesicles and cells to visceral organs, tissue organoids, and whole organisms. Since morphogenesis often involves changes in topology, a natural question is that of appropriate mathematical descriptions that provide an approach to topological transitions of thin surfaces. Here, we suggest a general intrinsic framework coupling morphogen organization to surface geometry. We propose a minimal geometric model in which smoothing competes with morphogen-induced deformation to regulate shape, while loss of this balance can bring a surface toward a topological transition via neck constriction. A simple dynamical model coupling a scalar field to the surface metric reveals two mechanisms: gradient-driven constriction at steep morphogen transitions and curvature-driven constriction near localized morphogen peaks. For frozen morphogen profiles in simple axisymmetric examples, the gradient-driven route gives exact algebraic contraction, while the curvature-driven route gives local exponential contraction.

authors.name: Farzan Vafa, Puskar Mondal, L. Mahadevan

papers.title: Lattice models of chiral random motion: A short review
papers.summary: Chirality, a systematic rotational bias, is ubiquitous in many random motion patterns, from bacteria cells, that swim in circles near surfaces and spinning colloids, to charged particles diffusing under the influence of magnetic fields. In two dimensions, chirality renders random transport \textit{odd}: the diffusion tensor acquires an antisymmetric part that leaves the mean-squared displacement invariant but modifies fluxes and boundary currents. Lattice models for random motion are a natural setting to study chirality, since they are exactly solvable, connect directly to heterogeneous media, cellular automata, and programmable robots, and in discrete time admit fully chiral limits with a localised bulk and edge transport. Lattice walks with a rotational bias have been introduced in different communities several times since 1960, yet without a common language or conceptual connection between them. Here we review these models from the perspective that on the lattice, chirality requires memory. Taking the recently introduced chiral random walk model as a template, we describe the walker with an internal degree of freedom. With a chiral biased updating rule, the full diffusion tensor of this chiral walker turns odd. Within this picture, we can unite persistent and chiral walks, run-and-tumble motion, and cyclic random motions in one framework. We discuss how the memory is followed into the environment; in Lorentz lattice gases, kinetic and rotor walks, and random odd environments; and into the path; in spiral self-avoiding walks.

authors.name: E. Kalz, J. Wojcik, J. Uhlig, N. Sherf, Y. Roichman, R. Metzler

papers.title: Snap-Through Symmetry Breaking in Multicellular Aggregates
papers.summary: Symmetry breaking is a fundamental process in biological organization. Yet the physical mechanisms that control its onset in multicellular systems remain poorly understood. Motivated by gastruloids -- multicellular aggregates in which cells differentiate and spontaneously break symmetry -- we study a two-phase viscoelastic solid drop as a minimal model of tissue polarization. We show that elastocapillary competition fundamentally alters the classical engulfing transition of fluid drops. While symmetry breaking occurs continuously in the purely viscous limit, bulk elasticity instead leads to a discontinuous snap-like transition. We demonstrate that this behavior can be understood as a wetting transition governed by a spreading coefficient which depends on the drop size and phase volume fraction. Applying our model to gastruloids, we find a critical volume fraction for symmetry breaking, providing a self-organized mechanism for robust developmental timing. Our results identify a generic elastocapillary transition that enables spontaneous symmetry breaking in biphasic drops.

authors.name: Mart\'i Planasdemunt-Hospital, David Oriola

papers.title: Quantum critical collapse to an extremal black hole
papers.summary: It has been emphasized recently that some extremal black holes are "critical" solutions, lying at the threshold between gravitational collapse and dispersion. We study the effect of quantum gravity on critical solutions for the collapse of a thin shell of charged dust. We consider the Hamiltonian that generates the shell equation of motion with respect to the exterior Killing time and coincides with the ADM energy on-shell. Near criticality, this Hamiltonian is shown to be canonically equivalent to that of a Liouville theory with negative potential. After quantization, this model predicts that a collapsing shell has a non-trivial probability of undergoing a quantum mechanical bounce when its energy above extremality is comparable to the "breakdown scale". The bounce probability approaches unity at extremality. Hence this model predicts that the critical surface in the classical theory is thickened quantum mechanically into a "critical layer". The probability density function for the black hole energy is suppressed below the breakdown scale in the same way as found recently by Turiaci and Wu.

authors.name: Hugo Lange, Harvey S. Reall

papers.title: The black hole IR triangle for scalar QED
papers.summary: We construct the black hole infrared triangle of scalar QED on a stretched Schwarzschild horizon at tree level. In the covariant phase space of the near-horizon Maxwell field, the soft charge is a corner term. The memory is the zero mode of the gauge-invariant radiative field along the generators. It is conjugate to the boundary gauge mode that labels the degenerate horizon vacua, and Gauss' law fixes it by the flux of charge through the horizon. The Noether flux of the residual gauge transformation through the stretched horizon is not conserved by the scattering, because charged matter crosses the stretched horizon in both directions. The flux with its matter part removed is the soft charge, which generates the large gauge transformation. Its Ward identity is equivalent to a soft photon theorem in every radiative partial wave, which we derive from the near-horizon Feynman rules and, where these do not control the emission, from the field equations at leading order. The main difference from null infinity is that on a stretched horizon both radial branches of the field are independent boundary data. The hard charge is a radial flux. With both branches present it weights each leg by the direction of its radial motion, and the soft factor is a sign per leg. The endpoint data on the two branches give two boundary observables, the time-integrated transverse magnetic and electric fields. The field radiated by a scattering process contributes only to the first, where it cancels the change in the Coulomb memory of the charges, so that the soft charge is conserved. A charge that crosses the horizon enters both. We also discuss the infrared divergence, the dressing of the external states, and the fate of the memory in the Hartle--Hawking state, where it performs a random walk driven by the Hawking radiation.

authors.name: Fabiano Feleppa, Nava Gaddam, Nico Groenenboom

papers.title: The OPE of lines beyond CFT
papers.summary: We discuss the fusion of parallel line defects in theories defined by relevant deformations of a conformal fixed point. We propose an operator product expansion to describe this limit in terms of a Wilsonian effective action whose coefficients are computable in conformal perturbation theory around the UV. This allows one to fix, order by order, the fusion limit of correlation functions involving the defects, up to non-perturbative coefficients associated to correlation functions (condensates) on the fused defect. It thus generalizes the familiar OPE of local operators in QFT. As a non-perturbative test of our proposal, we consider the short-distance potential between two magnetic impurities in the $2d$ Ising model. We find excellent agreement between the OPE framework and DMRG extractions of the potential and condensates (the latter also computed exactly with integrability). In addition, we consider a number of solvable models to illustrate different features of the framework.

authors.name: Jan Albert, Matthew Forslund, Alexandre Homrich

papers.title: The String Theory Photinoverse
papers.summary: Type-IIB string compactifications typically give rise to a significant number of RR-photons. These are generically massless and do not possess any light charged states, making them `superhidden'. However, since supersymmetry is present at least at some high scale, corresponding `dark photinos' are also predicted. The kinetic mixing of the photons together with the SUSY breaking mass terms of the photinos makes the latter observable. We identify geometries in which the mixing is induced by Wilson lines and show that their expectation values are generically non-zero. As a result, most of the dark photinos, which are lighter than the visible sector SUSY breaking scale, mix significantly with the bino and hence couple to the Standard Model sufficiently strongly to leave potentially observable traces. In particular, volume modulus and inflaton decays generically induce a cosmological abundance of dark photinos that can explain dark matter. We find that the `natural Photinoverse dark matter parameter space' is already accessible to current experiments, notably gamma ray observations, which therefore have discovery potential in the near future.

authors.name: Andreas P. Braun, Thibaut Coudarchet, Arthur Hebecker, Joerg Jaeckel, Jonathan Steiner

papers.title: Gauge groups of type 0 orientifolds
papers.summary: We determine the global form of the gauge groups of the orthogonal and symplectic type 0 orientifolds, using the constraints from perturbative and brane states. In the process, we correct some misprints in type 0 vacuum amplitudes that have propagated in the literature. For type 0A, our analysis reveals a parity condition on the numbers of D9-branes in the orthogonal orientifold and a puzzle concerning the decay of a tachyonic D0-brane in the symplectic orientifold.

authors.name: Vittorio Larotonda, Salvatore Raucci

papers.title: Unitarization from Spin Geometry
papers.summary: We derive the dimensional reduction of 10D super Yang-Mills theory on a general closed 6D spin manifold using spectral decompositions for the higher-dimensional gauge field and gaugino, keeping the infinite towers of Kaluza-Klein (KK) modes in the lower-dimensional theory. We then calculate tree-level $2 \rightarrow 2$ scattering amplitudes with external massive spinors and vectors in this lower-dimensional theory. By studying the high-energy behavior of these amplitudes and imposing perturbative unitarity, we derive several sum rules that involve the eigenvalues of Laplace and Dirac operators on the internal 6-manifold, together with products of cubic coupling constants of the KK modes. These give concrete realizations of the known unitarity sum rules for spontaneously broken gauge theories. We illustrate explicitly how the simplest sum rule is satisfied for flat tori and round spheres.

authors.name: Francesco Bertucci, James Bonifacio, Andrew Schrader

papers.title: Neural Network Field Theory and the AdS/CFT Correspondence
papers.summary: We develop a neural realization of massive scalar field theory on Euclidean anti--de Sitter space and its holographic boundary observables within neural network field theory (NN--FT). We construct Fourier--Bessel cosine neurons whose covariance reproduces the regulated massive AdS propagator exactly at finite network width, with the Gaussian field theory recovered in the infinite-width limit. We introduce quartic interactions through two complementary approaches. The first implements a prescribed interaction by deforming the neural parameter measure, while the second generates a local quartic interaction from the statistics of auxiliary binary neurons. Applying the BDHM prescription directly to the neural ensemble, we recover the scalar bulk-to-boundary propagator, the conformal boundary two-point function, and the leading connected four-point contact Witten diagram. We further show that distinct neural architectures can reproduce the same leading boundary correlators while defining inequivalent bulk theories. These results establish a framework for studying interacting scalar holography within NN--FT and clarify the role of neural architecture in encoding bulk dynamics and boundary observables.

authors.name: Dmitry S. Ageev, Yulia A. Ageeva, Anna S. Bernakevich

papers.title: Energy plateau cascades from complex-time local quenches in thermal two-dimensional CFTs
papers.summary: In this work, we study local operator quenches in thermal two-dimensional conformal field theories with complex-time evolution, which can be viewed as an effective description of conditional dynamics in a system interacting with an environment. In contrast to quenches of the vacuum, the thermal initial state allows several conformal families to participate in the evolution. We show that their competition can produce cascades of approximately homogeneous energy plateaux, with successive plateaux approaching the energies of different primary states. Using conformal Ward identities on the cylinder and torus, we determine the local energy density and illustrate this behavior in free-field theories, the Ising model and Wess--Zumino--Witten models. We develop a cold-limit spectral description in which the dominant primary channel determines the height of each plateau, while conformal dimensions and operator matrix elements govern the transitions between them. For a fixed compact unitary CFT, we show that only finitely many primary channels can contribute to the leading plateau sequence. Finally, we discuss the large-central-charge regime, relating light-operator plateaux to few-particle sectors in thermal AdS and examining the limitations of this picture for heavy quenches.

authors.name: Dmitry S. Ageev, Vladimir A. Bykov

papers.title: Bounds on Love Numbers and Quasinormal Modes from the Surface Impedance
papers.summary: The surface impedance of a body is fixed by its interior alone and encodes its entire tidal response. We derive bounds on Love numbers and quasinormal modes from constraints on the impedance that follow from either of two properties of a stable body: it is lossless, meaning that it dissipates no energy, or it is passive, meaning that it never gives back more energy than it has received. For a lossless body, every dynamical Love number is bounded from above and below, exactly in general relativity, in any renormalization scheme and at any scale. Earlier bounds are exact for Newtonian stars but fail for compact stars, because they take the response to arbitrarily fast tides to be zero or non-negative, whereas in general relativity it is negative. The quasinormal modes of a lossless body are also excluded from a region of the complex frequency plane set by the mass and radius. Each known Love number enlarges the excluded region. Conversely, the quasinormal modes bound each Love number from below, given the lower ones. For a passive body of horizon scale, such as a black hole, the static Love number lies in a window that closes onto the vanishing black-hole value as the body's surface approaches the horizon.

authors.name: Daniel McLoughlin, Mikhail P. Solon

papers.title: Chaotic singularities inside vacuum black holes
papers.summary: According to the conjecture of Belinski, Khalatnikov and Lifshitz, general relativity gives rise to chaotic dynamics in the vicinity of generic spacelike singularities. However, no vacuum black hole has been shown to exhibit this behaviour. Here we construct stationary, asymptotically locally AdS$_5$ black holes with regular, triaxially squashed horizons and causal exteriors, whose homogeneous interiors realize the cosmological billiard of generic five-dimensional vacuum gravity. We identify a simple algebraic condition on the horizon data that is necessary for the interior billiard to be chaotic, and show that solutions with regular horizons locally access an open set of billiard trajectories.

authors.name: Robie A. Hennigar, Ayan K. Patra

papers.title: RMT${}_2$: Random Spectral Correlations for CFT${}_2$ and AdS${}_3$ Gravity
papers.summary: We present the full framework of RMT${}_2$, a consistent unification of random matrix theory and modular invariance. The systematic prescription, which augments the existing construction by incorporating spin, lifts random matrix correlators to $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ Poincar\'e sums of their Mellin transforms, in a manner which enforces random matrix correlations near extremality in every spinning primary sector. The resulting RMT${}_2$ correlators are further expressible in terms of an orthogonal basis of Eisenstein series and Maass cusp forms. We demonstrate the construction by lifting the two-point correlators at arbitrary genus of the Airy model, in both unitary and orthogonal symmetry classes, exhibiting the modular-invariant topological expansion of RMT${}_2$; a resummation of the genus expansion shows that the modular-invariant spectral form factor preserves the ramp-plateau structure. Holographically, RMT${}_2$ provides a concrete benchmark and explicit candidate expressions for comparison with off-shell wormhole amplitudes in AdS${}_3$ gravity, with any number of torus boundaries.
