authors.name: Feng-Li Lin, Sayid Mondal

papers.title: Tensionless M5-brane in light-cone gauge. The spinor moving frame method is wanted
papers.summary: We perform the complete light--cone gauge fixing for the tensionless limit of the M-theory 5-brane the action for which was recently obtained in [1]. The problem of gauge fixing of local fermionic $\kappa$--symmetry becomes quite nontrivial because the projector of that is constructed from the gauge field strength which is required to be nonvanishing and nontrivial in this limit for its consistency. To resolve this problem the spinor moving frame method has been adapted. The corresponding moving frame is constructed on a vector quadratic in the gauge field strength, which is required to be nonvanishing and nondegenerate in the tensionless limit, and the derivative of the PST (Pasti-Sorokin-Tonin) scalar. The symmetries of the gauge fixed action and equations of motion are briefly discussed. To make a comparison with the case of usual tensionless p-branes (null-p-branes), those which do not carry worldvolume gauge fields, we also elaborate their spinor moving frame formulation.

authors.name: Igor Bandos

papers.title: Anomalies and the Berry Phase: From $\pi^0\to\gamma\gamma$ to the geometry of the fermion vacuum
papers.summary: We review the chiral anomaly from a historical perspective, from the $\pi^0\to\gamma\gamma$ puzzle and the work of Adler, Bell and Jackiw, to the Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) term. We then describe how the WZW term was motivated from quantum chromodynamics in 1983-85. Integrating out the non-Abelian gauge fields, that have a gapped spectrum, gives a Nambu-Jona-Lasinio type theory of quarks, and integrating out the quarks, which are gapped by chiral symmetry breaking, gives the WZW model. The fermion determinant splits into a regulator-dependent modulus, which gives the dynamics of mesons, and a universal phase, which is fixed by the anomaly and is the WZW term. Restricted to the collective coordinates of the baryon soliton, the WZW term imposes a U(1) constraint that makes the baryon wave functions monopole harmonics and fixes their spin, statistics and flavour multiplets. We then explain that this phase is a Berry phase: the Schwinger terms of current algebra are the curvature of a U(1) connection on the space of chiral field configurations, and the WZW term is its holonomy, which we call a Berry-Wilson loop. In 1+1 dimensions we write the connection explicitly in terms of Euler angles, exhibiting a Dirac monopole whose quantised charge is the level of the current algebra.

authors.name: Spenta R. Wadia

papers.title: Tripartite entanglement dynamics following a quantum quench
papers.summary: We investigate the dynamics of multipartite entanglement after quenches from initial states which generate multiplets of quasiparticle excitations beyond the usual pair structure. We focus on the dynamics of tripartite entanglement through the lens of the Markov gap -- a computable quantity that signals irreducible tripartite entanglement when positive. In the tight-binding chain, we show that the Markov gap is positive at intermediate times, implying the presence of tripartite entanglement. After a time delay, the Markov gap increases and then decays at longer times, thus exhibiting an entanglement barrier. We argue that those qualitative features are consistent with an interpretation of the spreading of tripartite entanglement by triplets of tripartite-entangled quasiparticles.

authors.name: Cl\'ement Berthiere

papers.title: Hadrons in group expansion
papers.summary: We develop a general framework for describing symmetry-breaking responses in physical systems with approximate symmetries. Hadronic systems provide a particularly rich setting for investigating such symmetries. For example, the flavor $SU(4)$ symmetry involving the $u$, $d$, $s$, and $c$ quarks is severely broken, the flavor $SU(3)$ symmetry involving the $u$, $d$, and $s$ quarks is moderately broken, and the isospin $SU(2)$ symmetry involving the $u$ and $d$ quarks is only slightly broken. An important question is how a physical system responds to further symmetry breaking when its symmetry has already been partially broken. Motivated by the observed mass nonadditivity of vector mesons, we formulate this framework in terms of the group expansion, in which higher-order responses may modify the coefficients within the inherited response space or unlock additional independent response directions outside this space. We refer to these two effects as coefficient evolution and response unlocking, respectively, and develop a differential description connecting the interaction flow, mass flow, and state flow. We apply this framework to $J^P=1^-$ vector mesons and $J^P=3/2^+$ and $1/2^+$ baryons within flavor $SU(4)$ and $SU(5)$ reference spaces. These analyses illustrate how the internal structure and dynamics of a physical system, together with additional symmetries, can shape and constrain its symmetry-breaking responses. The group expansion thus provides a unified framework for organizing the evolution, correlations, and constraints of symmetry-breaking responses, with potential applications beyond hadronic systems.

authors.name: Hua-Xing Chen

papers.title: Smooth binary evolution from wide resonances in boson clouds
papers.summary: Ultralight scalars can form superradiant clouds around rotating black holes. These may alter the dynamics of compact binaries and the ensuing waveform through orbital resonances and cloud ionization. We re-examine resonances involving states with nonzero decay width, deriving an effective treatment for resonances that are wider than the binary's frequency chirp. We demonstrate the utility of this approach by calculating an upper bound for the cloud's mass surviving up to the latest stages of the inspiral. Next, we study the accumulation of resonances with high-energy bound states. When these infinitely many, increasingly weak resonances are properly taken into account, they smooth out the "sharp features" in the binary's evolution that had been attributed to the ionization of the cloud. We compare our Newtonian results with recent relativistic calculations, highlighting common features as well as discrepancies. Our conclusions emphasize the need to carefully incorporate resonances in boson cloud waveform modeling.

authors.name: Giovanni Maria Tomaselli

papers.title: The Classification of 3+1d Symmetry Enriched Topological Order
papers.summary: We use a 2-categorical version of (de-)equivariantization to classify (3+1)d topological orders with a finite $G$-symmetry. In particular, we argue that (3+1)d fermionic topological order with $G$-symmetry correspond to $\mathbf{2SVect}$-enriched $G$-crossed braided fusion 2-categories. We then show that the categorical data necessary to define these theories agrees with that arising from a fermionic generalization of the Wang-Wen-Witten construction of bosonic topological theories with $G$-symmetry saturating an anomaly. More generally, we also explain how 2-categorical (de-) equivariantization yields a classification of all braided fusion 2-categories.

authors.name: Thibault D. D\'ecoppet, Matthew Yu

papers.title: Deformations of Locally Conformal Parallel Spin(7) Instantons
papers.summary: We study the infinitesimal deformation theory of $Spin(7)$-instantons on compact locally conformal parallel (LCP) $Spin(7)$ manifolds, that is, $Spin(7)$ manifolds whose fundamental 4-form satisfies $d\Phi=\theta\wedge\Phi$ with a closed, non-exact Lee form $\theta$. We show that the gauge-fixed linearized instanton equations are equivalent to a kernel problem for a twisted Levi-Civita Dirac operator $\mathcal{D}^-_A-\mathcal{A}_\theta\colon\Gamma(\mathcal{S}^-\otimes\mathfrak{g}_P)\to\Gamma(\mathcal{S}^+\otimes\mathfrak{g}_P)$, compute the zeroth-order term $\mathcal{A}_\theta$ explicitly, and show that its pointwise squared operator norm equals $\frac{49}{64}|\theta|^2$. Combined with the Lichnerowicz--Weitzenb\"ock formula and Ivanov's scalar curvature identity, this yields a sufficient condition for rigidity, which we show can never be satisfied by flat connections. Indeed, the trivial connection is never rigid: its deformation space contains $H^1(M;\mathbb{R})\otimes\mathfrak{g}$. Our main result concerns the product LCP manifolds $N\times S^1$, where $N$ is a compact nearly parallel $G_2$ manifold: for the pull-back of a $G_2$-instanton $B$ on $N$ we prove $\mathcal{H}^1_{Spin(7)}(\mathrm{pr}^*B)\cong\mathcal{H}^0_{G_2}(B)\oplus\mathcal{H}^1_{G_2}(B)$. This reduces the deformation theory of such instantons to the nearly parallel $G_2$ case, shows that this containment is an equality for the trivial connection, and produces non-flat examples on the Hopf manifold $S^7\times S^1$ and on other products with homogeneous nearly parallel $G_2$ manifolds.

authors.name: Ey\"up Yal\c{c}{\i}nkaya

papers.title: Hawking-Page phase transitions of black holes in the Hamiltonian formalism
papers.summary: We employ the Hamiltonian formalism proposed by P. M. Dirac to investigate the Hawking-Page phase transition of the non-rotating Ba\~{n}ados-Teitelboim-Zanelli (BTZ), Reissner-Nordstr\"{o}m (RN) and Kerr-Newman (KN) black holes in both on-shell and off-shell configurations. For the BTZ black hole, the on-shell Hamiltonian agrees with the corresponding Helmholtz free energy obtained from the Euclidean action, reproducing the established Hawking-Page phase structure, while the off-shell analysis is consistent with the corresponding continuous phase transition obtained from the Euclidean approach. The same agreement is found for the on-shell RN and KN black holes. We further investigate the previously unexplored off-shell configurations of the RN and KN black holes. We find that electric charge restricts the mass range of the thermal soliton state, while rotation in the KN case removes the upper mass bound and eliminates the distinction arising from arbitrary surface contributions between the thermal soliton and black hole states. These findings uncover new aspects of the off-shell thermodynamics of charged and rotating black holes and suggest a possible connection between their phase structure and the quantum nature of gravity.

authors.name: Tran Ngoc Thien, Vo Quoc Phong

papers.title: Quantum Riemannian Hamiltonian Descent
papers.summary: We propose Quantum Riemannian Hamiltonian Descent (QRHD), a quantum algorithm for continuous optimization on Riemannian manifolds that extends Quantum Hamiltonian Descent (QHD) by incorporating geometric structure of the parameter space via a position-dependent metric in the kinetic term. We formulate QRHD in both operator and path integral formalisms and derive the corresponding quantum equations of motion, showing that quantum corrections appear in the action integral but they are suppressed at late times by the time-dependent dissipation factor. This implies that convergence near optimal points is controlled by the classical potential while quantum effects influence early-time dynamics. By analyzing the semiclassical equation, we estimate a lower bound on the convergence time and numerically demonstrate whether QRHD works as a quantum optimization algorithm in some examples. A quantum circuit implementation based on time-dependent Hamiltonian simulation is also discussed and the query complexity is estimated.

authors.name: Yoshihiko Abe, Ryo Nagai

papers.title: Light-by-light scattering: asymptotic expansions, Coulomb resummation and NLO corrections
papers.summary: Light-by-light (LbL) scattering is one of the earliest predictions of quantum electrodynamics (QED). Interest in this process has been renewed following its experimental observation at the LHC and the prospects of future measurements at free-electron laser facilities. In this paper, we refine theoretical predictions for LbL scattering by improving the full fermion-mass-dependent two-loop QCD and QED helicity amplitudes using high- and low-energy asymptotic expansions, and by performing Coulomb resummation in the threshold region. The $W$-boson contribution, relevant when the di-photon invariant mass exceeds twice the $W$-boson mass, is included at one-loop accuracy. We present state-of-the-art predictions for LbL cross sections in the Standard Model and provide a new event generator, LbLatNLO, for Monte Carlo simulations of LbL scattering.

authors.name: Ajjath A H, Ekta Chaubey, Hua-Sheng Shao

papers.title: Time-Dependent Classical and Quantum Integrability in Sigma Models: From the $\lambda$-Model to the Perturbed $SU(2)_1$ WZW Model
papers.summary: Using the Hamiltonian formulation of the $\lambda$-model with time-dependent coupling, we compare classical Lax and quantum integrability in the isotropic current-current deformation of the $SU(2)_1$ Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) model. From the classical WZW current algebra at fixed level, we derive equations of motion for the coupled left- and right-moving currents and construct a generalized Lax connection whose flatness fixes the integrable time-dependent coupling. Equal-time Lax-matrix Poisson brackets take the generalized Maillet form, and the $r/s$ kernels satisfy the extended classical Yang-Baxter relation. A coupling redefinition and time reparametrization relate it to the $\lambda$-model with local couplings. At level one, non-Abelian bosonization identifies the deformed model with the interacting isospin sector of the chiral-invariant $SU(2)$ Gross-Neveu model. In its exact generalized Bethe ansatz (GBA) solution, the quantum Yang-Baxter equation constrains the time-dependent coupling. In the universal weak-coupling regime, it shares the leading inverse-affine time dependence imposed by classical Lax flatness of the $\lambda$-model. This common weak-coupling equation coincides with the one-loop renormalization-group equation of the static model, with time identified with the logarithm of the UV cutoff. Periodic boundary conditions in the GBA yield the quantum Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov equations, whose solution gives an exact many-body wavefunction admitting a Yang-Yang representation at any nonzero drive rate. In the slow-drive limit, dynamical dimensional transmutation generates an isospin mass gap decaying exponentially in time on the decreasing-coupling branch, while in the fast-drive limit the isospin sector approaches the $SU(2)_1$ WZW UV fixed point. We also compare classical and quantum integrability of higher-level WZW and noncompact-group sigma models.

authors.name: Parameshwar R. Pasnoori

papers.title: Norms, overlaps and Yangian descendants for the Haldane-Shastry spin chain
papers.summary: The Haldane-Shastry spin chain is a prototypical integrable model with long-range interactions, notable for hosting quasiparticles with fractional statistics and serving as a discrete analogue of a conformal field theory. Its remarkable simplicity is closely tied to a full Yangian spin symmetry. While the highest-weight states for this symmetry are known explicitly, a systematic treatment of the descendant states, needed for the computation of various physical quantities, has remained incomplete. In this work, we provide a detailed construction of these descendants in terms of the algebraic Bethe ansatz following recent work of Ferrando et al. In the limit of extreme twist, it includes the Gelfand-Tsetlin basis. As an application, we derive product and determinant formulae for norms and overlaps of these states.

authors.name: Yunfeng Jiang, Jules Lamers, Yuan Miao

papers.title: Unitarity with respect to the Clock of a Dynamical Local Observer and the Einstein Equivalence Principle
papers.summary: We investigate the unitarity of quantum evolution with respect to an internal time defined by a local observer's clock. The observer is modeled as a relativistic particle carrying both a clock and a matter-field detector, analyzed first on a fixed curved background and subsequently within a fully diffeomorphism-invariant theory of dynamical gravity. In the former case, we find that evolution relative to the internal clock is generally nonunitary, implying a violation of the Einstein equivalence principle at the quantum level. In contrast, in the latter case, diffeomorphism invariance allows us to adopt observer-centric coordinates. On the resulting partially reduced phase space, one of the diffeomorphism generators becomes linear in the clock Hamiltonian, generating a relational evolution that is consistent with the remaining diffeomorphism constraints. Assuming the existence of an effective quantum theory that consistently preserves diffeomorphism invariance, these features imply unitary evolution relative to the internal clock, thereby preserving the equivalence principle even in the quantum regime. Our results highlight the fundamental role of diffeomorphism invariance in shaping relational unitary evolution from the perspective of a local observer.

authors.name: Kengo Shimada

papers.title: Moore--Read construction and explicit monodromies of Laughlin states on Riemann surfaces
papers.summary: We revisit the Moore--Read construction of the $\nu=1/k$ Laughlin states on compact Riemann surfaces, deriving their conformal blocks from $U(1)_k$ Chern--Simons theory through the CS/WZW correspondence. We compute their explicit monodromies under quasi-hole transport and Aharonov--Bohm flux insertion, and prove that the monodromies associated with flux insertion asymptotically coincide with the corresponding physical adiabatic holonomies. In particular, we prove that the physical $L^2$ metric on the vector bundle of Laughlin states over the Jacobian is asymptotically projectively flat. We also relate our construction to the recently developed algebro-geometric approach to higher genus Laughlin states.

authors.name: Kiyoon Eum

papers.title: Mathematical inverse problem for the world data inference of the parton distribution functions of the proton
papers.summary: We show that the inference problem of constraining the parton distribution functions of the proton from deeply inelastic scattering data can be formulated as a linear tensor reconstruction inverse problem. This means that instead of fitting model parameters to the world data, a reconstructive approach to solve a system of coupled linear functional integral equations can be formulated. We leverage the mathematical structures of the integral equations defined by perturbative QCD and global analysis to pose the problem of global analysis as a coupled system of linear integral equations, and construct a proof-of-principle methodology to solve it. To formulate this approach concretely, we review all next-to-leading order accuracy results for inclusive virtual photon, neutral current, charged current, heavy flavor production, and neutrino deep-inelastic lepton--proton scattering. This mathematical methodology of inference opens a path towards a parametrization-bias-free extraction of the proton PDFs from the world data of deeply inelastic scattering in the spirit of indirect measurement employed in mathematical inverse problems, including robust estimation of uncertainties with reduced bias from model parametrization, while closely adhering to the established paradigm of perturbative QCD and global analysis.

authors.name: Henri H\"anninen

papers.title: Realizing Braided Fusion 2-Categories as (3+1)D Mixed-State Topological Orders
papers.summary: We construct large families of mixed-state topological orders in (3+1)D, including intrinsically mixed-state topological orders. We realize these theories by relating the data parameterizing braided fusion 2-categories to the strong higher-form symmetries and their anomalies that characterize mixed-state topological order. We focus here on bosonic theories, which include theories which admit an emergent fermion in the spectrum of line operators. Our general framework is exemplified on the lattice, where we present concrete models and identify how the data of braided fusion 2-categories are physically encoded. We then formalize this data and show that every braided fusion 2-category arises from a general construction (decoherence followed by strong and weak gauging) as the category of topological operators of a (3+1)D mixed state, with intrinsically mixed-state topological orders distinguished by the presence of strong higher-form symmetries whose anomalies cannot be realized in any (3+1)D gapped ground state. Notably, we show that (3+1)D admits a new mechanism with no (2+1)D counterpart: intrinsically mixed-state order whose topological operators braid non-degenerately, but which carries a gravitational anomaly.

authors.name: Ryohei Kobayashi, Abhinav Prem, Matthew Yu

papers.title: Exact algebraic separation of the gravitoelectromagnetic perturbations of Kerr-Newman-(anti-)de Sitter black holes
papers.summary: We obtain an explicit separation of the coupled gravitational and electromagnetic radiative equations on nonextremal Kerr--Newman--(anti-)de Sitter black holes with nonzero charge and rotation. By directly matching the Fourier coefficients, we construct a separating matrix with constant determinant that is independent of the frequency and azimuthal number and applies to both spin sectors. We establish that this transformation is smooth and invertible throughout the open AdS exterior and between the event and cosmological horizons in dS. The resulting radial and angular systems are valid at arbitrary complex frequencies. We also translate the regularity of the radiative Newman--Penrose variables at the rotation axes and future horizons into boundary conditions for the separated solutions. In the asymptotically flat limit, the transformation is related to Hintz's matrix integrating factor by the allowed frame freedom. These results provide a basis for studying quasinormal modes and black hole stability in Kerr--Newman--(anti-)de Sitter spacetimes, as well as exploring holographic applications to strongly coupled systems.

authors.name: Jun-Kun Zhao

papers.title: A new toric ALF gravitational instanton
papers.summary: We construct a new explicit toric ALF gravitational instanton. The instanton has Euler characteristic $\chi = 4$ and Hirzebruch signature $\tau = -1$. The topology at infinity is a lens space $L(3,1)$. The solution depends on one parameter and is constructed from the Belinski--Zakharov four-soliton solution. We prove that the instanton is smooth and positive definite on and away from the axis. This is the first example of a non-Hermitian ALF (not AF) gravitational instanton.

authors.name: Alfie Jones

papers.title: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
papers.summary: Scalar-induced second-order tensor perturbations comprise both a forced response and freely propagating gravitational waves, the radiative signal sought in observations. We define this free radiation as the out-state, whose amplitudes are given by the light-cone residue of the kernel for each scalar pair via a classical LSZ-type reduction formula. We prove a classical equivalence theorem: tensor redefinitions whose shifts have power-law envelopes and no tensor-frequency component leave the out-state invariant. For any constant equation of state $0<w<1$, the out-state is consequently universal across all intrinsic gauges, in which the slicing and spatial coordinates are fixed locally by matter and geometry without an external clock. This class includes the comoving and uniform-density gauges, whose spectra grow without bound at late times in radiation domination. Over this range of $w$, the late-time Newtonian-gauge kernel yields the out-state, justifying its standard use in computing the gravitational-wave energy spectrum. In matter domination, by contrast, the out-state isolates the free wave from the static tidal response that asymptotically dominates the Newtonian-gauge tensor perturbation.

authors.name: Yizhou Lu

papers.title: Testing the Unitarity of Three-Flavor Neutrino Mixing above the GUT Scale
papers.summary: We investigate how physics between the grand-unification and Planck scales affects neutrino mixing in the standard three-flavor framework, distinguishing genuine non unitarity from unitary shifts of the mixing parameters. First, we show that heavy gauge singlet states at or above the grand-unification scale induce deviations from unitarity of the effective (3\times3) Pontecorvo Maki Nakagawa Sakata (PMNS) matrix, suppressed by the ratio of the light-neutrino mass to the heavy mass. The resulting effects are estimated to be of order (10^{-27}), far below current oscillation constraints. Second, we examine the impact of a flavor-blind dimension-five Weinberg operator suppressed by a high-energy scale (\Lambda). This operator modifies the neutrino mass matrix and shifts the mixing angles while preserving the exact unitarity of the PMNS matrix. Using the NuFIT 6.1 best-fit parameters for normal mass ordering, including the Dirac CP-violating phase, and numerically diagonalizing the corrected complex-symmetric mass matrix, we find that the shift in (\theta_{12}) can reach approximately (0.12^\circ) at the Planck scale for a quasi-degenerate neutrino spectrum, compared with (0.011^\circ) for normal ordering. The corrections increase as (1/\Lambda), reaching approximately (6.5^\circ) for normal ordering near the grand-unification scale, where perturbation theory becomes unreliable for the quasi-degenerate spectrum. Since the Weinberg operator acts entirely within the active three-flavor sector, it introduces no additional non-unitarity parameters; instead, the correlated shifts of the three mixing angles are governed by a single parameter. Our results demonstrate that tests of active-flavor probability conservation cannot directly constrain this high-scale contribution. Its phenomenological signatures must instead be sought in the correlated modifications of the neutrino mixing parameters.

authors.name: Bipin Singh Koranga, Samrat Vashisht

papers.title: From nested soft-collinear subtraction to NNLO QCD predictions with large language models
papers.summary: We investigate whether large language models can construct reliable and efficient codes for computing NNLO QCD corrections to collider processes, starting from the general formula derived within the nested soft-collinear subtraction scheme. We use Higgs production in weak-boson fusion with and without an additional jet to compare numerical implementations by large language models, subject to various degrees of supervision, against a human-written reference code.

authors.name: Federica Devoto, Kirill Melnikov, Ivan Novikov, Raoul R\"ontsch, Chiara Signorile-Signorile, Davide Maria Tagliabue, Matteo Tresoldi

papers.title: Parton structure of mesonic states with tensor networks
papers.summary: We present the first direct tensor network calculation of flavor-resolved parton distribution functions (PDFs) for a pion-like isospin triplet in the two-flavor Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model in (1+1) dimensions. Four-fermion interactions bind the mesons without confinement. Using staggered fermions and a charge-symmetrized Hamiltonian, we prepare the bound states and compute light-cone correlators by real-time evolution. The resulting quark and antiquark PDFs obey the expected isospin relations under $u \leftrightarrow d$ exchange between charged pions and exhibit equal u and d distributions in the neutral pion. A flavor-independent antisymmetrization of the field ordering removes the vacuum-subtracted anticommutator contribution and restores charge-conjugation relations in both the correlators and PDFs across the triplet within numerical accuracy. These results provide benchmarks for quantum simulations of the partonic structure of the meson.

authors.name: Jack Y. Araz, Yamil Cahuana Medrano, Peter L. Nguyen, Zhong-Bo Kang, Jian-Wei Qiu, David Richards, Nobuo Sato, Marco Zaccheddu, Jia-Yue Zhang

papers.title: Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger: The $\Delta(1232)$ Resonance in Supernova QCD Axion Emission
papers.summary: The high-energy tail of supernova axion emission controls searches whose response grows with axion energy. We identify a novel production channel, in which the axion is emitted through an intermediate $\Delta(1232)$ resonance, which adds a hard component to the spectrum. We calculate the axion production rate from nucleon-nucleon Bremsstrahlung in chiral effective field theory through next-to-leading order. Including the $\Delta(1232)$ roughly doubles the luminosity at one second after bounce and increases the number of escaping axions above $200$ MeV by a factor of about $3$ over the first nine seconds, relative to the nucleon-only calculation. Adding this new production channel roughly doubles $\gamma$-ray counts from conversion in the progenitor's magnetic field and increases water-Cherenkov counts by about an order of magnitude through its combined effects on emission and absorption. The same hard component can mimic a higher core temperature or thermal-pion emission in $\gamma$-ray spectral fits. The $\Delta(1232)$ resonance is therefore crucial for predicting supernova axion signals and interpreting their spectra.

authors.name: Paolo Arcangeli, Konstantin Springmann, Michael Stadlbauer, Stefan Stelzl, Andreas Weiler

papers.title: Physics-informed neural networks for quark Dyson--Schwinger equations and propagator singularities
papers.summary: We develop a physics-informed neural-network (PINN) framework for solving the rainbow-truncated quark Dyson--Schwinger equation at real and complex momenta. The resulting dressing functions agree closely with conventional iterative solutions. We investigate the singularity structure of the quark propagator using two complementary methods. Analytic continuation of a PINN trained on the real momentum axis estimates the locations of poles and further reveals three complex-conjugate pole pairs. An independent reconstruction using PINN-parametrized spectral densities and a single pole pair yields $q=-0.146\pm0.391i~\mathrm{GeV}^2$. The agreement between the two methods substantially strengthens confidence in the properties of the leading singularities. Both spectral densities change sign, and the negative regions of the vector density and the complex poles indicate a violation of reflection positivity, consistent with quark confinement. Finally, we use the extracted poles and residues to calculate their contributions to two order parameters at finite quark chemical potential, the chiral condensate and the quark number density.

authors.name: Xin-Peng Li, Zhong-Hua Huang

papers.title: Divergence-type hydrodynamics of radial oscillations in viscous neutron stars
papers.summary: Based on a simplified model of a viscous neutron star in the Newtonian limit coupled to a quadratic dissipative fluid theory of divergence type with bulk viscosity only, we explore the impact of nonlinear effects on the evolution of radial perturbations, and compare it with the results of linear hydrodynamics. For high values of the bulk viscosity $\zeta_B \gtrsim 5\times 10^{31}$ g/cm/s, the linear theory develops growing oscillations, which do appear in the quadratic theory but at much higher values of $\zeta_B$. The quadratic theory shows stronger damping of oscillations, longer decay rates of non-hydrodynamic modes and also a ``stiffer'' evolution of radial perturbations that results in less deformation. These results suggest that nonlinear effects may be relevant to capture the dynamics of the long-lived non-hydrodynamic modes present at high $\zeta_B$.

authors.name: J. Peralta-Ramos

papers.title: Determination of the strong coupling constant from the R ratio obtained in KEDR and BESIII experiments
papers.summary: The experimental data collected by the KEDR and BESIII collaborations at energies below the charm quark threshold are compared with the massless QCD expressions for the $e^+e^-$ annihilation R-ratio truncated at different orders of perturbation theory. The fits demonstrate the dependence of the extracted $\alpha_s(M_Z)$ values on the orders of truncation of the corresponding approximations.

authors.name: Korneliy Todyshev, Andrei Kataev

papers.title: Singly-strange hidden-bottom and double-bottom molecular pentaquarks
papers.summary: Inspired by the observation of the singly-strange hidden-charm pentaquarks $P_{\psi s}^{\Lambda}(4459)$ and $P_{\psi s}^{\Lambda}(4338)$, we present a systematic investigation of the mass spectra of the singly-strange hidden-bottom and double-bottom molecular pentaquarks arising from the $\Xi_b^{(\prime,\,*)}B^{(*)}$ and $\Xi_b^{(\prime,\,*)}\bar B^{(*)}$ interactions. Using the one-boson-exchange model, we derive the effective potentials for the $\Xi_b^{(\prime,\,*)}B^{(*)}$ systems by exchanging light mesons. The effective potentials for the corresponding $\Xi_b^{(\prime,\,*)}\bar B^{(*)}$ systems are then obtained via the $G$-parity rule. By solving the coupled-channel Schr\"odinger equation with $S$-$D$ wave mixing and coupled-channel effects, we search for loosely bound states with all possible isospin and spin-parity quantum numbers. Our results show that the $\Xi_b B$ state with $I(J^P)=0(1/2^-)$, the $\Xi_b B^*$ states with $I(J^P)=0(1/2^-)$ and $0(3/2^-)$, the $\Xi_b^\prime B$ state with $I(J^P)=0(1/2^-)$, the $\Xi_b^* B$ state with $I(J^P)=0(3/2^-)$, the $\Xi_b^\prime B^*$ states with $I(J^P)=0(1/2^-)$ and $0(3/2^-)$, and the $\Xi_b^* B^*$ states with $I(J^P)=0(1/2^-)$, $0(3/2^-)$, and $0(5/2^-)$ are identified as promising candidates of the singly-strange hidden-bottom molecular pentaquarks. Their $\Xi_b^{(\prime,\,*)}\bar B^{(*)}$ partners are likewise predicted to be the singly-strange double-bottom molecular pentaquark candidates. These predictions provide concrete targets for future experimental searches for exotic hadrons in the bottom sector, for example at LHCb.

authors.name: Fu-Lai Wang, Jia-Ning Cui, Rui Chen, Xiang Liu

papers.title: Heavy quark drag coefficient using phonon-heavy quark EFT
papers.summary: The description of heavy quarks inside the QGP medium, especially at low momenta, remains challenging from first principles due to the strong coupling and large gluon occupation numbers. An alternative description in terms of perturbative degrees of freedom treats the interactions of heavy quarks with the collective excitations of the medium in the form of phonons. This description is derived as an effective field theory (EFT) and therefore allows for a naturally occurring power counting of the allowed interactions. This EFT has already been established in our previous work, where we derived the phonon-heavy quark interactions and calculated their thermal scattering cross section. In this work, we use these results, together with the heavy quark expansion, to calculate the heavy quark drag coefficient. Subsequently, we compare our results with the drag coefficient obtained from AdS/CFT calculations to determine the previously unknown Wilson coefficients for the quark-phonon coupling. Additionally, we determine the same Wilson coefficients by matching the EFT result for the drag force at low momenta with the QCD result at high momenta. Finally, we will compare our results with experimentally determined heavy quark diffusion coefficients.

authors.name: Andreas Kirchner, Noah Koliadko, Berndt Mueller, Jyotirmoy Roy

papers.title: Higgsino dark matter explanation of LZ high-recoil event from deflected AMSB with $U(1)_X$ generated $\mu$ term
papers.summary: Motivated by the recent LZ high-recoil event, we propose to study the Higgsino dark matter in a supersymmetric $U(1)_X$ framework with one charged visible singlet. The gauge symmetry forbids the bare Higgs bilinear and the cubic $S^3$ while allowing the singlet interaction that generates an effective Higgsino mass after symmetry breaking. We present the six-state neutralino mixing matrix, including the $U(1)_X$ gaugino and the singlino, and the resulting neutral Higgsino mass splitting. Different deflected-anomaly-mediated parameter regimes provide the soft-mass hierarchies needed for light, 1.1 TeV and heavy Higgsino candidates. The cosmological consequences of the messenger sector in deflected AMSB can affect greatly the thermal history of the dark matter. Late messenger decays can supplement an underabundant thermal population or dilute an overabundant one through entropy production. These possibilities are governed by a common final-yield relation: a dominating messenger must have sufficiently suppressed Higgsino production for net dilution to succeed. We organise the 500 GeV, 1.1 TeV and 100 TeV reference regimes around this condition. Direct-detection and solar-capture constraints are discussed as tests of the resulting spectrum and final abundance. The elastic bino- or singlino-like interpretation of the same event is also realized in this spectrum: the Higgsino asymmetry $|X_A|\simeq10^{-2}$ that a $248\keV$ recoil requires arises without tuning, with a spin-dependent rate lying close to the present experimental sensitivity.

authors.name: Ke-Lin Li, Fei Wang

papers.title: Collisional dynamics of neutrino flavor conversion: angular structures, inhomogeneity, and decoherence
papers.summary: Self-interacting neutrino gases exhibit collective behavior, in which additional incoherent collisions can induce collisional neutrino-flavor instability. We investigate the effects of energy dependence, anisotropy, and spatial inhomogeneity on the resulting flavor conversion through linear stability analysis and nonlinear quantum kinetic simulations. We find contrasting wavenumber dependences for the near/gapless and far/gapped branches, with maximum growth rates at collision-scale shifted wavenumbers and at collective-scale wavenumbers, respectively. Their eigenvectors reveal distinct energy and angular structures, which are reflected in the subsequent establishment of flavor swap and equipartition. The nonlinear evolution also features secondary flavor growth associated with changes in the stability of collective modes as the neutrino background evolves. Despite the spreading of flavor coherence across spatial scales due to nonlinear mode coupling, collisional decoherence tends to limit the development of spatial inhomogeneities, leaving the neutrino populations nearly homogeneous. These findings represent a step towards understanding and predicting the nonlinear flavor evolution of dense neutrino gases interacting with their surroundings, particularly in explosive astrophysical environments.

authors.name: Masamichi Zaizen

papers.title: Origin of flavour cancellations in thermal leptogenesis
papers.summary: In thermal leptogenesis with three hierarchical heavy neutrinos $N_1$, $N_2$ and $N_3$, the baryon asymmetry can be the small remainder of large contributions that cancel. Interference terms in the CP asymmetry are known to contribute to the final asymmetry through flavour-dependent washout. However, it remains unclear where the cancellation occurs, how large the interference contribution is, and how the accuracy of approximate equations changes when this information is lost. We split the CP asymmetry into diagonal and off-diagonal parts in the charged-lepton basis and evolve them with Standard Model transport equations. We find that the cancellation occurs mainly between the diagonal and off-diagonal parts of the same heavy neutrino, and that it is caused by flavour-dependent washout. We also find that the interference between the lepton state produced in the decay and the states orthogonal to it typically accounts for most of the $N_2$ and $N_3$ contribution. Approximations that reduce the CP asymmetry to flavour populations turn out to miss most of this contribution, whereas density-matrix equations with the full CP-asymmetry matrix agree much better.

authors.name: Teruyuki Kitabayashi

papers.title: Revisiting the collisional energy loss of a heavy quark in an anisotropic quark-gluon plasma
papers.summary: We revisit the collisional energy loss of a heavy quark in a quark-gluon plasma with a small momentum-space anisotropy. Within the Braaten-Thoma framework, we obtain the hard contribution in closed form and reduce the soft contribution to one-dimensional integrals. Our result demonstrates analytically that, at linear order in the anisotropy, the dependence on the artificial separation scale cancels between the two contributions. By considering the unnormalized anisotropic distribution together with two variants that hold either the parton number density or the energy density at its isotropic value, we find that the angle-dependent part of the anisotropy correction is identical in all three cases and is proportional to the quadrupole $P_2(\cos\alpha)$, where $\alpha$ is the angle between the heavy-quark velocity and the anisotropy direction. In addition, the sign of the anisotropy correction, which determines whether the energy loss is enhanced or suppressed relative to the isotropic result, depends jointly on the quark speed, coupling, and propagation angle. In particular, at fixed energy density, only the quadrupole term survives. For a positive coefficient of $P_2(\cos\alpha)$, the correction enhances the energy loss for $\cos^2\alpha>1/3$ and suppresses it for $\cos^2\alpha<1/3$, with the opposite behavior for a negative coefficient.

authors.name: Mingda Cai, Yun Guo, Enke Wang

papers.title: Determining the kaon distribution amplitudes by fitting the $D\to K$ transition form factor to investigate the equivalence of two chiral LCSR frameworks
papers.summary: In this work, we fit the $D\to K$ vector transition form factor (TFF) to the BESIII experimental data using a Monte Carlo (MC) method. We also calculate the TFF using QCD light-cone sum rules (LCSRs) with left-and right-handed chiral currents. For the TFF derived using the right-handed chiral current, the key input is the kaon twist-2 distribution amplitude (DA), for which we consider three models: the power-law parametrization ($\mathrm{R1}$), the truncated Gegenbauer expansion ($\mathrm{R2}$), and the light-cone harmonic oscillator (LCHO) model ($\mathrm{R3}$). The parameters of these models are determined by fitting the corresponding TFF predictions to the MC-fit results. For the TFF derived using the left-handed chiral current, the dominant input is the kaon twist-3 DA ($\mathrm{L4}$), which is constructed within the LCHO framework. Its parameters are determined from theoretical constraints rather than from the fit. In the large-recoil region, the resulting TFF are $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{R1}}=0.7381^{+0.0180}_{-0.0194}$, $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{R2}}=0.7320^{+0.0178}_{-0.0192}$, $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{R3}}=0.7324^{+0.0180}_{-0.0191}$, and $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{L4}}=0.7343^{+0.0459}_{-0.0573}$. We then calculate the decay widths and branching fractions of the semileptonic decays $D\to K e\nu_e$ and extract the CKM matrix element $|V_{cs}|$. Finally, we predict the two important ratios, $\mathcal{R}_{\pi^-/K^-}^{e}$ and $\mathcal{R}_{\pi^0/K^0}^{e}$. All the obtained results are consistent with existing experimental measurements and theoretical predictions.

authors.name: Fang-Ping Peng, Sheng-Bo Wu, Hai-Bing Fu

papers.title: Non-perturbative charm production from color ropes in relativistic heavy ion collisions
papers.summary: We present results on charm production in nucleus-nucleus reactions in the energy range $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5$-$20$ GeV, obtained with the SMASH transport approach extended to include color rope formation. We show that string fusion may provide a substantial additional non-perturbative source of charm production. This may help to explain the apparent charm enhancement (above the pQCD expectations) at low transverse momenta. Our predicted neutral $D$-meson yields are consistent with current experimental constraints and may provide valuable insights for upcoming data by the NA61/SHINE collaboration.

authors.name: Carl B. Rosenkvist, Marcus Bleicher

papers.title: Towards Quark-Gluon Correlations in Pion from the Dyson-Schwinger Equations
papers.summary: Twist-3 distributions encode quark-gluon correlations, and the pion's chiral-odd $e(x)$ is the simplest of them. QCD fixes its lowest moments exactly, yet the only rainbow-ladder (RL) calculation of $e(x)$ omitted the Wilson line and violated the equation-of-motion (EOM) sum rule for the first moment. We show that the discrepancy is not a failure of RL but of the omitted link: at first order in the coupling, the link contributes three classes of planar diagrams that cancel the EOM violation class by class, so the sum rule is restored exactly in RL. The resulting zeroth and first moments are complete RL results. The genuine twist-3 component changes sign near $x=0.45$, and the Wilson line more than doubles its magnitude in the negative region. This identifies the Wilson line as the missing ingredient in the RL description of $e(x)$ and sets the stage for a full resummation of the $gA$ expansion.

authors.name: Zanbin Xing, Jiayin Kang, Lei Chang

papers.title: Black hole accretion flows as dark matter bolometers
papers.summary: Astrophysical systems provide powerful probes of dark matter interactions, complementing direct-detection searches. We propose using accretion flows of the supermassive black hole as a bolometer for light DM. The kinetic energy of sub-MeV dark matter in the black hole gravitational potential can remain below the thermal energy of the plasma electrons. The colder dark matter population can therefore absorb energy through elastic scattering, cooling the electrons and modifying their emission spectrum. We integrate dark matter cooling into the advection-dominated accretion flow around M87$^{*}$ and solve the full set of thermodynamic equations to obtain the resulting temperature profile and radio-to-millimeter emission. By comparing the predicted spectrum with observations accompanying the Event Horizon Telescope campaign, we use, for the first time, the thermal energy balance of the hot accretion flow to constrain DM-electron scattering, obtaining stringent limits on keV-to-MeV DM for both heavy and light mediators.

authors.name: Ran Ding, Ningqiang Song, Cong Zhang

papers.title: Lower Bound on the Lightest Neutrino Mass with Resonant Neutrino Self-Interactions
papers.summary: We show the possibility of using the resonant $s$-channel scattering of ultra high energy astrophysical neutrinos with the low energy cosmic neutrino background to put a lower bound on the lightest neutrino mass. This can be realized and illustrated by neutrino self-interactions with a light scalar mediator of $\mathcal O(1)$ MeV mass. After analyzing the kinematics and cross section features of the $s$-channel resonance, we derive from first principles the double transport equations with double regeneration terms for the coupled evolution of neutrinos and anti-neutrinos. The simulated event spectrum is then compared with the HESE 7.5 year data observed at IceCube to give a clear lower bound on the lightest neutrino mass.

authors.name: Shao-Feng Ge, Joao Paulo Pinheiro, Shaoyang Qin, Ruitao Sun, Oleg Titov

papers.title: Complete NNLO QCD Calculations of $B_c^{(*)}\to J/\psi(\eta_c)$ Form Factors and Semileptonic Decays
papers.summary: We present the first complete next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) QCD calculation of all 34 vector, axial-vector, tensor, and axial-tensor form factors for the four $B_c^{(*)}\to J/\psi(\eta_c)$ transitions within nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD) factorization. Using automated multi-loop techniques based on \texttt{FeynCalc} and \texttt{AMFlow}, we provide a dataset with at least 40 significant digits at 35 exact rational points in the $(m_b,m_c,q^2)$ parameter space, covering $q^2\in[-10,10]~\mathrm{GeV}^2$. In the spacelike region ($q^2<0$) and near $q^2=0$, the NLO corrections typically enhance the LO form factors by $\mathcal{O}(70\%)$, while the NNLO corrections amount to $\mathcal{O}(20\%)$ of the NLO predictions and substantially reduce the renormalization-scale dependence, demonstrating good perturbative convergence. In contrast, fixed-order NRQCD predictions suffer from threshold instabilities and become less reliable at higher timelike $q^2$. We therefore extrapolate the form factors to the full physical region via $z$-series fits to the NRQCD results at spacelike and near-zero $q^2$, finding broad agreement with the latest lattice QCD results for $B_c\to J/\psi$. With the resulting NRQCD+$z$-series form factors, we predict the decay widths, branching fractions, and lepton-flavor-universality (LFU) ratios for $B_c^{(*)}\to J/\psi(\eta_c)\,\ell\nu_\ell$ ($\ell=e,\mu,\tau$) at LO, NLO, and NNLO. Higher-order corrections substantially enhance the absolute rates but largely cancel in the ratios, whose uncertainties are dominated by the choice of fitting points. In particular, our NNLO central prediction $\mathcal{R}(B_c\to J/\psi)=0.2836$ lies between the latest lattice QCD determination and the most recent LHCb measurement.

authors.name: Wei Tao, Zhen-Jun Xiao, Ruilin Zhu, Qin Chang

papers.title: Isospin violating decay of D wave charmonia
papers.summary: The experimental observations of $\psi(3823)$ and $\psi(3842)$ enrich the $D$ wave charmonia family. In our previous work the decays of $\psi(3823)$ and $\psi(3842)$ to isospin conserved non-$D\bar D$ hadronic decays are well studied. Since the isospin violated decay channel $\psi(3770)\to J/\psi \pi$ is measured clearly very recently, so in this work we fit the model parameter $\alpha$ through $BR(\psi(3770)\to J/\psi \pi)_{exp}$, then study the contribution of isospin violated decay channels of $\psi(3770)\to h_c\pi$, $\psi(3823)$ and $\psi(3842)$ to $J/\psi\pi$ and $h_c\pi$, respectively. With this range of parameters space, the branching ratio of $\psi(3770)\to h_c\pi$ is estimated to be $(2.7\sim4.4)\times10^{-7}$. The decay widths of $\psi(3823)$ and $\psi(3842)$ to $J/\psi\pi$ and $h_c\pi$ are also estimated. Our results show that the partial width of $\psi(3823)\to J/\psi\pi$ is $1.12\sim1.77$ eV, the value for $\psi(3823)\to h_c\pi$ is $0.71\sim1.04$ eV, and $0.028\sim0.044$ eV for $\psi(3842)\to J/\psi\pi$, $0.34\sim0.49$ eV for $\psi(3842)\to h_c\pi$, respectively. We hope those values could be tested by further precise measurements from the BES III, Belle II and LHCb Collaborations.

authors.name: Xing-Dao Guo, Qi Wu, Dian-Yong Chen

papers.title: Lighting up LZ with Loopy Transitions in a leptophilic Dark Sector
papers.summary: We study the direct detection phenomenology and cosmology of a multicomponent dark sector with a leptophilic t-channel portal. The coupling to right-handed Standard Model leptons is mediated by a charged vector-like fermion, allowing both a scalar and a vector dark candidate to connect to the SM through the same mediator. Motivated by the high-energy nuclear-recoil event recently reported by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment, we consider a nearly degenerate dark sector with mass splittings of order a few hundred keV and investigate the resulting inelastic transitions. Concretely, we focus on endothermic scattering of the dark states, which can shift the recoil spectrum towards the high-energy region preferred by LZ while suppressing low-energy events. We scrutinize the effective operators generating the dark-matter-photon coupling, which provides the essential interaction for nuclear recoils. Interestingly, the inelastic transition arises at dimension five whereas elastic scattering on nuclei is induced only at dimension six. This naturally explains the prominence of endothermic scattering compared to its elastic counterpart. We determine the parameter space compatible with the observed dark matter abundance and scrutinize the event rate and signal shape for scattering on xenon. Our results demonstrate that the observation of a single $E_R=248\pm 46$ keV nuclear recoil event in LZ can be accommodated by thermally produced dark matter in a leptophilic dark sector.

authors.name: Simone Biondini, Clara Hofheinz, Stefan Melchin, Lorenzo Tiberi, Stefan Vogl

papers.title: Ultralight Dark Matter Spectrum with Gravitational Focusing and Doppler Motion
papers.summary: Ultralight dark matter can produce signals in experiments through its couplings with the Standard Model particles. The resulting signal spectrum is determined by the phase-space distribution of dark matter, which encodes information about its production mechanism and the history of the local universe. However, the local environmental effects can modify the observed spectrum and should be included in signal modeling to avoid biased parameter estimates. In this work, we investigate how the gravitational focusing by Sun and the Doppler effect due to the detector's motion modify the signal spectrum and affect inferring the underlying dark matter parameters. We analytically estimate the signal significance and perform Bayesian analysis on simulated data to demonstrate their impact.

authors.name: Shao-Feng Ge, Yong Tang, Yue-Hui Yao

papers.title: Conditional multiparameter thermometry with neutrino oscillations: MSW energy diversity and a plasma-noise benchmark
papers.summary: We address temperature-parameter inference in a restricted two-flavor neutrino dephasing model with fixed mean electron densities. When two zone temperatures enter the propagated state via a single accumulated dephasing exponent, the single-energy quantum Fisher information matrix has rank at most 1. Independent, energy-resolved samples restore regular local identifiability when their thermal-sensitivity vectors are noncollinear. Matter-dependent mixing provides distinct weights in an illustrative two-zone model. A separate two-probe benchmark shows how complementary Bell sectors can distinguish temperature from spatial noise correlations. An electron-only Debye-cell estimate gives a conditional longitudinal quantum signal-to-noise ratio of approximately $3.1\times10^{-13}$ at 10 MeV for a uniform central-density medium over one solar radius. This estimate is not a microscopic upper bound or a detector sensitivity forecast. Complete phase averaging removes temperature information carried solely by longitudinal coherence damping; to retain solar sensitivity, a separate calculation of population, refractive, or production effects is required. The results distinguish conditional state identifiability from operational temperature inference.

authors.name: Jilali Loulijat, Abdallah Slaoui, El Hassan Saidi, Mohamed Gouighri, Berihu Teklu

papers.title: Recent Developments in Colibri: A Neural-Network PDF Model and Improved Bayesian Sampling
papers.summary: We present recent developments in Colibri, an open-source framework for flexible fits of parton distribution functions (PDFs). Colibri allows the implementation of any PDF functional form as well as Bayesian, Monte Carlo, and Hessian inference methods, making it particularly well suited for systematic comparisons of model architectures and uncertainty propagation treatments. In these proceedings, we report on two key updates to the framework: the release of colibri-n3fit, an open-source implementation of the neural-network model used by the NNPDF collaboration, and the integration of an upgraded, highly efficient Bayesian sampler, bridging the gap between the computational cost of Bayesian PDF fitting and other uncertainty propagation treatments. Combined, these updates extend Colibri's capabilities to neural-network PDF fits, enabling direct, quantitative Bayesian analyses of the n3fit architecture and opening new avenues for comparative studies.

authors.name: Ella Cole, Valentina Sch\"utze S\'anchez

papers.title: Majorana Neutrino Exchange in Free-Baryon $B_1B_2\to ppe^-e^-$ Reactions
papers.summary: The free-baryon reactions $B_1B_2\to pp e^-e^-$ are studied for six nonstrange and strange initial states, with light- and heavy-Majorana-neutrino exchange treated in the same baryon-level framework. For light-neutrino exchange, the cross sections scale with the square of the effective Majorana mass $m_{\beta\beta}$. The calculated cross sections increase as the off-shell cutoff $\Delta q^2$ is reduced, especially near threshold and in the hyperon channels, because more of the phase-space region where the squared four-momentum of the exchanged neutrino is close to zero is retained. At $\sqrt{s}=5.1~\mathrm{GeV}$, the six light-neutrino cross sections span $9.28\times10^{-49}$--$1.78\times10^{-45}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$ for $m_{\beta\beta}=30~\mathrm{meV}$ and $\Delta q^2=10^{-2}~\mathrm{GeV}^2$. For heavy-neutrino exchange, the cross sections scale with $\eta_N^2$, where $\eta_N=|U_{eN}|^2/m_N$. The leading propagator correction remains below one percent for $m_N\gtrsim50~\mathrm{GeV}$ over the phase-space region considered. At $\sqrt{s}=5.1~\mathrm{GeV}$, the heavy-neutrino cross sections span $7.55\times10^{-45}$--$1.98\times10^{-41}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$ for $\eta_N=4.0\times10^{-9}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. At higher energies, the two exchange cases give the same CKM-driven channel ordering, with the $nn$ cross section largest. At fixed $\sqrt{s}$, compared with the light-neutrino spectra calculated with $\Delta q^2=10^{-2}~\mbox{GeV}^2$, the heavy-neutrino peaks occur at a smaller squared invariant mass for the proton pair and a larger one for the electron pair. These results extend the free-baryon analogue of neutrinoless double-beta decay to strange initial states and provide theoretical reference results for comparing light- and heavy-Majorana-neutrino exchange.

authors.name: Yuan-Guo Xu, Bo Lan, Ben-Hou Xiang, Shuang-Shi Fang, Yi-Bing Zhang, Ru-Min Wang

papers.title: Confronting $b \to (s, d)\mu^+ \mu^-$ and $\mathcal{L}_{K^{*}\bar{K}^{*}}$ puzzle in a $U(1)_{B-3L_\mu}$ framework with neutrino phenomenology
papers.summary: Current data on several observables in $b \to (s,d)$ $\mu^+ \mu^-$ transitions reveal certain discrepancies with Standard Model (SM) predictions. Considering the possibility that these deviations stem from new physics, we explore a $Z^{\prime}$ framework based on $U(1)_{B-3L_\mu}$ model. The parameter space is examined in light of existing constraints from $b \to (s,d)$ $\mu^+ \mu^-$ transitions. Within this framework, we show that the quark couplings accommodating $b \to (s,d)$ $\mu^+ \mu^-$ anomalies, imprint correlated signatures on the non-leptonic puzzles $\mathcal{L}_{K^{*}\bar{K}^{*}}$ in $B_{s(d)} \to K^{{*}}\bar{K}^{{*}}$ decays. We find that the scenario with both vector and axial-vector contributions of opposite sign is favored by the data compared to pure vector contribution, offering a correlated probe of the underlying new-physics scenario. We further explore the neutrino phenomenology within the same framework in light of current data.

authors.name: Dhiren Panda, Priya Mishra, Manas Kumar Mohapatra, Rukmani Mohanta

papers.title: Rational terms and UV counterterms of the SMEFT at next-to-leading order in QCD
papers.summary: We compute the rational terms $R_2$ and the ultraviolet counterterms of the dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) at next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD without any flavour assumption, for complex Wilson coefficients, massive quarks and a general CKM matrix. We also compute the on-shell renormalisation factors of the quark fields in the presence of flavour mixing. We work with an anticommuting $\gamma_5$ and read closed fermion loops with a single $\gamma_5$ at the operator insertion. The results, also for common flavour assumptions, are provided in electronic form and in a Mathematica package attached to the paper. We use them to build example models for MadGraph5_aMC@NLO and give NLO predictions for representative processes.

authors.name: Giuseppe Ventura

papers.title: Gravity-induced mixing, regeneration and CP violation
papers.summary: The analysis of neutral mesons oscillations perturbed by Earth's gravity reveals a small coupling between flavor oscillations and quarks zitterbewegung. As a result of this small gravity-induced coupling between two very low energy oscillations, the mass eigenstates are no longer the Charge-Parity eigenstates. The three types of observed CP violation effects result from this gravity-induced mixing. The associated violation parameters are predicted in full agreement with the experimental data. Thus gravity-induced CP violation offers the accurate framework to understand the origin of CP symmetry violation in neutral mesons experiments. This origin renews in depth the problem of the required large-scale asymmetric baryogenesis in the early universe. Furthermore, the issues of the small time reversal violation in neutral kaons experiments and of the strong CP problem are fully clarified within this new framework of analysis taking into account gravity.

authors.name: Jean-Marcel Rax

papers.title: Entanglement entropy in low x Deep Inelastic Scattering
papers.summary: In a 2017 paper by Kharzeev and Levin, it has been proposed that hadronic entropy, extracted from the multiplicity of final state hadrons, provides a measure of entanglement in the proton wave function, observed in Deep Inelastic Scattering (DIS) of electrons and protons. In this contribution we discuss how the density matrix of the low x DIS system can give rise to a mixed state and therefore to finite entanglement entropy. We further present recent numerical results on the determination of low x dipole multiplicities, based on the solution of the Levin-Lublinsky evolution equation.

authors.name: Martin Hentschinski

papers.title: Tackling the DVCS inverse problem with finite element method
papers.summary: In this paper, we tackle the problem of shadow GPDs, arising from the non-invertibility of the measured $2\to 2$ exclusive processes at large virtualities (DVCS, TCS and DVMP). This problem arose five years ago as the main source of theoretical uncertainties, potentially dominating experimental ones by orders of magnitude. We show here that the deconvolution ambiguity can be elegantly eliminated by relying on finite element method. The problem is essentially converted at any finite discretisation area $a$ from a non-invertible to an ill-conditioned one. Given experimental uncertainties, this yields a theoretical lower bound on the discretisation area $a_\textrm{min}$, that can be interpreted as the maximal theoretical resolution one can obtain on the reconstruction of the lightcone momentum fractions. Associated with the local polynomial degree $p$, the pair $(a,p)$ provides an insightful and easily understandable regularisation framework, allowing one to systematically improve the description of the momentum fractions dependence of GPDs with the pQCD order at which the hard kernels of exclusive processes are computed.

authors.name: Marija \v{C}ui\'c, C\'edric Mezrag, Jos\'e Manuel Morgado Ch\'avez

papers.title: QED corrections to neutron and nuclear $\beta$-decay at order $\alpha^2$
papers.summary: We compute two-loop QED corrections to neutron and nuclear beta decay, including full electron mass dependence and real radiation contributions. The result for the neutron, $\delta_{R,\,\rm static}= ( 29.199 \pm 0.001 )\times 10^{-3}$, implies a factor $\sim 70 $ reduction in the uncertainty of the low-energy radiative corrections compared to previous results obtained in the large energy/small electron-mass limit, $m_e/(m_n-m_p) \to 0$. For superallowed nuclear decays we find that the $Z$-independent order $\alpha^2$ corrections range from $(0.1-0.5) \times 10^{-4}$ i.e., of roughly the expected size and comparable to current uncertainty estimates.

authors.name: Zehua Cao, Richard J. Hill, Ryan Plestid, Peter Vander Griend

papers.title: Probing Ultralight Dark Matter at the Electroweak Scale
papers.summary: Ultralight dark matter provides an explanation for astrophysical evidence for dark matter at all scales. This non-thermal dark matter requires a misalignment mechanism to reproduce the observed matter energy density of the Universe and therefore induce oscillating, time-dependent signals. We determine the sensitivity of current and future collider measurements of the width of the Z and Higgs bosons, and show that CP odd observables such as dipole moments in $Z\to \tau^+\tau^-$ decays provide a better sensitivity to ultralight dark matter than atomic clocks or equivalence principle tests.

authors.name: Martin Bauer, Sreemanti Chakraborti

papers.title: Heavy-flavor transverse energy-energy correlators in the color-glass condensate
papers.summary: We calculate the transverse energy--energy correlator (TEEC) for forward heavy-quark pair production in proton--nucleus collisions at leading order within the Color Glass Condensate framework. The calculation retains the heavy--quark mass, exact final-state parton kinematics and full relative azimuthal-angle dependence, without imposing a back-to-back approximation. Within the adopted collinear fragmentation prescription, a complete sum over hadron species in the two heavy-quark fragmentation branches eliminates the fragmentation functions through the momentum sum rule. We present numerical results for charm production at RHIC energies and charm and bottom production at LHC energies, using HERA-constrained McLerran--Venugopalan initial conditions evolved with the running-coupling Balitsky--Kovchegov equation. Relative to proton--proton collisions, the nuclear target suppresses the integrated TEEC per nucleon and shifts the relative angular weight towards configurations farther from back-to-back. The magnitude and angular dependence of these modifications vary with the quark mass, collision kinematics and nuclear geometry. These results illustrate the sensitivity of heavy-flavor energy correlations to nuclear small-$x$ dynamics while reducing their leading collinear fragmentation dependence.

authors.name: Zhong-Bo Kang, Carlos Lamas, Jani Penttala

papers.title: Screening of New Abelian Long-Range Forces
papers.summary: We study how bounds on new $U(1)$ long-range forces, resulting from gauging the Standard Model symmetries $B-L$ and $L_a-L_b$, $a,b=e,\mu,\tau$, are modified if the mediator mass is generated by the Higgs mechanism. Large baryonic and leptonic charges of astronomical bodies displace the Higgs field from its vacuum value, resulting in charge screening. Depending on the $U(1)$ Higgs mass, the screening relaxes the bounds on the new force strength and mediator mass from equivalence principle violation and neutrino oscillations experiments, and eliminates the bounds on the muonic $L_\mu-L_\tau$ force from neutron star binaries.

authors.name: Marco Costa, Andrey Shkerin, Ananda Thomlinson

papers.title: Probing the CKM Origin of CP Violation with Paramagnetic EDMs and Rare Kaon Decays
papers.summary: In the Standard Model, paramagnetic electric dipole moments (EDMs) are dominated by kaon exchange, which pairs the CP-violating short-distance transition $s\to d\,e^+e^-$ with a CP-conserving weak kaon-nucleon coupling. Long-distance two-photon exchange, which dominates $K_L\to e^+e^-$, gives an electron vertex about thirty-five times larger than the short-distance one and could obscure this origin. We show that it does not: the two-photon vertex conserves CP and must be paired with the CP-violating penguin component of the nucleon coupling, whose relative size is $3\times10^{-4}$, so that electromagnetic corrections stay at the few-percent level. Paramagnetic EDMs therefore measure $\mathrm{Im}(V_{ts}^*V_{td})$ and, together with the CP-violating $S$ wave of $K_S\to\mu^+\mu^-$ and $K_L\to\pi^0\nu\bar\nu$, determine the same imaginary coordinate of a kaon CKM plane with electrons, muons, and neutrinos, without $B$-decay input. Lepton-specific new physics, or CP violation that bypasses kaon exchange, would separate these determinations. Testing their common CKM origin calls for coordinated progress in molecular EDM searches, rare-kaon experiments at LHCb, NA62, and KOTO, and lattice determinations of weak nucleon matrix elements.

authors.name: Giancarlo D'Ambrosio, Luca Di Luzio

papers.title: ACT Excited: Reconciling Starobinsky and Quadratic Chaotic Inflationary Models with ACT Results via Excited States
papers.summary: Data Release 6 of the Atacama Cosmology Telescope, combined with Planck, CMB lensing and DESI BAO data, favours a higher scalar spectral index $n_{s}$ than Planck and a mildly positive running $\alpha_{s}$, putting the Starobinsky model in tension with the data, while the quadratic chaotic model is already excluded by its large tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$. We show that relaxing the Bunch--Davies assumption for the initial state of the scalar perturbations can restore agreement without modifying the inflaton potential. Parametrising the Bogoliubov coefficients by an excitation parameter $\chi_{S}$ and a relative phase $2\varphi_{S}$, we derive the shifts of $n_{s}$ and $\alpha_{s}$ induced by their scale dependence and map the regions of the $(\varphi_{S},\chi_{S})$ plane compatible with the $1\sigma$ ACT DR6 ranges, the bound $r<0.038$, and the requirement that the scale of new physics $\Lambda$ exceed the Hubble scale $H$. For the Starobinsky model, a scale-dependent $\chi_{S}$ or $\varphi_{S}$ works almost everywhere in this plane: only small neighbourhoods of $\varphi_{S}=0,\pi$ with $\chi_{S}\gtrsim1.22$ are excluded, and a scale-dependent phase fails at $\varphi_{S}=0,\pi/2,\pi$ and at $\chi_{S}=0$, where the required ${\rm d}\varphi_{S}/{\rm d}\ln k$ and ${\rm d}^2\varphi_{S}/{\rm d}(\ln k)^2$ diverge. For the QC model, the excited state must also suppress $r$, which requires $\chi_{S}\gtrsim0.63$ and $\Lambda\lesssim6H$. A scale-dependent $\chi_{S}$ must satisfy $|{\rm d}\chi_{S}/{\rm d}\ln k|\gtrsim0.0021$ in both models, and in the QC model we show analytically that $0.0021\lesssim{\rm d}\chi_{S}/{\rm d}\ln k\lesssim0.0058$ and $0.0008\lesssim{\rm d}^2\chi_{S}/{\rm d}(\ln k)^2\lesssim0.0062$. If the tensor modes remain in the BD state, the scenario also predicts a violation of the consistency relation $r=-8n_{T}$, testable once the tensor power spectrum and its tilt are measured.

authors.name: Amjad Ashoorioon, Abdolreza Yousefi-Sostani

papers.title: NuSrcAgent: An AI Agent for High-Energy Neutrino Source Searches
papers.summary: Identifying the sources of high-energy cosmic neutrinos is crucial for understanding cosmic particle accelerators and probing new physics. IceCube provides public data that allow researchers to search independently for neutrino sources, but these analyses require substantial technical expertise and careful scientific choices. We present \system, the first publicly available AI agent for high-energy neutrino source searches. Compared to public likelihood codes, \system is easier to install and use, and supports more analysis types. To start an analysis, users need only specify a source or catalog. The agent takes natural-language requests, runs likelihood analyses on public IceCube event data, and saves the settings and calculation records so users can repeat the analyses. We demonstrate \system through single-source and catalog stacking analyses, obtaining results consistent with IceCube results. These examples also show its ability to search the literature, analyze non-power-law spectra using user-provided model code, and develop new analysis functions, such as signal-injection simulations. \system is also a powerful tool for improving and testing existing analysis code, as we demonstrate by using it to refine the background probability density functions and reduce residuals and spurious signal contributions in stacking analyses. \system makes high-energy neutrino data analysis more accessible to the broader research community. Code and usage instructions: \href{https://github.com/beizhouphys/NuSrcAgent}{\faGithub\ {\tt github.com/beizhouphys/NuSrcAgent}}.

authors.name: Bei Zhou, Po-Wen Chang, Kohta Murase

papers.title: Gradient-flow scale setting from octet baryon masses in N$^3$LO covariant chiral perturbation theory
papers.summary: We determine the gradient-flow scale $t_0$ by analyzing the lowest-lying octet-baryon masses on the Coordinated Lattice Simulations (CLS) $N_f=2+1$ ensembles in covariant baryon chiral perturbation theory up to next-to-next-to-next-to leading order (N$^3$LO). By including the finite-volume corrections self-consistently and the discretization effects from Symanzik effective field theory, we obtain a good description of the RQCD data and determine the gradient-flow scale to be $\sqrt{8t_{0,\mathrm{ph}}}=0.4120(14)_\mathrm{stat.}(16)_\mathrm{sys.}$ fm with sub-percent precision. The predicted octet baryon masses agree well with the experimental values in the isospin limit. Using the Feynman-Hellmann theorem, we also estimate the nucleon sigma terms, which are consistent with direct determinations from three-point correlation functions on the same CLS ensembles.

authors.name: Xiu-Lei Ren

papers.title: Resonant top pair searches at the LHC: a window to electroweak phase transition
papers.summary: The dynamics of electroweak phase transition could have profound consequences for particle physics and cosmology. We study the prospects for the HL-LHC to probe the strong first-order electroweak phase transition (SFOEWPT) regime in the type-I 2HDM. We focus on the Higgstrahlung channel $pp\to ZH/A$ with a resonant top-quark pair final state $H/A\to t\bar t$. We find that the top-quark pair final state renders the largest sensitivity to the SFOEWPT regime, in comparison to the other Higgstrahlung searches already performed by ATLAS and CMS, that focus on the $H/A\to bb$ and $H\to WW$ final states. We also derive the complementarity of the Higgstrahlung searches with other relevant classes of searches at the HL-LHC and compare them with the gravitational wave sensitivity at LISA.

authors.name: Dorival Gon\c{c}alves, Ajay Kaladharan, Yongcheng Wu

papers.title: Study of anomalous charged triple gauge couplings with $W^-W^+$ process at $e^-e^+$ collider
papers.summary: We study anomalous charged triple gauge couplings (aTGC) in $e^-e^+\to W^-W^+$ at $\sqrt{s}=250$~GeV with longitudinally polarized beams, parameterized by the five dimension-six operators $\mathcal{O}_{WWW}$, $\mathcal{O}_{W}$, $\mathcal{O}_{B}$, $\mathcal{O}_{\widetilde{W}WW}$ and $\mathcal{O}_{\widetilde{W}}$ of the HISZ basis. All three decay channels, $\ell^\pm jj\slashed{E}$, $4j$ and $\ell^-\ell^+\slashed{E}$, are simulated explicitly at a leading-order including all diagrams that contribute to each final state and hence the interference of $W^-W^+$ with non-resonant amplitudes. The semi-leptonic signal is selected with cuts on $m_{j_1j_2}$ and $m_T^W$. The flavor identity of the two hardest light jets are classified as \emph{up}-type and \emph{down}-type jets with a dedicated boosted decision trees (BDT). In the $4j$ channel a multi-class BDT separates $W^-W^+$ from $ZZ$ and QCD production and the $W^\pm$ candidates are assigned using jet charge. In the dilepton channel $W^-W^+$ events are selected with cuts on $p_T^{\ell^-}$ and $m_{\ell^-\ell^+}$, and the two neutrino momenta are reconstructed analytically from the on-shell and beam-energy constraints. The cross section and 80 polarization and spin-correlation asymmetries in four disjoint bins of $\cos\theta_{W^-}$ are combined for both beam-polarization configurations through a covariance-based $\chi^2$. The two set of beam polarization offers an orthogonal cuts on parameter space leading to tighter bounds. The semi-leptonic and full-hadronic final states provides a competitive bounds on aTGCs, while full-leptonic offers the least sensitivity. Marginalized limits on aTGCs via. Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis for integrated luminosities for different values of integrated luminosities and systematic benchmarks are reported.

authors.name: Amir Subba, Ritesh K. Singh

papers.title: Lindblad-driven recombination of the X(3872) tetraquark
papers.summary: The internal structure of the exotic meson X(3872) remains an open question. We investigate its production in heavy-ion collisions under the hypothesis that it is a compact tetraquark. To this end, we derive a coalescence model from the Lindblad equation, assuming that unbound heavy quarks are thermalized within the quark-gluon plasma and that the adiabatic approximation holds. Using this model, we predict the nuclear modification factor of the X(3872) at LHC energies, with proton-proton baseline cross sections estimated from available experimental data. We also consider the effect of simplifying assumptions on the model, and a complementary approach based on chemical equilibration. Our results indicate that recombination is the dominant production mechanism for a tetraquark X(3872). It leads to a significant yield enhancement in heavy-ion collisions, suggesting that the nuclear modification factor is a powerful observable for probing the exotic nature of this state

authors.name: N\'estor Armesto, Miguel \'Angel Escobedo, Elena G. Ferreiro, V\'ictor L\'opez-Pardo

papers.title: Probing gluon saturation with forward di-hadron correlations in proton-nucleus collisions
papers.summary: We present a detailed numerical investigation of semi-inclusive forward di-hadron production in proton--nucleus collisions employing the Color Glass Condensate effective theory. We focus on the regime where di-hadrons are produced nearly back-to-back in the transverse plane, thereby justifying a transverse-momentum-dependent factorization approach in terms of small-$x$ gluon distributions. Our computation integrates several key elements: i) non-linear rapidity evolution via the Balitsky--Kovchegov equation with running coupling, ii) both perturbative and non-perturbative Sudakov resummation, and iii) a phenomenologically constrained model for the initial conditions for small-$x$ gluon distributions. We compare this phenomenological framework to experimental data from the STAR Collaboration on azimuthal correlations in forward di-pion production in both proton--proton and proton--gold collisions. We analyze the systematic theoretical uncertainties associated with the saturation scales of nuclei at the initial scale for rapidity evolution and with those associated with the hadronization process. Finally, we make predictions for the kinematics anticipated to be covered by the ALICE Forward Calorimeter (FoCal) upgrade at the Large Hadron Collider.

authors.name: Paul Caucal, Zhong-Bo Kang, Piotr Korcyl, Farid Salazar, Bj\"orn Schenke, Tomasz Stebel, Raju Venugopalan, Wenbin Zhao

papers.title: Critical fluctuation patterns and anisotropic correlations driven by temperature gradients
papers.summary: Studies of QCD phase transition signals are often conducted under spatially uniform temperature conditions. However, the influence of spatial temperature gradients on the signals emerging at the phase interface in the fireball generated by heavy-ion collisions has not yet been fully explored. Based on an Ising-like effective potential, we study the locally equilibrated systems with temperature gradients. In a 2D disk geometry, the low-energy fluctuation spectrum is explicitly resolved into radial and angular momentum modes. The nonlocal correaltions of singular eigen-mode exhibits strong anisotropy, which are long-ranged along isotherms but suppressed radially due to the thermal geometry of the system. Unlike homogeneous systems where the zero-momentum mode dominates, correlations in such inhomogeneous system result from the superposition of a series of zero and non-zero angular momentum modes with comparable contributions. We extract the singular angular momentum modes and establish their connection to experimentally observable anisotropic flow.
