We find azimuthally sensitive observables may offer a previously unexplored avenue for detecting the QCD phase transition.

authors.name: Lijia Jiang, Tao Yang, Jun-Hui Zheng

papers.title: Dark matter in classically conformal theories: WIMP and supercooling
papers.summary: Beyond solving the hierarchy problem, classically conformal (CC) theories naturally accommodate dark matter (DM). In this work, we explore the CC $SU(2)_X$ gauge theory with a triplet dark scalar, uncovering two distinct DM scenarios: weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) and supercooled DM. The production mechanisms are strongly influenced by the CC model's unique first-order phase transition evolution history, which differs significantly from those in non-conformal models. We obtain the viable parameter space for each scenario and investigate the current constraints and future sensitivities at experiments, demonstrating that gravitational wave signals from the phase transition provide a common detection channel for both the WIMP and supercooled DM regimes.

authors.name: Ke-Pan Xie, Cheng-Hao Zhan

papers.title: Higgs production in association with a Z boson at TeV-scale lepton colliders

authors.name: Hiroyuki Furusato, Satsuki Hosoya, Kentarou Mawatari, Shouta Suzuki

papers.title: $D^0$-$D_s^+$ Elliptic-Flow Splitting under Event-Shape Engineering: A Probe of Sequential Charm Hadronization
papers.summary: Recent work has proposed sequential hadronization of open-charm hadrons in the quark-gluon plasma, wherein more tightly bound species such as $D_s^+$ form earlier near $1.2 T_c$ and $D^0$ forms later at $T_c$. That work showed that this mechanism naturally reverses the sign of the $D^0-D_s^+$ elliptic-flow splitting relative to the conventional simultaneous baseline. In this work, we demonstrate that event-shape engineering (ESE) provides a sharper discrimination between the two pictures than inclusive measurements alone. By selecting large-$q_2$ and small-$q_2$ events in 0--10\% and 30--50\% centrality classes in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.02$ TeV, we show that the geometry-driven enhancement of charm-meson $v_2$ can be separated from the hadronization-time response: the positive $\Delta v_2(D^0-D_s^+)$ in the sequential scenario grows systematically with $q_2$, while the corresponding response slope $\chi$ reveals a species-dependent hierarchy $\chi(D^0) > \chi(D_s^+)$ that is robust against the overall flow normalization and absent in the simultaneous baseline. In the simultaneous case, the splitting is near zero or negative and does not follow the same geometry scaling. Notably, the semi-central 30--50\% class emerges as the optimal window, because the non-monotonic interplay between QGP lifetime and initial eccentricity maximizes the late-stage flow conversion. The $q_2$ ratios of the $D_s^+/D^0$ yield ratio remain close to unity, confirming that the splitting is a dynamical flow effect rather than a chemical yield modification. These results establish $\Delta v_2(D^0-D_s^+)$ and the response slope $\chi$ under ESE as complementary differential probes of the space-time structure of charm hadronization near the QCD transition temperature.

authors.name: Yu-Jie Huang, Wei Dai, Jiaxing Zhao, Tan Luo, Ben-Wei Zhang, Enke Wang

papers.title: Electroweak First-Order Phase Transition Triggered by Non-Gaussian Fluctuations of a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-Symmetric Spectator Scalar
papers.summary: We propose a novel mechanism to trigger a first-order cosmological electroweak phase transition using non-Gaussian primordial fluctuations of a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric spectator scalar field. We show that the large fluctuations of the spectator field can modify the Higgs thermal mass and enhance the thermal barrier, thereby enabling a strong first-order phase transition. Non-Gaussianities in the primordial fluctuation spectrum significantly increase the probability of large-amplitude fluctuations, allowing a substantial fraction of the Universe to undergo the transition. The spectator field also naturally serves as a cold dark matter candidate through its coherent oscillations, reproducing the observed relic abundance. The resulting stochastic gravitational-wave background peaks at $f\sim 10^{-3}-10^{-1}$ Hz, but its amplitude lies roughly ten orders of magnitude below the projected sensitivities of planned space-based and ground-based interferometers.

authors.name: Bo-Qiang Lu

papers.title: QCD sum-rule determination of the axial-vector mixing angle in the \(B_c(1P)\) sector
papers.summary: We determine the mixing angle between the \(1^1P_1\) and \(1^3P_1\) axial-vector states in the \(B_c(1P)\) sector using QCD sum rules. The operator product expansion includes the gluon condensates and the four-quark condensate up to dimension six, and the next-to-leading-order perturbative corrections to all three correlation functions; for the correlator of the axial-vector and tensor currents these corrections are calculated here for the first time. The analysis of the sum rules leads to \(\theta_{B_c(1P)}=(46.6\pm0.4)^\circ\) for the mixing angle between these two states. We also compare our result with theoretical studies available in the literature.

authors.name: T. M. Aliev, S. Bilmis, M. Savci

papers.title: $\lambda$, $\rho$, and $\sigma$ Regge trajectories for the quadruply heavy pentaquark $bb\bar{u}cc$ in the diquark-triquark picture
papers.summary: Systematic investigations of four series of Regge trajectories for quadruply heavy pentaquarks are still lacking. Using the diquark and triquark Regge trajectory relations, we propose the Regge trajectory relations for the quadruply heavy pentaquark ${bb\bar{u}cc}$: $M=2m_{b}+2m_{c}+m_{u}+5C/2 +\beta_{x_{\lambda}}(x_{\lambda}+c_{0x_{\lambda}})^{2/3} +\beta_{x_{\rho_1}}(x_{\rho_1}+c_{0x_{\rho_1}})^{2/3}+\beta_{x_{\rho_2}}\sqrt{x_{\rho_2}+c_{0x_{\rho_2}}} +\beta_{x_{\sigma}}(x_{\sigma}+c_{0x_{\sigma}})^{2/3}$. Four series of Regge trajectories, namely the $\lambda$-, $\rho_1$-, $\rho_2$-, and $\sigma$-trajectories, are investigated. We demonstrate that accounting for the internal structure and substructure of pentaquarks is indispensable for constructing the $\rho_1$-, $\rho_2$-, and $\sigma$-trajectories; without such structural considerations, functional form and trajectory parameters can only be obtained via pure fitting against theoretical or experimental data. We further prove that the Regge trajectories of diquark 1, triquark, and diquark 2 (embedded within the triquark) do not correspond one to one to the $\rho_1$-, $\rho_2$-, and $\sigma$-trajectories. Nevertheless, these trajectories govern the behaviors of the respective $\rho_1$-, $\rho_2$-, and $\sigma$-trajectories. For both configurations $(bb)(\bar{u}(cc))$ and $(cc)(\bar{u}(bb))$, the $\lambda$-, $\rho_1$-, and $\sigma$-trajectories exhibit behavior of $M{\sim}x^{2/3}$ ($x=n_{r_1},n_{r_3},l_1,l_3,N_{r},L$), whereas the $\rho_2$-trajectories exhibit behavior of $M{\sim}\sqrt{x}$ ($x=n_{r_2},\,l_2$). The functional behavior of Regge trajectories for diquarks and triquark offers guidance for fitting the pentaquark Regge trajectories. Additionally, we provide rough estimates for spin-averaged masses of the $\lambda$-, $\rho_1$-, $\rho_2$-, and $\sigma$-excited states.

authors.name: Xin-Ru Liu, Qi Liu, Jiao-Kai Chen

papers.title: Compositeness and decay properties of the flavor partner of $D^{*}_{s0}(2317)$
papers.summary: In view of the recent experimental finding of the heavy quark flavor partner of the $D_{s0}(2317)$ in the bottom sector, the $B_{s0}(5700)$, we perform a single and coupled-channel $B^{(*)}\bar{K}^{(*)}$ calculation in the hidden-gauge formalism within the on-shell and off-shell schemes, respectively. By fixing the $B\bar{K}$ bound state mass to the observed state with $J^P=0^+$, we also predict five new states with $J^P=\lbrace 0,1,2\rbrace^+$ in this sector, three of them with $J^P=1^+$. Additionally, in the coupled-channel calculation, two states with masses and decay widths similar to the $B_{sJ}(6114)$ and $B_{sJ}(6063)$ ones, with spins $J=0^+$ and $2^+$, respectivley, and decaying into $B\bar{K}$, are dynamically generated. Moreover, we evaluate the decay widths of the $B_{s0}$ and $B_{s1}$ states generated from $B^{(*)}\bar{K}$ through the isospin breaking decay mode $B_s^0\pi^0$ and $B_s^{*0}\pi^0$, respectively. We find that, because these states have large binding energies, the coupling to the bare component can reduce this decay width by more than half of the decay width, from $50$~keV in the purely molecular model to $10-20$~keV, when the $B_{s0}$ is coupled to the bare component. We also observe that, after considering heavy-quark-spin symmetry violating contributions, the decay width for the $B_{s1}$ becomes smaller than for the $B_{s0}$.

authors.name: J. S\'anchez-Illana, R. Molina, Pan-Pan Shi

papers.title: Revealing irregularities through distributional discrepancies in latent space via Stein-witness estimation
papers.summary: RIDDLE is a new method for resonant anomaly detection that uses a scalar Stein-witness function to identify discrepancies between unlabeled signal-region events and a background distribution inferred from dijet-mass sidebands. The witness is optimized in a latent representation of auxiliary jet observables against a differentiable background reference, without requiring an explicit signal model. The method is evaluated using simulated LHC Olympics dijet events and compared with its idealized and supervised benchmarks, which share the same statistical construction but use additional background or signal information, and with LaCATHODE as an independent anomaly detection method. RIDDLE demonstrates strong signal-background discrimination comparable to the idealized benchmark, generally outperforming LaCATHODE while largely preserving the background dijet-mass spectrum under anomaly-score selection. Tests incorporating additional angular information and deliberately mass-correlated features further demonstrate the method's robustness under the studied conditions. Together, these results highlight the potential of RIDDLE as a robust, data-driven approach for enhanced resonance searches that combines effective anomaly discrimination with background-shape preservation.

authors.name: Ali Eren Simsek

papers.title: Parton Branching evolution in updfevolv: NNLO spacelike evolution in the ZM-VFNS and NLO timelike evolution with heavy-flavour matching
papers.summary: We describe two extensions of the Parton Branching (PB) method as implemented in updfevolv: the next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) spacelike DGLAP evolution of parton densities in the zero-mass variable-flavour-number scheme (ZM-VFNS), and the leading and next-to-leading order (LO, NLO) timelike evolution of fragmentation functions, including the heavy-flavour matching conditions at the quark thresholds. We summarise the timelike PB formalism - momentum sum rule, Sudakov form factor, branching chain and kinematics. We give implementation details needed for the PB formalism to reproduce the semi-analytical solutions of APFEL for all flavours, including heavy quarks at threshold. This note supplements the updfevolv manual and is a technical release note for updfevolv version 2.6.0.

authors.name: H. Jung

papers.title: Electromagnetic Radiation from Baryon-Rich Matter in Heavy-Ion Collisions
papers.summary: We perform a study of electromagnetic radiation in heavy-ion collisions at Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC) Beam Energy Scan (BES) and SPS energies using the iEBE-MUSIC framework, which includes 3D dynamical Monte Carlo Glauber initial conditions, MUSIC (3+1)D viscous relativistic hydrodynamics, and the UrQMD hadronic afterburner. The multistage modeling has been calibrated to hadronic data at RHIC-BES energies using a Bayesian analysis. Integrating the thermal photon emission rates with the medium evolution, we study the direct photon yield and elliptic flow and how they vary with collision energy and emission source. We compare with results obtained by the STAR and PHENIX Collaborations. We employ next-to-leading order thermal QCD dilepton emission rates to compute dilepton invariant mass spectra and extract the effective temperature of the quark-gluon plasma at different collision energies.

authors.name: Xiang-Yu Wu, Charles Gale, Sangyong Jeon, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Paquet, Bj\"orn Schenke, Chun Shen

papers.title: Acoustic gravitational waves from primordial curvature perturbations
papers.summary: Standard perturbative calculations of scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) have neglected nonperturbative effects in the large-amplitude regime. We develop a hybrid numerical framework to signify nonperturbative effects on the stochastic gravitational wave (GW) background sourced by primordial curvature perturbations, focusing on the acoustic channel (fluid motions). Fully general-relativistic, spherically symmetric simulations are used to extract nonperturbative sound-shell profiles from isolated curvature peaks; these profiles are then embedded into three-dimensional lattice evolutions of relativistic hydrodynamics coupled to transverse-traceless metric perturbations to compute the acoustic GW spectra. The acoustic signal has a peak frequency determined by the comoving shell thickness, and its amplitude is extremely sensitive to the mean comoving separation of peaks, scaling approximately as $R_{*c}^{-7}$. We find a robust causal low-frequency tail $\propto k^{3}$, and the nonlinear hydrodynamic interactions can enhance the ultraviolet power. Comparing with SIGWs computed perturbatively from the same real-space configuration, we show that acoustic GWs can be amplified by an order of magnitude and display a peak shifted to a lower frequency in the large-amplitude regime. These results highlight the importance of nonperturbative effects for accurate predictions of stochastic GW signals induced from primordial curvature perturbations.

authors.name: Zhuan Ning, Zi-Yan Yuwen, Xiang-Xi Zeng, Rong-Gen Cai, Shao-Jiang Wang

papers.title: The production of lepton pairs in heavy-ion collisions at SPS and RHIC energies
papers.summary: We perform a quantitative study of dilepton production and elliptic flow in In+In collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=17.3$ GeV and isobar collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=200$ GeV, concentrating on the low and intermediate invariant mass regions. The medium evolution is simulated event-by-event with the multistage iEBE-MUSIC framework, and the electromagnetic emission combines for the first time quark-gluon plasma (QGP) emission calculated at next-to-leading order (NLO) in the strong coupling with in-medium radiation calculated with hadronic many-body theory. Freeze-out and surviving primordial $\rho$ decays are also included. The calculations are compared with the high-precision dimuon spectra measured by the NA60 Collaboration, and with STAR preliminary measurements of dielectron spectra and elliptic flow. We obtain effective temperatures extracted from the transverse-mass spectra, and we calculate the elliptic flow of the different dilepton sources. Our results suggest that dilepton measurements in the low-mass and high $p_T$ region can provide insight into higher-order corrections to the QGP emission rate.

authors.name: Xiang-Yu Wu, Han Gao, Charles Gale, Sangyong Jeon, Ralf Rapp

papers.title: Proceedings of "Accelerating ALICE background simulations: A WGAN Approach to slow-neutron induced TPC loopers" CHEP 2026, 26/05/2026
papers.summary: The simulation of background processes in high-energy physics can be computationally expensive and time-consuming. To provide the most realistic data description at the ALICE experiment using Monte Carlo simulations, we investigated alternative solutions to generate the products of electromagnetic interactions initiated by slow neutrons in the Time Projection Chamber (TPC). Specifically, electrons and positrons from these processes can spiral repeatedly within the magnetic field in the detector (so-called "loopers") and tracking them via full transport frameworks, such as GEANT4, requires extensive computing resources. A fast simulation framework based on a Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (WGAN) was developed to speed up the simulation process. Our solution is designed to bypass the significant computational cost associated with transporting neutrons to low energies by directly generating the kinematic properties (e.g., momentum, production vertex) of the resulting electron-positron pairs (from neutron capture) and electrons from Compton scattering. The generative model successfully reproduces the complex multidimensional distributions of the background tracks with high fidelity, maintaining agreement with the full GEANT4 simulation. By replacing the full transport of these specific background components with the WGAN inference, a tenfold speedup is achieved, making the simulation of loopers a negligible component of the total processing time. Moreover, the fast simulation framework is modular, allowing for the future inclusion of other background sources, such as nuclear spallation products.

authors.name: Marco Giacalone, Sandro Christian Wenzel, Mesut Arslandok, Andreas Morsch for the ALICE Collaboration

papers.title: Ratio of $\bar{\Lambda}$ to $K_\rm{S}^0$ production cross-sections in $pp$ collisions at 13.6TeV
papers.summary: The production cross-section ratio of promptly produced $\bar{\Lambda}$ and $K_\rm{S}^0$ hadrons is measured in proton-proton collision data at a centre-of-mass energy of 13.6TeV recorded in 2024 with the upgraded LHCb detector and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $64\rm{pb}^{-1}$. The ratio is presented as a function of transverse momentum, $p_\rm{T}$, and rapidity, $y$, in the ranges $0.15 < p_\rm{T} < 2.5\rm{GeV}/c$ and $2.0 < y < 4.5$. The results are in good agreement with previous measurements at different centre-of-mass energies. They are compared to predictions from currently available event generators and can be used as input in future event generator tunings.

papers.title: Letter of Intent: AN Underground Belayed In-Shaft (ANUBIS) detector
papers.summary: Long-lived particles (LLPs) arise naturally in many extensions of the Standard Model, notably in models with dark matter candidates or motivated by baryogenesis. LLPs produced at or above the electroweak scale with decay lengths of tens of metres escape the general-purpose LHC detectors and cannot be produced at sufficient rates in forward and beam-dump experiments. This Letter of Intent proposes the ANUBIS detector, which would instrument the ceiling of the ATLAS cavern and the bottom of its access shafts with about 1600~m$^2$ of resistive plate chambers in two tracking layers about 1~m apart, using the air-filled volume above the ATLAS detector as decay volume. The ANUBIS detector exploits the full ATLAS event information to suppress backgrounds, and exchanges triggers with the ATLAS experiment. With 3~ab$^{-1}$ at the High-Luminosity LHC, it would improve the sensitivity to exotic Higgs-boson decays into long-lived scalars by two to three orders of magnitude, probe heavy neutral leptons of all three flavours down to mixings of about $2\times10^{-8}$, and extend the reach for axion-like particles. The \textsl{pro}ANUBIS demonstrator, operated in the ATLAS cavern in 2024 and 2025, has validated the detector technology. The detector design, trigger concept, integration with the ATLAS experiment and a timeline towards installation in LHC Long Shutdown 4 are presented.

papers.title: Unexpected large relative strong phase and search for isospin breaking and $CP$ asymmetries in $J/\psi \to K^*(892)\bar K
papers.summary: Using a direct scan of 26 energy points near the $J/\psi$ resonance, we perform the first measurement of the relative phase $\phi_{\gamma, 3g}$ between the strong and electromagnetic amplitudes in $J/\psi\to\bar K^0 K^*(892)^0+\mathrm{c.c.}$ and $J/\psi\to K^+ K^*(892)^-+\mathrm{c.c.}$. Unexpectedly, the phase in the neutral channel is found to be $\sim 150^\circ$, deviating from orthogonality ($90^\circ$) by $4.8\sigma$ and from a relative real amplitude ($0^\circ$ or $180^\circ$) by $12.6\sigma$ or $2.8\sigma$, respectively. By contrast, the charged channel phase is consistent with $\sim 180^\circ$ within $1\sigma$, exhibiting channel-dependent behavior. The corresponding branching fractions are consistent with the world averages but achieve better than twofold improvement in precision. The ratios between the branching fractions of $J/\psi\to\bar K^0 K^*(892)^0+\mathrm{c.c.}$ and $J/\psi\to K^+ K^*(892)^-+\mathrm{c.c.}$ are also measured. After subtracting the electromagnetic contribution, the corresponding strong contribution ratios obey isospin symmetry within $1.4\sigma$. A search for direct $CP$ violation yields asymmetries consistent with zero.

papers.title: Strong and electromagnetic amplitudes, direct $CP$ and isospin asymmetries in the decays $J/\psi \to K^0_SK^+\pi^-+c.c.$
papers.summary: Using $e^+e^-$ annihilation data collected at 26 center-of-mass energy points between 3000.00 and $3119.88~\text{MeV}$ with the BESIII detector, corresponding to a total integrated luminosity of about $440.7~\text{pb}^{-1}$, we study the production cross section line shape of the $e^+e^-\to K_S^0 K^+\pi^-+c.c.$ process. A partial wave analysis is used to isolate the subprocesses $e^+e^-\to\bar K^0 K^*(892)^0+c.c.$ and $e^+e^-\to K^+ K^*(892)^-+c.c.$ with $K^*(892)^0\to K^+ \pi^-$ and $K^*(892)^-\to K_S^0 \pi^-$, respectively. The line shape fits determine the relative magnitude $\mathcal{C}$ and phase $\phi_{\gamma,3g}$ between the strong and electromagnetic amplitudes, together with the corresponding branching fractions $\mathcal{B}$. There is a twofold ambiguity in the relative phase determinations for two of the final states analyzed. Consequently, there are two equally possible sets of results on relative phase. For $(\phi_{\gamma,3g},\mathcal{C},\mathcal{B})$, the neutral mode has two solutions, $((147.0\pm 11.7)^\circ,\,3.80\pm 0.26,\,(4.62\pm 0.19)\times 10^{-3})$ and $((-146.0\pm 11.6)^\circ,\,3.85\pm 0.25,\,(4.80\pm 0.19)\times 10^{-3})$, whereas the charged mode has the single solution $((180.2\pm 35.2)^\circ,\,28.66\pm 2.68,\,(6.41 \pm 0.25)\times10^{-3})$. The neutral mode phase differs from $90^\circ$ by $4.8\sigma$, demonstrating that strong-electromagnetic orthogonality is not universal. The branching fractions agree with the world averages with substantially improved precision. A simultaneous fit to the neutral and charged channels gives that the neutral-to-charged strong contribution ratio $\mathcal{R}^{3g}_{K^*\bar K}=1.062\pm 0.070$ or $1.090\pm 0.063$, respectively, both consistent with isospin symmetry. The direct $CP$ asymmetry analysis shows no evidence for $CP$ violation. The uncertainties include both statistical and systematic contributions.

papers.title: A unified quenching model in Geant 4 simulation for $\alpha$, proton and electron particles in liquid scintillator detectors
papers.summary: The liquid scintillator (LS) detectors are widely used in reactor neutrino experiments. To precisely measure the oscillated neutrino spectrum, it is crucial to understand the LS energy response, especially the quenching effect. Numerous bench-top measurements have been conducted on quenching effects for $\alpha$ particles, protons, and electrons. These results have typically been described by Birks' law, but with different Birks' coefficients required for different particle species. In this study, we find that if more secondary electrons are allowed to be generated in Geant4 simulations, the bench-top results for all particles can be well fitted using a single Birks' coefficient of about $0.013~{\rm g\,cm^{-2}\,MeV^{-1}}$. The underlying reason is that a large fraction of the primary energy is deposited through the generation of $\delta$-electrons with energies below 4~keV, which should be tracked separately due to their different quenching behavior compared to primary particles. This study provides a unified framework for comparing Birks' coefficients from different bench-top measurements and helps experiments like JUNO and SNO+ better tune their simulations for precision energy measurements.

authors.name: Shubing Liu, Mingyuan Wang, Zeyuan Yu

papers.title: A measurement of the Higgs boson mass in the diphoton decay channel in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
papers.summary: A measurement of the Higgs boson mass in the diphoton decay channel is performed using proton-proton collision data at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV. The data set recorded with the CMS detector between 2016 and 2018 is used, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$. A refined detector calibration and new analysis techniques are employed to improve the precision of the results compared to earlier measurements. The Higgs boson mass is measured to be $m_\mathrm{H}$ = 125.13 $\pm$ 0.15 GeV = 125.13 $\pm$ 0.10 (stat) $\pm$ 0.12 (syst) GeV. In addition, a combination with the mass measurement at center-of-mass energies of 7 and 8 TeV in the diphoton final state is performed resulting in $m_\mathrm{H}$ = 125.06 $\pm$ 0.14 GeV = 125.06 $\pm$ 0.09 (stat) $\pm$ 0.11 (syst) GeV.

authors.name: CMS Collaboration

papers.title: Evidence of the $e^+ e^-\to f_1(1285)$ reaction with the CMD-3 detector at VEPP-2000
papers.summary: A search for the $e^+ e^-\to f_1(1285)$ reaction is performed with the CMD-3 detector at the VEPP-2000 collider. Data from a scan in the center-of-mass energy range Ec.m.=1.20--1.36 GeV with 109.1 pb$^{-1}$ of the integrated luminosity is used. A dedicated 51.7 pb$^{-1}$ have been collected at the $f_1(1285)$ resonance peak energy Ec.m.=1282 MeV, where $26.5 \pm 7.4$ events have been found in the $e^+ e^-\to\eta\pi^0\pi^0$ reaction. No indication of the signal is observed in the non-resonant scan data. We interpret the result as a statistical 4.5$\sigma$ evidence of the C-even resonance production in the $e^+ e^-\to f_1(1285)\to\eta\pi^0\pi^0$ reaction via the two-photon interaction. The production cross section is found to be $\sigma(e^+ e^-\to f_1) = 0.074 \pm 0.021 \pm 0.010$ nb, and the corresponding branching fraction to the $e^+ e^-$ pair is $B(f_1(1285)\to e^+e^-) = (8.3 \pm 2.3 \pm 1.1)\times 10^{-9}$.

papers.title: Unfreezing topology using out-of-equilibrium replica exchanges
papers.summary: Parallel Tempering on Boundary Conditions (PTBC) mitigates topological freezing by exchanging configurations between replicas that interpolate between periodic and open boundaries on a small defect. We generalize PTBC by replacing the instantaneous swap with a short out-of-equilibrium protocol, in which the defect couplings of two replicas are exchanged gradually while the fields around the defect are updated. We show that the swap rate depends only on the average work spent along the out-of-equilibrium trajectory by virtue of Crooks' and Jarzynski's fluctuation relations. From the theoretical derivation of the scaling of the work as a function of the number of replicas, protocol length, and defect size, we predict the swap rate and the optimal protocol length. These predictions are tested in the $2d$ $\mathrm{CP}^{N-1}$ model with $N=21$. The optimal setup agrees with the measured one, the total computational cost at fixed statistical precision decreases by $\gtrsim40\%$ with respect to standard PTBC for all explored lattice spacings, and the required number of replicas at fixed acceptance is halved.

authors.name: C. Bonanno, A. Bulgarelli, E. Cellini, R. Dionisio, A. Nada, D. Panfalone, D. Vadacchino, L. Verzichelli

papers.title: Lattice gauge theory computation of $1/m_Q$ and $1/m_Q^2$ corrections to the quarkonium potential
papers.summary: We compute the static quark-antiquark potential and its $1/m_Q$ and $1/m_Q^2$ corrections, i.e.\ the $1/m_Q$ potential and all $1/m_Q^2$ potentials, which can be expressed in terms of correlators of two field strength insertions, in SU(3) lattice gauge theory and provide parameterizations for quark-antiquark separations $0.2 \, \text{fm} \lesssim r \lesssim 0.7 \, \text{fm}$. The field strength insertions in generalized Wilson loops are renormalized using gradient flow, which also leads to small statistical uncertainties. All potentials are extrapolated to zero flow time and, in contrast to previous lattice studies, to the continuum, using three lattice spacings and four flow times. The spin dependent potentials are matched to the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ scheme at NLO and provided at $\mu = 3 \, \text{GeV}$. They can easily be converted to specific heavy quark masses, e.g.\ for Born-Oppenheimer effective field theory studies of quarkonium.

authors.name: Michael Eichberg, Marc Wagner

papers.title: OSIRIS-REx Lessons Learned Report: Insights from the Journey to Bennu and Back
papers.summary: OSIRIS-REx, NASA's third New Frontiers mission, was the first U.S. mission to return a sample from an asteroid. Proposed in 2010 for an \$811 million lifecycle cost, the mission was completed for \$828 million, returned more than \$52 million of Headquarters reserves unused, and delivered at least 121.6 g of pristine material from near-Earth asteroid (101955) Bennu in September 2023, more than twice the Level-1 requirement. It did so despite a surface far more rugged than predicted, the discovery of particle ejection, sampling in a regolith much weaker than expected, operations during the COVID-19 pandemic, and an off-nominal parachute sequence on Earth return. This report sets out the lessons learned by the mission's leadership across six areas: leadership and governance; cost, schedule and risk management; systems engineering; mission operations; sample return, curation and analysis; and data archiving. Recurring themes are that a PI-led structure integrating science, engineering and project management gives the discipline to make fast, informed decisions; that reserves and schedule margin spent early to retire risk, such as funding Natural Feature Tracking as a backup navigation system, buy the flexibility to absorb discovery; that heritage hardware reduces risk only when its verification and engineering knowledge are preserved; and that contamination knowledge, sample science and data stewardship are mission-long responsibilities, not post-flight tasks. Each section pairs background with specific recommendations for future sample-return and small-body missions.

authors.name: Dante S. Lauretta, Heather L. Enos, C. W. V. Wolner

papers.title: RIFT for the O4 era: operating points, calibration marginalization, and cross-code validation
papers.summary: The Rapid Iterative FiTting (RIFT) parameter inference algorithm provides a simulation-based-inference approach to efficient, highly-parallelized parameter inference for GW sources. In this paper, we describe improvements deployed during preparations for and analysis of O4 observations (versions 0.0.17.3--0.0.18.0) that broaden RIFT's reach for single-event inference with contemporary instruments. We provide additional options to increase compatibility and comparability with other codes, notably including (a) enhancing RIFT's capabilities for calibration marginalization; (b) managing our likelihood's internal, output, and time-interpolated representation; (c) introducing new coordinates for (transverse) spin and eccentric mean anomaly, enabling more robust inference of parameters with subtle and complex correlations to others, and (d) revised operating point choices better suited to the loudest, clearest signals. We identify and reconcile the most substantial sources of head-to-head likelihood differences between RIFT and other production inference codes, and describe automated waveform symmetry checks that detect upstream model regressions before they bias inference. Using the previously-reported RIFT/asimov interface for reproducible settings consistent with past work, we demonstrate these capabilities end to end.

authors.name: R. O'Shaughnessy, A. Jan, J. Lange, R. Mechum, N. Malagon

papers.title: RR Lyrae stars as distance indicators I. Sample selection and characterisation
papers.summary: RR Lyrae stars (RRL) are well-established Population II distance indicators, with period-metallicity-luminosity (PLZ) relations linking pulsational properties to absolute luminosity. Gaia parallaxes now allow these relations to be anchored to geometric distances with unprecedented precision, offering an independent route to the extragalactic distance scale. We present the first paper in a series aimed at deriving new empirical PLZ and metallicity-luminosity relations for RRL in the optical and near-infrared. We describe the selection and characterisation of a sample of bright nearby field RRL, with distances anchored to reliable Gaia DR3 parallaxes. We conducted a multi-band photometric campaign of 172 RRL: 101 in Johnson-Cousins UBVRI with the IAC80 telescope and 130 in JHKs with the IRSF telescope, with 59 stars in common. The iron abundances come from the Spectroscopic Rome RRL Catalog catalogue, mostly from high-resolution spectroscopy. The light curves were modelled with GLOESS (optical) and near-infrared templates, and the mean magnitudes, amplitudes, and Fourier parameters were derived via a bootstrap Monte Carlo method. The linear relations were fitted with a Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo method. The sample spans -3.4 to 0.2 dex in [Fe/H]. We found tight relations between the Fourier parameter $\phi_{31}$ in each optical and Gaia band and its V-band value for RRab stars (scatter below 0.06). The near-infrared amplitude ratios with respect to V or G increase continuously with period, without the break reported in globular clusters. We provide a homogeneous calibration of the colour at minimum light across all filter combinations from U-B to H-Ks, revealing significant period and metallicity dependences, and we use it to derive reddening estimates for 15 stars outside current 3D extinction maps.

authors.name: M. S\'anchez-Benavente, M. Monelli, M. Dall'Ora, V. F. Braga, J. P. Mullen, M. Marengo, N. Matsunaga, G. Bono, G. Fiorentino, C. Gallart, M. Marconi, I. Plaks, A. Capodagli, G. Ceci, C. E. Mart\'inez-V\'azquez, M. Tantalo

papers.title: Constraining Intergalactic Dust with Supernova Color Evolution: Current Constraints from DES and Forecasts for LSST and Roman
papers.summary: Dust is an important systematic in precision Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) cosmology, and while dust in the Milky Way and SN host galaxies has been extensively studied, the impact of potential intergalactic dust is less well constrained. Using estimates from B. M\'enard et al. (2010), we find that current intergalactic dust bounds could shift SN distance moduli by up to 0.02 mag at $z \gtrsim 1$ from simulations. However, we show dust models can be constrained independently by SN samples themselves via a specific predicted redshift-dependent evolution observed in SN colors. While current data from the Dark Energy Survey (DES) cannot distinguish between various amounts of intergalactic dust in our universe, we demonstrate that the Roman Space Telescope (Roman) will place a significant constraint on intergalactic dust models ($>$ 3$\sigma$). In contrast, the Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), even with its unprecedented statistics, will only reach $\lesssim$ 2$\sigma$ significance on any given intergalactic dust prediction relative to no dust. We propagate multiple parameterizations of intergalactic dust through to cosmology. For LSST, we see a $\sim$60% reduction in the figure of merit (FoM) for $w$CDM and a $\sim$20% reduction for $w_0w_a$CDM, and for Roman, a $\sim$20% reduction in the FoM for $w$CDM and a $\sim$5% reduction for $w_0w_a$CDM. Utilizing Roman as an external constraint on dust for LSST results in a slightly improved FoM ($\sim$50% reduction) for $w$CDM for LSST. Finally, we show that intergalactic dust uncertainties decrease the FoM of the previous DES analysis (16.9% for $w$CDM and 8.1% for $w_0w_a$CDM) and that intergalactic dust cannot explain away recent hints for evolving dark energy.
