papers.title: When precision exceeds fidelity: systematic error quantification for inference with misspecified simulators
papers.summary: As scientific datasets grow in complexity and precision, the primary source of uncertainty in parameter inference shifts from measurement noise to systematic errors within the simulators themselves. In this setting, Bayesian evidence concentrates on whichever misspecified model best approximates the data. Evidence-weighted model averaging can then underestimate systematic uncertainty when one model component compensates for the misspecification of another component. We posit that in this case, the key question is how each model responds to discrepancies between simulator and data. We show that the local response of an inferred parameter to perturbations in the data --- the model's influence map --- can be estimated efficiently from forward evaluations of the simulator at existing posterior samples. Propagating discrepancy residuals through these influence maps enables individual sources of systematic bias to be isolated. Applied to independent observations used to infer the mass of a supermassive black hole, we find that the error is dominated by model systematics. We identify a simplification shared by all models, propagate the discrepancies through each model's influence map, and apply a first-order correction of the resulting biases. This substantially improves the cross-observation consistency of the inferred black-hole mass within each model while preserving the between-model spread that represents remaining systematics.

authors.name: M. J. Yantovski-Barth, Hengyue Zhang, Nolan Smyth, Aristeidis Amvrosiadis, Martin Bureau, Yashar Hezaveh, Laurence Perreault-Levasseur

papers.title: line racer: Rapid Calculation of Exoplanetary Radiative Opacities
papers.summary: Detailed studies of exoplanet and brown dwarf atmospheres rely on precise knowledge of the spectral features of possible atmospheric species. These features are a result of the interaction of different molecules and atoms with the radiation of the host star or the intrinsic thermal radiation of the object. The interaction is described by the opacity of a species, which determines how much light is absorbed at a given wavelength. The strength and shape of these opacities are very dependent on the temperature and pressure of the atmosphere, which is why they have to be calculated for a wide range of conditions. line racer is a Python package that enables computing high-resolution opacities from large molecular and atomic line lists in an effective manner. It offers users a wide range of options to customize opacity calculations to their needs and available hardware. The code is designed for efficient parallelization on multi-core and multi-node systems and can produce outputs compatible with popular atmospheric modeling and retrieval tools.

authors.name: David B. H\"agele, Paul Molli\`ere, Michiel Min

papers.title: CHEX-MATE: Probing the thermal$-$non-thermal connection in radio halo clusters with LoTSS-DR2
papers.summary: The main baryonic component of galaxy clusters is in the form of a hot plasma observed in the X-rays. In addition, clusters host a non-thermal component (relativistic particles and magnetic fields) which is studied mainly via radio telescopes and is dynamically coupled to the thermal plasma. These two components evolve together within the system and are subject to both micro and macro-physical processes which can be traced only with deep and detailed observations. We present the first homogeneous spatially resolved radio--X-ray study of 18 radio halo clusters combining CHEX-MATE and the LOFAR Two metre Sky Survey DR2. Radio ($I_R$) and X-ray ($I_X$) surface brightness are clearly correlated (Spearman coefficient $r_s \ge 0.5$), following a typically sublinear $I_R-I_X$ relation ($67 \pm 5\%$ of the sample) that appears to be independent of other cluster properties, although a tentative trend with mass/redshift may be worth exploring with larger samples. When inspecting such a relation as a function of the radius, we observe a variety of behaviours, which suggest that the interplay between the thermal and non-thermal plasma components varies with radius. We find the averaged slope profile of dynamically disturbed clusters to be consistent with expectations from turbulent re-acceleration models where a constant ratio between cosmic-ray electron and thermal energy densities is assumed. Differently, less perturbed clusters require an increasing cosmic-ray-to-thermal energy ratio with radius. Finally, we show that radio halo surface-brightness profiles can be effectively rescaled using X-ray information and theoretical expectations. This procedure significantly reduces their scatter and reveals common underlying trends based on the cluster dynamics, resembling what is observed for the thermal ICM, and strengthening the idea of a strong interplay between these two plasma components.

authors.name: M. Balboni, F. Gastaldello, A. Bonafede, Y. E. Bahar, I. Bartalucci, A. Botteon, H. Bourdin, G. Brunetti, R. Cassano, F. De Luca, S. Ettori, M. Gaspari, M. Gitti, A. Ignesti, C. Jones, L. Lovisari, P. Mazzotta, E. Pointecouteau, G. W. Pratt, M. Rossetti, J. Sayers, M. Sereno, R. J. van Weeren, S. De Grandi, S. Ghizzardi

papers.title: The fate of Mercury's ejected mantle
papers.summary: Mercury's unusually high core mass fraction, inferred from its high bulk density, remains difficult to explain. Mantle stripping by a giant impact provides a plausible origin, but without efficient removal, the ejected debris remains on Mercury-crossing orbits and later gets re-accreted. Here, we show that re-accretion of impact debris onto Mercury is inefficient, making a giant-impact origin plausible. We combine N-body simulations of giant-impact ejecta with a collisional evolution model and consideration of processes acting on small dust. We find that, when the ejecta are dominated by large, several hundred km-sized non-vaporized fragments, the debris disk remains optically thin and the collisional cascade is truncated near the radiation-pressure blowout limit, where micron-sized grains are removed. In contrast, if vaporized, the ejecta recondense into mm to cm-sized droplets and form an optically thick disk, in which radiation pressure cannot efficiently truncate the cascade. The debris can then be ground down to nanometre-sized grains, where collisions become predominantly non-fragmenting and dissipative rather than destructive. Subsequent inelastic collisions damp the eccentricities and inclinations of the nanodust, producing a geometrically thin disk whose lifetime is governed by removal through exposed surface layers, where grains acquire large charge-to-mass ratios through solar UV radiation and are rapidly removed by electromagnetic forces. In either scenario, collisional evolution strongly reduces the re-accretion of debris and alleviates a key difficulty for the giant-impact origin of Mercury's large core. More broadly, highly energetic giant impacts in the inner regions of planetary systems may lead to short-lived populations of nanometre-sized dust.

authors.name: Tuhin Ghosh, Mark Wyatt, Alan P. Jackson, Oliver Shorttle, Maximilian Sommer

papers.title: Evidence for an Evolving Surface on the Partly Burnt Runaway Stellar Remnant GD 492
papers.summary: GD 492 (LP 40-365) is a partly burnt, hypervelocity runaway stellar remnant thought to have survived a thermonuclear supernova. We analyze 12 sectors of TESS photometry spanning more than four years to investigate the previously reported 8.9-hr photometric modulation of the star. We find that the modulation changes with time, with individual-sector fits yielding apparent periods ranging from 8.8606 to 8.9048 hr (0.5% changes), more than 25 times the formal measurement uncertainties. Both the period and shape of the modulation evolve on a timescales of approximately one to two months. We show qualitatively that a two-spot model with evolving surface structure can reproduce several of the observed light-curve morphologies, although the geometry of the spots is not uniquely constrained. These observations suggest that changing surface inhomogeneities are a plausible origin of the photometric variability. Differential rotation and magnetic activity may contribute to this evolution, potentially providing new constraints on the outer convective structure of GD 492 and on the interpretation of its atmospheric abundances.

authors.name: Reuben Dsouza, J. J. Hermes, Boris T. G\"ansicke, Ken J. Shen, Ciarra Coston, Roberto Raddi, Mark Hollands

papers.title: A Tale of Two Type IIb Supernovae: Radio-loud and Radio-silent Candidate Counterparts to Sub-solar Mass Gravitational-wave Triggers
papers.summary: On 2025 November 12, the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration reported S251112cm, a gravitational-wave (GW) candidate from a compact binary merger with at least one sub-solar-mass component. Optical follow-up identified SN 2025adtq, a Type IIb supernova (SN) within the localization volume that exploded a few days before the merger. SN 2025adtq is the second Type IIb SN found to be potentially coincident with a sub-solar-mass GW candidate, after SN 2025ulz (S250818k). A key question is whether such SNe harbor fast, possibly collimated ejecta from a central engine, as invoked in ``superkilonova'' scenarios for forming sub-solar-mass neutron stars. We present deep Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array observations of SN 2025adtq from the JAGWAR program, spanning 139-216 days after the GW trigger at 6-10 GHz. The radio properties of SN 2025adtq differ substantially from those of SN 2025ulz: whereas SN 2025ulz has a significant 6-10 GHz counterpart, SN 2025adtq remains undetected to 3sigma limits of ~7.8 uJy, implying a radio luminosity density one order of magnitude below that of SN 2025ulz at a comparable epoch, excluding jet models that remained viable for SN 2025ulz. This diversity in radio properties calls for systematic multi-wavelength follow up observations of candidate sub-solar events in future runs of the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA detectors.

authors.name: Tanner O'Dwyer (JHU), Alessandra Corsi (JHU), Raphael Baer-Way (NRAO), Mansi M. Kasliwal (Caltech), Poonam Chandra (NRAO), David L. Kaplan (UWM), Kunal P. Mooley (IITK), Deepika Yadav (IITK)

papers.title: Beyond the blur: Radial binning trumps stellar migration in resolved star formation histories
papers.summary: Spatially resolved galaxy properties are routinely derived from integral-field spectroscopy and increasingly from multi-band photometry as a wealth of photometric data become available in large surveys like LSST/Rubin. Spatially resolved star formation histories (SFHs) offer a detailed view of galaxy growth and quenching by tracing the timing and location of star formation within a galaxy up to one billion years in the past. However, stellar migration between spaxels may strongly bias these reconstructions. Quantifying this bias remains challenging as few Milky-Way mass simulations fully resolve initial stellar dispersions or migration rates. We use the well-validated h277 Milky-Way-mass cosmological zoom simulation, which resolves both via explicitly tying star formation to the non-equilibrium abundance of H2, to assess the quality of specific star formation rates (sSFR) radial profiles inferred from resolved SFHs against actual values from stellar particle tracking. Across several evolutionary windows spanning a range of stellar activity stages from quiescent to star-bursting, we find that the adaptive radial binning imposed by S/N constraints in photometric SED fitting actually mitigates most of the blurring/mixing effects of stellar migration on inferred radial profiles up to lookback times of 1.5 Gyr. This allows for proper recovery of not only the average sSFR but also its radial slope, its relative changes in scatter across radial annuli and even approximate localization of low-z star-forming clumps. Only galaxies having undergone a major merger across the considered lookback time display discrepant, unreliable sSFR profiles, hence should not be considered for such reconstructions.

authors.name: Charlotte Olsen, Charlotte Welker, Ena Chia, Anna C Wright

papers.title: Acoustic Priors from the Latest Cosmic Microwave Background Data
papers.summary: We revisit the physics of the acoustic peaks and illustrate how early-Universe information in the cosmic microwave background (CMB) can be disentangled from late-time signatures imprinted by gravitational lensing and the integrated Sachs-Wolfe (ISW) effect. Applying this separation to Planck PR4, ACT DR6, and SPT-3G D1 temperature and polarization data combined with the joint lensing reconstruction, we update the model-independent constraints on the angular acoustic scale and the physical densities, $100\theta_*=1.04100\pm0.00021$, $\omega_{\rm b}=(2.2440\pm0.0099)\times10^{-2}$, and $\omega_{\rm bc}=0.1410\pm0.0011$. These constraints are consistent with the previous Planck PR4-only analysis and remain stable for extended late-time cosmologies beyond $\Lambda$CDM. Adding ACT DR6 to the combination favors a higher $\omega_{\rm b}$ and, through their correlation, a higher primordial tilt $n_{\rm s}$ than PR4 alone. The reconstructed lensing spectrum exceeds that of $\Lambda$CDM, with two features near $L\simeq50$ and $L\sim10^3$, and the excess is reduced when WMAP replaces the Planck primary spectra. Marginalizing over the lensing-induced peak smoothing, rather than tying it to the late-time model, lowers the preference of the CMB and DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) for $w_0w_a$CDM over $\Lambda$CDM from $3.0\sigma$ to $1.9\sigma$, or from $3.2\sigma$ to $2.4\sigma$ when Union3.1 supernovae are added. We further use the acoustic prior to predict BAO distances from CMB data alone under several late-time expansion histories, testing their consistency with DESI measurements assuming standard pre-recombination physics.

authors.name: Kushal Lodha, Jun-Qian Jiang, Purba Mukherjee, Arman Shafieloo

papers.title: Toward Automated Strong-Lens Modeling with Agentic Workflows: An Application to Euclid Q1 Lenses
papers.summary: Ongoing and forthcoming wide-field surveys will discover $O(10^5)$ galaxy-galaxy strong lenses, shifting the main bottleneck from detection to reliable physical modeling. Conventional forward-modeling pipelines still rely on case-by-case expert judgment and manual tuning to mask contaminants, initialize priors, diagnose unphysical fits, and reconfigure failed runs. We present Lens-Orchestra, an automated workflow coupling a team of multimodal large language model agents to multi-stage physical modeling with elliptical power-law mass profiles, external shear, and pixelized source reconstructions. Launched via natural-language instructions, it modeled 185 Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1) grade-A lens candidates with published mass models without human intervention, completing 149 fits. Independent human evaluation confirmed 140 usable models, including 126 grade-I fits with noise-level residuals (with only 6.0% of completed fits unacceptable), and endorsed all 36 halted runs. Across the 140 usable systems, effective Einstein radii match released Q1 models (+0.12% median offset; 2.73% typical scatter), while hierarchical inference on the 126 grade-I imaging-only fits yields a mean mass-density slope of $2.002 \pm 0.009$ (intrinsic scatter $0.074^{+0.007}_{-0.006}$). A dedicated residual-screening agent also guided the selection of two candidate low-mass perturbers for parametric and free-form substructure modeling; although neither was confirmed, this end-to-end search illustrates how automated screening focuses computationally intensive substructure analyses on a few promising systems. Coupling multimodal agents to explicit forward modeling thus enables accurate, survey-scale lens analysis from macro mass profiles to small-scale dark matter structure.

authors.name: Xiaoyue Cao, Ran Li, Yunlong Yin, Rui Li, Liang Gao

papers.title: Planetary biotechnospheres, biotechnosignatures and the search for extraterrestrial intelligence
papers.summary: The concept of planetary intelligence as collective intelligence is used to consider possible evolutionary paths of biotechnospheres that emerge on the intersection of the technosphere with the biosphere and support coupling of the technosphere with the biosphere, thus affecting planetary evolution. In mature biotechnospheres, the intelligence of technologies and the intelligence of life forms, including engineered life forms, could act in concert to perform various tasks (e.g. monitoring and restoring planetary environments and biodiversity; supporting space missions; terraforming cosmic objects). Space exploration can expand biotechnospheres beyond planets and create cosmic ecosystems. Humankind, other civilizations or their intelligent machines may produce biotechnosignatures (i.e. observables and artefacts of biotechnospheres) in the Solar System and beyond. I propose ten possible biotechnosignatures and strategies for the search for these biotechnosignatures in situ and over interstellar distances. For example, if a non-human advanced civilization existed and built biotechnospheres on Earth in the past, the descendants of its engineered bacteria could currently exist on Earth and have properties pertaining to the functions of the ancient bacteria in the biotechnospheres; intelligent technologies created by the ancient civilization could migrate to the Solar System's outer regions; these two scenarios are described as the Cosmic Descendants hypothesis. Interstellar asteroids, free-floating planets, spacecraft and objects gravitationally bound to flyby stars might carry extraterrestrial biotechnospheres and pass through the Solar System. In connection to the fate of post-main-sequence stars and their Oort clouds, the probability for interstellar asteroids to carry biotechnospheres or to be interstellar spacecraft is estimated as very low.

authors.name: Irina K. Romanovskaya

papers.title: Photometric Uncertainty Correction for Time-Domain Surveys: Vera C. Rubin Data Preview 2 Case Study
papers.summary: Time-domain science, from variability detection to supernova cosmology, relies on accurate photometric uncertainties. We present a data-driven, catalog-level method to validate and improve the photometric uncertainties reported by time-domain surveys. The analysis is based on transforming light curves of non-variable objects into mean-variance whitened signals. We then estimate a correction to the uncertainties by matching the distribution of the whitened signals of all objects to the standard normal distribution, which they ought to follow when the uncertainties are correct. The correction can be modeled as a function of each measurement's flux, reported uncertainty, and available observational metadata, and can be applied to measurements of both non-variable and variable objects. Applied to the Rubin Observatory Data Preview 2 (DP2), the method shows that the uncertainties of bright sources are underestimated by up to a factor of five. The inferred corrections correspond to a magnitude error floor of about 10 mmag for both direct-image and difference-image photometry, decreasing to about 6 mmag in deeper fields. We provide the corrected uncertainties as part of the Rubin DP2 HATS catalogs.

authors.name: Konstantin Malanchev, Doug Branton, Sandro Campos, Neven Caplar, Mi Dai, Melissa DeLucchi, Olivia Lynn, Rachel Mandelbaum, Sean McGuire, Inar Timiryasov

papers.title: A Variability Metric Pipeline for AGN studies
papers.summary: Variability in active galactic nuclei (AGNs) is remarkably diverse, spanning multiple timescales, wavelengths, and physical processes. Variability probes accretion physics and the interplay between supermassive black holes and their surroundings. Building on early case studies, the field has shifted toward population-level analyses of increasingly large datasets, making scalable techniques crucial for upcoming time-domain surveys. We developed a Python-based pipeline to analyze AGN light curves using variability metrics and applied it to 14,061 nearby AGNs ($z\lesssim 0.09$) observed with ZTF. We examined metric distributions and correlations. Amplitude-based metrics (e.g., $F_{\rm var}$) help identify major flares but are sensitive to single deviant epochs. Temporal metrics such as $\eta$ provide a complementary check. Comparison with WISE infrared photometry suggests that $\eta$ traces the strength of AGN activity. Most Type~I and Type~II AGNs in our sample exhibit similar variability patterns based on these metrics. This overlap may partly reflect misclassifications that targeted spectroscopic follow-up could help resolve. To identify subsets of AGNs with distinctive variability, we used UMAP to group sources with similar metric values. The resulting embedding shows a region enriched in high-amplitude variables, including a subset with long-term flux trends. We find evidence that extremely variable quasars and changing-look AGNs may populate this region, which can help prioritize sources for follow-up. Our pipeline offers a scalable, survey-agnostic framework suitable for application to Vera C. Rubin Observatory's LSST and other ongoing and upcoming photometric surveys.

authors.name: Diego Mart\'inez Collipal (UdeC), Swayamtrupta Panda (NOIRLab)

papers.title: Stellar Obliquities of Cold Jupiter and Brown Dwarf Systems I: Spin-Orbit Misalignment Grows with Orbital Eccentricity
papers.summary: Stellar obliquity provides insights into the formation and dynamical evolution of planetary systems. Most obliquity measurements to date have focused on close-in transiting giant planets, whose orbits may have been altered by migration and tidal interactions. In contrast, the stellar obliquities of cold Jupiters, the most common class of giant planets, remain largely unexplored. Here, we measure the minimum stellar obliquity for 69 cold Jupiters and brown dwarfs (M_p > 0.3 M_J, a > 1 au), by comparing stellar inclinations derived from stellar rotation measurements with companion orbital inclinations constrained by radial velocities, relative astrometry and Hipparcos-Gaia absolute astrometry. We find that spin-orbit misalignments are common among cold Jupiters and brown dwarf companions, with 19/69 (28 +6/-5%) exhibiting significant misalignments. Furthermore, the stellar obliquities depends strongly on orbital eccentricity, whereby 0/17 (0 +8/-0%) companions with e_orb <= 0.15 are misaligned, compared to 19/52 (37 +7/-6%) with more eccentric orbits. This pattern reveals a connection between orbital eccentricity and stellar obliquity: companions on nearly circular orbits tend to be aligned with their host stars, whereas those on eccentric orbits exhibit a broader range of obliquities. This finding suggests that post-formation dynamical interactions, such as planet-planet scattering or secular chaos, may play an important role in exciting both orbital eccentricities and spin-orbit misalignments.

authors.name: Lauren I. Biddle, Jingwen Zhang

papers.title: 3D Shape Recovery of Human-Made Space Objects from Light Curves with Image Denoisers as Priors
papers.summary: This study presents a denoiser-regularized framework for recovering the three-dimensional convex shapes of human-made space objects from unresolved light curves. These shape estimates support object characterization for space situational awareness and mission support. Conventional methods for recovering the extended Gaussian image (EGI) using nonnegative least squares and directional refinement can discard surface-normal information needed to represent curved surfaces. The proposed framework represents the EGI as an area image on an equirectangular grid and recovers it in a randomly rotated frame using the plug-and-play alternating direction method of multipliers with a domain-adapted DRUNet denoiser. It then reconstructs a convex polytope from the recovered area image using scale-invariant support optimization with analytical gradients and volume normalization. Across seven faceted and curved shapes, with 10 runs per condition, the proposed method increases mean convex-hull intersection over union (IoU) from 0.615 for the baseline to 0.872 at a signal-to-noise ratio of 30 dB. Mean Hausdorff distance decreases from 0.198 to 0.050, and mean Chamfer distance decreases from 0.167 to 0.041. All three metrics improve for six of the seven shapes. The proposed method also retains much of its accuracy under noise, with mean IoU decreasing from 0.881 for noiseless measurements to 0.854 at 20 dB.

authors.name: Daigo Kobayashi, Carolin Frueh

papers.title: No Cluster Left Behind I: Joint Mass Calibration for Dark Energy Survey and South Pole Telescope Clusters
papers.summary: Multiwavelength observations of galaxy clusters are among the most promising probes of the growth of structure and dark energy. Optically identified clusters have a high number density and can thus probe the halo mass function well into the group regime, but their weak-lensing mass calibration suffers from a selection bias induced by line-of-sight projection effects. Clusters detected via their intracluster medium (ICM) -- through X-ray emission or the thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect (SZe) -- are less affected by such selection biases, but current survey sensitivity restricts ICM-selected samples to high-mass systems. Previous multiwavelength analyses tend to limit to clusters with millimeter detections and thus to the high-mass population. In this paper, we propose a flexible modeling framework in which all clusters from multiwavelength surveys can be combined and modeled, even if they are detected in only one survey. As a pilot study, we jointly model richness and lensing of clusters from the Dark Energy Survey and the SZe signal from the South Pole Telescope. This approach yields precise cluster mass calibration while self-consistently constraining optical selection biases. We have found a $\sim$20% bias in the large-scale lensing signal of clusters selected by richness, and a bias ranging from $\sim-20$% at low richness to zero at high richness for clusters selected by both richness and SZe. Compared to current approaches, this framework is highly scalable and readily extensible, paving the way for the full utilization of multiwavelength cluster data in next-generation surveys.

authors.name: C. Zhou, A. N. Salcedo, S. Grandis, T. Jeltema, M. Costanzi, L. E. Bleem, A. Farahi, M. Gatti, T. Shin, F. K\'eruzor\'e, C. L. Reichardt, J. H. Esteves, M. Aguena, S. Allam, D. Bacon, J. Blazek, S. Bocquet, D. Brooks, D. L. Burke, R. Camilleri, J. Carretero, L. N. da Costa, T. M. Davis, D. L. DePoy, S. Desai, P. Doel, A. E. Evrard, J. Garc\'ia-Bellido, D. Gruen, G. Gutierrez, D. L. Hollowood, D. J. James, K. Kuehn, O. Lahav, J. L. Marshall, J. Mena-Fern\'andez, R. Miquel, R. L. C. Ogando, A. A. Plazas Malag\'on, A. Porredon, A. K. Romer, E. Sanchez, D. Sanchez Cid, I. Sevilla-Noarbe, E. Suchyta, M. E. C. Swanson, V. Vikram, N. Weaverdyck, J. Weller

papers.title: Over a Half-decade Study of Crab Giant Pulses Observed with I-LOFAR
papers.summary: This work details the analysis of 1,048,138 single pulses from the Crab pulsar detected with the Irish LOFAR station over a 6-year observation campaign spanning 154 epochs and 347.9 hours at 110-190 MHz. Of the detections in the sample 550,445 are giant pulses (GPs, with S/N $\geq$ 10), making it the largest analysed sample to date. The power law indices for the S/N, flux density and fluence distributions range from 3.0-3.4 for the main pulse population and 3.3-3.5 for the inter-pulse population. A subset of 5,474 GPs (with S/N $\geq$ 100) were used to model scattering across the observing band to investigate the entanglement of dispersion measure (DM) and scattering. It was found that DM and scattering have a strong correlation coefficient of 0.70-0.71 across the entire campaign. Removing the long-term trend using a running median windowed at 125-190 days lowers the correlation to 0.48-0.50 respectively. The implications of these DM and scattering observations from the perspective of both the Crab Nebula's structure and the solar wind are discussed, including a rise in DM from August to October 2024 indicating AU-scale density variation consistent with fine substructure within Rayleigh-Taylor shaped filamentary ejecta.

authors.name: Owen A. Johnson, David J. McKenna, Sai C. Susarla, Evan F. Keane, Letizia Vincetti, Joseph P. McCauley, Aaron Golden

papers.title: Superfit: A Supernova Spectral Classification Tool with Host-Galaxy Decomposition
papers.summary: Superfit is a an open-source tool for automated spectroscopic classification of supernovae that accounts for redshift, reddening, and host-galaxy contamination. Here we present the latest version, which has been rewritten in Python and is now available as a web-based application. A user uploads an observed spectrum, and Superfit uses a curated library of transient and galaxy spectra to perform a simultaneous fit of transient and host galaxy spectra, while adjusting for color and redshift. In contrast to machine-learning algorithms, Superfit uses a least squares fitting approach, which is reproducible, verifiable, and understandable to users. The user may specify the binning of the spectra, set redshift and reddening limits, phase information, and restrict host galaxy and supernova templates for fitting. A new, expanded template library includes modern transient subclasses and associated observational metadata. A modern browser-based interface allows users to configure fitting parameters, visualize spectra, monitor fitting progress, and interactively inspect and compare ranked candidate matches and their individual components. We describe the fitting methodology, template library, software architecture, and web interface, and demonstrate its capabilities through classification examples.

authors.name: D. Andrew Howell, Alyona Kosobokova, Samantha Goldwasser, Ido Irani, Saanvi Tiwary, Ofer Yaron, Avishay Gal-Yam

papers.title: Moon Radio Interferometer for Science and Exploration (MoonRISE): A Mission Concept for a Low-Frequency Radio Interferometer on the Lunar Farside
papers.summary: The universe below 20 MHz remains one of space science's last unexplored frontiers, inaccessible from Earth due to its ionosphere and terrestrial radio frequency interference (RFI). We present the mission concept for the Moon Radio Interferometer for Science and Exploration (MoonRISE), an all-sky imaging, low-frequency radio telescope operating from 100 kHz-30 MHz from the lunar farside, the quietest radio environment in the inner Solar System. If realized, MoonRISE would be the first radio interferometer on the Moon and the first connected-element radio interferometer in space. Its science objectives are to (1) determine how solar wind turbulence drives plasma heating, acceleration, and space weather evolution in the inner heliosphere, by measuring the scattering of type III solar radio bursts between 2-20 solar radii; (2) constrain the density, structure, and variability of the lunar ionosphere and its effects on surface communication; and (3) resolve the plasma sources and magnetospheric dynamics that power Uranian Kilometric Radiation, observable for the first time since Voyager 2 in 1986. The same observations would yield all-sky maps of the low-frequency sky, subsurface structure at the landing site, and a characterization of the farside RF environment. The Radio Interferometer concept consists of nine 3.5 m dipoles embedded in a 1.5 km optical-fiber tether deployed by a rover, with power- and RF-over-fiber enabling RFI-free mapping. A rover-mounted Ground Penetrating Radar (300-2000 MHz) would measure regolith dielectric properties and bedrock depth to characterize the dipoles' RF performance. We describe the science objectives, a reference landing site in Lacus Luxuriae, a notional concept of operations, and the payload design and technology maturity. The concept builds on SunRISE and OVRO-LWA heritage and could serve as a basis for a future selected mission.

authors.name: Saptarshi Bandyopadhyay, Marin Anderson, Alexander Hegedus, Kalind Carpenter, Jack Burns, Andrew Romero-Wolf, Nivedita Mahesh, Olga Verkhoglyadova, Gregor Steinbr\"ugge, Benjamin Byron, Garth Franklin, Mark Haynes, Adrian Tang, Nacer Chahat, Christine Gebara, David Bugby, Roxanne Arellano, Malcolm Wright, Clara MacFarland, Matthew Keyawa, Gaurangi Gupta, Ashish Goel, Travis Brown, Ansel Barchowsky, James Stone, Gregg Hallinan, Judd Bowman, James Lux, Kathryn Plant

papers.title: Inference of Cosmic Dawn and Reionization Parameters from the 21 cm Global Spectrum Measurement of the DSL Mission
papers.summary: The 21 cm global spectrum is an important observable for cosmic dawn and epoch of reionization. The Discovering the Sky at the Longest Wavelengths mission (DSL, also known as Hongmeng), will measure the 21 cm global spectrum from the lunar orbit, thus avoiding the systematic effects common in ground based experiments, potentially producing the most accurate measurement to date. In this paper, we present a Bayesian inference framework, and investigate the constraints that can be placed on the cosmic dawn and reionization model parameters, either from the 21 cm global spectrum data alone, or from its combination with 21\,cm spatial power-spectrum data. For the global spectrum data, we assume a residual error equivalent to the thermal noise of a total observation of 30, 300, or 3000 orbit cycles of DSL. For the power spectrum, we adopt representative forecasts for HERA or SKA-Low. We find that there is generally a degeneracy between the foreground and the 21 cm global signal, and one has to make some restrictions on the form of either the foreground or the 21 cm global spectrum to break this degeneracy. Using the physically motivated emulator 21cmEMU, we generate the 21 cm global spectrum and power spectrum under a common astrophysical parameterization, while marginalizing over the foreground parameters. We derive constraints for two representative models, with their global spectrum absorption minimum at 105 and 94 MHz respectively. With only the global spectrum data, there remains much degeneracy in the astrophysical parameters. We find that the spatial power spectrum is highly complementary to the global spectrum, which can break the degeneracy and tighten up the constraints significantly.

authors.name: Chengliang Xu, Meng Zhou, Furen Deng, Yidong Xu, Xuelei Chen

papers.title: Transport of High Energy Protons from CME-Shock to the Sun and its Connection to Extended Gamma-rays Observed by FERMI
papers.summary: This work is motivated by the Large Area Telescope (LAT) observations of long-duration gamma rays from flares associated often with fast Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs), several of which originate behind the limb (BTL) of the Sun. Our aim is to test the feasibility of the scenario whereby the gamma-rays are produced by CME-shock accelerated particles escaping from downstream to the Sun by investigating the transport of protons in this process for the flare of 2014 September 1. We use results from the global MHD modeling by the Alfv\'{e}n Wave Solar Model (AWSoM) to obtain the characteristics of downstream plasma, such as magnetic field geometry, Alfv\'en speed, and energy density of turbulence. This allows us to evaluate the variations of the proton scattering mean free path with energy and distance from the CME-shock. Using an approximate analytic relation between the relevant time scales of the transport, we determine the energy dependence of the residence time at (or escape time from) different distances above the photosphere, and determine the evolution of the proton spectrum from the acceleration site to the photosphere. These results can be used to obtain the spectrum of the observed gamma-rays. Inversely, because of insignificant energy loss or gain during transport, this is a reversible process and the spectrum of protons at the photosphere, obtained from the observed gamma-rays, can be ``de-evolved" back to the CME using the same algorithm. Comparison of these spectra with the in situ observations of Solar Energetic Particles (SEPs) could then shed light on their transport from the CME to the Earth.

authors.name: Vahe Petrosian, Meng Jin

papers.title: JWST Reveals Contrast Overdensities around Two ALMA-CRISTAL Galaxies at $z\sim5.2$
papers.summary: The distribution of stellar mass between massive galaxies and their companions traces how galaxy assembly proceeds within early large-scale structure. We investigate the environments of two galaxies from the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) CRISTAL survey: CRISTAL-19 (C19; $z=5.235$) and CRISTAL-21 (C21; $z=5.256$), using F444W slitless spectroscopy from the Near-Infrared Camera (NIRCam) on the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) in COSMOS-3D. A friends-of-friends analysis of H$\alpha$ emitters identifies two distinct overdense nodes separated by approximately 25 comoving Mpc. Although C21 is the more massive galaxy, C19 has the more massive, actively star-forming companions. The companion populations around C19 and C21 have median stellar masses of $\log(M_\star/M_\odot)=9.43$ and 8.82 and median dust-corrected H$\alpha$ star formation rates of 31 and $16~M_\odot~\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, respectively. Their star formation rate contrast largely reflects the difference in companion masses. C19 contains only $4.5^{+0.9}_{-0.7}\%$ of the combined measured stellar mass of itself and its selected companions; the corresponding fraction for C21 is $39^{+5}_{-5}\%$. Thus, stellar mass remains more widely distributed among galaxies around C19, whereas a larger share resides in C21. Resolved interacting companions around C19 and [C II] kinematics consistent with a late-stage merger in C21 support this contrast in assembly state. These findings support the phase-dependent picture of Zou et al. (2026), in which the surrounding star-forming population changes as interactions and mergers build up a massive galaxy.

authors.name: Shaoze Geng, Siwei Zou, Manuel Aravena, Nikolaus Z. Prusinski, Yi W. Ren, Andreas L. Faisst, Lilian L. Lee, Lun-Jun Liu, Juan Molina, Michael Romano, Bahareh S. Salmasi

papers.title: Time-resolved Polarimetry of the Type Ibn Supernova 2025kzr Suggests a Possible Ejecta-CSM Misalignment
papers.summary: Type Ibn supernovae (SNe) are rare interacting transients. The dense, helium-rich circumstellar material (CSM) surrounding these events provides insight into the final stages of massive-star evolution. The geometries of the ejecta and CSM provide complementary constraints on the explosion and pre-SN mass loss, yet their temporal evolution has remained largely unexplored by spectropolarimetry. Here we present the first spectropolarimetric time series spanning the interaction-to-ejecta transition of the Type Ibn SN\,2025kzr. Three epochs of Very Large Telescope observations, combined with two epochs of published $V$-band imaging polarimetry, span 5--34 days after explosion. Continuum polarization is low at the earliest epoch, then rises to $\sim$0.6\% by day\,11 as the SN ejecta sweep up the dense CSM. This rise, together with a rotating polarization position angle, indicates a significant change in the geometry of the emitting region. The polarization subsequently falls below our detection limit as the photosphere recedes into the ejecta. Radiation-hydrodynamic and Monte Carlo polarization models illustrate that this evolution can be reproduced by an oblate CSM and prolate ejecta, with the symmetry axis of the cold dense shell tilted relative to that of the CSM. Binary mass transfer can produce an equatorially enhanced CSM, although the polarization data alone cannot identify the progenitor's formation channel. Similar polarization signatures in other supernovae suggest that misaligned ejecta and CSM may be common, making time-resolved spectropolarimetry a powerful probe of the link between pre-explosion mass loss and explosion geometry.

authors.name: Xudong Wen, Yi Yang, Lifan Wang, J. Craig Wheeler, Alexei V. Filippenko, Justyn R. Maund, Mattia Bulla, Simon de Wet, Chris Ashall, Steve Schulze

papers.title: Binary mass transfer fossil in the ancient GD-1 stellar stream
papers.summary: We report the discovery of J0930+2902, the first carbon-enhanced metal-poor star with s-process enrichment (CEMP-s) identified in the GD-1 stellar stream, which is widely believed to originate from the tidal disruption of an old, metal-poor globular cluster. Using high-resolution Subaru/HDS spectroscopy, we present a comprehensive chemical abundance analysis of this star. Stellar atmospheric parameters were re-derived using Gaia photometry and parallaxes, combined with an iterative non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) analysis of Fe lines. We determine abundances for 22 elements, including NLTE analyses of C, Na, Mg, Ca, Ti, Cr, Mn, Co, Sr, Y, Zr, Ba, and Eu. J0930+2902 exhibits pronounced enhancements of C, N, Na, and s-process elements, together with a low $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratio of 7.4, consistent with enrichment through binary mass transfer from a former asymptotic giant branch (AGB) companion. Large radial-velocity variations and a significant near-ultraviolet excess independently indicate the presence of a white dwarf companion, providing strong support for this scenario. Comparisons with FRUITY AGB nucleosynthesis models show that the residual neutron-capture abundance pattern is best reproduced by a low-mass AGB companion with an initial mass of approximately 3.0 $M_{\odot}$. Its enhancements of C, N, Na, and s-process elements make it chemically distinct from the other confirmed GD-1 members. These results identify J0930+2902 as a fossil record of binary mass transfer preserved in the ancient GD-1 stellar stream, demonstrating that binary interaction can leave long-lived chemical signatures in accreted stellar populations.

authors.name: Guochao Yang, Sofya Alexeeva, Jingkun Zhao, Wako Aoki, Tatyana Sitnova, Xianhao Ye, Nian Liu, Qianfan Xing, Gang Zhao

papers.title: Towards three-dimensional dark matter mapping in the extended solar neighbourhood with Gaia Data Release 3 and deep learning
papers.summary: We investigate a method for inferring the local dark matter (DM) density in the solar neighbourhood using a deep learning framework that learns the mapping between stellar kinematics and the underlying DM density field from cosmological simulations. To this end, we construct a training set from 7 Milky Way-like galaxies in the FIRE-2 simulation suite. We use three-dimensional stellar kinematic components, consisting of the tangential velocities along the right ascension and declination directions ($v_{\alpha*}$ and $v_{\delta}$) derived from parallaxes and proper motions, together with radial velocity, as input features to predict the three-dimensional DM density field. Two distinct architectures, VNet (arXiv:1606.04797) and ViT-VNet (arXiv:2205.08534), are trained on identical datasets. Both models reproduce the large-scale DM density gradient, whereas small-scale fluctuations are systematically smoothed. Applying the trained models to Gaia DR3 data yields our best estimates of the local DM density: $0.80^{+0.10}_{-0.10}$ and $1.12^{+0.15}_{-0.13}$ GeV cm$^{-3}$ from VNet and ViT-VNet, respectively. The quoted uncertainties reflect the inference scatter across the training set. We further examine systematics from model dependence and the simulation-Gaia domain mismatch, providing an initial step towards a framework for reconstructing local DM maps from future multi-epoch astrometric measurements, including those expected from Gaia DR4.

authors.name: Yigon Kim, Ho Seong Hwang, Sungwook E. Hong, Donghui Jeong, Mingyeong Yang, Ji-hoon Kim

papers.title: Planetary Habitable Zones around Magnetized White Dwarfs
papers.summary: White dwarfs are known to host remnant planetary material, indicating that rocky objects can survive post-main-sequence evolution and migrate into very close orbits. However, the decline of white dwarf luminosity makes it difficult for a planet to remain habitable for long when relying only on the white dwarf's irradiative heating. While several non-radiative energy sources have been proposed, the role of white dwarf magnetism in planetary energy budgets remains largely unexplored. We examine whether magnetic unipolar induction could provide sustained heating for close-in rocky planets. By coupling white dwarf cooling tracks with an orbit-dependent induction model, we evaluate the contribution of ohmic dissipation to planetary surface energy budgets and estimate the upper limit with efficient heat deposition. It is possible for the induction heating to supply a nearly steady surface energy flux for certain orbital distances and stellar spins, partially offsetting the decline in the white dwarf irradiation at late times. This leads to a persistent outer temperate region and, in some cases, a narrow inner zone that emerges after substantial cooling, identifying magnetic induction as a viable long-lived supplement to radiative heating.

authors.name: Xueyuan Wang, Cong Yu, Bo Ma, Di-Chang Chen, Jianheng Guo

papers.title: AT2024dky as an Off-nuclear Tidal Disruption Event Candidate
papers.summary: Through a retrospective search for tidal disruption events (TDEs) in the ZTF archives agnostic to their location within their host galaxies, we identify AT2024dky/ZTF24aagksvd as a promising off-nuclear TDE candidate. At $z=0.0592$, it lies at a projected offset of $3.72^{\prime\prime}$ (4.26 kpc) from the center of a massive ($M_{\rm gal}\sim10^{11}\,M_\odot$), quiescent galaxy. We present early-time ZTF and ATLAS optical photometry and late-time follow-up observations with Keck-I/LRIS, VLA, EP, and Chandra. With $M_{g,\rm peak}=-18.50$ mag, AT2024dky exhibits persistently blue color ($g-r\sim-0.1$ mag) through 80 d after peak. At $\delta t=858$ d, Keck reveals $M_{u'}=-13.07\pm0.09$ mag and $M_R > -14.15$ mag. At $\delta t=866$ d, VLA detects the transient at $\nu L_{\nu,10\,\rm GHz}=(1.26\pm0.17)\times10^{38}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. The combination of early photometric evolution, detected late-time radio and UV emission strongly favor a TDE interpretation. The properties of its host galaxy also bear remarkable similarities to the parent galaxies of known off-nuclear TDEs. Based on the low values of peak-time and late-time UV/optical luminosities, we favor a black hole mass of $\sim 10^5$--$10^6 M_\odot$. Together, these observations strongly favor an off-nuclear TDE.

authors.name: Yuhan Yao, Ryan Chornock, Itai Sfaradi, Jinyi Shangguan, Raffaella Margutti, Robert Stein, Elena Maria Rossi, Yijia Zhang, Zijian Zhang, Jane Lixin Dai, Wenbin Lu, Eric C. Bellm, Joshua S. Bloom, Collin T. Christy, Richard Dekany, Matthew J. Graham, Mansi M. Kasliwal, Russ R. Laher, Ashish A. Mahabal, Josiah Purdum, Ben Rusholme

papers.title: Less massive black holes in faint hosts: SED fitting of Little Red Dots within the Black Hole Star scenario
papers.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has revealed a population of compact sources known as ``little red dots'' (LRDs), characterized by a distinctive V-shaped spectral energy distribution (SED) from UV to optical wavelengths. The physical nature of these sources remains debated. The ``black hole star'' (BH*) scenario, wherein a super-Eddington accreting black hole is embedded in a dense gaseous envelope, has been proposed to explain them. We assemble a sample of 22 LRDs at $4.0 \lesssim z \lesssim 9.5$ from the ASTRODEEP-JWST database. We construct a composite ``host galaxy + BH*'' model using the \texttt{Cloudy} photoionization code, and perform SED fitting with \textsc{BayeSED3}. Our modeling reproduces the observed V-shaped features: the UV continuum blueward of the Balmer break is well reproduced by stellar emission within this decomposition, while the optical regime is dominated by the BH* component. Our fits reveal that LRDs are black holes hosted by faint, low-mass galaxies with median stellar and black hole masses of $M_* = 10^{8.7}\,M_\odot$ and $M_{\rm BH} = 10^{6.4}\,M_\odot$, respectively. These black holes are moderately overmassive relative to local scaling relations but less extreme than broad-line estimates. The median bolometric luminosity $L_{\rm BH^*} \sim 10^{44.9}\,\rm erg\,s^{-1}$ mitigates the reported number density tension from 1--2 orders of magnitude to a factor of a few. The host galaxies lie near the high-redshift star-forming main sequence, and stellar extinction correlates positively with star formation rate (SFR). The BH* scenario provides a self-consistent paradigm for LRDs, offering insights into the rapid growth of supermassive black hole seeds and their co-evolution with host galaxies during the cosmic dawn.

authors.name: Haitong Liu, Lulu Fan, Yunkun Han, Yibin Luo

papers.title: Constraining the Inner Accretion Geometry of GX 9+9 with Broadband Spectral and Timing Studies
papers.summary: We present a broadband spectral and timing study of the bright atoll neutron star low-mass X-ray binary GX~9+9, using simultaneous NICER, NuSTAR, and MAXI observations from 2019 and 2022. The broadband spectra are well described by a combination of multicolor disk emission, thermal Comptonization of blackbody seed photons from the neutron star surface or boundary layer, and associated disk reflection. We report a clear detection of reflection features in this source, including a moderately broad Fe K$\alpha$ complex and a reflection hump, confirming an earlier detection from a different observation. These features likely arise from the illumination of the moderately ionized disk by thermally Comptonized emission from the boundary layer or warm corona. While the source remained in the soft spectral state during both observations, the 2022 observation exhibits a relatively larger thermal contribution, together with a steeper Comptonized component and lower coronal optical depth. Both reflection and disk-continuum modeling favor a truncated disk, with the latter indicating a smaller inner disk radius in 2022. The inferred radial extent of the boundary layer of $\sim8~r_{\rm g}$ may play a role in the observed disk truncation. Assuming that the disk is truncated at the magnetospheric radius, we obtain an upper limit on the magnetic field strength of $\lesssim3\times10^{10}$ G. Timing analysis reveals a relatively stable disk component and a highly variable Comptonized component, consistent with the typical characteristics of the soft state.

authors.name: Swadesh Chand, Srimanta Banerjee, Hsiang-Kuang Chang, Andrzej A. Zdziarski, Gulab C. Dewangan, Vivek K. Agrawal

papers.title: Directional Statistics of Synchrotron Polarization in Mixed Emitting and Faraday-Rotating Turbulence
papers.summary: Polarization directions provide a sensitive probe of Faraday rotation without weighting the signal by polarized brightness. We develop their spatial statistics for a turbulent volume in which synchrotron emission and Faraday rotation coexist. For independent, zero-mean Gaussian polarized emissivity, we derive an exact relation for the directional correlation. We derive strong stochastic coherence-depth scalings, including an additional interval for steep Faraday-density spectra, and distinguish them from the conditions needed to infer directional spectral slopes. We also quantify the weak-rotation response of a coherent uniform emitter and demonstrate that the scalings of the normalized tangential polarization gradient follow directly from the direction spectrum. A combined use of the techniques, including those introduced earlier in Lazarian & Pogosyan (2016), provides a way for detailed study of astrophysical turbulence.

authors.name: A. Lazarian, D. Pogosyan, A. Melnichenka

papers.title: Fast radio bursts track cosmic star formation history with time delay: the effect of burst fluence
papers.summary: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are luminous millisecond-duration radio transients of extragalactic origin, yet their progenitor systems remain unidentified. The redshift evolution of the FRB event rate provides a powerful, model-independent discriminant between young progenitors and old progenitors, but recent studies have reached conflicting conclusions. In this work, we perform a forward-modeling analysis of the apparent non-repeating FRB sample from the CHIME/FRB catalogs to constrain the intrinsic FRB population. We find that the FRB rate follows the star formation rate (SFR) with little time delay when both dispersion measure (DM) and fluence are considered. In contrast, when only DM is taken into account, a significant time delay ($3 \sim 4$ Gyr) exists between the FRB rate and the SFR. The main reason for this discrepancy is that systematic biases exist in the mapping process from burst fluence to signal-to-noise ratio. These results support that at least a fraction of FRBs arise from a progenitor population whose event rate is delayed relative to star formation.

authors.name: X. D. Jia, D. H. Zhai, J. P. Hu, S. X. Yi, F. Y. Wang

papers.title: Multiwavelength Analysis of the Merging Cluster RM J121917.6+505432.8: A Three-way Merger in Disguise?
papers.summary: We identify the galaxy cluster RM J121917.6+505432.8 as a candidate bimodal merging cluster due to its optical properties listed in the redMaPPer cluster catalog. To confirm the cluster's merging state and reveal its dark matter halo and intracluster medium (ICM) morphologies, we conducted a multiwavelength follow-up campaign encompassing HST/ACS optical observations, XMM-Newton X-ray imaging, and Keck/Deimos multislit spectroscopy. The weak lensing mass reconstruction performed with the HST images shows two resolved peaks whose positions coincide with the two brightest cluster galaxies. The ICM morphology is consistent with a post-pericenter merger, with significant asymmetry in X-ray flux between subclusters. Our Keck/Deimos redshift measurements reveal a relative velocity $\Delta v_{\mathrm{LOS}} = 480$ km s$^{-1}$ between eastern and western subclusters. The eastern, more massive subcluster, however, exhibits a highly elongated shape, suggesting either a dark matter halo of considerable eccentricity or the presence of a third, unresolved halo, eliciting the question of whether RMJ1219 is truly binary or a three-way merger. To investigate these hypotheses, we fit the weak lensing shear data using four different combinations of spherical and elliptical NFW halo models and provide an estimate of the mass and concentration of each subhalo. Although the best fit is achieved with a three-halo model, the data are insufficient to determine whether the introduction of extra parameters is statistically justified.

authors.name: Rodrigo Stancioli, David Wittman, Kyle Finner, Faik Bouhrik, Zhuoran Gao

papers.title: Mass Spectral Evidence for Iron Sulfate in Venus' Cloud Aerosol
papers.summary: Venus' cloud aerosols play pivotal roles in the thermal, chemical, and optical properties of the atmosphere. Here, we present mass spectral evidence that the cloud aerosols contain abundant iron sulfates. Data from the Pioneer Venus Large Probe Neutral Mass Spectrometer (LNMS) suggest that cloud aerosols inadvertently collected into the inlets at ~48-51 km and thermally decomposed below the clouds, releasing several compounds into the LNMS. At 23 km and below, multiple iron species (54Fe+, 56FeO+, 54FeO+, 56Fe2O+, and 56Fe2O2+) and other decomposition gases were detected. Quantitative treatment of these mass signals suggested the release of Fe2O3, SO2, O2, SO3, H2SO4, and H2O, consistent with the thermal decomposition of hydronium-bearing ferric sulfates. The resulting mole ratio for iron to sulfate (2.0 +/- 1.1) aligns with hydronium jarosite ((H3O)Fe3(SO4)2(OH)6), which likely formed within the inlets after aerosol capture, dehydration, and loss of sulfuric acid. Our thermochemical calculations support these assessments. Speciation of the ferric sulfates in the native aerosols remains unconstrained (e.g., solution and/or particle phases). Peak fits to the thermal release profiles yielded the abundances of the bulk iron (0.8 +/- 0.4 mg m-3) and aerosol-derived compounds, including hydronium jarosite (2.2 +/- 1.2 mg m-3, 30 +/- 17 wt%), water (3.7 +/- 0.4 mg m-3, 50 +/- 10 wt%), and sulfuric acid (1.5 +/- 0.2 mg m-3, 20 +/- 5 wt%). Surface sourcing of the cloud iron is likely minor. Instead, cosmic dust influx could deliver iron to the clouds in a geologically short time (2.4 +/- 1.5 Myr).

authors.name: Rakesh Mogul, Mikhail Yu. Zolotov, Michael J. Way, Sanjay S. Limaye

papers.title: The role of hierarchy in Galactic molecular clouds
papers.summary: To probe the role of hierarchical gas structures in massive star formation, we statistically analyzed 13 Galactic massive star-forming regions using FUGIN CO survey data. Applying a non-binary dendrogram to the position-position-velocity data, we classified the extracted structures into trunks, internal leaves (the densest substructures within trunks), and isolated structures, and compared their properties with an analysis of variance controlling for regional differences. In representative regions, the trunks correspond to morphologies such as filaments and hub-filament systems, or to kinematic signatures of structure-forming events such as cloud-cloud collisions. Across the sample, the trunks are extended, massive, and strongly bound reservoirs, while the leaves are significantly more massive, denser, and more tightly bound than isolated structures of similar spatial scale. Using YSOs and Hi-GAL clumps, we find that the leaves have a lower low-mass star formation efficiency than isolated structures, whereas their clump formation efficiency is comparable. At a fixed gas mass, the leaves show no higher low-mass star formation efficiency than isolated structures but convert a larger fraction of their gas into dense clumps. We interpret these contrasts, together with inward gas motions in the position-velocity diagrams, as indicating that the deep potential of the trunks sustains continuous accretion onto the leaves and promotes mutual interactions among them. These processes may raise the characteristic fragmentation mass, as theoretically expected for a dynamically accreting medium, so that a larger fraction of the gas forms massive clumps without a corresponding increase in low-mass star formation. Our single-epoch data constrain only these structural contrasts, but indicate that the gas available for massive star formation is organized on scales larger than a single core.

authors.name: Kotora Sasaki, Nario Kuno, Hajime Fukushima, Shingo Nozaki

papers.title: UNIONS and Euclid: Calibrating point source-galaxy separation for ground-based surveys
papers.summary: Efficient separation of unresolved point sources from extended objects (star-galaxy separation) is essential for deep wide-field imaging surveys, particularly at faint magnitudes where morphological differences become subtle. We assess two morphology-based classification methods applied to single-band, ground-based imaging from the Ultraviolet Near-Infrared Optical Northern Survey (UNIONS), using Euclid observations as a high-fidelity reference to evaluate their performance and to train one of the methods. We analysed 8 deg$^2$ of overlapping UNIONS $r$-band and Euclid $I_E$ data, comprising more than $7\times10^{5}$ sources. The Euclid data enable robust morphological labelling down to $I_E\simeq 26$, which we used to train and validate two classification approaches applied to UNIONS alone: a curve-of-growth method and a supervised neural-network classifier, both based on aperture photometry and image-quality information. The curve-of-growth method yields an almost perfectly complete point-source sample ($>95\%$), but its purity decreases rapidly at $r \simeq 22.5$. The neural-network approach significantly improves the purity at the faint end, maintaining $\geq 80\%$ purity down to $r \simeq 24$, while the completeness decreases to almost $50\%$ at similar depths. In both cases, performance strongly depends on the image quality of the ground-based data. This work shows how Euclid data can be used to develop, calibrate, and validate star-galaxy separation methods for ground-based surveys, useful in regions not covered by Euclid. Both methods have already been applied to UNIONS data and are readily applicable to future surveys such as LSST, offering flexible solutions depending on whether completeness or purity is prioritised.

papers.title: Halo spin-axis correlations in IllustrisTNG: Lagrangian-to-Eulerian separation mapping, baryonic effects, and redshift-space distortions
papers.summary: We investigate correlations of halo and stellar spin axes in the TNG300 volume of the IllustrisTNG simulations and compare them with a model based on linear tidal torque theory (LTTT). Dark matter (DM) halo spin axes at $z = 0$ exhibit positive correlations as a function of Lagrangian pair separation. The LTTT-based model describes their separation dependence well, with weak variation in the fitted amplitude across mass thresholds. A Lagrangian-to-Eulerian separation mapping based on the conditional distributions of initial separations at fixed present-day separation, measured directly from the simulations, allows the model to reproduce the overall trends in both real and redshift space without additional fitting. The hydrodynamic and DM-only runs generally show similar DM halo spin-axis correlations, although the DM-only run exhibits a steeper rise at small real-space separations. In the hydrodynamic run, stellar spin-axis correlations are consistent with the same Lagrangian form as their DM halo counterparts, but with approximately 60% of the DM correlation amplitudes. Positive stellar correlations persist in both real and redshift space, and the mapped model captures their separation dependence. Initial spin-axis correlations of protohalos are substantially stronger than their present-day counterparts at the same Lagrangian separations, consistent with subsequent nonlinear spin evolution weakening these correlations. These results suggest that present-day halo and stellar spin-axis correlations retain signatures of the initial tidal field and that their general behavior can be understood through LTTT-based modeling combined with pair-separation mapping.

authors.name: Jun-Sung Moon, Teppei Okumura, Ue-Li Pen

papers.title: Characterization and empirical correction of a spatially coherent spectral artifact in Gemini/GMOS-N IFU observations
papers.summary: We report a recurring spectral artifact identified in observations obtained with the integral field unit (IFU) of the Gemini Multi-Object Spectrograph on the Gemini North telescope (GMOS-N). The artifact appears as a vertically aligned structure in reconstructed images of the IFU field of view, associated with a specific group of fibers and exhibiting a broad spectral feature around 8000~\AAng. Similar features were repeatedly identified in observations of different astronomical targets obtained between 2020 and 2022 using the R150 grating in the two-slit IFU mode. Taking advantage of the reproducibility of the artifact in the fiber and wavelength domains, we develop an empirical correction method in which the artifact is modeled as the product of a common spectral profile and a fiber-dependent amplitude distribution, with an overall normalization determined independently for each exposure. The artifact template is constructed from observations in which the affected fibers are largely separated from the astronomical source and subsequently applied to independent observations in which the artifact overlaps the source. The correction substantially suppresses the artificial spatial structure in the reconstructed images. Although the physical origin of the artifact remains unidentified, we present its observational characteristics and correction procedure to facilitate the identification and treatment of similar features by other GMOS-IFU users.

authors.name: Xiaoyang Chen

papers.title: An oxygen-rich supernova remnant in NGC 253 with narrow [N II] emission lines
papers.summary: Context. Supernova remnants (SNRs) are the final evolutionary stage of supernovae. In rare cases, the remnant persists as an optically luminous remnant decades after the explosion. We report the discovery of an unusual oxygen-rich (O-rich) SNR that was serendipitously discovered in the MUSE mosaic of the nearby (D $\sim$ 3.5 Mpc) galaxy NGC 253 released by arXiv:2506.14921. Aims. We search for SNRs in MUSE integral field spectroscopy data of NGC 253. Methods. We search for unresolved point sources with broad and strong [O III]$\lambda$$\lambda$4959,5007, [O I]$\lambda$$\lambda$6300,6364 or [O II]$\lambda$$\lambda$7320,7331 emission lines. We also search for possible counterparts at other wavelengths in archival data. Results. We find a single O-rich SNR in NGC 253 with [O III]$\lambda$$\lambda$4959,5007. For this object, we report a coincident X-ray source detected by Chandra and a non-detection at mid-infrared wavelengths by JWST. Additionally, we identify [N II]$\lambda$$\lambda$6548,6583 emission lines and no detectable hydrogen or [SII]$\lambda$$\lambda$6716,6731 emission. The [N II] emission lines are broader (230 km/s) than the surrounding interstellar medium lines but still narrow in comparison to the [O III] emission (>1500 km/s) from the SNR. No detections of [O I]$\lambda$$\lambda$6300,6364 and [O II]$\lambda$$\lambda$7320,7331 were made. Conclusions. The discovery of a single O-rich SNR after a systematic search of NGC 253 highlights their scarcity in nearby galaxies. The structure of [O III] emission indicates complex structure in the O-rich ejecta. The relative narrowness of [N II] emission lines compared to the [O III] lines and the non-detection of hydrogen show that the remnant is surrounded by an N-rich circumstellar medium. The ejecta is currently interacting with this material of the preceding supernova explosion.

authors.name: Timo Kravtsov, Enrico Congiu, Joseph P. Anderson, Hanindyo Kuncarayakti, Seppo Mattila, Amirnezam Amiri, Ashley T. Barnes, Daniel A. Dale, Sanskriti Das, Oleg V. Egorov, Kathryn Grasha, Eric Habjan, Smita Mathur, Hsi-An Pan, Thomas G. Williams

papers.title: Radio Emission From Low-redshift Little Red Dots
papers.summary: High-redshift Little Red Dots (LRDs) are radio faint in existing survey and deep-field samples. Nearby LRD analogues allow the radio emission and spectra of individual sources to be measured, which is not possible at $z\sim6$. Our sample comprises 44 low-redshift LRDs ($0.101 \leq z \leq 0.882$) . Eight objects are radio-detected: five at 144\,MHz with LoTSS, six at 3\,GHz with VLASS at $\geq3\sigma$, and J1047 through its published VLA data. The rest-frame 144\,MHz luminosities of the LoTSS detections span $1.8\times10^{30}$ to $3.6\times10^{31}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}\,Hz^{-1}}$. The LoTSS--VLASS spectral indices range from $-0.27\pm0.04$ (J2048) to $-0.78\pm0.11$ (J1200). J1051 lacks 144\,MHz coverage and has $\alpha_{0.9 \rm GHz}^{\rm 3 GHz} \simeq-0.93$. J1047 has a clear deficit at 144 MHz relative to its optically thin GHz spectrum, consistent with a turnover whose position and physical mechanism are not uniquely constrained by the archival data. The higher detection fraction among the Green Pea sample largely reflects their lower redshift: in this subsample LoTSS reaches luminosities roughly an order of magnitude fainter than in the more distant DESI gold sample. If their escaping spectra and radio luminosities are held fixed and extrapolated as power laws, the five LoTSS detections would have observed-frame 144 MHz flux densities of $\sim0.7$--$32\,\mu\mathrm{Jy}$. Low-redshift LRDs span more than an order of magnitude in radio luminosity among the detections, and more than two orders of magnitude when the J1047 upper limit is included. They also show several distinct spectral shapes, so the optically defined LRD class encompasses diverse radio properties. Current detection statistics are strongly shaped by redshift and survey sensitivity. The source-by-source luminosity limits provide a reference for interpreting future LRD samples.

authors.name: Ailing Wang, Tao An, Ruqiu Lin

papers.title: Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU): the fraction of radio-detected quasi-stellar objects at high redshift
papers.summary: The aim of this paper is to use the Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) to assess the fraction of high-z quasi-stellar objects (QSOs) that are radio-emitting at ~0.2 mJy/beam level and to establish if the radio emission is mainly produced by relativistic jets. A sample of 808 type1 QSOs in the redshift range 410) high-z QSOs is about 8% while the fraction of radio detections is a strong function of the optical magnitude and reaches values of ~35% when only the optically brightest (mag~18) QSOs are considered. Since all the radio detected QSOs, including those classified as radio-quiet (R10^46 erg s^-1) QSO population. Future observations with SKAO will be instrumental to unambiguously confirm the jetted nature of the QSOs currently detected by EMU.

authors.name: A. Caccianiga, D. Dallacasa, L. Ighina, A. Moretti, J. Afonso, S. Ant\'on R. Carvajal, Y. Gordon, A. Hopkins, M. J. March\~a, R. Norris, F. Rahman, G. F. Ramos, N. Seymour, C. Spingola, J. Th. van Loon

papers.title: High-Precision Photometry with a scientific CMOS Camera: III Lab and on-Sky testing of Andor Toran-26B
papers.summary: Scientific CMOS cameras are increasingly used in modern astronomy, offering CCD-like performance with lower power use, faster readout, and reduced cost. We evaluate the photometric precision of the Toran-26B camera, featuring the IMX571 sensor from Sony, a new CMOS camera from Andor Technology, through laboratory and on-sky tests in its two modes: high well capacity (HWC) and low noise (LN). Key metrics include read noise, dark current, photo and dark signal non-uniformity, quantum efficiency, and window transmittance. The median read noise is 1.07\,e$^-$ (LN) and 2.79\,e$^-$ (HWC). Bias shows minor dark signal non-uniformity: 0.076\,e$^-$ (LN), 0.173\,e$^-$ (HWC). Pixel well depth reaches 15700\,e$^-$ (LN) and 50000\,e$^-$ (HWC), with dynamic ranges of 83.39\,dB and 85.05\,dB, respectively. Linearities are 99.93\,\% (LN) and 99.82\,\% (HWC) within the 5-95\,\% range of the saturation signal. Photo response non-uniformity is 0.076\,\% (LN) and 0.05\,\% (HWC). Dark current at 0\,$^\circ$C is 0.001\,\eps, (LN and HWC). On-sky tests show that, for our test telescope configuration, the HWC mode can be camera noise limited for specific magnitude ranges, while the LN mode remains free of such limitations, making it the preferred choice.

authors.name: Ioannis Apergis, Leonidas Asimakoulas, Daniel Bayliss, Paul Chote, Morgan A. Mitchell, James McCormac, Ben Godson, Philip G. Steen

papers.title: Bar Kinematics in Paired and Isolated Galaxies: Slow Bars Are More Likely Found in Paired Galaxies
papers.summary: Bars are common structures in disk galaxies that can strongly influence the evolution of their hosts. Simulations predict that bars formed through tidal interactions tend to rotate slower than bars formed in isolation. We test this prediction observationally by studying the kinematics of 314 bars in galaxies between $0.016$0.250; $<$1.15$\sigma$).

authors.name: Brian Aziz, Tobias G\'eron, Izzy L. Garland, David O'Ryan, Hayley Roberts, Rebecca J. Smethurst

papers.title: Small-scale priors for large-scale cosmology: the case of $b_{\phi}$
papers.summary: Perturbative descriptions of galaxy clustering introduce free bias parameters that capture the complex physics of galaxy formation. Local primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG), parametrized by $f_{NL}$, induces a scale-dependent contribution to the galaxy bias that is proportional to $f_{NL} b_\phi$, where $b_\phi$ quantifies how galaxy formation responds to PNG. Accurately determining $b_{\phi}$ is therefore essential for robust constraints on $f_{NL}$. Current analyses usually adopt a modified universal relation, $b_\phi = 2\delta_c(b_1-p)$, with $p$ calibrated to simulations. This relies on the accuracy of the simulated galaxy-formation model and ignores the uncertainty on $b_\phi$, potentially biasing $f_{NL}$ constraints. We investigate whether $b_\phi$ can be constrained from small-scale galaxy clustering using a flexible empirical galaxy-formation model. We fit an extended Subhalo Abundance Matching (SHAMe) model to small-scale clustering measurements and combine it with dark-matter-only separate-universe simulations to infer a posterior on $b_\phi$. We validate the method using IllustrisTNG hydrodynamical separate-universe simulations. Without calibration on hydrodynamical simulations, SHAMe predicts $b_\phi$ with a median error of 10%, compared with 38% for a fixed halo occupation distribution (HOD) that neglects the occupation response to $\phi$, and 23% for the universality relation. The residual error is dominated by central galaxies near the selection threshold and persists when using the true stellar-mass assignment conditioned on the same subhalo properties. Small-scale clustering combined with a subhalo-based empirical model predicts most of galaxy-abundance response to local PNG. The remainder depends on galaxy-formation physics and should enter $b_\phi$ priors as a theoretical uncertainty. This provides a route to data-informed priors on bias parameters.

authors.name: Mathilde Pinon, Raul E. Angulo, Sergio Contreras, Azadeh Moradinezhad Dizgah

papers.title: A magneto-convective origin for solar-wind Alfvenic fluctuations
papers.summary: The solar wind is a highly structured and supersonic plasma outflow that originates in the Sun's outer atmosphere. The energy source driving the wind is still subject to intense debate. Recent observations point to magnetic reconnection as a primary driver, while Alfvenic waves launched by surface convection are often invoked as a key contributor. Whether fluctuations in the young solar wind originate in convectively driven waves has not been tested observationally. Here we show that they carry the spectral imprint of convective driving. Observations from the Solar Dynamics Observatory and the Upgraded Coronal Multi-channel Polarimeter reveal the predicted spectrum of convectively driven waves in both weakly and rapidly expanding open fields, the likely sources of the fast and slow Alfvenic wind. Averaged over 270 intervals below the Alfven surface, the young wind sampled by Parker Solar Probe carries a similar spectrum. High-resolution spectroscopy from the Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope resolves further spectral components that also appear in the wind. Convectively driven waves therefore supply a basal energy flux to the solar wind, alongside intermittent reconnection.

authors.name: R. J. Morton, Z. Huang, T. Schad, M. Velli

papers.title: High-energy Electron Transport with Discrete Inverse Compton Scatterings
papers.summary: After escaping from pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe), the transport of high-energy electrons in the interstellar medium (ISM) is usually described with the diffusion equation with a continuous radiative energy loss. However, when the electron energy approaches $\sim 100~\text{TeV}$ and the radiative energy loss is dominated by the inverse Compton scattering (ICS), the discrete nature of ICS becomes prominent, and the approximation of continuous radiative energy loss is invalid. Starting from the Klein--Nishina differential scattering rate, this paper constructs an integral-differential equation to describe the stochastic discrete nature of the inverse Compton cooling, and the equation is solved with the Fourier and Laplace transform method. Application to the TeV halo of Geminga pulsar leads to a diffusion coefficient {$\sim 15$\%} lower than that of the continuous energy loss model.

authors.name: Ruihao Jing, Siming Liu

papers.title: Optical Light-Curve Broadening in the Redback Binary PSR J2215+5135
papers.summary: Spider millisecond pulsars offer a direct route to constrain neutron-star masses, including candidates above two solar masses, via optical light-curve modeling of the irradiated companion. This assumes stable irradiation. We report new $g'r'i'$ photometry of the redback PSR~J2215+5135 from the Iranian National Observatory in 2024 and compare it with the 2014 data of \citet{linares2018peering}. Peak brightness and orbital period are unchanged within uncertainties, but the light-curve wings are significantly broader in 2024, as the local deviations exceed $3\sigma$ on the rising branch in all filters, with an additional $i'$-band excess on the falling branch, giving a global permutation-test significance of $4.26\sigma$. A single-hot-spot model fits the 2024 data better than a spot-free one, but systematic residuals remain. The broader wings are reproduced only through correlated shifts in the spot, inclination, filling factor and companion temperature, which we regard as model compensation, not physics. An extended, variable heating component may also fit. The best-fit spot temperature differs between epochs by about $1060$\,K, comparable to its model dependence (about $900$\,K between two codes for 2014), so we do not interpret this as physical. Two epochs cannot show whether the change is gradual, sudden or short-lived. The inferred neutron-star mass depends on the spot treatment: $2.13^{+0.16}_{-0.13}\,M_\odot$ for 2014 with a hot spot, and $M_\mathrm{NS}=1.95^{+0.11}_{-0.07}\,M_\odot$ for 2024. These agree within about $1\sigma$, but come from differently shaped light curves, and the statistical uncertainties exclude heating-prescription systematics.

authors.name: Amin Farhang, Soroush Shakeri, Habib Khosroshahi, Narjes Shahamat, Razieh Ranjbar, Jerome Orosz, Joshua Tan, Davood Rafiei Karkevandi, Hamed Altafi, Hamidreza Mahani, Amir Yarahmadi, Masoud Bidar, Ramin Shomali, Mohammadreza Rostamian, Hengameh Shalchian, Tayebeh Shokatpour, Ruholla Sadeghi Amin

papers.title: Physical quasar pairs in DESI DR1 as tracers of protoclusters at $z\approx2$
papers.summary: Close pairs of quasars at the same redshift are expected to mark overdense regions that will collapse into galaxy clusters. Earlier work with SDSS found about 2800 such pairs, too few to follow their environment with separation. We build the largest sample of physical quasar pairs to date from DESI DR1 and test whether pairs out to Mpc separations trace protoclusters. We select pairs with rest-frame velocity difference $|\Delta V|\leq900 km/s$ and projected separation $r_p\leq4$~Mpc at $1.2\leq z\leq2.8$, measure their purity and fibre completeness, and measure the clustering of pair members around all DESI quasars. We find 40\,626 physical pairs with projected separation $r_p\leq2.5$~Mpc, where their purity falls to 50\%, the effective radius of protoclusters at $z\approx2$. Pair members are $1.69\pm0.14$, $1.78\pm0.09$ and $2.01\pm0.06$ times more clustered than all quasars for projected separations $r_p\leq1$, 1--2.5 and 2.5--4~Mpc, while chance pairs show little excess ($1.08\pm0.05$). This corresponds to haloes of $\sim1.4$--$2.2\times10^{13}\,h^{-1}M_\odot$. Physical quasar pairs with projected separations up to 2.5~Mpc trace protocluster environments, at the level that AbacusSummit mocks predict in $\Lambda$CDM. The full DESI survey will turn them into a statistical census of protoclusters at cosmic noon.

authors.name: Martin G. Richiarte, Diego G. Lambas
