Conversion thus reduces to finding such a filter whose unnormalized output leaves a positive semidefinite remainder when subtracted from the target, a search we show to be solvable by semidefinite programming. Beyond deterministic conversion, the characterization of free operations can be used to study probabilistic and assisted manipulation of quantum-state texture. More broadly, since the construction relies on a pure fixed state, it also applies to other resource theories defined by free operations fixing such a state.

authors.name: Jose Alfredo de Leon

papers.title: Simultaneous computation of multiple excited states via double bracket flows
papers.summary: Efficient computation of excited states is essential for studying strongly correlated many-body systems and molecular electronic structure. In this work, we propose a framework for simultaneously simulating multiple excited states based on dynamical flows. The main idea is to exploit a common double bracket flow that drives different pure initial states toward different target excited states without such prior information. We establish a necessary condition for convergence and a sufficient condition for exponential convergence. We further develop two scheduling strategies: Chebyshev scheduling, which achieves optimal convergence near a fixed point but requires prior spectral information, and adaptive scheduling, which achieves comparable performance in numerical simulations without spectral information. Our results enable new classical and quantum algorithms for excited-state computation without prior preparation of lower-energy eigenstates.

authors.name: Reyhaneh Aghaei Saem, Mehrad Sahebi, Zo\"{e} Holmes, Yudai Suzuki

papers.title: Bound magic in multi-qubit systems
papers.summary: Magic captures nonstabilizerness, a resource required for quantum computational speedups. We prove the existence of multi-qubit nonstabilizer states from which no pure magic can be distilled, even with arbitrarily many copies and rounds of stabilizer operations. Such bound magic states have previously been only known to exist in odd Hilbert-space dimensions, where positivity of discrete Wigner functions can be used analogously to the positive partial transpose (PPT) criterion for bound entanglement. We introduce a PPT analogue for magic in multi-qubit systems that is closed under tensor products and stabilizer operations and reduces to the stabilizer polytope for one and two qubits. This enables the proof of multi-qubit bound magic and the explicit construction of bound magic states for $n \geq 3$ qubits.

authors.name: Jonas Kitzinger, Jens Eisert, Ravi Kunjwal

papers.title: Exact monogamy of steering and remote Wigner negativity for multimode Gaussian nodes
papers.summary: Optical quantum networks route correlations through nodes that hold several modes and are linked to many neighbors. Steering is the correlation behind one-sided device-independent tasks and behind the remote preparation of non-Gaussian states. It is monogamous for a single mode, which can be steered by only one party, but how many neighbors can steer a node with $k$ modes was not known. We show that for Gaussian states the answer is exactly $2k-1$ when the neighbors use Gaussian measurements, with any number of measurement settings. The limit follows from a simple bound. To every neighbor we assign a share, computed from the covariance matrix, and we prove that the shares of all neighbors add up to at most $k$, irrespective of the amount of squeezing, amplification or noise the network contains. A neighbor steers the node by Gaussian measurements exactly when its share exceeds one half, and a network built from a harmonic tight frame reaches the limit. The same number governs remote Wigner negativity. A heralded non-Gaussian operation at the node can make at most $2k-1$ neighbors Wigner negative, and in our network a single heralded projection makes all of them negative in the same run. With $n$ settings of arbitrary measurements, at most $nk-1$ neighbors can steer the node or violate a Bell inequality with it. More than $2k-1$ neighbors can therefore steer the node or violate a Bell inequality with it only if they use non-Gaussian measurements with at least three settings, whereas entanglement can reach any number of neighbors. These results determine exactly how many neighbors one multimode node can serve with steering and with remote Wigner negativity.

authors.name: Sudip Chakrabarty

papers.title: The Price of Quantum Advantage in Computational Chemistry
papers.summary: As the fault-tolerant era approaches, the question shifts from ``is it possible'' to ``is it worthwhile.'' To assess practical quantum advantage against reliable classical baselines, we examine 26 benchmark instances including FeMoco, iron-sulfur clusters, cytochrome P450, and ruthenium catalysts using two selected configuration interaction solvers, SHCI and TrimCI. Comparing classical workloads with fault-tolerant resource estimates, we calculate the break-even whole-QPU hourly price. Even at an optimistic price of US\$7{,}000 per whole-QPU hour, and with mid-range CPU clusters, classical computation remains cheaper for six of seven systems. FeMoco alone remains sensitive to the classical method and extrapolation strategy. Wavefunction analysis further reveals how orbital choice affects the determinant support required for target-state overlap in quantum phase estimation (QPE). Our results highlight the importance of reliable classical references and trial-state characterization, and quantify the economic conditions under which quantum computing can become competitive with classical alternatives.

authors.name: Haejung Koh, Katerina Gratsea, Hao Zhang, Matthew Otten

papers.title: Neural Network Decoders For Qubit Loss
papers.summary: Qubit loss is a significant source of error in many quantum hardware platforms, requiring circuits that periodically replace or reset qubits to maintain fault-tolerance. When the reset process includes loss-resolving measurements, this information can improve decoding and substantially reduce overhead compared to the case where this information is not available. Prior work has demonstrated loss-tolerant circuits for the surface code that show significantly improved thresholds and subthreshold scaling by incorporating loss information. However, the computational complexity of loss simulation and decoding, which falls outside of the usual stabilizer framework, has limited extending these studies to high-rate qLDPC codes, which are already challenging to decode in the absence of loss. In this work, we present a loss-aware convolutional neural-network (CNN) decoder framework that circumvents this challenge. Training is enabled by a novel sampler, \texttt{slim}, which achieves a throughput for circuits with Pauli noise and loss that is comparable to the state-of-the-art for pure Pauli noise. On the surface code with loss, the decoder matches the accuracy of computationally expensive most-likely error (MLE) decoders at much lower latency. For the $[[144,12,12]]$ bivariate bicycle (Gross) code, we study a walking syndrome extraction circuit with Pauli and loss errors. For physical error rates $p<1\%$, we observe a more than $10^3$-fold lower logical error rate for a pure loss model, relative to a pure Pauli error model at the same physical error rate, along with significantly enhanced sub-threshold error rate scaling. This demonstrates that loss-dominated error models can also significantly improve performance in a high-rate qLDPC code, and provides a simulation and decoder training platform that can be extended to other codes and algorithmic gadgets.

authors.name: J. Wilson Staples, Winston Fu, Yihe Dong, Jeff D. Thompson

papers.title: Complementary mechanisms of critical quantum metrology
papers.summary: Critical metrology conventionally exploits enhanced susceptibility to a system parameter near a phase transition. Here we identify a complementary mechanism for critically enhanced estimation of intrinsic system parameters via suppressed quantum noise rather than enhanced response. We demonstrate both mechanisms in coherently radiating spin states (CRSS)-correlated states of $N$ spin-$1/2$ particles defined as asymptotic eigenstates of the collective-spin lowering operator with complex eigenvalue $r e^{-i\varphi}$. At the critical value $r=1$, CRSS exhibit a second-order transition. We show that near criticality, estimation of $r$ benefits from enhanced susceptibility despite increased noise, whereas estimation of $\varphi$ benefits from suppressed quantum noise without enhanced response. Remarkably, both yield the same estimation error $\sim N^{-2/3}$, improving over the standard quantum limit $N^{-1/2}$. For $\varphi$, this establishes quantum-enhanced metrology of phases intrinsic to the critical system, rather than phases externally encoded by interferometry. We demonstrate these results for CRSS realizations in both dissipative (superradiant) and Hamiltonian (Ising) systems relevant to cavity QED and trapped ions, where fast preparation of CRSS is shown possible thanks to gap opening. Applications to metrology of coupling rates and phases or optical lengths are discussed.

authors.name: Nikita Leppenen, Shaked Levy, Ephraim Shahmoon

papers.title: Bound Entanglement with Negative Partial Transpose Exists
papers.summary: We show that the Werner state $\rho = (23 I - 3\,\mathrm{SWAP})/1448$ on $\mathbb{C}^8 \otimes \mathbb{C}^8$ has a negative partial transpose and is bound entangled: no LOCC protocol can distill entanglement from any number of copies of $\rho$, and even with separable operations the fidelity of a two-qubit output with a Bell state never exceeds $(1+\sqrt{2})/4 \approx 0.604$. It follows that distillable entanglement is neither additive nor convex.

authors.name: Islam Faisal

papers.title: Schism: Reconfigurable Scale-Up Domains for Distributed Quantum Computing
papers.summary: Switch-based quantum datacenters connect quantum processing units (QPUs) through photonic switches and shared Bell-state measurement (BSM) devices. Sharing BSMs saves hardware, but fixed connectivity constrains access to these resources. Local communication can overload one rack's BSMs while others remain idle; reaching those idle resources incurs additional optical loss and retries through switches and quantum frequency converters (QFCs). Programs remain locked into this locality-contention tradeoff as their communication patterns change. We propose Schism, an architecture that lets programs dynamically change which QPUs share each BSM pool. Schism places BSM pools at aggregation switches and QFCs on their core-facing uplinks. Top-of-rack switches establish reconfigurable native-wavelength circuits from QPUs to these pools, forming scale-up domains bounded by the optical loss budget. Reconfiguration reshapes resource sharing across racks without moving QPUs or migrating quantum states. Our key insight is that QPU grouping jointly determines photon-path loss and contention for BSM resources: locality alone cannot identify the best grouping, and a grouping pays off only if its savings outweigh the delay of reconfiguring to it. We develop an optimization framework that combines graph partitioning with resource-constrained completion-time estimates and dynamic programming to select how QPUs share BSM pools and when those groupings reconfigure, between or within circuit phases. Our evaluation using SeQUeNCe with trapped-ion parameters shows that Schism achieves communication speedups of 4.9-7.3x across 11 workloads on 32 QPUs compared to Fixed Clos connectivity and 3.6-8.3x compared to SwitchQNet. Schism also outperforms a hypothetical network-wide switch by 1.35-1.38x on the eight workloads whose phases fit in a pool, and trails it by 1.1-1.75x on the other three.

authors.name: Daniel Alexander, Deeksha P Rao, Nilesh Vyas, Vamsi Addanki

papers.title: Theory of Anomalous Diffusion and Superdiffusion in Integrable Spin Chains
papers.summary: Integrable systems can exhibit diffusive or Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) scaling in two-point correlations even when their current full counting statistics (FCS) differ from those usually associated with these universality classes. We explain this separation using a multispecies particle gas that preserves the scattering structure of integrable spin chains. For anisotropy $\Delta>1$, large particles are advected by a mobile bath. The resulting FCS has a Gaussian-mixture form and approaches the M-Wright distribution at late times, with finite-time rounding due to mobile species. At the isotropic point $\Delta=1$, all particles are mobile, and the charge transfer by large particles is discrete. A self-consistent Poisson distribution describes the FCS, with a nearly Gaussian bulk and model-dependent, non-Gaussian tails. By contrast, two-point correlations follow from the statistics of a large tracer particle. For $\Delta>1$, it undergoes Brownian motion, yielding Gaussian spreading. At $\Delta=1$, we provide evidence from fluctuating hydrodynamics for the emergence of the KPZ Pr\"ahofer--Spohn scaling function in dynamical correlations and trace it to the finite coupling of the largest particles to a continuum of slower ones, with long-ranged velocity fluctuations. Our framework shows how universal dynamical two-point correlations coexist with distinct model-dependent current statistics.

authors.name: Jitendra Kethepalli, Andrew Urilyon, Jacopo De Nardis

papers.title: Bosonic Magic Resources at Quantum Criticality
papers.summary: Non-Gaussianity is a resource for bosonic quantum information processing, providing a necessary ingredient for universal quantum computation in continuous-variable systems. Here we quantify non-Gaussianity in the ground state of the one-dimensional extended Bose-Hubbard model using quantum relative entropy (QRE), a measure determined solely by one-body correlations. The scaling of the QRE with system size reveals quantum phase transitions involving hidden and conventional order. We connect QRE scaling in the weakly interacting superfluid phase to Luttinger-liquid correlations and identify distinct critical signatures in its extensive and subleading contributions. At the Mott-Haldane transition, subtracting the extensive background reveals a pronounced peak in the subleading contribution, providing a clear signature of the onset of hidden string order. At the Haldane-density-wave transition, the extensive contribution to the QRE instead exhibits scaling consistent with Ising criticality. These results establish non-Gaussianity as a probe of many-body criticality, linking bosonic quantum resources to strongly correlated matter.

authors.name: Paolo Stornati, Piotr Sierant, Emanuele Tirrito

papers.title: Modular fluctuation relations on local causal horizons
papers.summary: Local causal horizons provide a setting for studying horizon thermodynamics in the neighborhood of any regular spacetime point. Here, we investigate this description beyond mean energy and entropy balances by studying fluctuations of boost-energy transfer induced by unitary perturbations of the horizon reference state. Using the modular structure of the horizon algebra and a thermal reference state, we construct an energy transfer probability measure and derive integral and detailed fluctuation relations with the mean entropy production being expressed in terms of the Araki relative entropy. The formulation accommodates type-III algebras without introducing a reduced density matrix and can be extended to global bifurcate Killing horizons admitting the required thermal reference state. For coherent scalar-field perturbations, we obtain a closed form for the characteristic function, identify the mean transfer with the excess boost-energy flux, and derive a thermodynamic uncertainty relation bounding the variance in terms of the mean transfer. We then explore the geometric implications by postulating a stochastic horizon entropy--area correspondence that associates an area change with each counted energy transfer. Under this additional hypothesis, we obtain fluctuation relations for area changes and an area change uncertainty bound for coherent perturbations.

authors.name: Marcos L. W. Basso

papers.title: Superconductivity from the Berry connection from many-electron wave functions: $U(1)$ gauge fluctuation, gauge invariance, and superconductivity
papers.summary: The electromagnetic $U(1)$ gauge invariance and superconductivity are examined by employing the Berry connection from many-electron wave functions and the fluctuations of it that give rise to the probabilistic random transitions among quantum states. The gauge invariance in the classical electrodynamics is regarded as the requirement that extracts unaffected parts by the gauge fluctuation. In quantum mechanics, dissipation-free states from the gauge fluctuation exist, and we identify them as superconducting states. We explain the reversible superconducting-normal phase transition in a magnetic field including the force balance. The present superconductivity theory lifts two fundamental disagreements between theory and experiment existing in the current standard theory with keeping the major results by the BCS theory. Thus, it may be considered as a superconductivity theory encompassing the current standard one.

authors.name: Hiroyasu Koizumi

papers.title: The transverse spin-gradient approximation in noncollinear spin density functional theory
papers.summary:
We prove a quantitative error bound for a fixed-axis variant of the transverse spin-gradient approximation (TSGA) in noncollinear spin density functional theory. Inspired by Eich and Gross, we use a spin-spiral wave (SSW) as the local reference for the grand-canonical Levy-Lieb energy with the Hartree term subtracted. We construct the thermodynamic limit of the electron gas with constant total density and a prescribed SSW magnetization. Its energy per unit volume $e_{m SSW}$ is evaluated at the local wavevector $
abla\varphi$, where $\varphi$ is the spiral phase. When $\varphi$ is the azimuthal angle of the magnetization $\mathbf{m}=(m_1,m_2,m_3)$, the approximation reads \[ E(ho,\mathbf{m})\approx\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}e_{m SSW} ig(ho(\mathbf{x}),\mathbf{m}(\mathbf{x}),
abla\varphi(\mathbf{x}) ig)\,d \mathbf{x}. \] Here $
abla\varphi$ measures the local rotation of $\mathbf{m}$ about the third axis. Wherever $m_1^2+m_2^2>0$, it equals $(m_1
abla m_2-m_2
abla m_1)/(m_1^2+m_2^2)$. The approximation thus depends only on the total density $ho$, the magnetization and its first derivatives. When the spin-polarized density in the rotating frame and the local wavevector vary on the length scale $N^{1/3}$, with $N$ the mean number of particles, we obtain an error $O(N^{5/6})$ for an energy of order $N$. Setting the phase to zero gives the noncollinear local spin density approximation (LSDA) for arbitrary magnetization directions.

authors.name: Mih\'aly A. Csirik

papers.title: Intrinsically nonlinear nanomechanical resonator toward the single-phonon Kerr regime
papers.summary: Manipulating a physical system at the single-quantum level typically requires an anharmonic energy spectrum. Nanomechanical resonators, however, are commonly admitted to be linear objects in the single-phonon regime, thus motivating most efforts to employ external sources of nonlinearity at the cost of added relaxation and decoherence channels. Here, we take a radically different approach by directly exploiting strong intrinsic mechanical nonlinearities. We quantify this nonlinearity using a novel method based on the coupling between bending modes. Using this technique, we establish an upper bound of 34.0 +/- 9.7 phonons for the onset of intrinsically mechanical bistability. In addition, we highlight a new tuning mechanism based on a mechanical polarization angle of an upward-buckled nanotube resonator allowing us to reach an optimal working point. Extrapolating this level of intrinsic nonlinearity to realistically shorter resonators shows that the single-phonon Kerr regime is within reach, allowing for the realization of purely mechanical Schr\"odinger-cat states and highly coherent mechanical qubits.

authors.name: S. Klingel, T. Althuon, C. Wassmer, C. S\"urgers, T. Cubaynes, W. Wernsdorfer

papers.title: Data-enhanced self-learning projective quantum Monte Carlo with Rydberg-atom measurements
papers.summary: We introduce a data-enhanced self-learning projective quantum Monte Carlo (PQMC) method that incorporates projective measurements from programmable quantum simulators into the guiding wavefunction of a ground-state projection. We demonstrate the approach for a two-dimensional Rydberg-atom array using restricted Boltzmann machine (RBM) and recurrent neural network (RNN) guiding wavefunctions. Experimental pretraining reduces finite-population effects and accelerates self-learning convergence, allowing unbiased estimation of ground-state properties to be obtained with fewer walkers and fewer self-learning iterations. The improvement is particularly pronounced for the RBM, while the more accurate RNN guiding wavefunction exhibits a smaller, though still observable, benefit from pretraining. Simulations across different system sizes suggest that the relative advantage of experimental pretraining may increase with system size. Improvements are also observed for the checkerboard order parameter, despite deviations of the experimental measurements from the equilibrium numerical results. Finally, finite-size scaling with self-learning PQMC without experimental pretraining yields the critical point and critical exponents of the disordered-to-checkerboard transition in agreement with previous numerical studies. Our results show that limited and imperfect experimental measurements can provide an effective initialization for self-learning PQMC, while imaginary-time projection combined with subsequent unsupervised learning progressively refines the guiding wavefunction toward the ground state.

authors.name: Vichayuth Imchitr, Luca Brodoloni, Sebastiano Pilati, Estelle Maeva Inack

papers.title: The asymptotic spectrum of tensors is connected
papers.summary: We prove path-connectedness of the asymptotic spectrum of complex tensors of every fixed order $k \geq 3$: every spectral point is connected by a path to every "one leg versus the rest" flattening rank. In particular, the asymptotic spectrum evaluated at any fixed tensor is a closed interval, answering a question of Strassen. This was previously known only on specific families of tensors (Strassen, FOCS 1986, Crelle 1987-1991; Wigderson and Zuiddam, Bull. AMS 2026) or for specific families of spectral points (Christandl, Vrana and Zuiddam, STOC 2018; Sakabe, Do\u{g}an and Walter, FOCS 2026; Alman, Li and Pratt, FOCS 2026). To obtain our path-connectedness theorem we develop a general method for "interpolating" between spectral points, which applies to Strassen semirings that are appropriately decomposable (in the sense of an information-theoretic "method of types" on the semiring) and whose spectral points satisfy a cover property (inspired by slice rank). This covers tensors and asymptotic rank (with "types" given by decomposition into symmetric group irreps), as well as other objects and asymptotic problems, like graphs and Shannon capacity, where it matches the interpolation of Vrana (2019). Using our interpolation methods we furthermore obtain new results and simpler proofs of previous results regarding the asymptotic spectrum of rectangular matrix multiplication, polynomial multiplication and non-crossing (laminar) quantum functionals.

authors.name: P\'eter Vrana, Jeroen Zuiddam

papers.title: $\mathsf{AC}^0 \not\subseteq \mathsf{BQAC}^0/\mathsf{qpoly}$ via Sublinear-Degree Pauli Approximation
papers.summary: We prove $\mathsf{AC}^0 \not\subseteq \mathsf{BQAC}^0/\mathsf{qpoly}$ in the single-copy, single-output model via an explicit $\mathsf{P}$-uniform family of linear-size monotone depth-2 CNFs. Every $\mathsf{QAC}^0$ circuit with arbitrary quantum advice achieves only an inverse-polynomial worst-case advantage over random guessing on this family. To prove this, we approximate the acceptance operator of any such circuit in operator norm by an advice-independent Hermitian operator of sublinear Pauli degree on a designated register alone, with degree exponent independent of width. Product-projection localization and Pauli twirling produce an auxiliary-register spectral cutoff that folds into contractions during backward peeling. The same approximation yields two stretched-exponential bounds against $\mathsf{QAC}^0$ circuits on $m$-qubit states. First, given polynomially many copies and input-independent quantum advice, single-output circuits distinguish exact or exponentially approximate state $2$-designs from Haar-random states with advantage at most $e^{-m^\alpha}$. Second, any state prepared from fewer than $k$ arbitrary input qubits and remaining $|0\rangle$ inputs has spectral weight at most $2e^{-m^\alpha}$ in a constant-energy-density band of an Anshu--Breuckmann--Nirkhe NLTS Hamiltonian encoding $k$ logical qubits. Both bounds hold for every fixed $\alpha\in(0,1)$.

authors.name: Xiaoming Sun, Jingheng Wang

papers.title: Monotonic probes of asymmetry and robustness of the quantum Mpemba effect
papers.summary: Entanglement asymmetry has emerged as a powerful probe of symmetry restoration and the quantum Mpemba effect. However, its conventional R\'enyi generalizations, defined as differences of R\'enyi entropies, are not monotones in the resource-theoretic sense. Here, we investigate an alternative family of asymmetry quantifiers based on sandwiched R\'enyi divergences, which satisfy monotonicity under symmetry-preserving quantum channels. Developing a two-parameter replica approach, we show how these quantities can be computed from charged moments and establish a remarkable correspondence with conventional R\'enyi asymmetries under the inversion of the R\'enyi index, $\alpha\leftrightarrow 1/\alpha$. This relation, exact for pure states, holds at leading order in the relevant scaling limits for homogeneous quantum quenches, including interacting integrable systems, and for Haar-random states. Applying these results to quenches from tilted ferromagnetic states, we demonstrate that the quantum Mpemba effect is remarkably robust, occurring throughout the entire family of sandwiched R\'enyi asymmetry monotones. We identify dynamical regimes in quenches from spatially inhomogeneous initial states where conventional R\'enyi asymmetries and genuine monotones exhibit qualitatively different behaviours. We also investigate a solvable toy model illustrating the possible dependence of Mpemba crossings on the R\'enyi index. Our findings establish a connection between conventional R\'enyi asymmetries and quantum resource theory, explaining their effectiveness in broad classes of nonequilibrium protocols while highlighting the additional information provided by genuine asymmetry monotones.

authors.name: Riccardo Travaglino, Michele Mazzoni, Pasquale Calabrese

papers.title: Practical limitations on robustness and scalability of quantum Internet
papers.summary: The realization of a desirably functional quantum Internet is hindered by fundamental and practical challenges such as high loss during transmission of quantum systems, decoherence due to interaction with the environment, fragility of quantum states under measurement, etc. We study the implications of these constraints by analyzing the limitations on the scaling and robustness of the quantum Internet. Considering quantum networks, we present practical bottlenecks for secure communication, delegated computing, and resource distribution among end nodes. In particular, we show that the device-independent quantum key distribution (DI-QKD) network of isotropic states with parameter $p$ has a finite diameter depending on $p$. Motivated by the power of abstraction in graph theory (in association with quantum information theory), that allows us to consider the topology of a network of users spatially separated over long distances around the globe or separated as nodes within the small space over a processor or circuit within a same framework, we consider graph-theoretic quantifiers to assess network robustness and provide critical values of communication lines for viable communication over quantum Internet. We consider some quantum networks of practical interest, ranging from satellite-based networks connecting far-off spatial locations to currently available quantum processor architectures within computers, and analyze their robustness to perform quantum information processing tasks. Some of these tasks form primitives for delegated quantum computing, e.g., entanglement distribution and quantum teleportation, that are desirable for all scale of quantum networks, be it quantum processors or quantum Internet.

authors.name: Abhishek Sadhu, Meghana Ayyala Somayajula, Karol Horodecki, Siddhartha Das

papers.title: Optimized experiment design and analysis for fully randomized benchmarking
papers.summary: Randomized benchmarking (RB) is a widely used strategy to assess the quality of available quantum gates in a computational context. RB involves applying known random sequences of gates to an initial state and using the statistics of a final measurement step to determine an effective depolarizing error per step of the sequence, which is a metric of gate quality. Here we investigate the advantages of fully randomized benchmarking, where a new random sequence is drawn for each experimental trial. The advantages of full randomization include smaller confidence intervals on the inferred step error, the ability to use maximum likelihood analysis without heuristics, straightforward optimization of the sequence lengths, and the ability to model and measure behaviors that go beyond the typical assumption of time-independent error rates. We discuss models of time-dependent or non-Markovian errors that generalize the basic RB model of a single exponential decay of the success probability. For any of these models, we implement a concrete protocol to minimize the uncertainty of the estimated parameters given a fixed time constraint on the complete experiment, and we implement a maximum likelihood analysis. We consider several previously published experiments and determine the potential for improvements with optimized full randomization. We experimentally observe such improvements in Clifford randomized benchmarking experiments on a single trapped ion qubit at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). For an experiment with uniform lengths and intentionally repeated sequences the step error was $2.42^{+0.30}_{-0.22}\times 10^{-5}$, and for an optimized fully randomized experiment of the same total duration the step error was $2.57^{+0.07}_{-0.06}\times 10^{-5}$. We find a substantial decrease in the uncertainty of the step error as a result of optimized fully randomized benchmarking.

authors.name: Alex Kwiatkowski, Laurent J. Stephenson, Hannah M. Knaack, Alejandra L. Collopy, Christina M. Bowers, Dietrich Leibfried, Daniel H. Slichter, Scott Glancy, Emanuel Knill

papers.title: Quantifying the Functional Size of Large-Scale Quantum Networks
papers.summary: Large-scale quantum networks enable distributed quantum tasks by sharing entanglement between distant nodes. Since entanglement distribution in such networks relies on stochastic local operations and classical communication (SLOCC), the resulting end-to-end entanglement degrades with path length and exhibits statistical variations, limiting the usable range while also making the quantification of its functional size challenging. Here, we develop a statistical framework to quantify a network's functional size by analyzing the statistics of end-to-end entanglement connections established through arbitrary entanglement-distribution protocols. This framework yields a global network metric in the form of the graph radius of viable regions up to which the distributed entanglement meets specified task thresholds. In addition to identifying absolute viable regions, within which a task is guaranteed to satisfy the prescribed thresholds, the framework identifies probabilistic viable regions, within which the task succeeds with a specified confidence. Further, it yields the viable node fraction, defined as the expected fraction of network nodes accessible from a given source node for the task, and reveals that network topology strongly influences the number of nodes contained within a network's viable region, even when the viable radii are identical. Applying the framework to quantum key distribution on random networks reveals sharp threshold behavior in the viable node fraction showing that small improvements in elementary-link quality can produce a rapid increase in the viable node fraction of the network. Viable regions in a quantum network obtained using our statistical framework therefore provide a task-oriented characterization of quantum-network functionality allowing comparison of entanglement-distribution strategies and network designs.

authors.name: Md Sohel Mondal, Vladimir S. Malinovsky, Siddhartha Santra

papers.title: Quantum squeezing amplification with a weak Kerr nonlinear oscillator
papers.summary: Quantum squeezed states, with biased quantum noise, have been widely utilized in quantum sensing and quantum error correction applications. However, generating and manipulating these nonclassical states with a large squeezing degree typically requires strong nonlinearity, which inevitably induces additional decoherence that diminishes the overall performance. Here, we demonstrate the generation and amplification of squeezed states in a superconducting microwave cavity with weak Kerr nonlinearity. By subtly engineering an off-resonant microwave drive, we observe cyclic dynamics of the quantum squeezing evolution in a displaced frame of the cavity. Furthermore, we deterministically realize quantum squeezing amplification by alternately displacing the Kerr oscillator using the Trotterization technique, achieving a maximum squeezing degree of 14.6 dB and a squeezing rate of 0.28 MHz. Our demonstrated displacement-enhanced squeezing operation offers a hardware-efficient approach for generating large squeezed states, promising potential applications in quantum-enhanced sensing and quantum information processing.

authors.name: Yanyan Cai, Xiaowei Deng, Libo Zhang, Zhongchu Ni, Jiasheng Mai, Peihao Huang, Pan Zheng, Ling Hu, Song Liu, Yuan Xu, Dapeng Yu

papers.title: Non-Perturbative Geometric Framework for Qubit Gates under Always-On Couplings
papers.summary: Always-on couplings in qubit arrays enable multi-qubit entanglement but also generate crosstalk. We present a geometric framework for a driven qubit at fixed detuning, in which the SU(2) evolution traces a curve on a sphere whose radius is determined by the detuning and the control pulse is the curve's geodesic curvature, reducing gate design to drawing a curve. Closed loops yield crosstalk-free single-qubit gates, with a zero-area condition for undetuned subspaces, while nonzero-area loops also permit entangling-gate constructions. The framework is non-perturbative in the conditional detuning, within a dispersive block-diagonal approximation valid when the transverse mixing $g/\Delta$ is small, and recovers perturbative dynamically corrected gate methods as its flat-space limit. Noise robustness can be imposed as an additional constraint. We show numerically that in two- and three-qubit Heisenberg chains the single-qubit gates are robust to coupling and frequency noise, and outperform a representative perturbative robust gate by over an order of magnitude where perturbation theory breaks down.

authors.name: Junkai Zeng, Lin Chen, Xiu-Hao Deng

papers.title: Quantitative Quantum Soundness for Bipartite Compiled Bell Games via the Sequential NPA Hierarchy
papers.summary: Compiling Bell games under cryptographic assumptions replaces the need for physical separation, allowing nonlocality to be probed with a single untrusted device. While Kalai et al. (STOC'23) showed that this compilation preserves quantum advantages, its quantitative quantum soundness has remained an open problem. We address this gap with two primary contributions. First, we establish the first quantitative quantum soundness bounds for all bipartite compiled Bell games via a newly formalized convergent sequential Navascu\'es-Pironio-Ac\'in (NPA) hierarchy: any polynomial-time prover's score is controlled by a finite-level hierarchy value, and finite-level convergence gives a negligible gap to the commuting quantum value, or to the tensor-product quantum value under flat optimality. Second, we develop the sequential NPA hierarchy as a computational tool of independent interest, establishing its convergence and a stopping criterion based on flatness, and identifying its conic dual as a sparse SOS hierarchy.

authors.name: Igor Klep, Connor Paddock, Marc-Olivier Renou, Simon Schmidt, Lucas Tendick, Xiangling Xu, Yuming Zhao

papers.title: The role of entropy production and thermodynamic uncertainty relations in the asymmetric thermalization of open quantum systems
papers.summary: The asymmetry between heating and cooling in open quantum systems is a hallmark of nonequilibrium dynamics. Here, we investigate the thermalization of a quantum system weakly coupled to a bosonic thermal bath under detailed balance, focusing on the entropy production rate and the quantum thermokinetic uncertainty relation (TKUR). Within the sector of states that remain diagonal in the energy basis we derive a perturbative expression for the time-dependent entropy production rate by expanding the relative entropy around equilibrium in terms of Liouvillian eigenmodes. Through this expansion, we determine that the spectral gap, the overlap of the initial state with the slowest decay mode, and the mode weight control the entropy production. Particularly for the thermal qubit, the ratio of the initial rates of heating and cooling has an exact closed form. Heating involves a higher initial entropy production, and hence faster thermalization, solely because of its larger spectral gap, i.e., the bath-temperature dependence of the dissipative rate. The TKUR is then used as a diagnostic tool that relates the asymmetry to the precision bounds on heat-current fluctuations. The analysis presented here is intended to clarify the thermodynamic origin of the asymmetry within the well-controlled Markovian case.

authors.name: \'Alvaro Tejero

papers.title: Learning photonic quantum states
papers.summary: Learning quantum state properties is both a fundamental and practical problem in quantum information theory. Classical shadows have emerged as an efficient method for estimating properties of unknown quantum states, with rigorous statistical guarantees, by performing randomized measurement on few copies of the state. With the advent of photonic technologies, formulating efficient learning algorithms for such platforms comes out as a natural problem. Here, we introduce a practical classical shadow protocol for learning photonic quantum states via randomized passive linear optical transformations and photon-number measurement. We provide rigorous theoretical guarantees showing that our scheme is sample- and time-efficient for measuring physical observables of interest. We experimentally demonstrate our photonic classical shadow protocol on both a twelve-mode and a twenty-four-mode integrated quantum processing unit, and showcase its versatility with five different applications, including Hamiltonian measurement and learning complex photonic states.

authors.name: Hugo Thomas, Ulysse Chabaud, Pierre-Emmanuel Emeriau

papers.title: Blockade-induced exchange primitives for scalable neutral-atom QPU
papers.summary: Many quantum hardware platforms natively support either phase or exchange operations, yet converting between these two forms of control typically incurs substantial overhead. Rydberg-blockade neutral-atom arrays are highly developed for phase control. Here, controlled exchange is introduced as a native, blockade-programmed phenomenon in a collective excited manifold. Target operations are engineered such that two competing exchange pathways between |01> and |10> destructively interfere, while a single collective four-photon channel mediated by a symmetric Rydberg excitation remains resonant and drives a direct SWAP, with all other qubit configurations undergoing an identity action. Exchange conditionality follows from blockade, where exciting a control atom to a Rydberg state shifts and blocks the target collective resonance, suppressing exchange, whereas leaving the control in the ground manifold enables exchange in a single step. This approach yields a family of controlled-exchange gates with coherent average gate fidelities above 99.99% at selected operating points, while reducing circuit depth and Rydberg-state exposure time by an order of magnitude relative to decomposed implementations. Joint parameter optimization reduces sensitivity to laser-intensity fluctuations, Doppler shifts, and interatomic-distance uncertainty, with several SWAP-family gates retaining fidelities above 99.6% under realistic experimental fluctuations and Rydberg decay. Finally, the anisotropic interaction generalizes the same principle to multiplexed controlled-exchange operations, providing compact hardware-level primitives for conditional information routing in extended neutral-atom arrays.

authors.name: Mohammadsadegh Khazali, Klaus M{\o}lmer

papers.title: Antisymmetrization of composite fermionic states for quantum simulations of nuclear reactions in first-quantization mapping
papers.summary: I present a first-quantization deterministic algorithm for antisymmetrizing a spatially separated target-projectile system containing $N_T$ and $N_p$ identical fermions, respectively. The method constructs a fully antisymmetric wavefunction from the product of two independently antisymmetrized many-body states, each of which may be a superposition of Slater determinants. The algorithm uses a Dicke-state ancilla register that coherently encodes all one-particle exchange channels between the two subsystems and, crucially, requires only single-particle swaps to generate the full antisymmetric structure. After consolidating distinct control conditions using logical or operations, the optimized circuit uses $N_TN_p$ single-particle exchanges, up to $N_p$ of which can be performed in parallel. The correct fermionic phase is incorporated through the application of $Z$ gates on $N_T$ ancillae, after which the ancilla register is efficiently uncomputed using a compact sequence of controlled operations. This construction provides a nontrivial and scalable protocol for preparing fully antisymmetric states in reaction and scattering simulations, significantly expanding the range of systems that can be addressed with first-quantized quantum algorithms.

authors.name: Ionel Stetcu

papers.title: Tunable many-body burst in isolated quantum systems
papers.summary: Thermalization in isolated quantum many-body systems can be nonmonotonic depending on an initial state. We demonstrate that a burst---a transient deviation from thermal equilibrium---can be created at a designated time from a low-entangled initial state for a nonintegrable mixed-field Ising chain, by developing a systematic numerical method to construct such a low-entangled state. Contrary to the typical spreading of information, the created burst is accompanied by a slow or even negative entanglement growth. We analytically show that a burst becomes probabilistically rare after a long time. Our results suggest that a nonequilibrium state is maintained for an appropriately chosen initial state until quantum scrambling becomes dominant. Our predictions can be tested by quench experiments with programmable quantum simulators.

authors.name: Shozo Yamada, Akihiro Hokkyo, Masahito Ueda

papers.title: On the emergence of quantum mechanics from stochastic processes
papers.summary: The stochastic--quantum correspondence reinterprets quantum dynamics in terms of an underlying stochastic process on a configuration space. We generalize its lifting prescription, overcoming restrictions on the reachable density matrices without enlarging the configuration space or its associated Hilbert space. A compatibility relation and Kraus dictionary connect stochastic kernels to completely positive, trace-preserving (CPTP) maps: every finite-dimensional kernel admits a compatible lift, and these lifts collectively encompass all quantum channels as the kernels vary. We describe sufficiently regular composable CPTP dynamics through time-local Lindblad generators. We establish that every rooted quantum dynamical family admits a stochastic realizer on the same configuration space, and that a revival of configuration-space distinguishability rules out every Markovian realizer on that space.

authors.name: Jason Doukas

papers.title: Detection of quantum imaginarity using moments and its interferometric realization
papers.summary: Complex numbers, intrinsic to the formulation of quantum theory, play a pivotal role in enabling advantages across a broad range of quantum information-processing tasks. Despite their fundamental importance, practical and scalable criteria for detecting quantum imaginarity remain relatively underexplored, particularly methods that enable its identification with reduced experimental overhead. In this work, we propose a realistic and experimentally feasible method to detect quantum imaginarity using a moment-based approach. Our framework relies on experimentally accessible moments of the Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distribution, enabling scalable detection in high-dimensional systems without requiring full state tomography. We then present illustrative examples to support our detection scheme. Finally, we present an interferometric scheme for measuring these moments, paving the way for experimental implementation of our detection protocol.

authors.name: Sudip Chakrabarty, Saheli Mukherjee, Ananda G. Maity, Bivas Mallick

papers.title: Robust quantum metrology using disordered probes
papers.summary: Disorder is ubiquitous in quantum devices including quantum probes designed and fabricated for quantum parameter estimation and sensing. We investigate the robustness of a quantum probe against the presence of glassy disorder. We define a disorder marker quantifying the effect of the disorder by expanding the quantum Fisher information in terms of different orders of the standardized central moments of the disorder-distributions. We classify the quantum probes in terms of the possible values of the disorder marker, and analytically show, for a disorder-sensitive probe with identical and weak disorder on all or a subset of the parameters of the probe-Hamiltonian, that the absolute value of the disorder marker exhibits a quadratic dependence on the disorder strength. We derive a robustness scale intrinsic to the probe that competes with the disorder, and provide a prescription for estimating the maximum disorder strength that the probe can withstand from the disorder-free probe-Hamiltonian for a given initial state of the probe, which can be computed without the disorder averaging. We also extend the prescription to classical Fisher information, and provide an operational perspective to the proposed marker in experiments. We demonstrate our results in the case of a single-qubit probe under disordered magnetic field, and a multi-qubit probe described by a disordered one-dimensional Kitaev model with nearest-neighbor interactions.

authors.name: Vishnupriya K., Harikrishnan K. J., Amit Kumar Pal

papers.title: The Quantum Kicked Rotor: A Paradigm of Quantum Chaos. Foundational aspects and new perspectives
papers.summary: The kicked rotor provides a simple yet powerful model for introducing many of the central concepts of classical and quantum chaos. Despite its apparent simplicity, it exhibits rich dynamical behavior and has found applications across a wide range of fields, including atomic and optical physics, condensed matter physics, and emerging quantum technologies. This chapter begins by exploring foundational ideas using the kicked rotor as a unifying framework. We first discuss the transition from regular to chaotic motion in the classical system, and then introduce key quantum phenomena such as dynamical localization and quantum resonances. Special attention is devoted to the emergence of characteristic time scales and their role in the quantum-classical correspondence. To make these ideas more concrete, we also provide a brief overview of experimental realizations of the kicked rotor and its variants, illustrating how theoretical concepts are implemented in practice. In the second part of the chapter, we guide the reader toward more recent and advanced developments. Topics include near-resonant dynamics, topological features of kicked systems, the emergence of quantum dynamical phases inferred from classical transport properties, and extensions to non-Hermitian physics. We conclude with a discussion of open problems and future perspectives, outlining directions in which the kicked rotor continues to offer valuable insights.

authors.name: Giuliano Benenti, Giulio Casati, Jiangbin Gong, Zhixing Zou

papers.title: Squeezing and measurement of a mechanical quadrature via PID feedback
papers.summary: Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) control is used for automatically regulating a measurable quantity to a desired setpoint. It is widely used in different types of classical control electronics. Here, we show how generalizing the feedback term in quantum systems to include derivative and integral components influences both the transient and steady-state behavior of the amplitude and squeezing of a mechanical quadrature in an optomechanical system. We show that, the derivative feedback leads to enhanced unconditional squeezing. Furthermore, we demonstrate how feedback may be employed to drive a mechanical quadrature to a desired setpoint, and to track an external force. Our findings offer new routes for an improved quantum state control and measurement precision.

authors.name: Alberto Hijano, Tero T. Heikkil\"a

papers.title: Quantum rotation sensing from superintegrability
papers.summary: Detection based on quantum principles such as entanglement has the capacity to achieve finessed levels of sensitivity, bringing transformative impacts to applications. In this study, we propose a rotation sensing protocol using an extended Bose-Hubbard model in a four-site configuration. The design, based on a simple population imbalance measurement to quantify rotation, profits from the property of superintegrability. The implementation of the sensing protocol achieves rotation-detection sensitivity scaling as $N^{-3/2}$, where $N$ is the number of particles. Remarkably, the sensitivity lies close to the quantum Cram\'er - Rao bound. Our results illustrate superintegrability opportunities for advancing the field of quantum sensing.

authors.name: Leandro Hayato Ymai, Karin Wittmann Wilsmann, Joel Bacellar Neves, Arlei Prestes Tonel, Jon Links, Angela Foerster

papers.title: Ancilla-Assisted Quantum Process Tomography using Bound entangled states
papers.summary: Lu \textit{et al.} [Ann. Phys. (Berlin) \textbf{534}, 2100550 (2022)] raised the question of whether bound entangled states can be useful for ancilla-assisted quantum process tomography (AAQPT). We answer their question in the affirmative by constructing bound entangled states that are faithful and hence allow complete reconstruction of an unknown quantum channel. We also study the effect of local filtering, which can increase the computable cross norm and realignment of a state while destroying its faithfulness. We further examine the performance of bound entangled probes, taking into account the stability of channel reconstruction rather than faithfulness alone. We find that bound entangled states can provide better-conditioned reconstruction than any separable probe, despite their entanglement being nondistillable.

authors.name: Gurvir Singh

papers.title: Construction of three-qubit positive-partial-transpose entangled states of rank four
papers.summary: Multiqubit positive-partial-transpose (PPT) entangled states provide canonical examples of bound entanglement and stringent test cases for multipartite separability criteria. We study PPT entangled states of the minimum possible rank in the three-qubit system, namely rank four. In the established terminology, states with a nonzero Lorentz invariant are called type I, whereas those with a zero Lorentz invariant are called type II. Every such state constructed from an unextendible product basis (UPB) has a nonzero Lorentz invariant and hence is of type I. We give a necessary and sufficient criterion for determining whether a type-I state is SLOCC-equivalent to a PPT entangled state constructed from a UPB. For type-II states, we obtain a Bell-basis normal form and prove that it exhausts all such states up to SLOCC equivalence. We further give a necessary and sufficient condition for two states in this normal form to be SLOCC-equivalent. We also determine the range of the Lorentz invariant for multiqubit states.

authors.name: Yonggang Cheng, Lin Chen

papers.title: Quantum theory of a three-photon Kerr parametric oscillator: from exact solution to the Kerr-cat qutrit
papers.summary: We investigate the quantum properties of a nonlinear Kerr oscillator driven by a three-photon pump. We identify an exact spectral degeneracy at which the interacting ground state admits a nonperturbative analytical solution. In the large-amplitude regime, the resulting manifold becomes threefold quasi-degenerate and forms delocalized three-headed quantum superpositions. Away from the exact degeneracy, we derive an approximate description of the threefold quasi-degenerate manifold in terms of $\mathbb{Z}_3$-symmetric superpositions of squeezed coherent states. These states differ qualitatively from conventional three-component cat states due to the presence of squeezing with a distinctive parametric dependence. By varying the pump-oscillator detuning, the squeezing can be enhanced, suppressed, or even reversed, leading to a squeezing-to-anti-squeezing transition. In the large-amplitude regime, the threefold manifold defines a noise-biased bosonic qutrit, which we term a Kerr-cat qutrit. We show that photon loss predominantly induces cyclic shift errors, while clock errors are suppressed, and quantitatively characterize the resulting noise bias. We further show that the detuning controls the noise bias through the squeezing. Going beyond stabilization, we construct arbitrary operations on a single Kerr-cat qutrit together with an entangling two-qutrit gate, providing a complete set of logical operations for universal qutrit quantum computation, and validate their action through full Lindblad simulations. Our results establish the three-photon Kerr oscillator both as a rich nonlinear quantum system with analytically tractable macroscopic states and as a platform for noise-biased bosonic qutrit quantum computation.

authors.name: Alessandro Bruno, Patrick P. Potts, Alexander Grimm, Matteo Brunelli

papers.title: Sudden death of entanglement, rebirth of magic
papers.summary: Local Markovian noise cannot bring entanglement back, but it can bring magic back. Local dissipation can push a state out of the stabilizer polytope as well as in. Under independent amplitude damping, the $n$-qubit state $\alpha|0^n\rangle+\beta|1^n\rangle$ with $0<\alpha<\beta$ loses its magic for a finite interval. The coherence between its ground and fully excited configurations keeps falling throughout. Magic returns when the fully excited population falls below that coherence. The damping probabilities for entanglement death and magic rebirth obey $\gamma_e+\gamma_+=1$ for every $n\ge2$. Magic returns to the register just as its reservoirs become entangled. For a sufficiently small ground-state amplitude the register is already fully separable at rebirth. Every proper marginal is a stabilizer mixture throughout, yet a joint parity measurement followed by Clifford decoding can concentrate the reborn magic onto one qubit. With thermal relaxation and dephasing, we find a range in which magic loss is permanent for every isolated qubit, yet two qubits exposed to the same noise can regain it.

authors.name: Chenfeng Cao

papers.title: A framework for the evaluation of transport-induced excitations in shuttling-based ion-trap quantum processors
papers.summary: We develop a theoretical and numerical framework to analyze the effect of transport on the motional states of ions in a trapped-ion quantum processor. We decompose the shuttling protocol into primitive operations and characterize these in terms of their heating performance. Instead of having to simulate the whole transport protocol for each complete ion trajectory, the method allows us to determine the heating properties of each primitive operation separately and obtain the global result through an algebraic expression. We demonstrate our method by applying it to an 8-qubit quantum processor design based on linear transport and swap operations for all-to-all connectivity. We show how to incorporate the price of motional operations at the level of the compiler as a cost function.

authors.name: Rodrigo Munoz, Phil Nuschke, Teresa Meiners, Brigitte Kaune, Christian Ospelkaus

papers.title: Adaptive identification of low-degree polynomials in quantum singular value transformation: application to nonlinear quantum properties estimation
papers.summary: Estimating properties of unknown quantum states via quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) often requires high-degree polynomials to handle small eigenvalues of density matrices. Specifically, the existing approaches determine the polynomial degree by relying on overly conservative worst-case bounds based on the minimum non-zero eigenvalue or the rank of the density matrices. In this work, we propose a spectral cutoff method that truncates the negligible eigenvalue tail depending on the task, the target accuracy, and the state, which enables the use of significantly lower-degree polynomials. To implement this, we develop a two-stage algorithm to estimate nonlinear properties, particularly von Neumann entropy and R{\'e}nyi entropy. In the first stage, we execute a search algorithm to identify the spectral cutoff directly from the unknown quantum state. In the second stage, we estimate the nonlinear properties utilizing QSVT with the degree of the polynomial adaptively determined by the cutoff. This two-stage algorithm enables adaptive property estimation without prior knowledge of the minimum eigenvalue or the rank, using low-degree polynomials beyond conventional worst-case choices.

authors.name: Jumpei Kato, Akira Tanji, Hiroyuki Harada, Kaito Wada, Kosuke Ito, Naoki Yamamoto

papers.title: Locally Acting Grover Mixers for Constraint-Preserving QAOA
papers.summary: The Grover mixer quantum alternating operator ansatz (GM-QAOA) employs the Grover mixer to confine the quantum evolution to the feasible subspace defined by the problem. Its mixing unitary, however, requires a global multi-controlled phase-shift gate acting on all qubits, resulting in substantial circuit overhead on near-term quantum devices. In this work, we propose locally acting Grover mixers with independent variational parameters, tailored to initial states that admit a product structure over disjoint qubit subsystems, which may be obtained by encoding only a subset of problem constraints into the initial state preparation. The proposed method preserves the search space defined by the initial state while reducing the mixing-circuit gate count and depth relative to the global Grover mixer, as the global multi-controlled phase-shift gate is replaced with local operations on disjoint subsystems. Numerical simulations on the exact-cover problem and the traveling salesman problem (TSP) demonstrate that the proposed method achieves solution probabilities comparable to those of the original GM-QAOA, while using shallower circuits with fewer gates. Comparisons with shared-angle local Grover and partitioned XY-ring mixers characterize the trade-offs between solution quality, circuit complexity, and optimization overhead. We further compare two constraint encoding strategies for the TSP, encoding only a subset of constraints versus all constraints into the initial state preparation, and show that the former combined with the proposed mixer can yield markedly more compact circuits at the point where comparable solution quality is achieved.

authors.name: Minjin Choi, Dongkeun Lee, Junghee Ryu

papers.title: Direct-Coupled Architectures for Magic-State Factories
papers.summary: In surface-code magic-state factories, the interface that passes level-1 T states to level 2, i.e., the transport channels, waiting spots, and $|0\rangle$ correction patches, occupies a large part of the factory area. We remove this interface by applying adaptive measurement, a principle known from gate teleportation, to the consumption of T states: in adaptive X/Y consumption, the T-state patch used for a $\pi/8$ rotation is read out in the X or Y basis depending on the merge outcome. The basis choice itself performs the $\pi/4$ correction, so no correction patch is needed and a T state can be consumed wherever it already sits. Building on this property, we present direct-coupled architectures in which level-1 suppliers are attached directly to the level-2 core. D1 consumes each T state in its supplier output slot and removes the interface entirely; D2 adds one small buffer per supplier so that the supplier continues distilling without pause. Because the method changes only how a supplied T state is consumed, it applies to the many factories that perform $\pi/8$ rotations by multi-patch Pauli measurements. As an example, we apply it to a CCZ factory and compare it with Litinski's factory under the same logical-error model and the same area accounting. For a maximum output period of 120 cycles, D1 and D2 reduce the area by 24% and 29% without increasing the space-time volume, and the smallest D1 factory is 37% smaller than the smallest Litinski design. The same approach also reduces the area of two-level T factories.

authors.name: Sungyeon Kook, Yujin Kang, Ilkwon Sohn, Jun Heo

papers.title: RubriQ: Rubric-Guided Group Relative Policy Optimization for Constraint-Aware Quantum Circuit Synthesis
papers.summary: Quantum circuits are crucial for understanding quantum algorithms and must be correct and efficient on quantum processing units (QPUs). Reinforcement learning (RL) with verifiers can train large language models (LLMs) to synthesize circuits; however, the reward system is unclear. In this study, we present RubriQ, a quantum rubric, where a verifier ensures correctness and scores assess cost. We demonstrate that, leveraging group relative policy optimization, the verifier controls correctness, while scores rank correct circuits. Our evaluation includes unitary, statevector, stabilizer-tableau, and randomized verifiers consisting of quantum Fourier transform (QFT), phase-estimation (QPE), and Trotter unitaries, along with Clifford, entanglement, unitary, arithmetic, and adder quantum circuits, up to 192 qubits. Our results show that training increases correct outputs from 7% to 91%, whereas the binary reward closes less than 10%. Notably, among verified circuits, the rubric reduces average cost by 91%. We believe our framework provides valuable insights into practical quantum computing.

authors.name: Ziqing Guo, Ziwen Pan

papers.title: Dynamical Complexity of Projected Ensembles: A Geometric Quantum State Approach
papers.summary: We study the emergence of complexity in finite-size quantum systems as their dynamics transition from closed and coherent evolution to interacting and effectively open behavior. Using a state-based geometric framework, we represent mixed quantum states as probability measures on complex projective Hilbert space. Obtained by conditioning on the environment in a fixed basis, these geometric quantum states coincide with the projected ensembles that underlie deep thermalization and emergent quantum state designs. This representation allows us to track how interactions reshape the underlying pure-state geometry. We introduce two complementary diagnostics, a distinguishability measure based on the Wasserstein distance between nearby projected ensembles, which quantifies sensitivity to initial states, and a state-space coverage index, which measures long-time exploration of the subsystem state space. Applied to the quantum kicked top, both diagnostics generally increase with interaction strength. Their dependence on environment size is structured by parity symmetry, with integer-spin systems often exhibiting greater sensitivity and state-space coverage than half-integer-spin systems. These results highlight finite-size quantum effects and provide a geometric approach to quantifying dynamical complexity deep in the quantum regime.

authors.name: Komal Sah, Fabio Anza, Alexandra M. Jurgens, James P. Crutchfield

papers.title: Statistical Mechanics of Non-Abelian Learnability Transitions
papers.summary: Monitored many-body quantum systems can undergo sharp learnability transitions characterized by how much information can be learned by the observer. When the dynamics conserves a non-Abelian charge, such as an $SU(2)$ spin, understanding how the observer learns the total charge remains an outstanding problem. Unlike the Abelian case, where charge measurements on distinct sites commute, the $SU(2)$-symmetric readouts are noncommuting fusion measurements, making learning a genuinely quantum inference problem. We propose a theory of $1+1d$ monitored quantum dynamics with $SU(2)$ symmetry, and show that it can be described by an effective replicated loop model comprised of a replica-pairing field and a diffusive ($z=2$) background sector that carries the $SU(2)$ charge and remains gapless throughout the phase diagram. Our theory predicts that the "spin-sharpening" and entanglement transitions coincide as a single transition, which is supported by numerics. Ordering of the pairing field produces volume-law entanglement and hides the background sector from measurements, leading to a learning time of $t\sim L^{3}$ for the total spin. When the pairing field disorders, the background sector alone gives logarithmic entanglement and a diffusive learning time $t\sim L^{2}$. Our analysis is controlled by a large-loop-fugacity expansion.

authors.name: Ruochen Ma, Romain Vasseur

papers.title: Robust Quantum Key Distribution Arbitrarily Close to Local Correlations
papers.summary: Recently, Wooltorton et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 210802 (2024)] and Farkas [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 210803 (2024)] have exhibited the mismatch between Bell inequality violations and their cryptographic application in device-independent quantum key distribution, by showing that arbitrarily close to the set of local behaviours there exist quantum correlations guaranteeing a constant rate of secret key. While these results require correlations attaining the maximum quantum value of a suitable Bell observable (aka the Tsirelson bound) and rely on a kind of ideal self-testing of a maximally entangled state and associated Bell measurement, here we show that the effect is robust: for every one of the Bell inequalities considered by Wooltorton \emph{et al.}, a constant rate of secret key ensues if the observed Bell violation is sufficiently close to the respective Tsirelson bound. For these and also the Bell inequalities of Farkas, we furthermore present numerical results based on semidefinite relaxations of the minimum min-entropy consistent with a certain Bell violation, which demonstrate that small but nonzero key rates can be guaranteed (in principle) by practical and efficient means.

authors.name: Hari Krishnan SV, Andreas Winter

papers.title: Electrostatic Stabilization of Near-Surface Quantum Sensors via Dielectric Interface Engineering
papers.summary: Control of charge-state stability in near-surface quantum defects is critical for nanoscale sensing, yet remains particularly challenging under ultra-high vacuum (UHV), where surface-induced band bending destabilizes the metrologically relevant charge-state. Here, we present a robust and reproducible approach for stabilizing shallowly implanted (< 10 nm deep) nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in near-UHV conditions (P = $3 \times 10^{-9}$ mbar) based on dielectric interface engineering. Through measurements on individually addressable NV centers, we demonstrate that a TiO2 coating on the diamond suppresses surface-induced electrostatic fields, yielding a 79% increase n NV- population and a 45% enhancement in NV-spin resonance contrast at room temperature. Coherent control measurements further reveal suppressed charge-state conversion dynamics. These results establish dielectric screening as a powerful and reproducible strategy to engineer charge transition energetics of NV centers in scanning-probe-compatible geometries under extreme conditions.

authors.name: Atharva Paranjape, Kathrin K\"uster, Olga Shevstova, Lisa Ebo, Toni Hache, Klaus Kern, Rainer St\"ohr, J\"org Wrachtrup, Aparajita Singha

papers.title: Simultaneous Reduction of Observables and Measured Qudits in Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Local Recovery
papers.summary: Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be the finite field with $q$ elements, $q$ being a prime power. For an entanglement-assisted or unassisted stabilizer code defined by an $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear space $C\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^{2n}$, a set of erasures and an associated repair group, we propose a procedure to compute a reduced set of observables and a reduced repair group of codeword qudits for correcting the given erasures. The computed set of observables has the smallest possible size for correcting the given erasures, within the stabilizer measurement model. The repair group is reduced by eliminating qudits that need not be measured. In classical local recovery, such symbols can be found by Gaussian elimination, although the resulting repair group need not be a smallest one. In the quantum case we eliminate an admissible set of qudits. Finding a largest admissible set is a linear matroid parity problem, and for Calderbank--Shor--Steane (CSS) codes defined by two linear codes it is a linear matroid intersection problem. Both problems are solvable in deterministic polynomial time. We give closed-form upper bounds on the size of reduced repair groups for general codes and for codes from Euclidean and Hermitian orthogonality, and, for two-code CSS codes, a sharper bound with a min--max formula. Based on these bounds, we propose quantum counterparts of the concept of dimension locality of classical local recovery.

authors.name: Carlos Galindo, Fernando Hernando, Ryutaroh Matsumoto

papers.title: Optimal GHZ extraction from MABK violations
papers.summary: For $n\geq3$ parties, we prove that the least Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger (GHZ) extractability compatible with a Mermin--Ardehali--Belinskii--Klyshko (MABK) score between the biseparable bound and the quantum maximum equals $(1+t)/2$, where $t$ rises linearly with the score from $t=0$ to $t=1$ across this range. The minimum is over all states and binary measurements in arbitrary local dimensions, and the extractability of a state is the supremum over local channels of the overlap with the GHZ state. With a qubit at every party, the minimum is strictly larger for $00$ by the MABK score and the expectations of five calibrated binary measurements on the qutrit, assuming known local dimensions and a known two-dimensional qutrit subspace invariant under both Bell observables of that party; the bound vanishes when these expectations equal their values in the mixture.

authors.name: Avraham Kreindel (Yohananov), Aryeh Lev Zabokritskiy (Yohananov)

papers.title: Sufficient quantum provenance: retained fields and certified recording precision
papers.summary: Quantum executions that share a provenance record can still produce different output distributions. We determine which execution details a record must retain, and at what precision, to guarantee agreement within a declared Hellinger tolerance. Under a specified channel model, a certificate combining independent stochastic mechanisms and coherent rotation differences fixes the recording precision without output simulation or explicit dependence on register dimension. For four-qubit quantum approximate optimization at depth one, a 13-bit comparison record suffices at tolerance 0.05 over a declared continuous noise range, uniformly in programmed angles for each fixed task, against 19 bits for a gate-by-gate sum over the same bin family. Pairwise separation constraints characterize sufficient field sets on finite context classes and expose omissions that pass individually but fail jointly. Separately, six-qubit measurements on an IBM Heron processor show, over six tested contexts, that raw outputs need a two-label record, supplied by qubit layout, whereas outputs after a fixed application decoder need no additional context bits, at tolerance 0.15 with 97% simultaneous confidence under stationary, independent shots. Execution records can thereby be designed to carry checkable agreement guarantees.

authors.name: George Kourousias, Sergio Carrato, Roberto Pugliese, Aljo\v{s}a Hafner, Francesco Guzzi, Matteo Bill\`e, Fulvio Bill\`e, Panagiotis Dimitrakis

papers.title: Secure Quantum Handshakes: Quantum Network Verification Via Simon's Algorithm
papers.summary: Quantum networking represents the future of secure communication, enabling fundamentally new capabilities through quantum information exchange. However, these networks require secure, high-fidelity quantum communication channels. Currently, there is no reliable method to verify whether clients entering a quantum network truly possess quantum state communication capability over robust channels. In this work, we introduce a client-validation protocol that functions as a proof-of-quantum-communication handshake. Our protocol secures a quantum network against classical spoofers, faulty quantum computers, and genuine quantum devices connecting to the network over noisy or insecure channels. We validate the efficacy of this protocol through numerical simulations under erasure, dephasing, and depolarizing noise models.

authors.name: Reece Robertson, Sejal Patil, Sebastian Deffner

papers.title: The Generalized BEADS Representation: A Correlation-Based Visualization of Mixed Quantum States
papers.summary: Quantum mechanics and particularly quantum information theory suffer from a lack of intuitive images. Visualization tools offer novel perspectives on many problems in quantum physics by revealing important properties of quantum states and processes that are otherwise obscured by abstract mathematical formalisms. Here, we extend the previously established BEADS representation of pure states to the so-called generalized BEADS representation of mixed quantum states. We introduce spherical functions, so-called beads to visualize correlation structures of mixed quantum states in an informationally complete way. A recursive optimization scheme is used to obtain minimum-entanglement pure state decompositions of all subsystems of a given N-qubit state. We show how correlation function components can be decomposed into individual contributions that correspond to different types of correlations of mixed states. This allows us to visually characterize the total correlation, genuine n-partite entanglement, nonclassical quantum-discord-type correlations as well as classical correlations. We further introduce a new quantifier for W-type entanglement for identifying W-class states. After outlining the mathematical details relevant for constructing the representation, we examine the generalized BEADS representations for various types of mixed states including product, classically correlated, separable but nonclassically correlated, as well as entangled states. As exemplary applications of the generalized BEADS representation, we showcase entanglement distillation and the effects of noise channels.

authors.name: Celina Br\"autigam, Steffen J. Glaser, Dennis Huber

papers.title: Recovery gates as a resource in repetition-code process tomography: exhaustive gate-optimal designs for three, five and seven qubits
papers.summary: Repetition-code tomography compares a code's logical channel with a reference through a decoder, almost always standard minimum-weight. We ask how many single-qubit Pauli gates it needs with the measurement basis fixed---the constraint that makes the count a resource. Exhaustive enumeration at $n=3$, $5$ and $7$, ranks decided in exact arithmetic, gives minima of $0$, $1$ and $5$ gates, against $6$, $10$ and $14$ for first-order and $6$, $50$ and $308$ for full decoding. The count depends only on how many sites are corrected, not which, so it splits into a budget and a placement that decides identifiability; more sites is not monotonically better: at $n=7$ full decoding has rank $24$ of $27$, and the $n=3$ precision curve is U-shaped under a calibration floor. The three-gate design is $9.0$ times more precise than the standard six-gate decoder at the median of $40$ working points and better at every one, by $1.8$ to $88$-fold; fixing the placement in advance gives $6.9$, or $3.1$ for a pre-commitment never worse. Two certified placements lose no direction either sees and reach $10$\,mrad within twice the shots wherever identifiable. Measuring the reference everywhere gives a $16(n+2)$-component map, full rank at $n=3$, $5$ and $7$ with no gate and $44$ to $93\%$ fewer settings, though at $n=5$ and $7$ its floor stays one and three orders above target. The optima are not covariant under chain reversal.

authors.name: Long Huang

papers.title: The importance of shear strain in narrow Si/SiGe quantum wells
papers.summary: Several heterostructure profiles have been proposed for Si/SiGe quantum wells, to improve the operation of quantum-dot spin qubits. These structures share a common goal of generating either of the two wave vectors that govern the conduction-band valley coupling, dubbed $k_0$ and $k_1$. Here, we focus on the long-wavelength $k_1$ term that couples valleys when paired with shear strain, and which governs the Dresselhaus spin-orbit coupling. We show that shear strain induced by metal top gates may be enough to activate the $k_1$ valley-coupling mechanism, mitigating the need for "ultrasharp" interfaces, as commonly assumed for large valley energy splittings. We propose a scheme featuring narrow quantum wells that does not require ultrasharp interfaces, but should still provide large deterministic valley splittings (when paired with shear strain), and large spin-orbit couplings and $g$-factor corrections, which are of great interest for experimental implementations.

authors.name: Hudaiba Soomro, Talise Oh, M. A. Eriksson, Benjamin D. Woods, Mark Friesen

papers.title: Gate-tunable spin splitting for Andreev spin qubits in Ge quantum well heterostructures
papers.summary: Ge-based super-semi heterostructures are a promising platform for implementing Andreev spin qubits (ASQs).
