Combining large-scale density-matrix renormalization group with bosonization methods, we map the phase diagram of a spin-1 chain with next-nearest-neighbor (NNN) coupling and single-ion anisotropy (SIA). We pinpoint two topological phase transitions: a weakly first-order transition between the Haldane and NNN-Haldane phases with a tiny gap and a continuous transition from the Haldane phase to the large-$D$ phase located via level spectroscopy with Richardson extrapolation. For negative SIA, a spontaneous dimerized phase emerges between the N\'eel and NNN-N\'eel phases. Its transition into the N\'eel phase is a deconfined quantum critical point falling into the eight-vertex universality class, with central charge $c = 1$ and critical exponents varying continuously along the phase boundary. For positive SIA, we identify two vector-spin-chirality orders---an ordinary chiral phase and a narrow Haldane-chiral phase---with a weakly first-order transition between them, evidenced by a soft jump in the string order parameter. Our results reveal that frustration and anisotropy generate emergent orders and non-Landau criticalities, providing a platform for deconfined and topological phase transitions.

authors.name: Qiang Luo, Shijie Hu, Jize Zhao, Sebastian Eggert, Xiaoqun Wang

papers.title: Foundation interatomic potentials capture structural disorder in metallic glasses
papers.summary: Foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials transfer well across chemical and structural space, yet their reliability for highly disordered metallic states is less established. Metallic glasses are a demanding benchmark: they have traditionally been modeled with Embedded Atom Method (EAM) potentials fitted to specific compositions, while ab initio molecular dynamics remains too expensive at the required sizes and timescales. Using the prototypical Cu-Zr-Al glass, we show that foundation potentials capture structural disorder, reproducing the structure, quenching dynamics, and elastic, mechanical and thermal properties of the amorphous state at near first-principles accuracy. We benchmark MACE foundation models against a classical EAM potential along molecular dynamics quenches, validating against density functional theory and experiment, first at Cu46Zr46Al8 and then across the good glass-forming region of the ternary. We further test two specialization routes: fine-tuning on glass structures generated with Lennard-Jones surrogate models, and on automatically generated small periodic cells (ASSYST). Models pre-trained on databases that include non-equilibrium liquid and amorphous configurations, such as OMAT, are accurate and transferable across composition out of the box, clearly outperforming the composition-specific EAM potential. Fine-tuning on target glass structures brings only modest gains, while specialization on small crystalline cells degrades the description of disorder. The readiness of foundation potentials for disordered metals is therefore set mainly by the diversity of their pre-training data rather than by system-specific fine-tuning, shifting the modeling effort from bespoke dataset generation to pre-training coverage and careful validation of the resulting dynamics.

authors.name: Dario Massa, Luca Leoni, Antoni Wadowski, Kacper Cybinski, Anshul D. S. Parmar, Carmine Autieri, Cesare Franchini, Jan Wrobel, Silvia Bonfanti, Piotr Sankowski

papers.title: Length-scales and fractal scaling in dairy gels: comparisons of the insights from ultra-small angle neutron scattering and rheology
papers.summary: A key structural parameter that dictates the textural properties of a particulate gel is the fractal dimension (Df) of the network indicating self-similarity within the spatial range defined by the correlation length (xi). In this study dairy gels are formed from reconstituted skim milk at defined CM volume fractions via two different mechanisms: acidification, and enzymatic (rennet)-induction. Oscillatory rheology is performed to obtain the gelation times, the time-scale for the maturation of mechanical properties of the gel, and the viscoelastic properties of the gel. A direct probe of gel structure is ultra-small-angle neutron scattering (USANS) examining length-scales from approximately 60 nm up to 15 microns. Structural information is extracted from USANS of matured gels by comparing the measured differential scattering cross-section with that calculated from a model constrained by the sample composition. Time-scales for structural equilibration from USANS perspective were shorter than the rheological gelation time for both gels. Rheological scaling theories are utilized to relate the microstructure to their bulk mechanical properties. We show that the fractal scaling at low-q (scattering vectors), due to aggregation of CM, extracted from the USANS at the longest timescales is described by a power-law density-density correlation function, and that rheology relates - through Shih-Wu-Morbidelli models - the local elasticity both within and between the fractal flocs formed by these particles over different size ranges to the bulk moduli of the gels. There are similar values of fractal dimensions from both techniques but different sizes attributed to the complex fractal evolution during dairy gelation, which leaves space to refinements of the models.

authors.name: Koduvayur A. Ramya, Liliana de Campo, Markus Strobl, Fran\c{c}ois Bou\'e, Christopher J. Garvey

papers.title: Quantum-centric assessment of saturated ferromagnetism beyond the flat-band limit
papers.summary: Saturated ferromagnetism has been proven for every on-site repulsion $U > 0$ in Hubbard models with a flat lowest band, and the interaction required for it grows with the band width $W$ when the band becomes dispersive. We study the dispersive case at quarter filling by quantum-selected configuration interaction and sample-based quantum diagonalization with IBM Quantum's Heron processors, focusing on the quantized square of the total spin of the computed states. We treat a sawtooth chain of 16 unit cells on 64 qubits, whose full configuration space of $1.1\times 10^{14}$ determinants exceeds that of one of the largest full configuration interaction calculations, and obtain the stability diagram of saturated ferromagnetism on the decorated square lattice in the plane of $U$ and $W$. For the chain, a subspace of only $3\times 10^{-5}$ of the full configuration space gives a state with more than $97\%$ of its weight in the sector of maximal spin. For the decorated square lattice of $4\times 3$ unit cells on 48 qubits, the computed states in subspaces of less than $1\%$ of the full configuration space switch from low-spin states to nearly fully polarized states at $U \simeq 2W$. The calculations also give a rigorous lower bound of $1.9W$ on the critical interaction of the $4\times 3$ lattice.

authors.name: Kosuke Nogaki, Tomonori Shirakawa, Seiji Yunoki, Ryotaro Arita

papers.title: Hidden f-wave TIVC and Quantum Phase Transitions in Metallic States of Twisted Bilayer Graphene
papers.summary:
We study the ground state phase diagram of twisted bilayer graphene at magic angle as function of carrier density and the Coulomb interaction. The carrier density is varied between the fillings $
u=-2$ and $
u=-3$ and the Coulomb interaction is tuned by changing the gate distance. Our results reveal that the well established Kramers intervalley coherent (KIVC) phase near $
u=-2$, contains a hidden $f$-wave time-reversal symmetric intervalley coherent (TIVC) order, whose strength gradually increases within the metallic regime of the intervalley coherent (IVC) phase away from $
u=-2$. This finding is interesting in the light of a recent experimental work [26], where the signatures of the TIVC phase has been reported in ultra-clean samples. We further show that the system goes through multiple phase transitions as the carrier density is tuned. Near the $
u=-2$, the IVC phase is the ground state, which gives way to valley polarized phase through a second-order-like phase transition as the carrier density is lowered. Further tuning of density pushes the system into the quantum anomalous Hall phase through gradual development of the sublattice polarization. These phase transitions are accompanied by major reconstructions of the Fermi contours.

authors.name: Arindam Pramanik (Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, India, Academic Centre for Materials and Nanotechnology, AGH University of Krakow, Poland), Unmesh Ghorai (Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, India, School of Physics and Astronomy, Tel Aviv University, Israel), Rajdeep Sensarma (Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, India)

papers.title: Patterns and correlations in time-reversal symmetry breaking
papers.summary: Time-reversal symmetry (TRS) breaking is the hallmark of non-equilibrium statistical physics. This notwithstanding, in translationally invariant systems, it is almost always treated only as a global quantity. We propose to use the local entropy production rate as a spatio-temporal field to describe extended homogeneous non-equilibrium systems. We find that this field generically displays spatial correlations, with a typical length that grows as we approach some non-equilibrium phase transitions. We also show that the correlation length associated with the local entropy production rate follows heretofore unknown scaling laws involving control parameters as well as the observation time used for trajectories. Our work paves the way to the use of the local entropy production as a powerful observable to identify the scale and source of TRS breaking in non-equilibrium systems.

authors.name: Ido Patish, Mathias Casiulis, Dov Levine

papers.title: Fractional Chern Insulator in a Finite-Range One-Band Model
papers.summary: A common route for realizing fractional Chern insulators (FCIs) is to engineer bands that mimic the physics of Landau levels, which serve as the single-particle topological background for the emergence of strongly correlated fractional quantum Hall states. Here we show that FCIs can also arise in a one-band model devoid of any single-particle quantum geometry. Through a systematic trivialization of the single-particle quantum geometry in FCI models that go beyond the Landau-level paradigm, we construct a single-band, interaction-only model on the square lattice, with all terms confined to individual plaquettes. At one-third filling, exact diagonalization and density-matrix renormalization-group calculations reveal a three-state low-energy manifold, a Hall conductance of $-2e^2/(3h)$, and fractional charge pumping without translation-symmetry breaking. We trace this behavior to nontrivial topology in the repulsive two-particle sector, offering a microscopic perspective on the strongly correlated origin of fractional quantum Hall order.

authors.name: Tong Liu, Hoi Chun Po

papers.title: Anisotropic magnetic-field modulation of hysteretic sheet resistance in few-layer ferroelectric WTe2
papers.summary: Ferroelectricity in few-layer WTe2, a polar semimetal, originates from interlayer sliding and can be probed through gate-dependent resistance hysteresis. Yet the role of magnetic fields in this transport signature remains largely unexplored. Here, we examine magnetic-field-induced changes in the hysteresis in exfoliated few-layer WTe2. Applying an out-of-plane magnetic field produces a pronounced hysteresis enhancement, while an in-plane field yields a negligible response. Analysis of the individual hysteresis branches reveals distinct magnetotransport responses of the two ferroelectric states, which increase their resistance separation under magnetic field. The enhancement exhibits a robust power-law field dependence and a temperature evolution closely resembling that of magnetoresistance. Our results reveal a close association between anisotropic magnetotransport and ferroelectric hysteresis, underscoring the interplay between magnetic response and ferroic order in a two-dimensional polar semimetal.

authors.name: Arpan Manna, Soumik Mukhopadhyay

papers.title: Magnetization, susceptibility, and entanglement entropy in antiferromagnetic star-shaped homometallic tetranuclear and pentanuclear Cu(II) complexes
papers.summary: We present a theoretical investigation of the magnetization, magnetic susceptibility, and quantum entanglement entropy in antiferromagnetic star-shaped tetranuclear ($Cu_4$) and pentanuclear ($Cu_5$) Cu(II) clusters, motivated by experimentally realized molecular spin systems. In both cases, the study presents a discussion of the comparison between experimental data and theoretical analytical calculations of magnetic susceptibility as a function of temperature. The correlation between magnetization jumps and magnetic susceptibility peaks, along with the presence of entanglement entropy plateaus as a function of external magnetic fields, is analyzed in the low-temperature regime. Overall, the results demonstrate that the cluster size, geometry, and interaction anisotropy play a crucial role in shaping both the thermodynamic and the entanglement properties. In addition, the study is based on antiferromagnetic Heisenberg spin Hamiltonians, with the inclusion of the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction.

authors.name: Gor Mirzoyan, Vladimir V. Papoyan, Andrea Trombettoni, Nikita Titov, Lev Ananikyan, Nerses Ananikian

papers.title: Collective relaxation dynamics and vitrification in hexatic smectic binary equimolar mixtures containing component with varying C$_3$F$_7$CH$_2$OC$_m$H$_{2m}$- chain length
papers.summary: Differential scanning calorimetry, polarizing optical microscopy, and broadband dielectric spectroscopy are applied for investigation of phase transitions in equimolar binary mixtures consisting of the MHPOBC liquid crystal as one component and 3FmHPhH6 homologs as a second component with different C$_3$F$_7$CH$_2$OC$_m$H$_{2m}$- chain length (m = 2-7). The paraelectric smectic A* - ferroelectric smectic C* - antiferroelectric smectic C$_A$* - hexatic smectic X$_A$* - glassy smectic X$_A$* sequence is observed for all mixtures. The appearance of the bond-orientational order in smectic X$_A$* is accompanied by an additional relaxation process P$_{hex}$ in dielectric spectra at the low-frequency side of the P$_H$ phason, consistent with its assignment to bond-orientational fluctuations. The empirical exponential-power relationship is proposed for the ratio between the relaxation times of P$_{hex}$ and P$_H$. The behavior of the structural $\alpha$-relaxation and secondary $\beta$-relaxation in smectic X$_A$* depends on the m parameter, changing from overlapping $\alpha$ and $\beta$ processes for m = 2 to well-separated for m = 6, 7. A double glass transition is observed by calorimetry on heating for m = 5-7. The calorimetric glass transition temperature shows a composition-dependent correspondence with temperatures at which either the P$_H$ or $\alpha$-relaxation time reaches 100 s, suggesting that different relaxation processes may contribute to vitrification.

authors.name: Aleksandra Deptuch, Mateusz P\k{a}czek, Anna Drzewicz, Marcin Piwowarczyk, Magdalena Urba\'nska, Ewa Juszy\'nska-Ga{\l}\k{a}zka

papers.title: Electronic topological modes in hexagonal NbSi$_{2}$ with a double helix
papers.summary: Chiral systems can host nontrivial topological states, including characteristic edge modes and Fermi arcs. Here, we investigate the electronic properties of hexagonal NbSi$_2$ with chiral symmetry using first-principles calculations for both bulk and slab geometries. We find that spin--orbit coupling (SOC) is relatively weak. Notably, the topological edge state originates from structural chirality rather than the SOC. From the Berry curvature analysis, we confirm the existence of Weyl points, some of which carry a Chern number of $\pm 2$. Furthermore, we demonstrate the existence of chiral edge modes with extended Fermi arcs around high-symmetry points. Finally, we investigate the real-space localization using spatially resolved and site-dependent density of states (DOS). We demonstrate that the surface states can be exclusively associated with the chiral Si chains.

authors.name: Issam Mahraj, Andrzej Ptok

papers.title: A Thermodynamically Consistent Model of a Rechargeable Salt-in-Polyelectrolyte Battery
papers.summary: We present an isothermal, thermodynamically consistent model of a salt-in-polyelectrolyte battery with intercalation and deintercalation reactions of cations occurring at the electrode-electrolyte interfaces under galvanostatic conditions. For the electrolyte, we consider polyelectrolytes, which are polyanions, with neutralizing cations (i.e., counterions) such as lithium, along with a monovalent salt containing the same cations. Models of batteries containing either a dual-ion-conductor (DIC) electrolyte (i.e., uncharged polymers with added salt) or a single-ion-conductor (SIC) electrolyte (i.e., charged polymers without added salt) emerge as limiting cases of this thermodynamically consistent model. Once the model is presented in its most general context, we make specific choices so that it captures well-known mechanisms. In particular, the governing diffusion equations recover Fick's law of diffusion, and the cation-transfer reaction rate is described by the Butler--Volmer equation. The DIC and SIC limiting cases provide a framework for comparing the corresponding batteries. One-dimensional DIC and SIC charge--discharge simulations at matched current and duration illustrate concentration redistribution, polarization, and electrode utilization. Numerical accuracy checks quantify sensitivity to discretization; distinct initial inventories qualify the comparison.

authors.name: Charlotte Beckford, Rajeev Kumar, Steven M. Wise

papers.title: Exact Lyapunov spectrum and localization length of the multichannel disordered Schr\"odinger equation
papers.summary: We consider the multichannel Schr\"odinger equation, describing the evolution of $N$ transverse modes in a finite width wire, in the presence of a Gaussian white noise potential in the unitary symmetry class. For arbitrary energy $E$ and disorder strength $T$, we compute exactly the set of Lyapunov exponents $\{ \gamma_n(E,T) \}_{1 \leq n \leq N}$ which define the decay rates of the wave functions. In the large energy regime, we recover that the Lyapunov exponents are equally spaced, as predicted by the so-called DMPK approach. However we show that this property breaks down at arbitrary energy, giving rise to a richer Lyapunov spectrum. We also uncover a direct relation between the localization length, given by the inverse of the smallest Lyapunov exponent, and the density of states. Our derivation relies on the analysis of matrix stochastic differential equation for a modified Riccati matrix.

authors.name: Aur\'elien Grabsch

papers.title: Signatures of multiorbital density waves in the electronic Raman response of bilayer nickelates
papers.summary: Recent Raman scattering experiments on bilayer nickelates have revealed pronounced spectral features in the spin-density-wave state, whose microscopic origin remains controversial, with interpretations ranging from two-magnon excitations to electronic transitions across SDW-induced gaps. Here, we demonstrate that the multiorbital electronic structure of low-pressure bilayer nickelates naturally generates distinct orbital-selective Raman signatures in different symmetry channels. Using a two-orbital bilayer model incorporating the $d_{3z^2-r^2}$ and $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbitals in the orthorhombic structure, we analyze the electronic Raman response of the multiorbital spin-spinless double stripe SDW state and show that the $B_{2g}$ response exhibits a peak at the energy scale $(M_{z^2}+M_{x^2})/2$, associated with SDW gap openings in weakly hybridized bands. In contrast, the dominant peak in the $B_{1g}$ channel emerges at the multiorbital energy scale $(M_{z^2}^2+M_{x^2}^2)^{1/2}$, reflecting the strongly hybridized character of the relevant electronic states. These distinct energy scales provide a unified interpretation of several Raman signatures observed in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ and offer a means of disentangling the orbital contributions to the SDW order parameters. Our results highlight that in contrast to the superconducting state, Raman peak positions in the SDW state cannot generally be identified with a single SDW gap and establish symmetry-resolved electronic Raman scattering as a sensitive probe of multiorbital density-wave order.

authors.name: Lauro B. Braz, Ge He, Luis G. G. V. Dias da Silva, Ilya M. Eremin

papers.title: Seebeck and Hall effects in charge-neutral ballistic graphene as probes of electron-electron interactions
papers.summary: Electron-hole asymmetry of the Coulomb velocity renormalization is responsible for finite Seebeck and Hall coefficients in charge-neutral graphene. In the ballistic regime the thermopower is small, $0.1$--$1~\mu$V/K, because the chemical-potential shift required by $n_e{=}n_h$ cancels its leading part. When the electron-electron scattering length falls below the sample length, the thermopower crosses over to a collision-dominated value of $4$--$10~\mu$V/K, that is an order of magnitude larger. This crossover is a direct thermoelectric marker of the breakdown of ballistic transport and a baseline for identifying the Dirac fluid.

authors.name: Z. Z. Alisultanov, A. V. Kavokin

papers.title: Mode-resolved spin-wave spectroscopy by a single paramagnetic center
papers.summary: We demonstrate mode-resolved ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) spectroscopy using optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) of a single nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center in (111)-oriented diamond. A two-tone drive couples the magnetization dynamics to the NV spin resonance via the magnon Kerr effect. We show that the NV can detect the static stray field produced by this effect down to precession cone angles $\theta \approx \SI{1}{\degree}$, providing a generic scheme to measure the linear FMR spectrum with the spatial resolution of an atomic-size probe. We validate the approach on a normally magnetized yttrium iron garnet (YIG) microdisk, resolving its intrinsic quantized spin-wave modes. Scanning the probe across the surface, we map the spatial profile of the modes and find quantitative agreement with analytical models.

authors.name: Cl\'ement Fourniols, Maki Umeda, Eric Clot, Eyub Yildiz, Isabelle Joumard, Benjamin Pigeau, Olivier Klein

papers.title: LetzElPhC: an electron-phonon code for efficient exciton-phonon workflows
papers.summary: We present \texttt{LetzElPhC}, an open-source software package that computes electron-phonon matrix elements from the output of density functional perturbation theory calculations performed with the \texttt{Quantum ESPRESSO} code. By interfacing directly with the \texttt{Yambo} code and exploiting crystal symmetries, \texttt{LetzElPhC} enables a scalable workflow for evaluating exciton-phonon matrix elements while enforcing strict gauge consistency between one-electron Bloch states and Bethe-Salpeter excitonic wave functions across the full Brillouin zone. This symmetry-preserving approach avoids phase ambiguities and significantly reduces both computational costs and memory requirements. To support large-scale simulations on dense momentum grids, the package incorporates Fourier interpolation of dynamical matrices and perturbed Kohn-Sham potentials, accounting for long-range dipole and quadrupole interactions in both two- and three-dimensional materials, combined with multi-level parallelization and efficient parallel I/O. Together, these capabilities seamlessly complement the \texttt{Yambo} code to enable first-principles simulations of phonon-assisted optical spectroscopies, which we demonstrate through applications to resonant Raman scattering in monolayer $\text{WSe}_2$ and phonon-assisted luminescence in cubic AgBr.

authors.name: Muralidhar Nalabothula, Ludger Wirtz

papers.title: AFM metrology for 3D high aspect ratio semiconductor structures
papers.summary: Transistors have long been the foundation of the semiconductor industry, with continuous architectural innovations enabling the scaling of integrated circuits while maintaining high performance. Advancements in deposition and lithographic techniques have further expanded design possibilities, while increasing structural complexity demands stricter process control. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) offers a rapid and reliable metrology solution, providing high-resolution measurements and robust statistical analysis of critical parameters. In this work, we present clearly resolved individual profiles of lines and spaces in high aspect ratio (HAR) gate all around FET (GAAFET)-type structures on both the nanosheet (NS) region and in the isolation region between the nanosheets and we present a comprehensive statistical evaluation of their critical dimensions.

authors.name: Hokyun Chin, Shihwei Yu, Lucas Rencker, Omid Tajalizadehkhoob, Khalid El Maghawry Elsayed, Po-Cheng Wu, Duygu Akbulut, Niranjan Saikumar, Hamed Sadeghian

papers.title: Magnetic Reconfiguration Controls Spin Splitting and Spin-Orbit-Coupled Responses in Compensated Magnets
papers.summary: Compensated magnets provide a versatile platform for spin-dependent electronic and transport phenomena. Here, we show that magnetic reconfiguration, i.e., selective reversal of local moments without changing the underlying crystal structure, can profoundly transform the nonrelativistic spin splitting and spin-orbit-coupled responses of spin-degenerate antiferromagnets (AFMs), altermagnets (AMs), and compensated ferrimagnets (cFIMs). Strikingly, magnetic configurations with nearly degenerate energies can exhibit qualitatively different spin-split band structures and anomalous Hall responses, allowing a small magnetic-energy scale to produce large changes in physical properties. Combining tight-binding models, oriented spin space group analysis, and first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that converting an AM configuration into cFIM states activates staggered onsite-potential contributions to spin splitting, complementing the anisotropic-hopping mechanism of AMs and removing symmetry-enforced degeneracies. Moreover, cFIM symmetry permits an anomalous Hall response at first order in spin-orbit coupling, in contrast to the higher-order or orientation-constrained responses of corresponding AM states. We demonstrate this regime in Mn2Mo3O8, one of 12 cFIM candidates identified in the MAGNDATA database, and further demonstrate its generality by designing cFIMs from collinear AFMs, exemplified by MnGeO3 and Co2Mo3O8. Our results establish magnetic reconfiguration as a powerful symmetry-guided strategy for dramatically reshaping electronic and transport responses in compensated magnets.

authors.name: Yongqian Zhu, Lu Liu, Xiaobing Chen, Tong Zou, Yuntian Liu, Zehao Ji, Qihang Liu

papers.title: Diffusion Effects on a Stochastic Amplifier Driven by the Square of a Gaussian Field: Discontinuous Transition to Intermittency
papers.summary: We study the effects of diffusion on the transition to intermittency in stochastic amplification driven by the square of a Gaussian field. The transition is characterized by an order parameter quantifying the spatial uniformity of the amplification. We consider a model in which the diffusion-amplification process is embedded in a random lattice of point absorbers in such a way that the Feynman-Kac formula is restricted to Brownian paths with a range not exceeding a finite cut-off. In this setting, with the Gaussian driving field in a wide class of physical interest, we show that diffusion-induced damping of the amplification is sufficiently strong to change the nature of the transition: from continuous in the absence of diffusion, to discontinuous in the presence of diffusion.

authors.name: Philippe Mounaix

papers.title: High-Throughput Orientation Extraction via Symmetry-Adapted Filters
papers.summary: An algorithm for finding the orientation of objects in an image that have a known rotational symmetry, the symmetry-adapted filter (SAF) algorithm, is presented. It is deterministic and training-free, which makes it fast and reproducible. A filter that encodes the known rotational symmetry and approximate peak width is centered on the symmetry center of the object of interest, masked to the region of interest, and rotated to maximize its inner product with the image. The approach is demonstrated on more than 20,000 small-angle neutron scattering images of a torque-driven skyrmion lattice. It is also demonstrated on atomically resolved real-space images, where mapping local atomic orientations enabled the identification of grains and grain boundaries and the quantification of lattice relaxation.

authors.name: Caden Myers, Yucong Chen, Nathan Chalus, Morten R. Eskildsen, Tess Smidt, Simon J. L. Billinge

papers.title: EGQCA Code: automated high-throughput thermodynamic modeling of solid solutions
papers.summary: Modeling disordered systems from first principles across the full composition range is a long-standing computational challenge. We present a code package implementing the extended generalized quasichemical approximation (EGQCA), which describes solid solutions through the statistics of a finite set of clusters and enables their thermodynamic modeling at arbitrary compositions and temperatures. The package automates the complete workflow and interfaces with both DFT codes and universal machine-learned interatomic potentials (uMLIPs). We show that replacing DFT with uMLIPs reduces the cost of the cluster calculations by up to five orders of magnitude while preserving the thermodynamic predictions. To make computationally demanding properties tractable, we additionally introduce a cluster-selection algorithm that identifies the most relevant configurations. Together, these developments establish EGQCA as a fast and accurate framework for the thermodynamic modeling of solid solutions and a practical route toward high-throughput screening of disordered materials.

authors.name: Dominik Spath, Luka Wibmer, Kieran Bozier, Ralf Meyer, Eva Kogler, Efisio Madeddu, Chris Pickard, Markus Aichhorn, Simone Di Cataldo, Luiz T. F. Eleno, Christoph Heil, Pedro N. Ferreira

papers.title: Measuring the Roughness of Quasi-Circular Interfaces at Finite Resolution
papers.summary: Interface roughness characterizes the boundary fluctuations across different length scales, which can reveal information about a material''s pinning landscape and collective interfacial behaviour. Finite sampling and image resolution can bias the measured scaling properties, however. These effects can particularly complicate comparisons between circular domains of different sizes, where the number of resolved boundary points, and the relationship between angular and physical separations vary with the interface radius. Here, we benchmark the recovery of the roughness exponent and amplitude using synthetic self-affine interfaces generated by Fourier synthesis, mapped onto circular contours, and rasterized onto a pixel grid. We first compare displacement-correlation (B(r)) and structure-factor (S(q)) estimates for different interface lengths. To address non-uniform angular and radial spacing in a circular interface, we assess a reconstruction procedure that weights slope minimization against medial interface position. We find that while spectral estimates were most effective in the original interfaces, this advantage did not persist after circular mapping. Moderate smoothing was found to improve parameter recovery, but stronger smoothing can bias both the scaling exponent and roughness amplitude. These results, verified on both synthetic datasets, and an experimental ferroelectric system, identify limitations of circular-interface roughness measurements and provide a basis for further investigations into the evolution of circular domains under finite resolution experiments.

authors.name: Ralph Bulanadi, Asraful Haque, Sumner B. Harris, Rama Vasudevan, Yongtao Liu

papers.title: Origin of the anomalous shape of the $\gamma$-loop in paramagnetic Fe1-xCrx alloys from coupled Atomistic Spin Dynamics and ab initio Molecular Dynamics
papers.summary: The region of fcc stability in Fe-rich Fe-Cr alloys, the $\gamma$-loop, has an anomalous shape: at low temperatures, Cr addition initially stabilizes fcc, but above 8 at.% Cr it stabilizes bcc. At high temperatures, Cr always stabilizes bcc. This behavior reflects a delicate balance between magnetic, vibrational and configurational free-energy contributions that is challenging to capture from first principles. We investigate phase stability in Fe1-xCrx (x = 0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15) using coupled atomistic spin dynamics and ab initio molecular dynamics with thermodynamic integration. Gibbs free energy differences between fcc and bcc are calculated from 800 to 1800 K. Our calculations reproduce the experimental $\gamma$-loop and its compositional dependence, with near-quantitative accuracy for the $\gamma$-$\delta$ transition. The $\alpha$-$\gamma$ boundary, including its anomalous shape, is reproduced qualitatively, although transition temperatures are underestimated by approximately 200 K. Static calculations of magnetically ordered and disordered states provide an explanation: in ordered states, increasing Cr initially reduces the energetic preference for bcc over fcc, whereas in disordered states, Cr progressively stabilizes bcc at all compositions. Vibrational effects contribute to phase stability, while atomic short-range clustering at higher Cr content ($x \geq 0.15$) may explain the observed closing of the $\gamma$-loop from below. The simulations reveal finite Cr moments in the paramagnetic state, whose magnitudes depend on their local magnetic environment. The results demonstrate that the anomalous $\gamma$-loop arises from the interplay of magnetic energetics, magnetic disorder, lattice vibrations and chemical clustering, which must be treated on equal footing to capture phase stability from first principle

authors.name: Joakim Stenborg, Davide Gambino, Bj\"orn Alling

papers.title: Frozen Phonons on Dense $\mathbf{q}$-Grids Using Set Covers
papers.summary: Phonon dynamics determine a vast number of properties in the solid state, such as the heat capacity, thermal expansion, and thermal conductivity. Phonons are obtained through the dynamical matrix, which, in the frozen phonon approach, is calculated as a finite difference derivative of the analytical Hellmann-Feynman force. This approach unfortunately typically suffers from requiring very large supercells, even for modest $\mathbf{q}$-grids. The non-diagonal supercell method remedies this issue by determining the smallest supercell commensurate with a given $\mathbf{q}$-point, drastically reducing the supercell size, but in turn requiring a new supercell for each $\mathbf{q}$-point on the grid. This introduces redundancy, however, since a single non-diagonal supercell may be commensurate with several $\mathbf{q}$-points. In this work I present a method to determine a minimal set of supercells, such that every $\mathbf{q}$-point on the grid is commensurate with at least one supercell. I present an algorithm to solve the problem and prove that it yields the optimal solution, before summarizing the algorithm using pseudocode. The scaling of the number of supercells with the density of the grid is discussed. Numerical results on a variety of systems show the significant computational advantage of the method, which increases with the density of the grid.

authors.name: Sebastian Riis Thomsen

papers.title: Transverse Shifts Driven by Geometric Orbital Torque in Altermagnets
papers.summary: Anomalous transverse shifts in interface reflection are conventionally attributed to spin-orbit coupling or its pseudospin analogue. Here, we uncover a distinct geometric mechanism driven solely by an orbital torque arising from Fermi-surface anisotropy. During total reflection, an incident wave packet penetrates the anisotropic transmitted medium as an evanescent wave. There, the broken rotational symmetry about the interface normal exerts an orbital torque, and the accumulated angular impulse---the product of the torque and the dwell time---leads to a transverse spatial shift. Applying this mechanism to altermagnets without spin-orbit coupling, we show that the orbital torque is odd in spin. As a consequence, the two spin channels are deflected to opposite sides of the incident plane, giving an intrinsic spatial spin separation in altermagnets. The shift also inherits the angular symmetry of the altermagnetic spin splitting and is strongly enhanced near the onset of total reflection. Our work thus uncovers a new mechanism for transverse shifts, predicts a novel spin separation effect in altermagnets, and offers a direct probe of the altermagnetic order.

authors.name: Runze Li, Yugui Yao, Zhi-Ming Yu

papers.title: From Spin Glass Theory to Optimization in High Dimensions and Modern Artificial Neural Networks
papers.summary: This chapter pays tribute to Giorgio Parisi by reviewing the influence of his work on spin glasses and replica symmetry breaking (RSB) on combinatorial optimization and artificial neural networks. We first introduce replica and cavity methods through the matching and traveling salesman problems, before discussing random satisfiability and the development of survey propagation. We then examine applications to neural networks, emphasizing the connections between the geometry of solution spaces, computational hardness, and learning. Particular attention is given to rare regions of high local entropy and their role in algorithmic accessibility. Examples involving overparameterized models and asymmetric recurrent networks illustrate how these ideas connect constrained optimization and inference with concepts developed in spin-glass theory.

authors.name: Riccardo Zecchina, Gianmarco Perrupato

papers.title: Emergent Chern metal in strongly correlated moir\'e bilayers
papers.summary: We investigate the topological properties of a strongly correlated moir\'e transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) bilayer (such as twisted $\mathrm{MoTe}_2$ or $\mathrm{WSe}_2$) hosting a spin-charge separated state coupled to a layer-polarized helical spin texture. Analyzing an effective low-energy Hamiltonian for mobile spinless holons moving through this non-coplanar spinon background, we reveal pronounced asymmetric band warping. This warping closes the global indirect band gap across most of the parameter space, restricting true topological insulators to fine-tuned critical trajectories. However, a finite local direct gap persists, stabilizing broad regions of a topological Chern metal ($C = \pm 1$). Computing the Chern number and density of states, we demonstrate that this phase naturally yields a sizable, non-quantized anomalous Hall response accompanied by finite longitudinal conduction, providing a purely electronic strong-coupling mechanism for dissipative anomalous Hall states in moir\'e systems.

authors.name: Kaushal Kumar Kesharpu, Evgenii A. Kochetov

papers.title: Localization of an Individual Charge Fluctuator in a Si/SiGe Spin Qubit Device
papers.summary: Charge noise from two-level fluctuators (TLFs) limits gate fidelities in semiconductor spin qubits, yet locating individual fluctuators within a device remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate a spatial triangulation method that combines the gate dependence of a TLF's detuning with the chemical potential shifts it induces in a sensing dot. Applying this method to previously reported measurements from a gated Si/SiGe quantum dot device, we use electrostatic simulations to jointly constrain the fluctuator's three-dimensional position and the magnitude of its electric dipole moment. We localize the fluctuator to a region spanning 31 nm by 1 nm laterally and 4 nm vertically within the bulk of the atomic layer deposited aluminum oxide, identifying the material hosting this individual charge-noise source. The measurements are consistent with a vertically oriented TLF with a magnitude of 3 to 4 e$\mathring{A}$. This approach provides a route to determining which materials and interfaces host active charge fluctuators in semiconductor spin qubit devices.

authors.name: Leah Tom, John Nichol, Chris Anderson, Mark F. Gyure

papers.title: Measuring a buried Bi$_2$Te$_3$ epitaxial film through a protective Te cap: an exact three-layer terahertz analysis
papers.summary: Air-sensitive chalcogenide films are routinely protected by a capping layer, which must then be removed, or contacted through, before electronic transport can be measured, destroying the surface the cap was meant to preserve. Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy requires neither, but using it quantitatively demands a transmission model in which cap, film and substrate are treated on an equal footing. We formulate the cap/film/substrate problem exactly using a transfer matrix with a time-gated substrate, and show that the intuitive construction in which each thin layer contributes an independent Fabry--P\'erot factor fails for two adjacent thin films. In the thin-film limit we obtain a closed-form inversion together with a criterion for the error incurred by ignoring the cap. We apply the framework to Bi$_2$Te$_3$ films grown by molecular beam epitaxy on GaAs at three thicknesses, each prepared with and without a 25 nm Te cap. A Te-on-GaAs witness shows the cap to be optically indistinguishable from bare substrate, transmitting 1.00(4) of the substrate amplitude between 0.2 and 1.5 THz, which limits the error from neglecting it to 3.6 % for the 90 nm film, although the same estimate reaches 48 % at 25 nm. In this matched set, the capped films form an ordered series, monotonic in thickness in both conductance magnitude and lineshape, whereas the uncapped films do not. The capping layer therefore presents no obstacle to terahertz characterization, and in this set it coincides with a more reproducible film response.

authors.name: Guilherme R. Russo, Laura O. Dias, Eduardo D. Stefanato, Nicolas M. Kawahala, Sukarno O. Ferreira, Leonarde N. Rodrigues, Felix G. G. Hernandez

papers.title: Spin Loop Currents and Bulk-Edge Structure in Correlated Topological States of WSe$_2$/MoTe$_2$ Bilayers
papers.summary: Motivated by recent experiments, we theoretically investigate AB-stacked WSe$_2$/MoTe$_2$ bilayers. Our theory incorporates valence fluctuations, local and extended (longer-range) Hubbard interactions, including non-local interactions between carriers on the MoTe$_2$ layer. Within the parton mean-field framework, we show that the non-local interaction between MoTe$_2$ carriers can drive a transition between a topological Kondo semimetal(TKSM) and a topological Kondo insulator(TKI) at the filling fraction $\nu =2$. We attribute this transition to an emergent spin-loop current arising from the interplay between Ising spin-orbit coupling and non-local electron correlations. In addition, we investigate how the emergent spin-loop current affects edge transport and show that the two-point conductance takes a quantized value at certain bias voltages.

authors.name: Po-Jui Chen, Kevin P. Lucht, Andreas Gleis, Andrew J. Millis, J. H. Pixley, Daniele Guerci

papers.title: Brightening spin- and parity-forbidden interlayer excitons through rhombohedral stacking
papers.summary: Brightened symmetry-forbidden excitons can provide critical information about the electronic structure and many-body interactions in semiconductors. Recently, interlayer atomic registry has emerged as a new way to control atomically thin layered materials in both ground and excited states. Here we show that the rhombohedral stacking in a 3R-MoS_2 homobilayer can brighten two symmetry-forbidden interlayer excitons: one is a spin-unlike 1s exciton and the other is a parity-odd 2p exciton. The nature of these interlayer excitons is revealed by their gfactors as well as the hybridization patterns observed when they are tuned to resonate with intralayer excitons. Surprisingly, the hybridized 2p exciton exhibits a constructive quantum interference between the acquired transition dipoles, revealing a hidden gauge-invariant phase contrast between the constituent electronic states. Our results establish stacking control as a powerful approach for modulating quantum phases of excitons in 2D semiconductors.

authors.name: Haodong Hu, Chih-En Hsu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Hung-Chung Hsueh, Zhenglu Li, Ziliang Ye

papers.title: Moir\'{e}-induced self-trapping in a Bose-Einstein Condensate
papers.summary: The effect of moir\'{e} modulations on two-dimensional materials flattens their electronic energy bands, which enhances the effects of interactions and has been seen to give rise to several emergent electronic phases. We demonstrate this behavior with a moir\'{e} modulation extends to a quasiperiodic hopping model of interacting bosons on the honeycomb lattice. Without interactions, the velocity vanishes at a magic-angle transition, where a sharp onset of the zero-energy density of states and multifractal low-energy states appear. Including interactions, we study its interplay with quasiperiodicity by tuning the scale associated with self-trapping and diffusive wave packet dynamics. Near the magic-angle, we find that substantially weaker interactions lead to self-trapping and diffusive wavepacket dynamics, which we attribute to the vanishing moir\'{e}-induced minibandwidth. A new computational approach is presented that combines split-step time evolution with a truncated Chebyshev expansion as an efficient and general purpose approach to solving the Gross-Pitaevskii equation in the absence of translational symmetry. We discuss how our results can be explored in ultracold atom experiments using momentum space lattices or tweezer arrays.

authors.name: Keshav Badri, Kevin P. Lucht, Justin H. Wilson, Jedediah H. Pixley

papers.title: Magnons in solids with correlated atomic and nanoscale disorder
papers.summary: Atomic defects and disorder affect both the microscopic magnon excitations and the macroscopic physical properties of real-world magnetic materials. The rationalization of this relation has hitherto remained elusive, because of the intertwined challenges of simulating with quantum accuracy atomic- and nanoscale inhomogeneities and correlations, and their effect on the magnon spectral function determining observables such as spin stiffness. Here, we introduce a theoretical and computational framework to address these challenges. First, we develop the Coupled Optimization of SpIN Environment (COSINE) algorithm for efficiently relaxing the atomic structure and magnetic configuration of a solid with defects or disorder to a local energy minimum. Then, we discuss how to efficiently obtain exchange interactions accounting for local compositional, structural, and magnetic-moment inhomogeneities. Finally, we develop a paraunitary unfolding approach for Bogoliubov bosons, which allows us to predict the magnon spectral function in materials with any magnetic order, including systems with canting and full, partial, or no magnetic-moment compensation. We showcase our approach in a representative defective ferrimagnet for generality, and then combine it with state-of-the-art spin-informed machine-learning potentials to quantitatively predict how nonuniformities in the spatial distribution of vacancy defects control blurring of effective magnon bandstructures.

authors.name: Alex Moorhouse, Joseph Barker, Michele Simoncelli

papers.title: A microscopic continuum model for moir\'e transition metal dichalcogenides
papers.summary: Twisted transition metal dichalcogenides (tTMDs) have emerged as a fascinating platform for many-body phases --- displaying fractional Chern insulators and superconductivity as a function of doping. Here, we give a microscopic derivation of a continuum model which accurately describes their bandstructure across a range of twist angles with angle-independent parameters. This angle-independent description rests on retaining both the monolayer valence and conduction bands, which introduce tunnelling paths through AB-stacked regions; upon downfolding to the valence band, these paths supply a substantial twist-tunable contribution to the interlayer coupling. We show that the model is a perturbation of a chiral model with a magic angle, explaining the near-ideal quantum geometry of the moir\'e bands. The model further produces a strongly different orbital magnetic moment to the single-orbital theory --- predicting an anomalous Landau level slope --- and a redistribution of charge between the layers, modifying the moir\'e ferroelectric potential.

authors.name: Julian Ingham, Harshitra Mahalingam, Raquel Queiroz

papers.title: A computer-assisted proof of one-cell snaking and lattice trapping for a nonlinear square lattice
papers.summary: We establish a computer-assisted proof of lattice trapping in an infinite nonlinear square lattice with interaction potential $\phi(t)=(1-e^{-3t^2})/6$ and an antiplane crack far field $K\sqrt{r}\sin(\theta/2)$. We construct a connected branch of equilibria whose single-cell segment contains exactly two nondegenerate quadratic folds, with a stability sequence of stable, Morse index one, and stable in the full energy space. The fold loads satisfy $0.458970.00296$. A uniqueness argument establishes exact translation closure and smooth continuation across lattice cells. The proof combines renormalized energy, Schur complement estimates, analytic infinite-tail bounds, interval arithmetic, and exact integer positivity certificates. All finite input data, verification programs, and recorded certificate outputs are provided in the accompanying certificate archive.

authors.name: Jiangchao Qian

papers.title: On the level lines of bilayer potentials with a finite number of harmonics
papers.summary: We consider ``bilayer'' potentials formed by the superposition of two periodic potentials in a plane. We assume that both potentials share the same rotational symmetry and employ an approximation involving a finite number of harmonics in their Fourier expansions. An analysis of the level lines of the resulting quasiperiodic potential (a problem posed by S.P. Novikov) near the percolation threshold makes it possible to describe the behavior of large-scale closed level lines in this limit. The results presented here can also be applied to broader classes of bilayer potentials that possess ``good'' analytical properties.

authors.name: A. Ya. Maltsev

papers.title: Discotic columnar phase in a three-dimensional monomer-tetramer model of Heilmann and Lieb with side-to-side attraction
papers.summary: We study Model III of Heilmann--Lieb (1979), a lattice model for liquid crystals consisting of tetramers (plaquettes) on the cubic lattice at chemical potential $\mu$, interacting via a hard-core repulsion and a lateral attraction of strength $a>0$ between coplanar, aligned tetramers. The model was conjectured to exhibit liquid-crystalline order at low temperature provided that $\mu+2a>0$. We establish discotic columnar order throughout this regime, fully resolving the conjecture. Specifically, we prove the existence of exactly twelve extremal and periodic Gibbs measures, each breaking rotational symmetry, with one of three tetramer orientations dominant, and translational symmetry in exactly two directions, with one of four tetramer parities dominant within that orientation. Thus, the tetramers form one-dimensional columns arranged on a square lattice. This arrangement is not a priori evident from the zero-temperature picture, where energy only enforces a layered structure: each layer is fully packed and crystalline, but different layers are free to shift independently within their planes. The main novelty here lies in showing how thermal fluctuations lift this degeneracy in favor of the twelve ground states in which all tetramers share a common parity.

authors.name: Qidong He

papers.title: Quartet currents in a biased three-terminal diffusive Josephson junction
papers.summary: Biasing a three-terminal Josephson junction (TTJ) with symmetrical voltages $0,V,-V$ leads to new kinds of DC currents, namely quartet Josephson currents and phase-dependent multiple Andreev reflection (MAR) currents. We study these currents in a system where a normal diffusive metallic node $N$ is connected to three terminals $S_{0,1,2}$ by barriers of arbitrary transparency. We use the quantum circuit theory to calculate the current in each terminal, including decoherence. In addition to the stationary combination $\varphi_Q=\varphi_1+\varphi_2-2\varphi_0$ of the terminal phases $\varphi_i$, the bias voltage $V$ appears as a new and unusual control variable for a DC Josephson current. A general feature is the sign changes of the current-phase characteristics, manifesting in minima of the quartet ``critical current". Those sign changes can be triggered by the voltage, by the junction transparency or by decoherence. We study the possible separation of quartet currents from MAR currents in different regimes of parameters, including an "funnel" regime with very asymmetric couplings to $S_{0,1,2}$. In the regime of low transparency and asymetric couplings, we provide an analytic perturbative expression for the currents which shows an excellent agreement with the full numerical results.

authors.name: T. Jonckheere, J. Rech, C. Padurariu, L. Raymond, T. Martin, D. Feinberg

papers.title: Tomographic Electron Flow in Confined Geometries: Beyond the Dual-Relaxation-Time Approximation
papers.summary: Hydrodynamiclike electron flows are typically modeled using the Stokes-Ohm equation or a kinetic description that is based on a dual-relaxation-time approximation. Such models assume a short intrinsic mean free path $\ell_e$ due to momentum-conserving electronic scattering and a large extrinsic mean free path $\ell_\text{MR}$ due to momentum-relaxing impurity scattering. This assumption, however, is overly simplistic and falls short at low temperatures, where it is known from exact diagonalization studies of the electronic collision integrals that another large electronic mean free path $\ell_o$ emerges that describes long-lived odd electron modes---this is sometimes known as the tomographic effect. Here, using a matched asymptotic expansion of the underlying Fermi-liquid kinetic equation with multiple electron relaxation times, we derive a transport theory for tomographic flows in arbitrary smooth boundary geometries. Our key results are a set of governing equations for the electron density and electron current, their slip boundary conditions (which are applied at diffuse boundaries), and boundary layer corrections near diffuse edges. We find that the tomographic effect strongly modifies previous hydrodynamic theories for electron flows: In particular, (i) a local equilibrium is established in the bulk, where the flow is governed by Stokes-Ohm-like equations with significant finite-wavelength corrections, (ii) the velocity slip condition at the boundary is strongly modified and not accounted for by the widely used hydrodynamic slip-length condition, (iii) a large kinetic boundary layer of width $\sim\sqrt{\ell_e \ell_o}$ arises near diffuse boundaries, which is much larger than in conventional near-hydrodynamic theories, and (iv) all these effects are strongly suppressed by an external magnetic field. We illustrate our findings for electron flow in a channel.

authors.name: Nitay Ben-Shachar, Johannes Hofmann

papers.title: The flux of particles in a one-dimensional Fleming-Viot process
papers.summary: The Fleming-Viot process describes a system of $N$ particles diffusing on a graph with an absorbing site. Whenever one of the particles is absorbed, it is replaced by a new particle at the position of one of the $N-1$ remaining particles. Here we consider the case where the particles lie on the semi-infinite line with a biased diffusion towards the origin which is the absorbing site. In the large $N$ limit, the evolution of the density becomes deterministic and has a number of characteristics similar to the Fisher-KPP equation: a one-parameter family of steady state solutions, dependence of the long time asymptotics on the initial conditions, Bramson logarithmic shift, etc. One noticeable difference, however, is that in the Fleming-Viot case, the solution can be computed explicitly for arbitrary initial conditions and at an arbitrary time. By modifying the diffusion rule near the origin, one can produce a transition in the flux of absorbed particles, very similar to the pushed-pulled transition in travelling waves. Lastly, when a cut-off of order $1/N$ is added to the hydrodynamic equation, we find corrections of order $(\ln N)^{-2}$ or $N^{-\gamma}$ to the flux of absorbed particles, depending on whether the front is pulled or pushed, as for the correction to the velocity in travelling waves.

authors.name: \'Eric Brunet, Bernard Derrida

papers.title: Coulomb Interaction and Density-Independent Exciton-Scattering Processes in Atomically Thin Semiconductors
papers.summary: In quantum-kinetic approaches to the dynamics of Coulomb-bound many-body correlations such as excitons, trions, biexcitons or higher-order correlations, a detailed knowledge of the many-body Coulomb Hamiltonian serving as a starting point is important. In this manuscript, the second-quantized description of the Coulomb interaction between Bloch electrons in a Heisenberg-equation-of-motion approach in atomically thin semiconductors is derived and reviewed. Emphasis is put on a discussion of Umklapp processes and the dielectric screening including all local-field effects. A link between \textit{ab initio} methods of screening and few-band models in effective-mass approximations for the quantum kinetics is established and important Coulomb scattering processes contributing to the exciton energy landscape and density-independent exciton scattering are discussed.

authors.name: Henry Mittenzwey, Andreas Knorr, Thorsten Deilmann

papers.title: Breaking of clustering and macroscopic coherence under the lens of asymmetry measures
papers.summary: In one-dimensional systems, spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB) states are fragile by nature, as the injection of a non-zero energy density above the ground state is expected to restore the symmetry. This instability implies that local perturbations can lead to macroscopic correlation profiles, a breaking of clustering properties and even macroscopic quantum superpositions. In this work, we investigate the effect of interaction on this phenomenology by considering an interacting model with conserved domain wall number, that possesses a ferromagnetic ground state breaking the Z2 symmetry of the Hamiltonian. We first show that a local quench in this system amplifies quantum interferences, producing a macroscopic magnetisation profile that directly reflects the scattering phase of the model. Then, we use two asymmetry measures, namely the Entanglement Asymmetry (EA) and Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), to characterise the quantum coherence associated with the fluctuations of the magnetisation. By focusing on subsystems comparable in size to the light-cone of the perturbation, we confirm the emergence of macroscopic quantum coherence throughout the whole perturbed region. Finally, we discuss the link between EA and QFI and show that the variance/EA inequality for pure state can be generalised to a QFI/EA inequality for mixed states.

authors.name: Florent Ferro

papers.title: Rotational Phonons Activated by Magnetism as a Key Ingredient of Cuprate Physics
papers.summary: Circularly polarized lattice vibrations carry angular momentum and can link lattice dynamics to collective responses in strongly correlated materials, particularly cuprate superconductors. Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) reveals ubiquitous quasiparticle "kinks" near ~70 and ~40 meV in cuprates, often accompanied by peak-dip-hump (PDH) features, indicating strong coupling between electrons and low-energy bosonic excitations. However, the relevant phonon modes and the role of circularly polarized vibrations in these spectral anomalies remain largely elusive. Here, we investigate electron-phonon coupling (EPC) in hole-doped infinite-layer CaCuO2 at four selective hole dopings (12.5%-56.25%) using the Strongly Constrained and Appropriately Normed (SCAN) density functional with explicit magnetic interactions. At 25% doping, the magnetic phase exhibits substantially stronger EPC (lambda ~ 0.5), five times that of the nonmagnetic phase, producing kinks and PDH features over 40-80 meV, with self-energy magnitudes comparable to experiment. Oxygen rotational phonons dominate the coupling over 50-65 meV, while breathing modes play a lesser role; the rotational modes emerge exclusively in the magnetic phase. At 37.5% doping, lambda increases to ~1.6 due to strong coupling of low-frequency phonons near the Fermi-surface nesting wave vector, whereas at 56.25%, where Cu magnetic moments vanish, lambda decreases to ~0.4. The rotational modes carry staggered angular momentum that cancels in the unperturbed lattice; a time-reversal-breaking gyrotropic coupling on Cu sites lifts this cancellation, yielding a finite phonon thermal Hall conductivity. Our findings establish magnetism-enhanced EPC as an important ingredient of cuprate physics and identify rotational oxygen phonons as relevant to spectral anomalies, superconductivity, and the pseudogap thermal Hall effect.

authors.name: Yanyong Wang, Manuel Engel, Christopher Lane, Sougata Mardanya, Bahadur Singh, Henrique Miranda, Lin Hou, Sugata Chowdhury, Bernardo Barbiellini, Adrienn Ruzsinszky, John P. Perdew, Robert S. Markiewicz, Arun Bansil, Jianwei Sun, Ruiqi Zhang

papers.title: AlphaDiffract: Automated Crystallographic Analysis of Powder X-ray Diffraction Data
papers.summary: Materials identification and structural understanding from powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) data are long-standing challenges in materials science, fundamental to discovering and characterizing novel materials. A prerequisite for full structure solution is the accurate determination of the crystal lattice, including lattice parameters and crystallographic symmetries. Traditional methods for this are iterative and typically require expert input, and while existing deep learning approaches have shown promise, a robust, single-shot method for comprehensive lattice determination from experimental data remains a key goal. Here, we introduce AlphaDiffract, a deep learning framework for jointly predicting the crystal system, space group, and lattice parameters directly from PXRD patterns. AlphaDiffract utilizes a 1D adaptation of the ConvNeXt architecture, a modern convolutional neural network that integrates key design principles from transformers, coupled with dedicated prediction heads for each crystallographic property. The model is trained and validated on the largest-to-date physics-based dataset of over 31 million simulated diffraction patterns, generated by augmenting 312,267 curated structures from the ICSD and Materials Project databases. Crucially, it demonstrates strong transfer from simulated training data to experimental measurements, achieving 81.7% crystal system accuracy and 66.2% space group accuracy on the RRUFF dataset while additionally predicting all six lattice parameters. By providing a unified model for rapid, simultaneous prediction of lattice symmetry and parameters from PXRD data, AlphaDiffract represents a significant step forward in leveraging deep learning for high-throughput materials discovery.

authors.name: Nina Andrejevic, Ming Du, Hemant Sharma, James P. Horwath, Aileen Luo, Xiangyu Yin, Michael Prince, Brian H. Toby, Mathew J. Cherukara

papers.title: Efficient all-electron Bethe-Salpeter implementation using crystal symmetries
papers.summary: We describe an all-electron implementation of the Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) for the calculation of optical absorption spectra in the full-potential linearized augmented-plane-wave (FLAPW) method. So far, FLAPW implementations have resorted to a simple plane-wave basis for the bare and screened Coulomb potentials, thereby forgoing the all-electron description to some extent. In contrast, we expand the interaction potentials in the all-electron mixed basis. As in most implementations, the BSE is solved by the diagonalization of a two-particle Hamiltonian matrix, whose dimension is proportional to the number of $\mathbf{k}$ points. Because of the large number of $\mathbf{k}$ points required to converge the BSE, the resulting matrix becomes large even for small unit cells. We describe a method that exploits the crystal symmetries to accelerate the construction and diagonalization of the two-particle Hamiltonian. In particular, we employ group theoretical tools to bring the Hamiltonian into block-diagonal form. Furthermore, it is shown that often only one of the blocks needs to be taken into account for the optical absorption spectrum, leading to a considerable speedup of the diagonalization step. The code allows for the inclusion of spin-orbit coupling and is parallelized with the possibility of storing the Hamiltonian in distributed memory over many nodes, keeping the memory demands low. To validate our implementation, we show optical absorption spectra and report exciton binding energies for bulk Si, LiF, and MoS$_2$. By exploiting the crystal symmetries, we can reduce the dimension of the Hamiltonian matrix of Si by a factor of five, resulting in a 125-fold speedup in its diagonalization. The calculated exciton binding energies of 22~meV and 76~meV for Si and MoS$_2$ are closer to experimental values than in previous BSE studies.

authors.name: J\"orn St\"ohler, Stefan Bl\"ugel, Christoph Friedrich

papers.title: Stability and superstructural ordering of alkali-triel-pnictide clathrates A$_8$T$_{27}$Pn$_{19}$
papers.summary: Clathrates are a class of inclusion compounds that offer various useful and surprising phenomena, including superconductivity, thermoelectricity, and the potential for high-density ion storage. Stability conditions within the Alkali-Triel-Pnictide A$_8$T$_{27}$Pn$_{19}$ family of unconventional clathrates are investigated with high-throughput density functional theory calculations, establishing trends in formation energy, structural and electronic properties, and identifying several new potential candidates. Electronic structure calculations and first-principles molecular dynamics simulations show that all alkali guests are fully ionized in the framework, and that the stability of electron-exact clathrates correlates with the ionization potential of the guest atoms, while their rattling behavior is governed primarily by the size of the guest ions relative to the cages. Targeted reactive synthesis from elemental precursors is attempted, resulting in four previously unreported ternary phases, two of which are structurally characterized. However, the predicted clathrate phases are not obtained. Further analysis reveals that the stability of ATPn clathrate compounds containing heavy elements, such as bismuth, depends strongly on relativistic spin-orbit coupling, which is often neglected in high-throughput studies that compute formation energies. Finally, chemically induced superstructural ordering is described in relation to Wyckoff sites in the prototypical type-I clathrate unit cell.

authors.name: Frank Cerasoli, Xiaochen Jin, Genevieve Amobi, Kirill Kovnir, Davide Donadio

papers.title: Intrinsic grain-size gradients upon grain growth near a free surface
papers.summary: Grain growth fundamentally shapes the microstructure of crystalline materials upon annealing, affecting their overall mechanical and functional properties. Recently, it has been rationalized that grain growth in polycrystals does not result solely from weighted curvature flow, but elastic effects (intrinsic stress) arised from shear coupling also need to be taken into account. We characterize and examine the effect of free surfaces on grain growth kinetics of high-purity, bulk polycrystalline nickel. By analyzing the microstructural evolution on cross sections of 1 mm thick specimens from the surface to the interior, as well as through in-plane investigations on specimens with varying thickness (1 mm, 40 $\mu$m, and 10 $\mu$m), an intrinsic grain-size gradient was identified, characterized by a gradual increase in grain size towards the interior. Interestingly, this grading was not restricted to the very surface but continued to depths of five to ten layers of grains, where effects from thermal grooves are considered negligible. We demonstrate that this behavior is significantly affected by elastic relaxation at the free surface, which alters the internal stress fields generated by shear-coupled grain boundary migration. These findings emphasize the relevance of free surfaces to the microstructural evolution of polycrystal.

authors.name: Jing Tang, Runlu Yan, Donglan Zhang, Ronald Schnitzer, Lorenz Romaner, Marlene Kapp, Marco Salvalaglio, Oliver Renk

papers.title: Covariant Onsager and Onsager-Machlup principles for active and inertial dynamics
papers.summary: The Onsager principle provides a variational route to the phenomenological equations of dissipative dynamics through the minimization of the Rayleighian. We develop a covariant formulation of the Onsager principle for active and inertial systems, ensuring geometric consistency under coordinate transformations. To further incorporate thermal fluctuations, we formulate the Onsager-Machlup principle for active and inertial systems by considering the Onsager-Machlup functional and the corresponding path probability for stochastic trajectories. Requiring that the path probability obeys the detailed fluctuation theorem, we show that the extended Onsager-Machlup theory is consistent with stochastic thermodynamics. The extended OP and OMP offer a unified and useful variational framework for deriving the dynamical equations of active and inertial systems.

authors.name: Kento Yasuda, Bin Zheng, Zhongqiang Xiong, Zhanglin Hou, Kenta Ishimoto, Xinpeng Xu, David Andelman, Shigeyuki Komura

papers.title: Energetics of stochastic limit-cycle oscillators: when does coupling reduce dissipation?
papers.summary: Non-linear oscillators occur in a wide range of biological and engineered systems. In noisy environments, the steady-state entropy production rate (EPR) quantifies time irreversibility and, under a thermodynamic interpretation, the associated energy dissipation. We study an idealized, analytically tractable family of stochastic circular limit-cycle oscillators and examine how mutual coupling in pairs and populations alters dissipation. The dynamics are characterized by a dimensionless effective temperature given by the ratio of radial relaxation and diffusion timescales. For identical oscillators, we derive analytical results for the EPR under radial, phase (Kuramoto-like), and Cartesian couplings. The phase-coupling analysis also considers nonidentical intrinsic frequencies. Coupling can increase or decrease EPR through changes in the radial mean and variance and in probability currents, with the response depending on effective temperature and system size. In particular, weak attractive Cartesian coupling lowers the EPR of identical oscillators at any effective temperature. At sufficiently low effective temperature, full Cartesian coupling produces a finite-coupling minimum below the uncoupled EPR throughout the oscillator family considered. Reduced EPR can also accompany improved individual and collective temporal coherence.

authors.name: Anton F. Burnet, Vansh Kharbanda, David Tobias, Benedikt Sabass

papers.title: Geometric Formulation of Power-Efficiency Bounds in Carnot-like Engines
papers.summary: We formulate the power-efficiency constraint of Carnot-like heat engines as a geometric optimization problem in the plane of normalized branch dissipations. In this plane, efficiency contours are straight lines, so maximizing the efficiency at fixed power reduces to bounding the slope of an admissible line. For branch dissipations that scale inversely with a power of the process time, the fixed-power constraint defines a two-dimensional attainable region, and the resulting slope-bound problem reduces to a linear-programming problem. This geometric framework yields the exact power-efficiency constraint for Carnot-like heat engines with power-law dissipation.

authors.name: R. X. Zhai

papers.title: Anisotropic Crystallization Kinetics and Interfacial Dynamics of Phase-Change Material Sb$_2$S$_3$
papers.summary: Antimony sulfide (Sb$_2$S$_3$), an Earth-abundant and sustainable chalcogenide, has emerged as a promising phase change material (PCM) due to its ultra-low optical losses, broadband transparency, and reversible phase-change capacity. In this work, we developed a machine learning force field based on the moment tensor potential approach, allowing us to understand the atomistic origin of the structural evolution and crystallization kinetics in Sb$_2$S$_3$ for the first time, by enabling large-scale molecular dynamics simulations (up to 7680 atoms for 40 ns). Sb$_2$S$_3$ has anisotropic growth rates with the (100) facet ($Pnma$ space group) exhibiting the fastest growth due to the strong Sb-S covalent bonding along its quasi-1D ribbon-like structure of its crystalline phase. The maximum growth rate was observed at 875 K, with an optimal undercooling degree of ~100 K, significantly lower than other PCMs like Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$ (GST) and GeTe. The activation energy for crystal growth was calculated be around 0.56 eV. Interfacial atomic dynamics revealed an Arrhenius-to-non-Arrhenius transition at ~800 K, with the (100) facet showing the highest diffusion activation energy of 1.56 eV. Unlike the GST and GeTe, the lower activation energy for crystal growth in Sb$_2$S$_3$ indicates that its heterogeneous crystallization is interface-controlled rather than diffusion-limited, with atomic attachment at the solid-liquid interface being energetically favoured over long-range atomic transport. Bonding and ring statistics analyses confirmed that directional covalent bonding plays a fundamental role in guiding structural ordering during crystal growth. These findings provide key insights into the structural, thermodynamic, and kinetic properties of Sb$_2$S$_3$, paving the way for optimizing its functionality including switching speed, reliability, and energy efficiency.

authors.name: Souvik Chakraborty, Wen-Qing Li, Yun Liu

papers.title: Two-dimensional stealthy hyperuniform polycrystalline disk packings
papers.summary: Polycrystals consist of grains of local crystalline order separated by grain boundaries. Conventional polycrystals are generally not hyperuniform because their randomly sized and oriented grains sustain long-wavelength density fluctuations. We use collective-coordinate optimization to generate ultradense, two-dimensional polycrystalline packings of identical disks that are stealthy hyperuniform (SHU): their structure factor vanishes over a finite range of wave numbers around the origin. We compare them with nonhyperuniform polycrystalline disk packings generated by a modified Lubachevsky-Stillinger (LS) rapid compression algorithm, a molecular dynamics protocol that models conventional polycrystalline microstructures. We compare two-point statistics, grain-size distributions, specific surface area, diffusion spreadability, and the imaginary part of the effective dynamic dielectric constant. At high packing fractions, the grain-size distribution of SHU polycrystals exhibits a peak at a characteristic size, reflecting long-range correlations between grains. This peak is absent in LS polycrystals. SHU packings also exhibit enhanced long-time diffusion spreadability. Within the nonlocal strong-contrast expansion, dielectric SHU packings are perfectly transparent to electromagnetic waves at small wave numbers, whereas LS packings retain finite attenuation. Although SHU polycrystals are not generally expected to form spontaneously, long-range interactions or correlated substrates may provide routes to their formation. They can also be fabricated as metamaterials by nanolithography or 3D printing.

authors.name: Carlo Vanoni, Paul J. Steinhardt, Salvatore Torquato

papers.title: Probing spin dynamics in MnSi under pressure by energy-integrated time-of-flight small-angle neutron scattering
papers.summary: We demonstrate that energy-integrated time-of-flight small-angle neutron scattering can determine the long-wavelength spin-wave stiffness of field-polarized MnSi inside a pressure cell. A forward model maps neutron energy loss and gain into the recorded time-of-flight coordinates, allowing a joint fit of radial profiles in several apparent-wavelength windows to constrain a common stiffness. Ambient-pressure powder and polycrystal measurements reproduce the established stiffness scale of MnSi. At effective pressures of 3.5 and 7.8 kbar, the fitted stiffness spans 43--61 meV $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}^2$ across the measured states and is comparable in magnitude to the scale inferred from the helical wave vector and applied upper critical field. The characteristic SANS ordering temperature decreases from 28.8 K at ambient pressure to 17.4 K at 7.8 kbar. The long-wavelength gradient stiffness alone therefore does not account for the pressure evolution of helimagnetic ordering. These results demonstrate a route to quantitative studies of spin-wave dynamics under pressure on time-of-flight SANS instruments without final-energy analysis.

authors.name: E. V. Altynbaev, D. O. Skanchenko, Zhenhua Xie, Yubin Ke, Yuan Bao, Hui Cheng, A. V. Tsvyashchenko

papers.title: A method for measuring the dispersion of elastic waves in disordered computer-solids
papers.summary: The dispersion of elastic waves in disordered solids plays a key role in determining the vibrational density of states and harmonic wave attenuation rates. As such, the availability of robust computational approaches to the precise extraction of the dispersion is of key importance. Here we present a simple method -- the imposed wave method (IWM) -- , which provides direct access to the dispersion of elastic waves in computer models of solids, without any fitting involved. We directly benchmark the method against the `ground-truth' obtained from direct diagonalization of solids' hessian matrices, to find good agreement. We discuss limitations of and finite-size effects in the method, and show that exploiting the method's finite-size scaling provides access to a fundamental quantifier of mechanical disorder that determines wave attenuation rates and spectral widths.

authors.name: Edan Lerner

papers.title: Magnetic Contributions to Phase Stability in the Co-Ni Binary: A First-Principles CALPHAD Study
papers.summary: We propose a simple method to employ ab-initio calculations to determine magnetic contributions to free energy of alloys. Validation on the Co-Ni binary demonstrates that this ab initio approach reproduces experimental FCC-HCP phase equilibria while providing physically transparent, structure-dependent magnetic parameters suitable for multicomponent extrapolation. Our results demonstrate that physically grounded magnetic parametrization, derived directly from electronic structure calculations, enables predictive phase diagram modeling for magnetic alloy systems.

authors.name: Prajna Jalagam, Zhigang Wu, John Lawson, Axel van de Walle
