papers.title: Symmetry-protected cubic-touching topological surface bands with tunable singularities
papers.summary: We propose a class of topological surface bands in three-dimensional topological insulators that have symmetry-protected cubic-order band touching. Within the symmetry constraint, the band dispersion can continuously vary between cubic dispersion, moat band and multi-mini-valley structure with van Hove singularities by adjusting particle-hole asymmetry and anisotropy. Thus, there is a family of tunable density-of-state singularities ranging from power-law to logarithmic divergences. This offrs a versatile platform for engineering strongly correlated phases of matter in topological surface states. We provide an example realization in a prism-lattice tight-binding model of angular-momentum-3/2 electrons.

authors.name: Jingtian Shi, Taylor L. Hughes, Ivar Martin

papers.title: Skew scattering induced contribution to orbital Hall response
papers.summary: Our study investigates the orbital Hall (OH) conductivity originating from the disorder induced mechanisms, namely side-jump and skew scattering. On treating the disorder potential within the first-order Born approximation and beyond and employing the quantum kinetic approach, the general scaling law for both mechanisms in terms of disorder potential is provided to signal out the process experimentally. The calculations have been processed for the three-dimensional Weyl semimetals under an oscillating electric field. We reveal that the higher order disorder contributions leading skew scattering process dominates the orbital Hall conductivity over the intrinsic and side-jump processes. In addition, we demonstrate the tunable nature of the extrinsic orbital Hall conductivity with the strength of the disorder potential and the external field. Finally, our findings highlights disorder scattering as a potential route for orbital transport.

authors.name: Dayana Joy, Vivek Pandey, Rhonald Burgos Atencia, Pankaj Bhalla

papers.title: Computational Study of Water Adsorption and Dissociative Mechanisms Impacting g-C3N4's Optical and Electronic Properties
papers.summary: In the quest for sustainable energy solutions, water splitting emerges as a crucial process for generating clean hydrogen a versatile and renewable fuel essential for energy storage, emissions reduction, and achieving sustainability goals. This study employs a comprehensive computational approach, utilizing atomistic simulations to systematically investigate the effects of water absorption on the electronic and optical properties of g-C3N4 nanosheets. Our methodology integrates ab initio computations grounded in density functional theory (DFT), which allows for a detailed characterization of the nanosheet and serves as a benchmark for self-consistent charge density functional tight binding (SCC-DFTB) simulations. This approach provides valuable insights into the behavior of the nanosheet under the influence of absorbed OH and H2O molecules by considering calculated parameters for photocatalytic efficiency. Additionally, we extend our investigation to classical molecular dynamics simulations within the ReaxFF framework, modeling the emission of multiple H2O molecules and assessing the subsequent rate of H2 evolution. A key finding of our study reveals that the dissociation of H2O into HO and O molecules significantly enhances both the optical absorbance and conductance of the nanosheet compared to its pristine state. These results underscore the potential of g-C3N4 nanosheets as effective materials for water splitting applications.

authors.name: Amil Aligayev, Ulkar Jabbarli, F. Javier Dominguez-Gutierrez, Ulkar Samadova, Jialin Li, Stefanos Papanikolaou, Qing Huang

papers.title: Many-Anyon Braiding in Non-Abelian Fractional Quantum Hall Effect with Hybrid Monte Carlo Simulation
papers.summary: We use the hybrid Monte Carlo method to efficiently compute the many-anyon non-Abelian braiding matrices for different Moore-Read quasiholes braiding schemes. Using both a traditional two-anyon braiding scheme and a newly proposed braiding scheme based on global rotation, we approximate the non-Abelian characteristic length of Moore-Read quasiholes around $2.8$ times the magnetic length. We also apply this method to braiding schemes involving six anyons and explicitly show that the well-known ``even-odd effect'' can be flipped by tuning electrostatic potentials. This phenomenon emphasizes the importance of accounting for all anyons within a non-Abelian system, even if the braiding involves only several anyons locally. Our results are relevant to the experimental realization of non-Abelian physics in fractional quantum Hall and other analogous systems, including the fast-growing field of fractional quantum anomalous Hall states in moir\'e materials.

authors.name: Ting-Tung Wang, Ha Quang Trung, Qianhui Xu, Min Long, Bo Yang, Zi Yang Meng

papers.title: Photogalvanic transport of nonreciprocal Cooper-pair fluctuations
papers.summary: We develop a theory of the nonlinear optical and transport responses of two-dimensional noncentrosymmetric superconductors in the fluctuation regime above the transition temperature, encompassing the photogalvanic effect, second-harmonic generation, and the photovoltaic Hall effect. Near the transition these responses are strongly enhanced by preformed Cooper pairs, whose nonreciprocity enters the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau description in two distinct ways: through thermodynamic Lifshitz invariants, which encode an asymmetric pair spectrum, and through kinetic Lifshitz invariants, which encode an asymmetric pair relaxation and are locked to the Langevin noise by the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. We derive generalized formulas for the Aslamazov-Larkin and Maki-Thompson channels of the nonlinear current, valid for Gaussian fluctuations at drive frequencies below the scale set by temperature and to linear order in the nonreciprocal perturbations, and reduce them to closed-form dimensionless functions. Circular polarization distinguishes the mechanisms: for reciprocal noise without momentum structure the Aslamazov-Larkin channel is helicity independent and its circular photogalvanic response vanishes for any pair spectrum, whereas the Maki-Thompson channel and the nonreciprocal noise support helicity-odd rectified currents, including a fluctuation photovoltaic Hall current transverse to the strain axis. Applications to Rashba-type ($C_{3v}$) and Ising-type ($D_{3h}$) superconductors show how the point-group symmetry dictates the vector structure of the nonlinear currents, and how polarization analysis together with the frequency and dephasing dependences can separate the individual channels experimentally.

authors.name: Joaquim Telles de Miranda, Alex Levchenko

papers.title: Systematic and accurate anharmonic formation free energies of metastable defects via a constrained Bayesian Adaptive Biasing Force framework
papers.summary: Computing the formation free energies of metastable defects at finite temperature remains challenging due to anharmonicity, the multiplicity of basins and the frequent occurrence of migration events. Using the previously introduced constrained Bayesian Adaptive Biasing Force method (BABFc) [1], we establish a practical framework for computing restricted anharmonic formation free energies associated with individual metastable defect basins. We demonstrate that BABFc can be exploited as a robust, systematic and numerically efficient tool for addressing a long standing bottleneck in atomistic materials science: the finite temperature thermodynamic characterization of metastable defects in complex, highly anharmonic energy landscapes. The proposed workflow requires only a reference local minimum and a confinement strategy and does not rely on defect specific collective variables. It therefore provides a general route to assign well-defined free energies to individual metastable basins, even when these basins are separated by low barriers. In this setting, BABFc enables stable, bias corrected free energy estimates with statistical accuracies at the meV/atom level and a very low failure rate, including for systems containing approximately one thousand atoms. We demonstrate this capability through thousands of independent free energy calculations covering hundreds of four-interstitial and four-vacancy configurations in bcc {\alpha}-Fe over a broad temperature range, using both a traditional empirical potential and a data driven force field. The study also highlights the critical role of energy landscape regularity in defect thermodynamics. This approach has many powerful applications, ranging from building extensive databases of free energies for data-driven force fields to enabling fully automated workflows for characterizing defects in materials at finite temperatures.

authors.name: Clovis Lapointe, Anruo Zhong, Manuel Ath\`enes, Mihai-Cosmin Marinica

papers.title: Excited-state structure and photoluminescence of the M-center in Si
papers.summary: Color centers in silicon offer great possibilities for scalable quantum technologies. The M-center, proposed to originate from a carbon-hydrogen complex, offers telecommunications-band emission and a paramagnetic ground state similar to the T-center. Here, we report on photoluminescence lines in the vicinity of the M-center and investigate their properties, including their dependence on temperature, implantation fluence, implantation isotope, and annealing temperature. Three emission lines are observed that are blue-shifted by 1.1, 2.8 and 3.6 meV relative to the 761 meV zero phonon line of the M center. The 2.8 meV line exhibits negative thermal quenching with an activation energy of 1.5 meV, strengthening the assignment of the line to a second excited state of the M-center. However, the remaining blue-shifted emission lines, together with two additional red-shifted (4.7 and 6.4 meV) emission lines display normal thermal quenching, and are unaffected by an isotope shift of the implanted carbon atom ($^{12}$C versus $^{13}$C implantation) and implantation fluence. Thus, they likely arise either from other defects with similar emission energies or from a perturbed configuration of the M-center.

authors.name: Aurora Teien, David R. Gongora, Arnulf Johannes Snedker-Nielsen, Viktor Bobal, Augustinas Galeckas, Peter Granum, Stefano Paesani, Marianne Etzelm\"uller Bathen, Lasse Vines

papers.title: Electron Spin Pumping by Thermal Radiation
papers.summary: This Letter demonstrates that thermal radiation can pump angular momentum into the spins of itinerant electrons across a vacuum gap, without spatial spin transport or net charge flow. In a monolayer transition metal dichalcogenide radiatively coupled to a thermal emitter, Rashba spin-orbit coupling enables spin-selective transitions between helical conduction bands. Two distinct mechanisms are identified: chiral spin pumping mediated by interference between polarization components of thermal radiation from a nonreciprocal emitter, and nonchiral spin pumping arising from Zeeman-induced asymmetry between opposing spin-flip transitions driven by nonchiral thermal fluctuations.

authors.name: Gaomin Tang

papers.title: A General Algorithm for Minimal Uncoupled Stress--Strain Calculations of Elastic Constants
papers.summary: We have developed a general algorithm for constructing the minimum number of strain configurations required to extract second-order elastic constants from first-principles stress-strain calculations without algebraic coupling between the constants targeted for extraction. The method operates on the sparsity structure of the symmetry-reduced elastic stiffness matrix, represented by an auxiliary binary matrix, and generates admissible strain patterns algorithmically rather than prescribing separate strain sets for individual crystal symmetries. Each independent elastic constant is obtained from a single stress component, while additional stress relations generated by the same deformation provide internal consistency checks. Because the six-dimensional strain space contains only 2^6-1=63 non-empty strain patterns, the minimality of the resulting sets can be verified exactly for every elastic-symmetry type considered. The construction reproduces established high-efficiency strain sets in cases where they are minimal and yields improved sets for symmetry classes in which previously tabulated schemes require additional configurations. Because the formulation is based on stress-strain derivatives, it can also be readily extended to finite temperatures using consistently sampled ensemble-averaged thermodynamic stresses. Explicit strain sets are derived for all elastic-symmetry types spanning the 230 crystallographic space groups, and their accuracy and computational efficiency are benchmarked against established approaches.

authors.name: S. I. Simak, Utkarsh Singh

papers.title: Probing the wave-vector gap in nanoscale magnonics
papers.summary: Short-wavelength spin waves are central to miniaturizing magnonic devices and to studying exchange-dominated magnetization dynamics. Yet the wave-vector range between roughly 30 and 300 radians per micrometre has remained difficult to access experimentally, posing challenges for both excitation and detection. This Perspective reviews recent advances in emerging measurement techniques and discusses prospects for their future development. Optical and microwave techniques are restricted to the vicinity of the Brillouin-zone centre. Inelastic neutron, electron and resonant hard x-ray scattering cover the full Brillouin zone but lack the energy resolution needed for low-frequency magnons at intermediate wave vectors. This Perspective examines five emerging approaches that are beginning to close this gap: Mie-enhanced Brillouin light scattering, colour-centre magnetometry, magnon momentum microscopy, extreme-ultraviolet transient-grating spectroscopy, and time-resolved scanning transmission x-ray microscopy. For each, we discuss the physical principle, demonstrated capabilities, current limitations and prospects for development. Compared side by side, the techniques give complementary access to magnon frequencies, local stray fields, real-space dynamics and momentum-space distributions, and they differ in their sensitivity to coherent and incoherent excitations. We therefore discuss the main advantages and use cases of each technique and consider the practical requirements for addressing different scientific questions. We highlight opportunities for further development, including higher sensitivity, improved spatial and temporal resolution, and broader frequency and wave-vector coverage. Together, these advances could enable, for example, systematic studies of nonlinear magnon interactions at nanoscale wavelengths and investigations of emerging magnetic materials such as altermagnets.

authors.name: Ond\v{r}ej Wojewoda, Samer Kurdi, Toeno van der Sar, Daniel Schick, Sebastian Wintz, Alexei Maznev

papers.title: Orientation-Dependent Universality of Spin-Conductance Fluctuations in d-Wave Altermagnets
papers.summary: Universal conductance fluctuations reflect the symmetry and geometry of phase-coherent transport. However, it remains unclear whether crystal orientation relative to the device can tune fluctuation plateaus in spin-conserving altermagnets. Here, using quantum transport simulations of a two-dimensional $d$-wave altermagnet with scalar disorder, we show that crystal orientation tunes longitudinal and spin-Hall fluctuation plateaus while each spin sector remains in the orthogonal symmetry class. At intermediate disorder, tuning the crystal orientation toward the device diagonal weakens longitudinal spin-conductance fluctuations and enhances spin-Hall fluctuations. Both responses exhibit well-defined plateaus at the diagonal orientation, with amplitudes that depend only weakly on disorder and altermagnetic strength over the ranges studied. A variance decomposition shows that, at this orientation, increasing disorder drives the longitudinal spin-channel covariance toward zero, while the transverse covariance shifts from enhancing to suppressing the spin-Hall variance. Our findings suggest that spin-conductance fluctuations can probe transport anisotropy in altermagnets.

authors.name: Yihan Zhang, Zheng Qin, Dong-Hui Xu, Junjie Zeng, Zhen Ning, Rui Wang

papers.title: In Situ Thermal Preparation by CO2-Laser and Chemical Characterization of Oxide Substrates Across Multiple Crystallographic Orientations
papers.summary: Atomically flat and chemically controlled oxide substrate surfaces are essential for high-quality epitaxial growth of complex materials and heterostructures. Previous studies have demonstrated in situ thermal preparation of selected oxide substrates, primarily focusing on conventional low-index orientations such as SrTiO$_3$ (100) and LaAlO$_3$ (100). Here, we extend these methodologies to a broader range of oxide substrates and crystallographic orientations, including challenging polar surfaces. We present a systematic study of the in situ thermal preparation of SrTiO$_3$ (100), SrTiO$_3$ (111), GdScO$_3$ (110), LaAlO$_3$ (111), (LaAlO$_3$)$_{0.3}$(Sr$_2$AlTaO$_6$)$_{0.7}$ (001), and NdGaO$_3$ (110) single crystal substrates. The substrates are annealed in a vacuum chamber under a controlled oxygen background environment using a CO$_2$ laser heating system. The optimized annealing conditions produce atomically flat step-and-terrace structures, long-range surface crystallinity, and effectively clean surfaces across all the investigated substrates. Our results establish a versatile, reproducible, and broadly applicable platform for the in situ preparation of oxide substrates immediately prior to epitaxial growth. These results also provide practical guidelines for interface engineering and surface-sensitive investigations of complex materials.

authors.name: Neethu Rose Leyo, Sethulakshmi Sajeev, Arnaud P. Nono Tchiomo, Prosper Ngabonziza

papers.title: Hidden Triakontadipole Order in the Triangular-Lattice Magnet CeMgAl$_{11}$O$_{19}$
papers.summary: The absence of magnetic Bragg peaks and a broad excitation continuum are commonly recognized experimental features of a quantum spin liquid. The Ce-based triangular-lattice hexaaluminate CeMgAl$_{11}$O$_{19}$ exhibits both signatures, yet its effective model and ground state remain under debate. Experiments have variously suggested a quantum spin liquid, proximate umbrella point, and disorder-suppressed magnetic order. Here we trace these contradictions to an overlooked multipolar degree of freedom, and establish a dipole--triakontadipole XXZ model with $J_{\perp} \simeq 0.65$ K and $J_c \simeq -0.13$ K via precision tensor-network calculations. The resulting planar triakontadipolar superfluid order is hidden from dipolar probes, explaining the absence of a magnetic Bragg peak in neutron scattering. The zero-field excitations separate into a low-energy triakontadipole wave and a broad higher-energy continuum. We further propose nuclear spin-lattice relaxation and spin-current experiments to probe the gapless excitations of this hidden triakontadipole superfluid. Our findings thus offer a hidden-order caveat for spin-liquid searches and provide a new platform for exploring high-rank multipolar physics in rare-earth triangular-lattice magnets.

authors.name: Yu-Bo Liu, Yuan Gao, Zhen Ma, Shufan Cheng, Xinyang Liu, Jinsheng Wen, Wei Li

papers.title: Non-Perturbative Resolution of Luttinger's Theorem Violations in Strongly Correlated Systems
papers.summary: Many-body physics faces an apparent paradox concerning violations of Luttinger's theorem in strongly correlated systems. The theorem relates the electron number to the Luttinger count---the monodromy of the logarithm of the imaginary-frequency Green's function $\bd{G(i\epsilon)}$---and, at finite magnetic field, connects the Hall conductivity to the magnetic-field derivative of the Luttinger count via the Streda formula. Luttinger's theorem seemingly follows from particle-number conservation alone, without resorting to perturbation theory, and yet it is found to be violated. Here, we provide a non-perturbative solution to this paradox. We show that the Luttinger integral, which accounts for the mismatch between the particle number and the Luttinger count, is a pure zero-frequency boundary term, which the conventional proof implicitly discards. Hence, violations of Luttinger's theorem do not require a breakdown of the skeleton-diagram formalism, whose validity is independent of the convergence of the skeleton-diagram expansion to the exact solution. This advancement in understanding resolves a longstanding point of contention in many-body theory. We also find that the Luttinger integral is a genuine topological invariant, tied to the Luttinger-Ward functional rather than to the Green's function alone; like the monodromy of $\bd{\ln G(i\epsilon)}$, it stems exclusively from the zero-frequency point where the Matsubara trajectory crosses the branch cut of the logarithm. Correspondingly, the magnetic-field derivative of the Luttinger integral makes the Hall number in topological insulators differ from its Green's-function expression by a vertex correction, itself invariant, which can take fractional values.

authors.name: Nazzareno Africani, Herbert E{\ss}l, Alessandro Toschi, Michele Fabrizio

papers.title: Optimizing one-dimensional lithographically defined nanowires in semiconducting heterostructures
papers.summary: One-dimensional nanowires can host remarkable electronic properties and are central to studying quantum transport. Although heterostructure-defined confinement combined with gate-defined potentials can greatly reduce the effects of impurities as measured via electron mobilities, the realization and interpretation of novel effects at this scale are complicated by disorder. Experiments on lithographically defined one-dimensional nanowires therefore do not exhibit ideal behavior. Using theoretical and computational models, we predict that optimizing the geometry of split gates in semiconducting heterostructures will lead to higher-quality channels for transport measurements. Further, we show that this optimization is essential for resolving features of interest such as the Rashba-induced spin gap. This new approach to lithographically defined conduction channels provides better energy resolution and is less susceptible to disorder.

authors.name: Leah Tom, Yik Kheng Lee, Karina L. Hudson, Krittika Kumar, Jackson S. Smith, Alex R. Hamilton, S. N. Coppersmith, Jared H. Cole, Mark Friesen

papers.title: Kitaev Exchange and Altermagnetism in the Double Perovskite Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$: An Ab Initio Study
papers.summary: The Co$^{2+}$-based double perovskite Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$ attracts attention due to its nontrivial magnetic properties. \textit{Ab initio} density functional theory calculations reveal a substantial ferromagnetic Kitaev exchange $|K|\sim J/3$ between nearest neighbors that, combined with the face-centered cubic lattice, leads to pronounced exchange frustration and places Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$ among Kitaev materials with moderate Kitaev interaction strength. In addition, Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$ is found to be altermagnetic with a sizable non-relativistic spin splitting, which can give rise to a transverse piezomagnetic effect and a nontrivial magneto-optical response.

authors.name: Alexey V. Ushakov, Sergey V. Streltsov

papers.title: $^{55}$Mn-NMR/NQR study on the kagome metal Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$: Re-examining the possibility of spin-singlet paired state
papers.summary: Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$ is a Mn-based kagome metal that has been proposed to be close to a ferromagnetic instability. Recent $^{55}$Mn nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) study suggested the emergence of a spin-singlet paired state below $\sim$10 K. To clarify its low-energy magnetic and electronic properties, we performed $^{55}$Mn NMR and nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR) measurements on single-crystalline Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$. From the detailed NMR/NQR spectrum measurements and the DFT calculations, a quadrupolar frequency of $\nu_{\rm Q}$ = 4.6$\sim$4.8 MHz and an asymmetry parameter of $\eta$ = 0.45$\sim$0.48 as well as the principal axes of electric field gradient EFG for the Mn site were determined. The temperature dependence of Knight shift ($K$) shows a similar temperature dependence of the DC magnetic susceptibility $\chi$ except for the low-temperature region below $\sim$ 50 K where $K$ is almost constant while $\chi$ keeps increasing, which suggests that the increase in $\chi$ at low temperatures is not intrinsic. $^{55}$Mn spin-lattice relaxation rate divided by temperature ($1/T_1T$) is found to be nearly constant, confirming the metallic state of Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$ from a microscopic point of view. Furthermore, no peak in $1/T_1T$ is observed near 10 K, and neither the Knight shift nor the linewidth shows any reductions at low temperatures. These results suggest no clear signature for the spin-singlet pairing around 10 K in Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$.

authors.name: Qing-Ping Ding, Yongbin Lee, Charuni Dissanayake, Yasuyuki Nakajima, Yuji Furukawa

papers.title: From Growth Inhibition to Fluctuations: Testing an Ising Model of Bacterial Responses to Antibiotics
papers.summary: Complex networks of biochemical reactions have been proposed to exhibit emergent cooperativity that can be described by an effective Ising model, with a small number of parameters encoding collective interactions. Here this mapping is experimentally tested using the response of three bacterial species to a range of antibiotics acting on different cellular targets. The Ising description is compared to the conventional Hill model, examining both the mean growth-rate response and, importantly, its population growth-rate heterogeneity (PGRH). While both models describe the mean growth-rate dependence on antibiotic concentration comparably well, we find that the Ising model provides a markedly better description of PGRH, offering an additional and more stringent test of the collective description. The fitted Ising interaction strength is systematically related to the Hill exponent and increases with the functional distance of the antibiotic target from the protein-production machinery. These results provide experimental support for describing complex biochemical reaction networks through effective cooperative Ising interactions, and suggest that the collective response of bacterial growth to antibiotics reflects the organization of the underlying metabolic network.

authors.name: Pietro Cicuta, Morten Kals, Nir S. Gov

papers.title: Scalable Low-Cost Laboratory Automation: A Digital Twin-Integrated Robotic Platform for Autonomous Liquid Handling (RAINBOT)
papers.summary: Laboratory automation accelerates discovery, yet its adoption is constrained by the high cost, proprietary design, and limited remote supervisability of commercial liquid-handling systems. This work presents RAINBOT\textsuperscript{TM}, a low-cost, openly reproducible liquid-handling robot built by converting a consumer-grade Cartesian 3D printer (Elegoo Neptune 4 Max). The printer extruder is replaced by a precision single-channel pipette actuated through the printer's own G-code-driven X--Y--Z gantry, with plunger and tip-eject motions effected by two compact linear actuators under Python control. To make experiments transparent and remotely supervisable, a browser-based digital twin is implemented to synchronise bidirectionally with the physical platform, mirroring kinematics and pipetting states in real time and exposing remote monitoring, intervention, and an emergency stop from any web browser. As a proof of concept, RAINBOT\textsuperscript{TM} performed sequential exchanges of differently coloured aqueous solutions while an integrated colour sensor quantified the resulting mixtures; measured red, yellow, and blue (RYB) responses agreed with expected mixing behaviour to within a mean absolute error of two percentage points, validating correct execution and real-time tracking. Closing the loop, the platform is coupled to the CEID\textsuperscript{TM} (Cooperative Explorer for Inverse Design) framework, which recasts experimentation from iterative manual guessing into a goal-directed inverse-design search while keeping a human in the loop. The complete hardware costs under US\$1300, which is roughly an order of magnitude below entry-level commercial handlers, thereby establishing an accessible physical--virtual framework for self-driving laboratory automation.

authors.name: Mohamed Rami Ayeche, Souhil Sid, Ahyen Mostofa, Rehaan Hussain, Ali Shayesteh, Fadwa El Mellouhi

papers.title: Discrete-time Kuramoto model with phase lag: Linear stability analysis and onset of synchronization
papers.summary: We investigate the discrete-time version of the Kuramoto model with phase lag, which comprises globally-coupled phase oscillators of distributed frequencies that are evolving under a nonlinear map. In the continuum limit of an infinite number of oscillators ($N\to \infty$), we derive the exact Frobenius-Perron equation for the time evolution of the single-oscillator probability density, and study linear stability of the incoherent state. Instability signals onset of synchronization. The corresponding synchronization threshold is obtained analytically for the case of a Lorentzian distribution of the oscillator frequencies. The threshold differs from that of the continuous-time Kuramoto model, reflecting the fundamentally different stability conditions for discrete-time maps and continuous-time flows. Beyond synchronization threshold, we observe several interesting nonlinear phenomena: Unlike the classical Kuramoto model, the discrete-time version exhibits periodic and chaotic states. Numerical simulations of the finite-$N$ system confirm the analytical prediction for the synchronization threshold, while highlighting breakdown of the celebrated Ott-Antonsen ansatz invoked to conveniently study the continuous-time Kuramoto model in terms of a low-dimensional description.

authors.name: Prashant M. Gade, Shamik Gupta

papers.title: Partitioning and Merging in Phase Unwrapping: A Systematic Review of Methods and Evidence
papers.summary: Phase unwrapping underlies radar interferometry, magnetic resonance imaging and optical metrology. When an image is too large or too difficult to unwrap in one piece, many methods cut it into units, unwrap each unit, and merge the results. To our knowledge, no systematic review had brought these partitioned methods together. This review gathers them, for two-dimensional images and three-dimensional volumes. It describes how the units are built: fixed tiles, adaptive tiles, regions computed from the data, or pieces imposed by the acquisition, such as subapertures, slices and scenes. It then classifies how the units are merged, in four classes: after each unit is unwrapped, through one integer per jump-free region, during the solve, or through an external reference. Three findings stand out: building the units and merging them are two separate decisions; the merging rule decides whether the merged phase stays congruent with the measured one; and most tests change both decisions at once, so few results show which one helps. We state what a study can report to support a claim on memory, speed or accuracy. Our aim is to document the methods, not to rank them. Following PRISMA 2020, four bibliographic databases (OpenAlex, IEEE Xplore, Web of Science and Scopus), searched on 1 October 2026, returned 1,800 records. After removing duplicates, screening titles and abstracts, adding a citation search and reading 298 full texts, we included 149 studies, published from 1987 to 2026. The review was not registered and received no specific funding.

authors.name: Antoine Moevus, Max Mignotte

papers.title: Simulation-Assisted Radio Map Reconstruction with Sparse Field Measurements
papers.summary: Field measurements are essential for evaluating radio map reconstruction under real-world conditions, but their acquisition is costly. This letter proposes a simulation-assisted parameterized-background data-weak (SA-PBDW) method that combines propagation simulations with sparse field measurements, which jointly estimates background coefficients and a spatial correction to account for discrepancies between simulated and measured power distributions. Dense field measurements are collected for multiple transmitter positions at an urban site. Evaluations on the collected data and RadioMapSeer demonstrate improved reconstruction accuracy and structural fidelity over benchmark methods at reduced sampling rates.

authors.name: Lang Ming, Longhui Wang, Yazhou Sun, Xi Chen, Jian Wang, Yu Wang

papers.title: Conformal Risk Control for Sentinel-1 Flood Maps under Event Shift and Local Recalibration
papers.summary: Conformal Risk Control (CRC) selects a threshold to limit missed labeled positives under exchangeability, but low omission risk can come at the cost of an excessively large flood map. We examine this trade-off with a frozen bi-temporal Sentinel-1 predictor, 403 expert-labeled source groups, and ten evaluable leave-one-event-out folds. At a target risk of 0.10, source-calibrated thresholds produce mean group losses of 0.1726 in Somalia and 0.1985 in Nigeria (four groups). The other eight folds select zero thresholds, labeling every valid pixel as flooded; their excess predicted area is 3.15-20.55 times the labeled positive area. Local threshold recalibration is feasible in 559 of 570 scheduled splits. The equal-event frequency of meeting the observed risk target with a positive threshold is 0.95% at ten labeled groups and 8.00% at twenty, using different predefined event pools. At fifty groups, exploratory recalibration meets both conditions in 24/30 Paraguay splits and none in India or the United States. Labels include permanent water, so the loss does not isolate newly flooded land. The results show why omission risk should be reported alongside mapped area, calibration feasibility, and event-specific outcomes.

authors.name: Izzath Nisfer, Rahim Iqbal, Shazan Shaheed, Asfi Ahamed, Muhammadu Ilham, Dileesha Manamperi, Thimira Sahan, Sandareka Wickramanayake

papers.title: Voltage-Feedback Backoff and Restoration for Priority-Based EV Charging Control
papers.summary: Uncoordinated residential electric vehicle (EV) charging can cause sustained undervoltage in distribution networks. This paper proposes a centralized voltage-feedback backoff and restoration (VFBR) framework that separates concurrent charging-count control from EV selection. The controller adjusts the allowable charging count using monitored critical-bus voltages, without load forecasts, online power-flow calculations, or optimization. Initial charging suspension relieves undervoltage, followed by group-wise restoration and backoff as voltage conditions permit. A complementary priority score combines charging urgency with voltage sensitivity precomputed offline to balance time-critical requests against their location-dependent voltage impacts. One-week simulations on the unbalanced IEEE 123-bus feeder with 500 EVs show that VFBR reduces the proportion of charging-period bus-time samples below 0.95 p.u. from 15% to less than 1%. Among the evaluated strategies, combined allocation with urgency and sensitivity weights of 0.75 and 0.25 delivers 25% more energy than random allocation and achieves the highest mean departure state of charge and fairness. These results demonstrate that simple voltage-feedback control, coupled with urgency- and sensitivity-based allocation, effectively mitigates undervoltage while improving charging service.

authors.name: Eyad Alsulayhim, Ning Lu

papers.title: Fuel-Efficient Formation Flying via Constrained Extremum Seeking
papers.summary: This paper presents a model-free autonomous guidance architecture for minimal drag of a trailing aircraft in formation flight. Realizing the fuel savings resulting from such a formation requires learning and tracking a time-varying vortex while avoiding locations where the aircraft experiences an abrupt rolling moment disturbance. A guidance architecture for fuel-efficient safe flight, called Adaptive Plateau-seeking Optimal Guidance with ModulatEd Excitations (APOGEE), is proposed herein. Key features of APOGEE are its ability to modulate the amplitude of the excitation required to learn the unknown objective and constraint functions, to adaptively adjust the learning rates, and to keep the flight safe during the search for the optimal formation. A threshold-gated modulation reduces the amplitude of excitation when the objective function reaches an acceptably large value, thus improving flying qualities and further reducing fuel consumption. Furthermore, a Newton-based learning rule, whose estimate of the inverse of the Hessian is spectrally clamped, adapts the learning rates to the local curvature of the objective function in order to accelerate convergence and lower the chance of overshooting the optimum. Finally, a safety filter having an unknown constraint function is used to prevent a loss of control event prompted by the above mentioned disturbance. The efficacy of APOGEE is demonstrated by using a high-fidelity model of an F-16 jet and an experimentally obtained vortex model. Being model-free, APOGEE does not require modeling the dependence of the unknown functions on the characteristics of the leading aircraft, the flight condition, the crosswind, and the vortex-induced turbulence.

authors.name: Kwang Hak Kim, Luis G. Crespo, Michael J. Acheson

papers.title: MVDC Power Cables for Future Wide-Body All-Electric Aircraft: A Research Journey from System-Level Requirements to Modeling, Design, Fabrication, and Testing
papers.summary: Future wide-body all-electric aircraft require lightweight electrical distribution systems capable of delivering megawatt-scale propulsion power under demanding thermal and electrical conditions. This article reviews our research program on medium-voltage direct-current (MVDC) power cables, from aircraft-level requirements through modeling, design, fabrication, and low-pressure electrical testing. It connects successive investigations and explains the decisions guiding their development. Aircraft-level power-flow and single-contingency studies establish a +/-5 kV distribution architecture and a 1 kA design objective for the most heavily loaded cable circuits. Coupled electrical, thermal, and airflow models examine multilayer multifunctional electrical insulation, conductor geometry, bipolar pole spacing, duct configuration, and forced convection. Flight-phase studies distinguish higher-current takeoff operation from lower-current operation at reduced cruise pressure. Experiments progress from bonded flat specimens to wrapped cable prototypes, examining fabrication methods, partial discharge, and dielectric breakdown at atmospheric pressure and pressures down to 18.8 kPa. The results highlight the roles of insulation interfaces, wrapping method, cable geometry, and installation conditions in achieving compact designs with improved electrical performance. Together, these studies provide a development framework linking aircraft requirements to manufacturable prototypes. Predicted current-carrying capability is distinguished from measured insulation performance, and the combined electrical, thermal, mechanical, and endurance evaluations needed for aircraft qualification are identified.

authors.name: Babak Porkar, Mona Ghassemi

papers.title: Subspace-Coding for Bistatic ISAC: Taming Interference via Array Geometry
papers.summary: This paper introduces a subspace coding perspective to bistatic integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), highlighting the role of receiver array geometry in the coupling between communication decoding and sensing. A central insight is that the impact of the interference caused by the sensing channel on the line-of-sight communication path is controlled by the subspace distance between the sensing and communication subspaces, {\em which strongly depends on the array geometry}. By studying a commonly used successive decoding approach, we derive upper and lower bounds on the communication error probability in terms of an effective SINR, which is explicitly determined by this subspace distance. This reveals that array geometries designed to form well-separated sensing subspace codes can also improve communication reliability in bistatic ISAC. In particular, Bose--Chowla arrays, shown to be near-optimal subspace codes for spatial sensing in our earlier works, can outperform uniform linear arrays in terms of symbol decoding errors. The performance gap is significant when the communication and sensing channels are strongly correlated, and it increases with the number of antennas. Numerical experiments confirm that subspace-coded array geometries provide more favorable sensing--communication tradeoffs than ULAs for iterative joint target localization and decoding (JTD) receiver.

authors.name: Parthasarathi Khirwadkar, Mohamed Ghada-Waeel Hamdy, Robin Rajam\"aki, Piya Pal

papers.title: Geometry-Time Graph Attention for 3-D TOA Localization in Underwater Acoustic Sensor Networks
papers.summary: In underwater acoustic sensor networks, depth-dependent variations in sound speed refract acoustic rays, complicating the estimation of target positions from travel-time measurements. Propagation-model-based methods rely on an assumed or estimated sound speed profile (SSP), and a mismatch between that profile and the current environment can bias position estimates. To address this limitation, this paper proposes an underwater graph attention network (UGAN) that fuses synchronized time-of-arrival (TOA) observations from multiple stations with reference-station coordinates to estimate three-dimensional target positions without requiring the current sound speed profile at inference. UGAN constructs one graph per target for batch inference. Its geometry--time attention mechanism combines interstation geometry with ordered pairs of TOA observations to compute attention weights in all three graph layers and enrich the messages in the last two layers. A shared nonlinear encoder supplies individual TOA features directly to every layer. In ray-tracing simulations with a fixed five-station deployment and two SSPs held out from training and validation, UGAN achieves mean localization root mean square errors (RMSE) of 0.307, 0.577, and 0.989~m at three increasing TOA noise levels, representing reductions of 52.0\%, 31.0\%, and 22.8\% relative to the evaluated GATv2 baseline, respectively. At the intermediate noise level, incorporating station-pair relations into the messages reduces the mean localization RMSE by 9.4\% with relation-based attention scoring enabled. For 4,000 target observations, UGAN takes a median of 58.14~ms on the same GPU, 7.0\% less time than GATv2.

authors.name: Wei Huang, Hongfei Chang, Kaitao Meng, Tianhe Xu, Hao Zhang, Yanan Wu, Qian Sun

papers.title: Optimization of a Hybrid Solar-Biogas-Battery Energy Storage Microgrid: A Case Study
papers.summary: Low-income regions like eastern Uganda often lack reliable grid power. This paper presents the techno-economic optimization of the Soroti Integrated Renewable Energy Microgrid (SIREM), a hybrid renewable system for grid-access expansion where Soroti District household grid access stands at 16.7\%. The microgrid integrates concentrating solar power (CSP) with thermal storage, biogas combined cycle generation, and lithium iron phosphate battery storage. Using Xendee optimization software with six years of NASA POWER data, the optimal configuration comprises a 37 MW CSP field, 70 MWh molten-salt storage, a 5 MW CSP turbine, a 6 MW biogas CCGT, and a 10 MWh battery system. The design delivers 61.3 GWh annually with a 42.91% IRR, 2-year payback, and levelized cost of electricity of 0.1991 USD/kWh generation (0.3752 USD/kWh load-served), achieving 32.2% total savings versus grid-only supply while exporting 28.8 GWh annually, demonstrating the viability of hybrid renewable microgrids for grid expansion in sub-Saharan Africa.

authors.name: John Elomunait, Jesse Thornburg

papers.title: PICE: Prototype-Informed Conditional Model Evolution Toward Self-Evolving Medical Image Recognition
papers.summary: Medical image classifiers in clinical practice must continually evolve to accommodate emerging disease categories while maintaining reliable classification of existing conditions. This is challenging because privacy and data-sharing restrictions limit access to historical patient data, while assigning dedicated capacity to each new diagnostic task causes linear model growth. Effective evolution requires preserving prior disease knowledge without retaining historical images while expanding model capacity only when necessary. To this end, we propose PICE, a Prototype-Informed Conditional Model Evolution framework organized around what to preserve, when evolution is needed, and how that evolution is realized. PICE preserves prior disease knowledge in a prototype-statistical memory. For each incoming task, it assesses compatibility with historical references reconstructed from memory, reusing the closest adapter when compatibility is sufficient and instantiating a new one when evolution is required. PICE then realizes evolution by updating the memory and recalibrating the unified classifier with Gaussian pseudo features, thereby integrating new knowledge into the cumulative diagnostic space. During inference, memory-derived similarities guide task-agnostic adapter selection and fusion, enabling prediction over all learned disease categories. Experiments on Skin8, Kvasir-V2, and Path16 demonstrate the effectiveness of PICE across diverse clinical scenarios. On Skin8, PICE achieves a 7.60\% improvement in accuracy over the SOTA method on new tasks, while maintaining 71.10\% accuracy on previous tasks. It also reduces additional learnable parameters by 18.51\%. These results indicate that PICE improves classification while balancing knowledge retention, adaptation, and parameter growth, supporting continual model evolution as new diagnostic categories emerge without access to historical images.

authors.name: Yifan Zhu, Jie Xu, Zeju Li, Yi Guo, Yuanyuan Wang

papers.title: Impact of the Performance of Autonomy and Communication Subsystems on the Level-of-Safety of Partially Autonomous Machine Systems
papers.summary: The level-of-safety of a partially autonomous machine system depends on two subsystems: the autonomy subsystem that manages the system between human interventions; and the communication subsystem that enables those interventions. These subsystems are typically evaluated independently. We model the level-of-safety analytically as a function of their joint performance. Three parameters characterize the autonomy subsystem: the Mean Time Between Interventions (MTBI); the urgency $\mathcal{U}$ or mean time within which an intervention must be completed to avoid failure; and the complexity $\mathcal{C}$ or mean time to understand, decide on and execute it. Two characterize the communication subsystem: its availability $P_A$ and its latency $\varepsilon$. A dimensionless criticality ratio $\rho=(\mathcal{C}+\varepsilon)/\mathcal{U}$ prescribes the shape of the Pareto tradeoff between the MTBI and $P_A$ at a constant level-of-safety. At $\rho=0.01$, a perfect link lowers the required MTBI by two orders of magnitude. At $\rho=1$, it only halves it. Under exponential timing assumptions the model is in closed form, and compliance with a safety budget can be stated at a chosen assurance level. We illustrate it for remotely piloted aircraft with assumed parameter values and propose a simulation procedure to estimate them.

authors.name: Yutian Pang, John-Paul Clarke

papers.title: Symbol-Level Precoding With Microwave Linear Analog Computers (MiLACs): Performance Limits and Stem-Connected Hardware Design
papers.summary: Symbol-level precoding (SLP) improves multiuser transmission by exploiting constructive interference based on user symbols. A microwave linear analog computer (MiLAC) maps a reduced number of radio-frequency (RF) port input signals to a large antenna array through a tunable passive microwave network. Their combination enables MiLAC to reduce the RF-chain burden of SLP, while SLP offers symbol-dependent design flexibility that can alleviate the performance loss caused by a limited number of RF chains and practical circuit constraints of MiLAC. This work investigates the joint design of SLP and MiLAC and analyzes how a limited number of RF chains and practical circuit constraints affect performance. For ideal MiLAC networks, we characterize the condition for attaining fully digital SLP performance and quantify the associated performance loss otherwise. We propose the joint effective subspace MiLAC-SLP (JES-MiLAC-SLP) algorithm to jointly optimize the analog beamforming matrix and SLP signals over a symbol block. For stem-connected MiLAC networks with finite tuning ranges and quantized tuning states, we propose the hardware-constrained JES-MiLAC-SLP (HC-JES-MiLAC-SLP) algorithm. It identifies circuit state changes for which SLP can better compensate the errors caused by circuit limitations, and updates the circuit state accordingly. Numerical results validate the derived findings and show that joint design reduces errors relative to separate MiLAC and SLP designs. Under the considered configurations, HC-JES-MiLAC-SLP substantially narrows the gap to fully digital SLP.

authors.name: Yafei Wang, Yuchen Zhang, Yiming Zhu, Jiayang Wan, Wenjin Wang, Symeon Chatzinotas, Bj\"orn Ottersten

papers.title: DynaSeek: Large Language Model-Driven Hybrid Dynamic Model Discovery for Grid-Tied Inverters from Limited Measurements
papers.summary: Discovering the unknown governing equations of grid-tied inverters from limited measurements is essential for the stability analysis of modern inverter-dominated power systems. However, existing identification methods struggle to jointly resolve unmeasured internal control memory and saturation-induced mode transitions from accessible terminal waveforms. To address this challenge, this paper proposes DynaSeek, a large language model (LLM)-driven framework for discovering explicit hybrid differential-algebraic equations (DAEs) of current-limited inverters. The framework integrates physics-constrained symbolic skeleton synthesis with the joint numerical estimation of shared model parameters and record-specific latent initial states across multi-island experience archives. Furthermore, two complementary structural diagnostics evaluating cross-record state closure and cross-window consistency are established to detect structural deficiencies across distinct input histories and transient stages. Guided by diagnostic feedback, DynaSeek directs variable-dimensional latent-state expansion and current-limiting and anti-windup refinement to yield self-contained hybrid DAEs unifying unsaturated regulation, current limiting, and post-fault recovery. Controller-hardware-in-the-loop (CHIL) experiments and closed-loop system-level simulations demonstrate that DynaSeek reduces transient trajectory reconstruction errors by one to two orders of magnitude compared with symbolic and neural baselines while accurately preserving reference critical clearing times, enabling reliable large-signal stability assessment of inverters with inaccessible internal controls.

authors.name: Hongwei Zhen, Chao Shen, Jianfeng Niu, Xin Xiang, Wuhua Li, Mingyang Sun

papers.title: Shared-Harmonic Characterization and Robust Orientation-Selection Certification for Directional Sensing Under Anisotropic Target Motion
papers.summary: Directional sensors are often oriented using historical target trajectories, while future trajectories remain uncertain at deployment. This letter addresses two post-placement questions: i) when orientation materially affects detection and ii) when a historically selected orientation remains reliable under future target-motion shift. We develop a placement-aware framework for anisotropy-induced detection (AID), showing that orientation sensitivity is governed by harmonic modes shared by the locally visible target-direction distribution and the sensor trajectory-incidence response. The resulting AID measure admits an exact RMS interpretation for the retained-harmonic orientation response. We then introduce a sensor-induced directional discrepancy, derive a conditional bound on future orientation regret, and obtain sufficient certificates for robust orientation selection whenever the future sensor-relevant shift lies within a prescribed discrepancy radius. Using 2025 AIS ship-traffic data near Terrebonne Bay, Louisiana, historical AID is strongly correlated with held-out orientation sensitivity ($r=0.908$). Across four angular-response widths, AID explains orientation-sensitivity variation with $R^2=0.920$, compared with $R^2=0.239$ for target-only anisotropy. At the nominal threshold, 316 of 350 locations are empirically classified as orientation-useful, and all retain gain above the threshold across five held-out windows.

authors.name: Mingyu Kim, Daniel J. Stilwell, Jorge G. Jimenez

papers.title: Domain-Generalizable Semantic Communications With Pilot-Assisted Adaptation over Wireless Channels
papers.summary: Semantic communication offers a promising approach to support intelligent services in next-generation wireless networks by efficiently transmitting task-relevant information. However, its performance can degrade significantly when input data and wireless channel conditions differ from those encountered during training. In this paper, we propose a robust semantic communication framework that addresses these distributional mismatches through two independent but complementary modules. At the transmitter, a domain-generalization module extracts task-relevant features while suppressing domain-specific information. At the receiver, a pilot-assisted channel characterization module extracts channel context from received pilot signals to guide semantic recovery under varying wireless conditions. Through the end-to-end training of semantic encoder-decoder pair with domain alignment and channel adaptation models, the proposed framework improves task performance under simultaneous input and channel distribution shifts with limited transmitter-receiver coordination during deployment. Simulation results show that the proposed framework improves classification accuracy by more than $18\%$ over a conventional semantic communication baseline in the unseen scenarios.

authors.name: Haoran Chang, Sweekar Piya, Xiajun Jiang, Qianqian Zhang

papers.title: Evaluating Cine and Tagged MRI-to-Speech Synthesis with Complementary Metrics and MRI-Free Controls
papers.summary: Relating tongue motion measured with dynamic MRI to the speech it produces could inform rehabilitation after glossectomy. Prior studies have translated cine or tagged MRI into log-mel spectrograms and used the two-dimensional Pearson correlation between predicted and recorded spectrograms (Corr2D) to quantify the acoustic information captured by each imaging modality. However, Corr2D has not been calibrated against MRI-free predictors that preserve basic acoustic structure. Our contribution is an evaluation framework for speech synthesis from cine MRI, tagged MRI and their combination; the synthesis network is held fixed. On identical leave-one-subject-out folds, we compare four trained input configurations with two MRI-free controls: a static mean-spectrum baseline and a time-aligned cohort template. Across 44 subjects (18 after glossectomy) producing two utterances, the cohort template, which never sees an MRI, reached a Corr2D of 0.745 and 0.664. The static baseline, which contains no timing, reached 87 to 89% of that score. No trained configuration outperformed the template on Corr2D, a cepstral distance or ESTOI; seven of the eight fell significantly short on Corr2D. For cine MRI this held across three positional encodings, an encoder temporal-attention module and a training objective matched to the metric. Cine and tagged MRI differed consistently within subjects, although the direction depended on the metric. Absolute Corr2D alone therefore does not show that a model recovers acoustics from the MRI. The two controls are a reusable method: any study can compute them from its own training recordings, so a model's margin over them measures what its images contribute.

authors.name: Karlo Vrancic, Fangxu Xing, Jiachen Zhuo, Maureen Stone, Jerry L. Prince, Jonghye Woo

papers.title: Detecting Transmit Precoding in Commodity Wi-Fi Channel State Information and Its Effect on Measured Channel Statistics
papers.summary: Channel state information (CSI) from commodity Wi-Fi receivers is increasingly used to estimate delay spread and fading. For multi-stream data frames, the access point may apply transmit beamforming, and the CSI then describes the precoded channel $\mathbf{HQ}$ instead of the propagation channel $\mathbf{H}$. This letter gives a blind test for eigen-beamforming based on the near-orthogonality and power ordering of the stream columns, evaluated at the receive-chain gain ratio that minimizes their coherence. The test needs no calibration or packet alignment, tolerates gain changes between sounding and data frames, and builds on the $\mathrm{Beta}(1,N_r-1)$ law of the squared column coherence under unprecoded Rayleigh fading. Simulations with compressed feedback, subcarrier grouping, feedback delay, antenna correlation, and SNRs of 10-30 dB give false-alarm rates of at most $2.9\times10^{-3}$ at the chosen thresholds and show precoding scales the per-entry RMS delay spread by factors of 0.3 to 5.7. The per-subcarrier Gram matrix $\hat{\mathbf{H}}\hat{\mathbf{H}}^{H}$ is preserved: the Frobenius norm is unchanged with two transmit antennas and within 1.7 dB (95th percentile) with four. With two generations of commercial access points at 5 and 6 GHz, 880 of the 896 two-stream data frames they sent to the client tested as precoded, including 601 of 605 IEEE 802.11be frames without a beamforming flag. A third access point gave 0 of 5221 in 802.11n mode and 4003 of 5225 flagged frames in 802.11ac mode, fewer in motion; a fourth gave 3283 of 3296 with beamforming on and 0 of 3223 with it off.

authors.name: Raghuram C. Kamath, Carlos Aldana, Kavya Guruswamy

papers.title: Asymptotically Efficient Finite Impulse Response System Identification without Noise Knowledge
papers.summary: Efficient identification of finite impulse response systems under unknown or heavy-tailed noise remains a challenge in system identification. Classical estimators, including least squares (LS) and robust alternatives like least absolute deviations (LAD), are often sensitive to outliers or statistically inefficient when noise characteristics deviate from their underlying assumptions. To address this, we propose a novel class of adaptive estimators that achieves asymptotic efficiency without requiring prior knowledge of the noise distribution. Our approach leverages kernel density estimation to construct two nonparametric maximum likelihood-type estimators: the estimated maximum likelihood estimator (eMLE) and the estimated profiled MLE (epMLE). These estimators approximate the likelihood using residuals from consistent initial estimates, avoiding parametric assumptions on the noise. We establish theoretical guarantees showing that, under mild regularity conditions, both eMLE and epMLE are consistent, asymptotically normal, and attain the Cram\'er--Rao lower bound, thereby achieving asymptotic efficiency. Additionally, we develop computationally efficient one-step Newton--Raphson algorithms that implement these estimators without sacrificing asymptotic efficiency. Extensive simulations across various noise distributions confirm that the proposed methods outperform classical LS and LAD estimators in both robustness and accuracy, often matching oracle MLE performance.

authors.name: Zichen Liu, Biqiang Mu

papers.title: Exact Error Analysis of Noise-Domain OTFS with Paired Covariance Signaling
papers.summary: Noise-domain orthogonal time frequency space (ND-OTFS) encodes bits through opposite correlations in Gaussian delay--Doppler pairs of equal average energy. This letter derives the exact conditional bit error probability (BEP) of maximum-likelihood detection using generalized covariance eigenvalues and characteristic-function inversion. For scalar channels, we obtain an incomplete-beta expression and its finite-sum Rayleigh average. Partial correlation yields an error floor for a fixed observation count. At unit correlation, the conditional BEP decays with an signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) exponent equal to the number of pair observations, and common Rayleigh fading yields diversity order one. Simulations validate the analysis and quantify pair-placement effects.

authors.name: Mahmoud Aldababsa, Khalid Yahya

papers.title: Passivity Shaping over Frequency Bands: A Differentiable Optimization Approach
papers.summary: The energy transition replaces traditional inertial synchronous machines with power electronic converters, introducing new grid stability challenges. Passivity provides a compositional input-output framework for assessing stability in interconnected grid subsystems, yet tuning controllers for this property over specific frequency ranges - a practical requirement in converter-dominated grids - still relies largely on practitioners' experience, typically based on intuition or trial and error. We address this gap in three steps: (i) we formulate the passivity index over arbitrary frequency bands as the optimal value of a parametric Semidefinite Program (SDP) using the generalized KYP (gKYP) lemma; (ii) we derive analytical sensitivities of this optimal value with respect to controller parameters via the Envelope Theorem; and (iii) we embed these elements in a bilevel optimization scheme that tunes controller parameters to maximize the passivity index. We validate the proposed method on two case studies of increasing complexity: a grid-following converter and a multi-converter microgrid.

authors.name: Alberto De Luca, Pol Jane-Soneira

papers.title: On the Grouping-based RIS-aided Multi-user Networks: A Graph Theoretic Approach
papers.summary: In this letter, we propose a graph theoretic framework for grouping-based reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided multi-user wireless networks. By considering both the ideal as well as the practical RIS-based phase shift models, the aspect of the RIS-user association is formulated as a graph matching problem. Thereafter, we derive conditions, which on satisfying, guarantee that the ideal RIS-based optimal RIS-user association remains uniquely optimal even in the practical RIS-based scenario. Finally, extensive Monte Carlo simulations validate the importance of the proposed framework.

authors.name: Udit Raj, Priyadarshi Mukherjee

papers.title: UMAI: UM Aware Inference with a Frozen Qwen3-ASR
papers.summary: Speech recognizers often leave filled pauses such as uh and um out of the transcript. Fine-tuning on verbatim transcripts can bring them back, but it can also change the rest of the output. We show that most missing fillers can be recovered from values recorded during a single greedy decoding pass of a frozen recognizer, Qwen3-ASR-1.7B. For each gap between output words, UMAI (UM Aware Inference) pools frame-class posteriors over an audio window located by decoder attention. It combines them with the decoder states through two stages of linear discriminant analysis and calibrates the score by isotonic regression. No parameter is trained by gradient descent. UMAI inserts [uh] and [um] tags and leaves every recognized word unchanged. On the held-out AMI evaluation set, filler F1 rises from 12.2 to 82.6. On the Nyra verbatim benchmark, where the operating threshold was chosen, it rises from 37.2 to 96.5. Total processing time increases by 14%.

authors.name: Gyeongmin Kim

papers.title: MIMOS: A Toolbox for Multivariable Modal Identification
papers.summary: Accurate and physically interpretable models are essential for the analysis and control of complex multivariable systems. This paper presents the Multivariable Identification of Modal Optical and mechatronic Systems (MIMOS) toolbox, an open-source MATLAB toolbox for identifying physical modal models from measured multivariable frequency response functions. The two-stage approach first estimates an additive input-output model from measured frequency responses and subsequently recovers the physical modal structure through information-weighted projection. MIMOS implements this approach in a practical and scalable workflow combining frequency response preprocessing, interactive modal initialization and refinement, and support for proportional and general viscous damping. Experimental results on a publicly available $6\times8$ vibration isolation benchmark and a $7\times17$ prototype wafer stage demonstrate the capability of MIMOS to effectively handle identification problems involving thousands of parameters and estimate accurate, minimal-order physical modal models.

authors.name: M. van der Hulst, R. A. Gonz\'alez, K. Classens, P. Tacx, N. Dirkx, J. van de Wijdeven, T. Oomen

papers.title: Passive Fault-Tolerant Antenna Stabilisation for Ship-to-Shore Communication
papers.summary: Directional ship-to-shore radio links require continuous antenna alignment with the shore station, while vessel heave induces variations in antenna height above the sea surface, thereby altering the multipath interference governing the received power. In conventional stabilised gimbals, attitude compensation is provided, whereas fault tolerance is rarely considered. To address these limitations, a passive fault-tolerant control scheme is proposed, whereby the antenna is mounted on a ship-mounted six-degree-of-freedom manipulator, enabling simultaneous regulation alignment and antenna height. Through feedback linearisation, the manipulator dynamics are decoupled into perturbed integrators, each controlled by a multi-barrier adaptive super-twisting sliding-mode controller. The nested barriers are associated with the performance regions of fault-tolerant control, such that inter-sample barrier crossings under discrete-time implementation lead to graceful performance degradation rather than loss of confinement. Under simulated conditions, superior pointing and heave accuracy is achieved compared with single-barrier designs, for which either precision or confinement is compromised.

authors.name: Antoine Thibault Vi\'e, Mikkel Reinholdt Hansen, Roberto Galeazzi, Dimitrios Papageorgiou

papers.title: Travelling-Wave-Based Protection of DC Hubs in Bipolar HVDC Grids
papers.summary: This paper presents a stationary wavelet transform (SWT)-based method for DC fault detection and classification in a three-terminal bipolar modular multilevel converter (MMC)-based HVDC system with a dedicated metallic return (DMR). The system incorporates DC switching stations (DCSSs) with interconnected DC circuit breakers (DCCBs). The method uses line-mode voltage wavelet detail energy for fault detection and wavelet detail energy derived from pole voltages and DMR current for fault classification, distinguishing pole-to-pole, pole-to-ground, and pole-to-DMR faults. Its performance is evaluated using a real-time hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) platform integrating an real-time digital simulator (RTDS) with embedded processing hardware. Busbar and cable faults with varying fault types, resistances, and locations are investigated. The results demonstrate the feasibility of real-time implementation and characterize the effects of fault location and travelling-wave propagation on transient energy and protection response time. The effectiveness of pole-voltage and DMR-current detail energy features in distinguishing fault types is also evaluated.

authors.name: Rahul Rane, Victor Daniel Reyes Dreke, Wilhelm Winter, Aleksandra Leki\'c

papers.title: Fast Fluid Antenna Multiple Access: Exact Analysis and Fixed-Aperture Asymptotics
papers.summary: In this paper, we investigate the interference-limited outage performance of fast fluid antenna multiple access (FAMA), in which the receive port is selected according to the instantaneous symbol-based signal-to-interference energy ratio. For any positive-definite spatial covariance matrix and an arbitrary finite number of candidate ports, we show that constant-modulus multiuser interference admits an exact reduction to the comparison of two independent correlated exponential random vectors. This representation leads to a nonnegative double multi-index series for the outage probability, a recursive coefficient evaluation, and a certified truncation-error bound. We then study the distinct asymptotic regime where the number of candidate ports goes to infinity while the physical aperture remains unchanged, assuming exponential spatial correlation. For this model, we derive an explicit finite-port series requiring no numerical integration, and characterize continuous port selection through a convergent one-dimensional series for arbitrary thresholds. The analysis further yields an exact expression relating the maximum supportable number of users to the antenna aperture size and target outage probability. Numerical results validate the finite-port and asymptotic analyses, and illustrate that given sufficient aperture size, a user utilizing fast FAMA can overcome a massive number of interferers for decent communication performance.

authors.name: Gustavo Fraidenraich, Thales Wulfert Cabral, Farshad Rostamighadi, Kai-Kit Wong, Kin-Fai Tong

papers.title: Decentralized Control Barrier Function Filters for Frequency Containment With Inverters
papers.summary: This paper addresses the design of safety filters for grid-following (GFL) inverters in power transmission systems. The goal of the filters is to constrain frequency nadir and zenith following generation-demand imbalances, by supplementing primary frequency control. Using a reduced electromechanical model and control barrier functions (CBFs), we define an ideal filter through a convex quadratic program (QP). The ideal QP filter renders the set of admissible frequencies forward invariant; however, its direct implementation is impractical, as it requires centralized implementation and model-based computation. We then use a dual proximal formulation and a two-time-scale implementation to obtain decentralized dynamic filters that can be implemented at each inverter and use only local frequency and rate-of-change-of-frequency estimates. To assess the performance and the ability to regulate frequency, we derive bounds on the distance between state trajectories under the dynamic and ideal CBF filters. The bounds quantify the effects of the filter time constant, initialization, load variation, and frequency estimation errors, and provide estimates of possible frequency-limit violations. We validate the proposed method on the IEEE 39-bus system using a high-fidelity electromagnetic-transient (EMT) model.

authors.name: Damola Ajeyemi, Emiliano Dall'Anese

papers.title: Grey-Box Experimental Identification of Reduced-Order Models for Grid-Forming Converters
papers.summary: This paper proposes a grey-box system identification for identifying and validating reduced-order models (ROMs) of grid-forming (GFM) converters. Three reduced-order modeling techniques are compared within a common identification procedure: singular perturbation with frequency cutoff and participation factors (SP-PF), singular perturbation with energy residuals (SP-Energy), and balanced truncation (BT). Testing is on experimental data with real-life components. Results show that BT achieves the highest time-domain fit, followed by SP-Energy and SP-PF; SP-Energy better preserves key properties of the identified full-order model; BT places the dominant mode closest to the stability boundary and exhibits the highest sensitivity to parameter variations; SP-Energy outperforms SP-PF in both fit quality and consistency of modal preservation. Findings suggest that the model with the best time-domain fit does not always provide the most reliable representation of the modal properties for small-signal stability, with SP-Energy offering the best compromise between accuracy, physical interpretability, and modal preservation for the considered case study.

authors.name: Marcelo Cardenas, Stephan Kenzelmann, Matteo Saviozzi, Federico Silvestro, Fabrizio Sossan

papers.title: A Real-Time Low-Cost Platform for Non-Contact Respiratory Rate Monitoring: A Comparative Evaluation of RGB Optical Flow and Time-of-Flight Depth Sensing
papers.summary: Respiratory rate (RR) is one of the earliest indicators of clinical deterioration, which makes its continuous measurement clinically valuable. In routine practice, however, RR is monitored almost exclusively with contact-based sensors, which require skin attachment, may alter natural breathing, and are poorly tolerated by vulnerable groups such as newborns and elderly patients. Non-contact sensing removes these constraints, with RGB video and depth imaging among its most accessible modalities. In this work, we present a low-cost, real-time platform based on a single multimodal sensor that provides both RGB and time-of-flight (ToF) data streams, implemented on a Raspberry Pi 5 edge device. The system integrates three RGB optical-flow pipelines, namely Farneb\"ack, Horn--Schunck, and Lucas--Kanade, together with a depth-based pipeline incorporating region-of-interest stabilization and distance-derived signal extraction, enabling the two modalities to be evaluated independently under the same experimental protocol. The proposed approach was evaluated on twelve healthy volunteers following a controlled protocol, including normal breathing, hyperventilation, and breath-holding, using a piezoresistive respiratory belt as a reference. RGB-based methods achieved lower RR estimation errors, with Lucas--Kanade attaining the lowest median MAE (3.83 BPM), whereas the ToF-based pipeline, although less accurate for RR estimation (median MAE 6.24 BPM), reached a higher apnea detection sensitivity (0.66 vs 0.51-0.55). These findings highlight the complementary strengths of both modalities and support their integration into unified low-cost platforms.

authors.name: Dominik Jasi\'owka, Patryk Ci\k{e}\.zarek, Joanna Zysnawska, Ludwin Molina Arias

papers.title: Doppler RaDAR Single-Frame Anomaly Detection and Consistency Assessment by Velocity-Conditioned Gaussian Spectral Modeling
papers.summary: Reliable speed-over-ground estimation is essential for automated railway vehicles. However, the accuracy of a velocity estimate alone does not indicate whether the underlying RaDAR measurement is physically plausible. This paper introduces a velocity-conditioned Gaussian spectral modeling framework for anomaly detection and velocity consistency assessment. A neural encoder estimates the vehicle velocity from complex Doppler spectra, while a Gaussian decoder models the expected spectral distribution conditioned on a velocity estimate. Three complementary inference-time online indicators are derived: the spectral anomaly score (SAS), conditional anomaly score (CAS), and absolute velocity disagreement (AVD). Experiments demonstrate the sensitivity of the scores to velocity deviations. Under controlled spectral anomalies, SAS and CAS outperform conventional spectral indicators in most conditions. Furthermore, AVD exhibits strong correlations with actual velocity estimation errors (Pearson $r>0.99$) for the investigated extra-peak and local anomalies. These results demonstrate the potential of online conditional spectral modeling to assess measurement plausibility and velocity estimation reliability without requiring ground-truth velocities during inference.

authors.name: Malte Stelzer, Timo Bartels, Dinu Mihailescu-Stoica, Niko Harnge, S\"oren Kohnert, Florian Poprawa, Marc Zeller, Tim Fingscheidt

papers.title: Gaussian Processes for Optimal Space-Filling Input Design
papers.summary: The quality of a model resulting from (black-box) system identification is highly dependent on the quality of the data that is used during the identification procedure. As nonlinear system identification is sensitive to modeling and extrapolation errors, having experiments that explore the considered operation range of interest are of high importance. The Gaussian-Process based space-filling input design strategy introduces an experiment design technique that aims to achieve a space-filling distribution within the argument space of a (nonlinear) approximator used for modeling the true system. Experiments carried out on simulation examples show that models trained with space-filling signals generalize better over the region of interest compared to models obtained from non-space-filling experiments. Moreover, the method is connected to the optimality theory of experiment design (V- and D-optimal design), allowing the experimenter to tailor the designed space-filling signal to maximize its information content with respect to the experiment objective.

authors.name: M\'at\'e Kiss, Yuhan Liu, Maarten Schoukens, Roland T\'oth

papers.title: Device-Referred Channel Sounding With Commodity Wi-Fi Receivers: Error Budget and Body-Worn Measurements at 5 and 6 GHz
papers.summary: A wireless product experiences the channel through its own antennas and, when worn, its user's body. Commodity Wi-Fi receivers report channel state information (CSI) per frame and can serve as device-referred sounders if their impairments are corrected. Synthetic ground truth reproducing a commercial receiver's impairments shows that five corrections are needed: subcarrier mapping, receive-chain order, per-packet alignment, received-signal-strength referencing, and window-response removal. Without them, the RMS delay spread reads up to 191% high, the coherence bandwidth falls to about half, or the Rician $K$-factor and Doppler estimates lose their meaning; with all five, the median delay-spread bias is between $-6\%$ and $+14\%$. Applied to beacons from seven access points, including a body-worn receiver at six indoor sites at 5 and 6 GHz, the chain gives delay spreads of 24-96 ns; walking lowers the median correlation over one beacon interval from 0.85 to 0.15, near the estimator's floor. Unprecoded data frames gave 0.2-1.2 times the beacons' delay spread on the same channel, so the two should not be pooled.

authors.name: Raghuram C. Kamath, Carlos Aldana, Kavya Guruswamy

papers.title: Adaptive Control Barrier Functions for Nonlinear Singularly Perturbed Systems
papers.summary: Control barrier functions (CBFs) have emerged as a flexible and efficient approach for enforcing dynamic safety constraints. In this paper, we consider a class of uncertain nonlinear systems with singular perturbations and develop an adaptive CBF framework for such systems to enforce safety constraints on both the slow and fast subsystems in the overall singularly perturbed nonlinear system with uncertain parameters.
