We first develop a robustness property showing that if an adaptive controller for the slow subsystem satisfies the slow CBF condition with an appropriate safety margin, then for sufficiently small values of the singular perturbation parameter $\varepsilon$, the slow subsystem remains within an $O(\varepsilon)$-neighborhood of its safe set. We then consider the more general case of safety constraints on both the fast and slow subsystems and provide conditions under which joint slow-fast safety is achieved despite the parametric uncertainties. The reduced-order slow model and the slow and fast CBF conditions are evaluated using an online parameter estimate and the parameter mismatch between the estimated and true reduced-order models is addressed via a state-dependent robustness margin in the CBF inequalities. To illustrate the proposed framework, we present simulation studies for two systems with parametric uncertainties: a synthetic two-time-scale fourth-order example system and a unicycle with a fast turn-rate actuator and an obstacle avoidance safety constraint.

authors.name: Prashanth Krishnamurthy, Farshad Khorrami

papers.title: From Entropy Source to Stochastic Bit-Stream: Low-Cost Converters for True-Random Stochastic Computing
papers.summary: Stochastic computing (SC) encodes values as the probability of ones in random bit-streams, which allows arithmetic circuits with very low area and power and a natural tolerance to faults. The accuracy and security of an SC system depend on the quality of those bit-streams. Conventional generators build them from pseudo-random or quasi-random sequences, which are predictable, periodic, and correlated across streams drawn from the same generator. This work proposes three methods for converting the unbiased outputs of a true random number generator (TRNG) into stochastic bit-streams (SBS) with arbitrary target probabilities: a block extraction and comparison circuit, a counter-logic circuit, and a cascaded majority-logic pipeline. All three accept bits from any true- random source and are built from standard CMOS logic. They reach the accuracy of a software random generator for both independent and correlated stream generation, and they support the common SC arithmetic operations with error that falls with stream length at the same rate. Hardware synthesis results show that the converters offer favorable area, energy, and area-delay trade-offs relative to pseudo- and quasi-random baselines. Under injected soft errors, block extraction degrades no faster than the best deterministic baseline. By bridging raw entropy sources and application-ready bit-streams, this work makes true-random SC practical on standard CMOS.

authors.name: Mehran Moghadam, Abu Masum, M. Hassan Najafi, Sercan Aygun, Di Wu

papers.title: A general-purpose safe manipulator planning framework for diverse environments without retraining
papers.summary: Nowadays, robots need to be retrained whenever their operating environment changes, and this prohibitive training cost keeps them far from daily use. The community is calling for innovations that bestow on a robot the ability to safely grasp different objects under different conditions without excessive training data and computing power. In response to this call, we present a general-purpose manipulator mission-planning framework, allowing a robot to safely perform manipulation tasks, such as grasping objects that fit in its gripper, across different operating environments without retraining its controllers. The framework rests on two innovations: a finite-state abstracted model, bisimilar to the original system dynamics, that describes accessibility of the space in front of the robot under its given arm and gripper, and a block-conservative specification generation method that turns each manipulation task under any specific operational environment into specifications about state accessibility of the abstracted model. A task proven feasible and safe on the abstracted model is guaranteed to be safe and achievable by the robot. Real-world case studies conducted on a Unitree G1 U1 humanoid show that manipulation tasks commonly encountered in daily life, such as grasping an object, pressing an elevator button or picking up a berry, can be handled within this framework, where an abstracted model of the G1 U1 robot is built only once to avoid costly model reconstructions, and different tasks are simply captured by specific block-conservative specifications, achievable by a generic mission planner with vision-based feedback control.

authors.name: Mingkang Long, Rong Su, Luhang Hong, Qingqing Wang, Ruochen Tai

papers.title: Certified Outage Bounds for RIS-Assisted NOMA with Source-Side Thermal Energy Harvesting
papers.summary: Gaussian useful-gain and mean-interference approximations can cause opposite power-sizing errors in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA). We extend a source-side thermal energy harvesting model with Poisson interference and certify two-sided outage bounds. In a tested environment, the combined required signal-to-noise ratio error has opposite signs at 20 and 24 elements per user. Under another power convention, mean or moment-matched Gamma-distributed interference can predict false feasibility with exact useful gain. In the Gamma case, the Gaussian gain approximation can mask this false feasibility. Propagated Chernoff bounds give sufficient designs. Results concern the specified model and tested regimes.

authors.name: Victor Rabiet (MIC, ENS-PSL)

papers.title: A Robust Optimization Framework for Energy System Capacity Expansion under Line Outage Uncertainty
papers.summary: Capacity expansion models are widely used in climate and energy policy analysis to find optimal investments in generation, storage, and transmission. As the share of renewable generation grows, these models rely more on transmission lines to balance supply and demand across regions. Transmission lines, however, can fail due to aging, extreme weather, or accidents. Models that represent outages as time-dependent events come mainly from electrical engineering and are applied to small-scale systems, as they quickly become computationally intractable for inter-regional capacity expansion. We develop a capacity expansion model in which the risk of line failures shapes the investments in all parts of the system. We formulate it as a two-stage, scenario-based robust optimization problem that samples time-varying outage scenarios from a Markov model and hedges the investments against the most severe ones. To solve the model, we propose a memory-augmented Benders decomposition algorithm combined with Monte Carlo simulation that can handle thousands of scenarios. The selected plan is then evaluated with an out-of-sample simulation to bound the Value-at-Risk (VaR) of its system cost. In a 25-node case study of Germany and its neighboring countries, the gap between the lower bound and the simulated VaR bound is below 1%. We compare the robust plans with a deterministic plan, which assumes all lines are always available, and with a reserve-margin heuristic, which requires local firm capacity to be above peak demand. Like the heuristic, the robust plans nearly eliminate loss of load in 1000 simulated outage scenarios. Their mean system cost is within 0.2% of the deterministic plan and about 4.5% below the heuristic. Instead of adding more generation capacity, the robust approach mainly changes the type and location of capacity, for example, by spreading storage across the network.

authors.name: Kamran Forghani, Lina Reichenberg, Fredrik Hedenus, Iegor Riepin

papers.title: Scaled Coordinate Descent for Convex Quadratic Programs
papers.summary: We study a modification of coordinate descent for unconstrained symmetric positive definite quadratic programs that combines a coordinate correction with an exact scaling of the current iterate. For a selected coordinate, the method minimizes the objective function over the two-dimensional subspace spanned by the current iterate and the corresponding standard basis vector. Closed-form expressions are obtained for the two update parameters and for the resulting objective decrease. The scaling produces a state-dependent effective curvature that is no larger than the diagonal curvature used by standard coordinate descent, so the exact scaled update makes at least as much progress for the same selected coordinate. We discuss initialization, numerical stability, randomized coordinate selection, experimental comparisons with ordinary two-coordinate descent, and a block coordinate extension. In the spirit of previous theoretical results, we give a probabilistic linear convergence result. Finally, we provide experimental results to show the effectiveness of the proposed method on synthetic data.

authors.name: Cristian Rusu

papers.title: Investigation of generalization to unseen audio generation models in audio--text semantic-alignment score prediction
papers.summary: Text-to-audio generation (TTA) requires reliable evaluation of semantic alignment between generated audio and input text. Existing learning-based alignment-score prediction models have been evaluated only on audio generated by models included in the training data, leaving their generalization to unseen generation models unexplored. In this paper, we investigate the generalization of audio--text semantic-alignment score prediction models to unseen TTA models and introduce adversarial training using a generation-model classifier with a gradient reversal layer (GRL). Experimental results show that pretrained audio encoders capture generation-model-specific characteristics and that alignment-score prediction performance degrades on audio generated by unseen TTA models. Applying the GRL improves prediction performance in some settings, although its effectiveness in suppressing generation-model-specific information is limited.

authors.name: Yuki Okamoto, Noriyuki Tonami, Takao Kawamura, Keisuke Imoto, Ryotaro Nagase, Riki Takizawa, Minoru Kishi, Shinnosuke Takamichi

papers.title: AutoRSP: An AI Agent for Radar Sensing Pipeline Design
papers.summary: Radar sensing demands a pipeline that is well-thought-out across hardware and software. We ask whether an AI agent can automatically design radar sensing pipelines at a fraction of the time, cost, and expertise that current practice needs. We present AutoRSP, an agent that embeds radar-system-level structure through sub-agents mapped to five stack layers, a code-based representation of every layer with explicitly modeled cross-layer dependencies. Feedback for the agentic search process comes from a pipeline of realistic RF simulation, on-sensor emulation, and execution on real edge devices, rather than from an LLM judge. Because such feedback can be slower than an LLM call, we present methods to efficiently optimize agentic loops. We evaluate AutoRSP on robotic imaging, automotive perception, and vital sign sensing. It produces executable pipelines with performance comparable to or better than human-expert pipelines and closed-source agents. AutoRSP's harness, tools, and benchmarks will be released to bridge the rising gap in agentic research abilities outside of frontier labs.

authors.name: Zhi Zheng, Xincheng Xie, Avery Gump, Sacha Jungerman, Hongyang Li, Yin Li, Mohit Gupta, Akarsh Prabhakara

papers.title: On the Distance Properties of Huffman Sequences
papers.summary: In this letter, we study pairwise distances between sequences with a common aperiodic autocorrelation function. First, we show that pairwise distances are determined by a ternary signed pattern encoding the relative zero flips between spectral factors. Then, for Huffman sequences, we prove that Dihedral symmetries of the zeros preserve pairwise distances, and we further derive lower bounds on the minimum distance. The results in this letter offer a starting point for designing codes with a fixed autocorrelation. These codes are relevant in integrated sensing and communication.

authors.name: Parker Huggins, Alphan Sahin, Elza Erkip

papers.title: Sliding-Window Detection of Hidden Regimes under Stochastic Switching
papers.summary: A sliding-window average is a simple estimator of the current state of a hidden regime-switching process, such as a hidden Markov model. A longer window averages out more noise but is more likely to contain a switch, and the question is what such a switch costs. We analyse the decoder that assigns the average of the last $m$ observations to the nearest regime mean. For two regimes with conditionally independent, stochastically ordered observations, a switch inside the window, averaged uniformly over its positions and directions, causes an error with probability exactly $1/2$. Consequently, for every stationary switching law, the error is at most $\bar P(m)+\bar s(m-1)/2$, where $\bar P(m)$ is the stationary-weighted single-regime error and $\bar s$ the switch rate. Under Markov switching, time reversal shows that a window whose oldest and current regimes differ is misclassified with probability exactly $1/2$, however many switches it contains, and the bound is attained up to a factor $p_{\min}^{m-1}$. For Gaussian noise with common variance, minimizing the bound gives an explicit window length which, in units of $\sigma^2/\Delta^2$, depends only on the expected number of switches in that time. As switching probabilities vanish proportionally, the optimal error is $\bar s\log(1/\bar s)/(2I)(1+o(1))$, with $I$ the single-regime Chernoff exponent. In the Gaussian case this is twice the Bayes error. For symmetric switching, exponentially weighted moving averages reduce this factor to at most $2\log2\approx1.39$, and two-block weights adapted to the switch rate attain the Bayes rate. For three or more regimes, long-window switch costs are set by the geometry of the regime means. For Markov-modulated random walks with $\pm1$ steps on a reflecting lattice, a position-aware decoder learns as fast as without walls under holding boundaries, while steps at bouncing boundaries carry none.

authors.name: Arina Pambukyan, Hayk Nersisyan

papers.title: Exact Average Consensus over Unreliable Directed Networks with HARQ Feedback: Almost-Sure Convergence and Rate Characterization
papers.summary: We study discrete-time average consensus over strongly connected directed networks with unreliable communication links, where packet errors trigger Hybrid Automatic Repeat reQuest (HARQ) retransmissions and packets are permanently dropped after a finite retransmission limit. We propose a HARQ-based ratio-consensus algorithm that exploits ACK/NACK feedback to explicitly account for successfully delivered, delayed, and eventually dropped information mass, thereby preserving the exact network-wide average despite asymmetric communication and packet losses. To model the dependence induced by HARQ combining, we describe retransmission errors through conditional decoding-failure probabilities where we simply require the conditional probability of successful transmission to be uniformly bounded away from zero. We construct an augmented sample-path representation of the resulting delayed and dropped information flows and establish its exact equivalence with the proposed distributed iterations at the actual network nodes. Using this representation, we prove that all node ratios converge almost surely to the exact arithmetic average of the initial values. Beyond asymptotic convergence, we derive an explicit geometric bound on the expected consensus error, a high-probability error bound, and a finite upper bound on the expected time required to reach a prescribed consensus accuracy. Numerical experiments illustrate the effect of the channel reliability, HARQ combining gain, and retransmission limit on the convergence-communication trade-off, and compare the proposed method with existing robust ratio-consensus schemes.

authors.name: Evagoras Makridis, Christoforos N. Hadjicostis, Themistoklis Charalambous

papers.title: Safety-Critical Formation Control of Non-Holonomic Multi-Robot Systems in Communication-Limited Environments
papers.summary: This paper proposes a decentralized estimator-based safety-critical controller for formation control of non-holonomic multi-robot systems operating without inter-agent communication. Each follower reconstructs its predecessor's motion with a closed-form estimator and applies closed-form control barrier function (CBF) based laws that are robust to the resulting estimation error, enforcing collision avoidance and prescribed longitudinal and lateral formation offsets without online optimization. Lyapunov analysis establishes exponential convergence of the estimator under constant predecessor velocities and input-to-state-type ultimate boundedness under time-varying motion, from which the estimation-error bounds used by the robust CBF constraints are derived. The longitudinal spacing policy is shown to be L2 string stable under an explicit gain condition. Simulations and Gazebo experiments demonstrate accurate formation tracking, safety preservation, and disturbance attenuation.

authors.name: Vishrut Bohara, Siavash Farzan

papers.title: Low-Complexity Near-Field Beam Training with DFT Codebook based on Beam Pattern Analysis
papers.summary: Extremely large antenna arrays (ELAAs) operating in high-frequency bands have spurred the development of near-field communication, driving advancements in beam training design. This paper introduces an efficient near-field beam training method that utilizes the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) codebook traditionally employed for far-field users (FUs). We begin by analyzing the received beam pattern and deriving closed-form expressions for its width and central beam gain as a function of user location. Building on these derived expressions, we propose a beam training method that estimates user distance from the received signal powers using DFT beams, with a computational complexity of O(1). Simulation results confirm the efficacy of our approach, demonstrating its ability to perform low-complexity near-field beam training with high estimation accuracy. Notably, our proposed scheme achieves up to a 1.96 dB SNR gain over exhaustive search methods in multi-user beamforming scenarios.

authors.name: Zijun Wang, Rama Kiran, Shawn Tsai, Rui Zhang

papers.title: Sparsity-Aware Near-Field Beam Training via Multi-Beam Combination
papers.summary: This paper proposes an adaptive near-field beam training method to enhance performance in multi-user and multipath environments. The approach identifies multiple strongest beams through beam sweeping and linearly combines their received signals - capturing both amplitude and phase - for improved channel estimation. Two codebooks are considered: the conventional DFT codebook and a near-field codebook that samples both angular and distance domains. As the near-field basis functions are generally non-orthogonal and often over-complete, we exploit sparsity in the solution using LASSO-based linear regression, which can also suppress noise. Simulation results show that the near-field codebook reduces feedback overhead by up to 95% compared to the DFT codebook. The proposed LASSO regression method also maintains robustness under varying noise levels, particularly in low SNR regions. Furthermore, an off-grid refinement scheme is introduced to enhance accuracy especially when the codebook sampling is coarse, improving reconstruction accuracy by 69.4%.

authors.name: Zijun Wang, Rama Kiran, Jinesh Nair, Chien-Hua Chen, Tzu-Han Chou, Shawn Tsai, Rui Zhang

papers.title: Precise Near-Field Beam Training with DFT Codebook based on Amplitude-only Measurement
papers.summary: Extremely large antenna arrays (ELAAs) operating in high-frequency bands have spurred the development of near-field communication, driving advancements in beam training and signal processing design. In this work, we present a low-complexity near-field beam training scheme that fully utilizes the conventional discrete Fourier transform (DFT) codebook designed for far-field users. We begin by analyzing the received beam pattern in the near field and derive closed-form expressions for the beam width and central gain. These analytical results enable the definition of an angle-dependent, modified Rayleigh distance, which effectively distinguishes near-field and far-field user regimes. Building on the analysis, we develop a direct and computationally efficient method to estimate user distance, with a complexity of O(1), and further improve its accuracy through a simple refinement. Simulation results demonstrate significant gains in both single- and multi-user settings, with up to 2.38 dB SNR improvement over exhaustive search. To further enhance estimation accuracy, we additionally propose a maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) based refinement method, leveraging the Rician distribution of signal amplitudes and achieving accuracy close to the Cramer--Rao bound (CRB). Simulation shows the single-user and multi-user achievable rates can both approach those obtained with ideal channel state information.

authors.name: Zijun Wang, Shawn Tsai, Rama Kiran, Rui Zhang

papers.title: On the Relation of Characteristic Modes of Different Conducting Structures
papers.summary: A formalism is derived to analyze the scattering of a conducting structure based on the characteristic modes of another structure whose surface is a superset of the first structure. This enables the analysis and comparison of different structures using a common basis of characteristic modes. Additionally, it is shown that the scattering matrices and perturbation matrices are no longer diagonal in these cases. Based on this, a modal transformation matrix is defined to describe the mapping between the characteristic fields and the weighting coefficients of the two structures. This matrix enables the conversion of the perturbation matrices in different bases. Finally, three examples are provided along with a discussion of some aspects of the theory. The first two examples aim to validate and illustrate the formalism. The third example shows how the formalism can be applied in the design process of an antenna element that is gradually modified, starting from a base structure.

authors.name: Leonardo M\"orlein, Dirk Manteuffel

papers.title: Cross-Layer Design for Near-Field mmWave Beam Management and Scheduling under Delay-Sensitive Traffic
papers.summary: Next-generation wireless networks will rely on mmWave/sub-THz spectrum and extremely large antenna arrays (ELAAs). This will push their operation into the near field where far-field beam management degrades and beam training becomes more costly and must be done more frequently. Because ELAA training and data transmission consume energy and training trades off with service time, we pose a cross-layer control problem that couples PHY-layer beam management with MAC-layer service under delay-sensitive traffic. The controller decides when to retrain and how aggressively to train (pilot count and sparsity) while allocating transmit power, explicitly balancing pilot overhead, data-phase rate, and energy to reduce the queueing delay of MAC-layer frames/packets to be transmitted. We model the problem as a partially observable Markov decision process and solve it with deep reinforcement learning. In simulations with a realistic near-field channel and varying mobility and traffic load, the learned policy outperforms strong 5G-NR--style baselines at a comparable energy: it achieves 85.5% higher throughput than DFT sweeping and reduces the overflow rate by 78%. These results indicate a practical path to overhead-aware, traffic-adaptive near-field beam management with implications for emerging low-latency, high-rate next-generation applications such as digital twin, spatial computing, and immersive communication.

authors.name: Zijun Wang, Anjali Omer, Jacob Chakareski, Nicholas Mastronarde, Rui Zhang

papers.title: Compressive Beam-Pattern-Aware Near-field Beam Training via Total Variation Denoising
papers.summary: Extremely large antenna arrays envisioned for 6G incurs near-field effect, where steering vector depends on angles and range simultaneously. Polar-domain near-field codebooks can focus energy accurately but incur extra two-dimensional sweeping overhead; compressed-sensing (CS) approaches with Gaussian-masked DFT sensing offer a lower-overhead alternative. This letter revisits near-field beam training using conventional DFT codebooks. Unlike far-field responses that concentrate energy on a few isolated DFT beams, near-field responses produce contiguous, plateau-like energy segments with sharp transitions in the DFT beamspace. Pure LASSO denoising, therefore, tends to over-shrink magnitudes and fragment plateaus. We propose a beam-pattern-preserving beam training scheme for multiple-path scenarios that combines LASSO with a lightweight denoising pipeline: LASSO to suppress small-amplitude noise, followed by total variation (TV) to maintain plateau levels and edge sharpness. The two proximal steps require no near-field codebook design. Simulations with Gaussian pilots show consistent NMSE and cosine-similarity gains over least squares and LASSO at the same pilot budget.

authors.name: Zijun Wang, Maria Nivetha A, Ye Hu, Rui Zhang

papers.title: Channel Uncertainty-Aware Robust Beamforming for RIS-Assisted RSMA Communication With Movable Antennas
papers.summary: This work investigates a robust resource allocation framework for a downlink multi-user communication system integrating movable antennas (MAs) and reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) under the rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) transmission protocol. Unlike conventional fixed-position antenna architectures, the considered MAs-enabled system introduces spatially adaptive channel variations in which antenna positions directly influence the effective channel responses. Under imperfect channel state information (CSI), changes in the MAs positions and RIS reflection coefficients affect both the estimated effective channels and the corresponding uncertainty radii under the adopted uncertainty model. This dependence leads to a highly coupled robust optimization problem. To address this challenge, we formulate a system sum-rate maximization problem by jointly optimizing the transmit precoding vectors, RIS reflection matrix, common-rate allocation, and MAs positions, subject to quality-of-service (QoS), power-budget, common-rate decoding, and minimum antenna-separation constraints. The resulting non-convex problem is efficiently handled through an iterative robust optimization framework, where the original problem is successively decomposed into active beamforming, RIS reflection matrix, and MAs position optimization subproblems, and tractable convex surrogate functions are constructed to enable iterative optimization. Moreover, conservative bounds on the common- and private-stream rates are derived under the bounded CSI uncertainty model to enforce the rate requirements within the adopted uncertainty sets. Finally, extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves significant performance gains and enhanced robustness compared with benchmark schemes, while also exhibiting fast and stable convergence behavior under practical imperfect CSI conditions.

authors.name: Muhammad Asif, Asim Ihsan, Zhongliang Wang, Irfan Muhammad, Tong Shen, Manzoor Ahmed, Ertugrul Basar, Symeon Chatzinotas

papers.title: Multi-UAV Trajectory Optimization for Bearing-Only Localization in GPS Denied Environments
papers.summary: Accurate localization of maritime targets by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) remains challenging in GPS-denied environments. UAVs equipped with gimballed electro-optical sensors are typically used to localize targets; however, reliance on these sensors increases mechanical complexity, cost, and susceptibility to single-point failures, limiting scalability and robustness in multi-UAV operations. This work presents a new trajectory optimization framework that enables cooperative target localization using UAVs with fixed, non-gimballed cameras operating in coordination with a surface vessel. This estimation-aware optimization generates dynamically feasible trajectories that explicitly account for mission constraints, platform dynamics, and out-of-frame events. Estimation-aware trajectories outperform heuristic paths by reducing localization error by more than a factor of two, motivating their use in cooperative operations. Results further demonstrate that coordinated UAVs with fixed, non-gimballed cameras achieve localization accuracy that meets or exceeds that of single gimballed systems, while substantially lowering system complexity and cost, enabling scalability, and enhancing mission resilience.

authors.name: Alfonso Sciacchitano, Liraz Mudrik, Sean Kragelund, Isaac Kaminer

papers.title: Sample-based detectability and moving horizon state estimation of continuous-time systems
papers.summary: In this paper we propose a detectability condition for nonlinear continuous-time systems with irregular/infrequent output measurements, namely a sample-based version of incremental integral input/output-to-state stability (i-iIOSS). We provide a sufficient condition for an i-iIOSS system to be sample-based i-iIOSS. This condition is also exploited to analyze the relationship between sample-based i-iIOSS and sample-based observability for linear systems, such that previously established sampling strategies for linear systems can be used to guarantee sample-based i-iIOSS. Furthermore, we present a sample-based moving horizon estimation scheme, for which robust stability can be shown. Finally, we illustrate the applicability of the proposed estimation scheme through a biomedical simulation example.

authors.name: Isabelle Krauss, Victor G. Lopez, Matthias A. M\"uller

papers.title: FSC-Net: Integrating Fast Fourier Convolutions and Progressive Learning for Speech Bandwidth Extension
papers.summary: Speech bandwidth extension (BWE) aims to reconstruct high-fidelity wideband audio from narrowband inputs. While recent approaches have made significant progress, they often struggle to reconstruct realistic high-frequency phase and harmonic structures, leading to perceptual artifacts. In this paper, we propose FSC-Net (Full-Spectrum Context Network), a parameter-efficient architecture designed to explicitly model cross-band harmonic dependencies. By integrating Fast Fourier Convolutions (FFCs) into a complex spectral mapping framework, FSC-Net expands its receptive field to the entire spectrum, capturing long-range frequency interactions effectively. To address the ill-posed nature of high-frequency generation, our novel frequency-progressive learning curriculum guides the network to reconstruct spectral details from coarse to fine. Experimental results on the VCTK and unseen EARS datasets demonstrate that FSC-Net delivers consistently strong reconstruction quality and generalization, particularly in the challenging VCTK 4 kHz-to-48 kHz task. Compared to scaled-up baselines, our model attains leading LSD and PESQ scores while maintaining a highly compact parameter footprint (1.54 M).

authors.name: Xinan Chen, Xiaobin Rong, Qinwen Hu, Kai Chen, Jing Lu

papers.title: Speaker-Aware Temporal Aggregation Strategies on Segment Representations for Depression Detection in Dyadic Interaction: A Benchmark Study
papers.summary: Speech-based depression detection compresses features from short audio segments into one speaker-level decision, a step called temporal aggregation rarely studied on its own. Most benchmarks fix a single self-supervised encoder and a single hand-picked layer, so a reported gain may reflect the pipeline rather than the aggregation method itself. We introduce DEPOOL, a controlled benchmark that compares six aggregation architectures with six frozen speech backbones on an English and a Mandarin depression corpus, where each configuration learns which backbone layers matter rather than fixing one by hand. Across the resulting 72-configuration grid, a third of configurations collapse into predicting a single class for every speaker, a failure tied to the backbone as much as to the method, and the architecture that is most stable in a single seed run becomes unreliable when training repeats across seeds. Robustness to backbone and seed, rather than average accuracy across a single pipeline, should be a first-class benchmarking criterion for temporal aggregation in clinical speech.

authors.name: Anisha Pattanayak, Huang-Cheng Chou, Shrikanth Narayanan, Sudarsana Reddy Kadiri

papers.title: Layer-wise Cross-Lingual Depression Detection from Speech: Analysis with Contrastive Alignment
papers.summary: Significant disparities exist in the diagnosis and clinical presentation of depression across different linguistic populations. Speech-based depression detection performs well mono lingually, but cross-lingual generalization remains an open challenge. A key reason is that prior work uses segment-level random splits without speaker grouping, leading to identity leakage that inflates reported metrics. We propose CLeaD, a supervised contrastive alignment framework that maps WavLM embeddings from English and Mandarin into a shared clinical space, without parallel data or target-language fine-tuning. Evaluating 52 Mandarin speakers, contrastive alignment modestly outperforms the baseline (F1: 0.640 vs. 0.622) under leave-one speaker-out evaluation. It also improves depressed-class recall at intermediate layers (7-8), though the small test set limits generalizability. Two findings remain robust: model scaling degrades cross-lingual performance while improving monolingual English, and a controlled within-pipeline ablation shows that speaker identity leakage alone inflates Mandarin F1 from 0.628 to 0.856, an artifact we reproduce and quantify.

authors.name: Anisha Pattanayak, Hanie Kang, Huang-Cheng Chou, Shrikanth Narayanan, Sudarsana Reddy Kadiri

papers.title: Making Highway Performance Measures Actionable: A Controllability-Aware Measure of Traffic Congestion
papers.summary: Emerging intelligent transportation systems (ITS) show substantial benefit in reducing congestion, emissions, and accidents and enable lower-cost alternatives to highway lane expansion. However, there currently exists no actionable metric by which agencies can assess the improvement potential from these interventions and then invest in infrastructure where it will be most promising. To guide ITS deployment, we introduce controllability-aware performance measures that quantify the upper bound of improvement that speed-based vehicle control can achieve under fixed demand. We operationalize this with controllable congestion, the maximum achievable reduction in system delay from controlling speed limits, which we estimate via a locally optimal receding-horizon optimization framework. This nonlinear optimization framework is grounded in a smooth reformulation of the METANET macroscopic traffic model and solved using model predictive control (MPC). Using both a synthetic scenario and highway data from the I-24 SMART Corridor in Tennessee, we find that controllable congestion is largely independent of total delay, revealing that for two days with nearly identical travel times, controllable congestion varies from 35% to 86%. We further show how the realizable share of this upper bound depends on the operational constraints imposed. On I-24, the minimum posted speed limit has little effect on controllable congestion, while the frequency of speed limit updates and the maximum difference between adjacent gantries have large impacts. This framework allows highway operators to distinguish between congestion that is structurally constrained by capacity and congestion that is highly responsive to ITS, enabling more cost-effective deployment of control-based traffic infrastructure.

authors.name: Shreyaa Raghavan, Edgar Ramirez-Sanchez, Monica Chan, Zhengbing He, Cathy Wu

papers.title: Parallel Policy-Gradient Methods for Parameter Optimization of Nonlinear Feedback Controllers
papers.summary: Structured feedback controllers provide stability guarantees, but their performance depends on manually tuned parameters. Policy-gradient methods offer a systematic way to tune these parameters, but evaluating the gradient is computationally expensive because it requires a sequential forward rollout of the state dynamics followed by a backward rollout of the costate dynamics. This letter develops a time-parallel policy-gradient framework for discrete-time nonlinear control-affine systems. We evaluate the policy gradient by formulating the forward state and backward costate rollouts as residual-minimization problems and solving them with Gauss-Newton (GN) iterations that use parallel associative scans. We show that global asymptotic stability and local exponential stability of the closed loop guarantee convergence of the parallel state solver without requiring bounds on Jacobian products throughout the state space. Near the exact trajectory, GN iterations converge quadratically in a neighborhood whose size is independent of the horizon T. When initialized at the equilibrium trajectory, a clipped variant converges at a linear rate that is also independent of T. We also quantify how horizon truncation and solver tolerance affect the accuracy of the policy gradient. Experiments on an LQR problem and a lossless Lorenz-96 system with saturated passivity-based control demonstrate improved closed-loop performance and computational benefits.

authors.name: An Nguyen, Leilei Cui

papers.title: Beyond Tomorrow -- Electrification of Hard-to-Abate Sectors
papers.summary: Reaching net-zero greenhouse-gas (GHG) emissions requires deep electrification beyond ground transportation, buildings, and conventional industry automation. This article discusses direct electrification pathways for hard-to-abate sectors, which today account for 30% of global GHG emissions and include steel, cement, chemicals, aviation, and shipping. Whereas indirect electrification via hydrogen and synthetic fuels will remain indispensable for some applications, direct use of electricity is generally preferable from an efficiency perspective. We review selected emerging opportunities for power electronics in industrial process electrification, including steelmaking through hydrogen plasma smelting reduction or molten-oxide electrolysis, electrified cement production, high-temperature process heat, plasma-assisted chemistry, and electrochemical synthesis. Across these examples, power converters must interface with highly application-specific loads, ranging from low-voltage high-current electrolysis cells to dynamic plasma reactors and megawatt-scale induction heating systems. In addition, high-power grid interfaces and in-plant energy management/buffering solutions must be clarified. Thus, future electrified industrial processes open new "beyond-tomorrow" research challenges for power electronics in close interdisciplinary collaboration with scientists from neighboring disciplines.

authors.name: Jonas Huber, Johann W. Kolar

papers.title: Public Battery Field Data
papers.summary: Battery systems and algorithms are developed and evaluated primarily on laboratory cycling data, but fielded battery systems are subjected to duty cycles, temperatures, and measurement conditions that cannot be reproduced in a lab. Field data from batteries in service has begun to appear in public releases attached to individual papers, but each release has its own format, units, labels, and other gaps that make it difficult to compare against others. We present a curated collection of 37 public field-data releases from 28 research groups, covering applications that span passenger EVs, buses, light electric mobility, grid-scale storage, distributed storage, consumer electronics, industrial robotics and satellites. Where the releases are complete enough to measure, this heterogeneous collection contains 256 GB of data from at least 150,626 lithium-ion cells, 3,287 batteries, 115.6 MWh of energy storage capacity, and 3,040 unit-years of service. Critically, it also contains 957 labeled or reported faults, which provide greater visibility into what real battery performance and safety issues look like outside the lab. We release a public repository of metadata and code for each of the field datasets. For each dataset it provides a registry entry with sources, license and access links, checksums to confirm a download is complete, a metadata table, and code for how to load it. We also report where released datasets differ from their papers. We hope the collection can help serve researchers (human or otherwise) as a useful platform for improving battery field diagnostics, fault detection and health estimation. Better field evidence can also feed back to improve manufacturing quality, inform second-life screening and residual-value estimates, and broadly accelerate electrification.

authors.name: Robert Masse

papers.title: Performance Analysis of EDMA-NOMA Enhanced V-SWAN-Assisted ISAC Systems
papers.summary: This paper proposes a vertical segmented waveguide-enabled pinching antenna (V-SWAN)-assisted downlink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) environmental division multiple access (EDMA) framework for simultaneously supporting multi-user communication and target sensing. In the proposed framework, multiple pinching antennas (PAs) are deployed along a segmented vertical dielectric waveguide to serve communication users (CUs), aerial users (AUs), and sensing target (ST). CUs are distributed on the ground, whereas AUs and ST are above the ground, where line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) propagation conditions coexist. In particular, SWAN provides an effective platform for realizing EDMA by reducing the effective propagation distance and in-waveguide attenuation, thereby suppressing co-channel interference and enabling efficient multi-user transmission. The communication and sensing model are formulated, followed by the corresponding SINR expressions. We formulate the statistical characterizations for the combination of LoS and NLoS propagation for CUs, and LoS propagation for AUs and sensing channels for generalized multi-user, multi-PA scenarios. Based on these statistical characterizations, the segment outage and sensing outage probabilities are derived and evaluated for the generalized framework. The results show that the proposed framework outperforms the conventional H-SWAN and single vertical pinching antenna system (V-PASS) in terms of segment outage probability, sensing outage probability, and segment sum rate. Monte Carlo simulation results closely match the analytical results, validating the accuracy of the derived expressions. The results further highlight the impact of different system parameters on the performance of the proposed framework.

authors.name: Arnav Hari, Sagnik Bhattacharyya, Keshav Singh, Meng-Lin Ku, Brijesh Kumbhani

papers.title: Karhunen-Lo\`eve Transforms of Autoregressive Windows Based on Matched Symmetry Groups
papers.summary: The Karhunen-Lo\`eve transform of a window of a stationary autoregressive process of any order $p$ is described through its poles, extending the Algebraic Diversity framework, which selects a transform by the matched group. For simple roots every basis vector is a sum of at most $p$ sinusoids, at the frequencies where the spectrum equals the eigenvalue, plus modes decaying from the ends. The window covariance differs from a member of the class diagonalized by the type-II discrete cosine transform by a closed-form matrix of rank $2p$, exactly when no pole is zero, so the eigenvalues interlace spectrum samples on the cosine grid, and the coding-gain loss of the cosine transform is an exact function of that matrix, below 1.2 percent for the $8\times8$ Markov block at pole $0.95$. By Kronecker's theorem the rank is at most $2\max(p,q)$ for rational spectra. A moving-average window departs in its Hankel corners, and an integrated (ARIMA) window departs by low rank from the type-VII sine class, exactly for the random walk. The exact symmetry is generically the reflection and contains a wreath product for interleaved windows. The dihedral group of the even extension is matched approximately, the dominant pole's sign choosing cosine or sine. The two groups give the transform a fast form: a parity fold, half-length cosine cores and a cascade of at most $p$ first-order Cauchy stages, exactly $p$ for a minimal AR($p$) model. The first-order case recovers results obtained by other means. This version adds complex data on the cyclic group with a border departure of rank exactly $2p$, the mixed and integrated classes, odd-length cores, and a released implementation whose kernel evaluation counts are flat in $M\log_2(M/n_{\mathrm{leaf}})$ to 5.3 percent. Experiments on recorded acoustic-array, radar and vibration data state where the transform helps and where existing methods match it.

authors.name: Mitchell A. Thornton

papers.title: Emilia2: A Large-Scale Dataset for Controllable Long-Form Speech Generation
papers.summary: Generating long-form speech requires models to keep content, speaker identity, turn-taking, and expressive style consistent over time. Yet most open training corpora contain examples lasting only tens of seconds and open long-form benchmarks cover at most two speakers per recording. We introduce Emilia2, a 229K-hour multilingual dataset for controllable long-form speech generation. From in-the-wild data, Emilia2 constructs short utterances, single-speaker long-form speech, and multi-speaker dialogues, preserving transcripts, speaker identities, pauses, and acoustic transitions. Examples longer than five minutes account for 50.0% of single-speaker long-form hours and 66.8% of dialogue hours. To support expressive control, Emilia2 provides natural language instructions for 4.77M examples and nonverbal-vocalization tags for 933K examples. We also introduce Emilia2-testset, 23 hours of bilingual recordings of up to 30 minutes and four speakers, each speaker paired with reference audio. We train autoregressive (AR) and non-autoregressive (NAR) models on Emilia2. Our 0.6B-backbone NAR model achieves the lowest Chinese CER and English WER on TTSD-Eval (5.27%/9.93%) among compared systems, while our AR model is on par with Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-VD on InstructTTSEval (zh/en: 76.2/78.3 vs. 77.1/77.9). These results validate Emilia2 as a comprehensive data foundation for long-form speech generation and minute-scale expressive control. Demo: https://charlesnii.github.io/Emilia2-demo/.

authors.name: Qinke Ni, Dekun Chen, Junwen Qiu, Huan Liao, Xu Li, Xingwen Han, Wan Lin, Kunyu Feng, Yuxiang Wang, Yusheng Mu, Chaoren Wang, Yingda Shen, Mingjie Chen, Haolong Zheng, Xulin Fan, Mark A. Hasegawa-Johnson, Zhizheng Wu

papers.title: Recursive Semi-Blind Receivers for Wideband Array Processing
papers.summary: Using the commonly employed uniform rectangular array (URA) as an illustrative example, we have recently shown that the block-term tensor decomposition (BTD) model provides a natural representation for the output signal of a multi-dimensional separable sensor array structure in the presence of channel multipath. A palette of effective and efficient semi-blind joint channel estimation/data detection (JCD) algorithms for URA processing, which wed BTD modeling with existing JCD schemes, has thus been developed, and recently extended so as to be applicable in large-scale arrays and/or time-varying environments. However, both the model and the algorithms were based on the assumption of narrowband signals, arriving through paths of effectively the same delay. In this paper, recursive JCD algorithms for wideband sources are developed and evaluated through simulations in a time-varying setting and across different constellation sizes, in comparison with their batch counterparts and the training-only-based solution. They are seen to enjoy the ability to track channel variations and detect the transmitted symbols `on the fly', with the aid of only a short initial training stage.

authors.name: Eleftherios Kofidis

papers.title: From Very Fine Vertical Resolution to Range Super-Resolution on BIOMASS P-BAND SAR Data
papers.summary: This paper demonstrates range super-resolution over arid regions using SAR tomography data with very fine vertical resolution from the European Space Agency's BIOMASS mission. As the first civilian spaceborne P-band SAR mission, BIOMASS is operating with a bandwidth limited to 6~MHz by International Telecommunication Union regulations, yielding a native slant-range resolution of approximately 25 m. The large spatial baseline data acquired during the commissioning phase in July and August 2025 provide a valuable opportunity to enhance range resolution based on the InSAR wavenumber shift principle. According to this principle, a wider effective bandwidth can be synthesized by combining complementary sub-bands of the ground reflectivity spectrum sampled across acquisitions at different look angles. Unlike existing literature, this paper offers a novel interpretation of this problem from the perspective of SAR tomography. Furthermore, the proposed method also accounts for residual topography errors. The range resolution enhancement performance is validated using all 20 available acquisitions from the July-August 2025 commissioning phase over Lop Nur, China, and Wadi al-Hayat, Libya, achieving spatial detail comparable to optical satellite imagery in a grid finer than 2 m. Furthermore, the reconstructed range spectrum of the central Libyan oasis exhibits an effective bandwidth exceeding 70 MHz. The point spread function (PSF) of a point like target in the scene demonstrates a slant-range resolution finer than 2.1 m, representing more than a twelvefold improvement over the native resolution.

authors.name: Yanghai Yu, Stefano Tebaldini, Yang Lei, Fabio Rocca

papers.title: From Pilots to Position: Experimental Near-Field Localization for ISAC
papers.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables wireless systems to reuse communication signals for environmental sensing, potentially reducing the need for dedicated sensing resources. However, the achievable localization accuracy of communication-centric waveforms under practical hardware constraints remains an important challenge. In this paper, we experimentally investigate near-field target localization using OFDM pilot signals in a distributed communication system. We consider both coherent and noncoherent localization approaches, exploiting multistatic propagation delays and time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA) information extracted from pilot-based channel estimates. A hardware setup comprising two transmitters and four receivers was developed and configured to operate at 3.4 GHz with 198 MHz occupied bandwidth to evaluate localization performance under realistic propagation and synchronization conditions. Experimental results across 16 static target positions demonstrate mean localization errors of 19.8 cm and 18.8 cm for coherent backprojection and noncoherent delay-TDOA fusion, respectively. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of occupied bandwidth on localization accuracy of the two proposed algorithms. These findings provide experimental insights into the capabilities and practical limitations of OFDM pilot-based sensing, supporting resource-efficient localization in future ISAC systems.

authors.name: Yunxin Li, Emiel Vanspranghels, Jialun Kou, Georgios Mystriotis, Achiel Colpaert, Rodney Martinez Alonso, Sofie Pollin

papers.title: Automated classification of modal displacements
papers.summary: The bending, torsional, or coupled character of a mode shape helps determine the dynamic behaviour of aerospace and civil structures. In vibration testing, it is assigned by inspecting mode shape plots, and depends on the analyst. This work proposes four indices to describe the motion of a mode from a few sensor vectors: a bending score, a torsion score, a twist share and an in-plane ratio. They are assessed on the first eight finite element modes of a tapered plate with a swept trailing edge. They are applied to identified XB-2 wing modes and to the published modes of the Sheraton Universal Hotel, a reinforced concrete (RC) building. On the plate, the twist share separates bending, coupled and torsion modes. The XB-2 modes include one bending and three coupled modes (one dominated by in-plane bending and two by out-of-plane bending). The coupled mode dominated by in-plane bending (15.25 Hz, in-plane ratio 1.33) was not investigated in earlier campaigns on the wing. On the RC building, all five modes are bending (twist share below 0.0005). The twist share and the in-plane ratio indicate the type of each mode. Hence, modes are classified without visually inspecting the mode shapes. Code and processed data are openly released.

authors.name: Gabriele Dessena, Marco Civera, Saray Undiano Ech\'aniz, Oscar Bonilla-Manrique

papers.title: Derivative Estimation from Coarse, Irregular, Noisy Samples: An MLE-Spline Approach
papers.summary: We address numerical differentiation under coarse, non-uniform sampling and Gaussian noise. A maximum-likelihood estimator with $L_2$-norm constraint on a higher-order derivative is obtained, yielding spline-based solution. We introduce a non-standard parameterization of quadratic splines and develop recursive online algorithms. Two formulations---quadratic and zero-order---offer tradeoff between smoothness and computational speed. Simulations demonstrate superior performance over high-gain observers and super-twisting differentiators under coarse sampling and high noise, benefiting systems where higher sampling rates are impractical.

authors.name: Konstantin E. Avrachenkov, Leonid B. Freidovich

papers.title: PIRA: Pan-CDN Intra-video Resource Adaptation for Short Video Streaming
papers.summary: In large scale short video platforms, CDN resource selection plays a critical role in maintaining Quality of Experience (QoE) while controlling escalating traffic costs. To better understand this phenomenon, we conduct in the wild network measurements during video playback in a production short video system. The results reveal that CDNs delivering higher average QoE often come at greater financial cost, yet their connection quality fluctuates even within a single video underscoring a fundamental and dynamic trade off between QoE and cost. However, the problem of sustaining high QoE under cost constraints remains insufficiently investigated in the context of CDN selection for short video streaming. To address this, we propose PIRA, a dynamic resource selection algorithm that optimizes QoE and cost in real time during video playback. PIRA formally integrating QoE and cost by a mathematical model, and introduce a intra video control theoretic CDN resource selection approach which can balance QoE and cost under network dynamics. To reduce the computation overheads, PIRA employs state space pruning and adaptive parameter adjustment to efficiently solve the high dimensional optimization problem. In large scale production experiments involving 450,000 users over two weeks, PIRA outperforms the production baseline, achieving a 2.1% reduction in start up delay, 15.2% shorter rebuffering time, and 10% lower average unit traffic cost, demonstrating its effectiveness in balancing user experience and financial cost at scale.

authors.name: Chunyu Qiao, Tong Liu, Yucheng Zhang, Zhiwei Fan, Pengjin Xie, Zhen Wang, Liang Liu

papers.title: Physics-Embedded Neural ODEs for Learning Antagonistic Pneumatic Artificial Muscle Dynamics
papers.summary: Pneumatic artificial muscles (PAMs) enable compliant actuation for soft wearable, assistive, and interactive robots. When arranged antagonistically, PAMs can vary joint stiffness through co-contraction, but their coupled, nonlinear, and rate-dependent dynamics are difficult to model. This paper presents a hybrid neural ordinary differential equation (Neural ODE) framework that embeds physical structure into a learned model of antagonistic PAM dynamics. The formulation combines parametric joint mechanics and pneumatic state dynamics with a neural network force component that captures antagonistic coupling and rate-dependent hysteresis. The forward model was trained on 29 selected co-contraction conditions and predicted joint motion and chamber pressures over 196 held-out conditions with a median $R^2$ of 0.89. An inverse formulation, derived from the learned dynamics, computes feedforward pressure commands offline for desired motion, stiffness, and payload profiles. With the valves closed, the mean identified stiffness was within 3\% of the commanded value from 136 to 176~N/mm and remained consistent across operating velocities, unlike a static model. In a payload-holding task, the model predicted the displacement under payloads of up to 173~N within 14\%, and its feedforward plans removed 93--95\% of it, against 81--82\% for the static model.

authors.name: Xinyao Wang, Jonathan Realmuto

papers.title: Global Exponential and Inverse Optimal Stabilization of a 3D Nonholonomic Vehicle in Spherical Coordinates
papers.summary: For the 3D nonholonomic vehicle actuated in surge velocity, pitch rate, and yaw rate, we construct continuous time-invariant feedback laws that stabilize both the roll-free and roll-augmented kinematic models to a target position and orientation in spherical coordinates. The design uses a spherical coordinate transformation with a singular set of codimension two and measure zero. We first present a backstepping design that yields explicit unidirectional, cusp-free feedback laws and strict barrier control Lyapunov functions (CLFs). These establish global exponential stability in spherical coordinates with user-assigned decay rates, while ensuring bounded Cartesian trajectories and exponential convergence to the target, consistent with Brockett's obstruction. The barrier terms guarantee avoidance of the coordinate singularities away from the target. The strict CLFs are then used to develop families of asymptotically stabilizing inverse optimal feedback laws for both systems that minimize a meaningful infinite-horizon cost. These laws inherit infinite gain margins from driftlessness, respect user-defined input bounds through Legendre-Fenchel transformations, and are implementable with either bidirectional or unidirectional surge actuation. Two penalty choices are illustrated: a quadratic input penalty whose associated state running cost approaches a prescribed quadratic form, and an input-constraining penalty that enforces user-defined bounds. This paper lays the foundation for constructive stabilization of the 3D nonholonomic vehicle.

authors.name: Kwang Hak Kim, Velimir Todorovski, Mamadou Diagne, Miroslav Krstic
